The outline of the building follows the shape of the coast, and Grasshopper shapes its undulating roof after the rise and fall of the waves. Inside, a memorial hall, auditorium, mourning hall and pier lead mourners from farewell toward the sea. Life and death continue between the tides like shells laid one upon another, giving remembrance a place where it can finally rest.

zh-Hant.heading: 靈魂渡口-以牡蠣生長為喻的海葬墓園
zh-Hant.body: 強制火化的政策與傳統的土葬觀念相互衝突，許多人難以接受。作品在一條濱海道路上，探索一種為海葬而設的新型墓園，並從這座海濱城市的生物與習俗中汲取靈感。牡蠣以新殼附著在舊殼上生長，這樣的生命循環成為世代延續的隱喻；海浪、漣漪與牡蠣殼的形態，被描摹為建築的一系列形體。模型把碼頭與紀念場館安置在山邊的海岸，兩條紀念路線延伸至海上的墓園島。弔唁者可以選擇在紅樹林間樹葬、立碑，或乘船海葬。建築的輪廓順著海岸線的形狀展開，參數化工具則依海浪的起伏，塑造波動的屋頂。室內的紀念堂、禮堂、告別廳與碼頭，引領弔唁者從道別走向大海。生與死在潮汐之間相續，如同一層層附著的殼，讓思念有了可以安放的歸處。

pins.title: Sky Garden — Zhuhai Old Community Renewal
pins.description:
A sky bridge that turns empty roads above a busy intersection into a community park.

Qingnian Road, Xiangzhou, Zhuhai, China | Community renewal and sky bridge | May–Aug 2021 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空中花園——珠海老舊社區更新
zh-Hant.description:
將繁忙路口上方的閒置道路轉化為社區公園的空中天橋。

中國珠海香洲青年路｜社區更新與空中天橋｜2021 年 5–8 月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The renovated event venue wraps a jogging track around shaded rest areas.
改造後的活動場地以慢跑道環繞遮蔭休息區。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Field research and interviews with residents found three key problems in an old community on Qingnian Road in Zhuhai: earlier planning left no space for a community park, three schools crowd one intersection, and neighbours have no place to meet. The project proposes to use the empty motor vehicle roads and the free space above the intersection to create a community park.
captions: Residential, school, commercial and park areas around the site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 田野調查與居民訪談發現，珠海青年路一處老舊社區有三個關鍵問題：過去的規劃沒有留下社區公園的空間、三所學校擠在同一個路口、鄰里之間沒有交流的地方。本案提出利用閒置的機動車道與路口上方的空間，打造一座社區公園。
captions: 基地周邊的住宅區、學校區、商業區與公園區。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Most flyovers in Chinese communities only carry traffic, so the study asks whether a pedestrian bridge can become a planned place for people. The bridge is meant to raise living standards and give residents more space for activities.
captions: Morphogenesis: selecting important nodes and connecting them to the event venue.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 中國社區裡的天橋大多只承載交通，因此研究探討人行天橋能否成為一個為人規劃的場所。這座天橋希望提升居住品質，並為居民提供更多活動空間。
captions: 形態生成：選取重要節點並與活動場地連接。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The bridge is drawn through the important nodes of the community and connected to a renovated event venue. Stepped rest areas, ramps and an air platform are added step by step along the route.
captions: Morphogenesis: event venue renovation and the air platform.
Slow pedestrian ramp with a sunshade decorative building.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 天橋穿過社區中的重要節點，並與改造後的活動場地相連。沿著路線逐步加入階梯休息區、坡道與空中平台。
captions: 形態生成：活動場地改造與空中平台。
設有遮陽裝飾構築物的慢行坡道。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The sky bridge links the primary school, the old park, the bus station and a new event park that replaces cluttered flowerbeds with a stepped rest space. Where the two bridges meet, a sunshade inspired by the flowers of the community's decades-old kapok tree shelters space that residents can use as they like.
captions: Aerial view of the sky bridge.
New event park.
The sky bridge at the street and the community entrance.
Where the two bridges meet.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 空中天橋連接小學、舊公園、公車站，以及一座新的活動公園，以階梯休息空間取代原本雜亂的花圃。兩座天橋交會之處，以社區中數十年老木棉樹的花朵為靈感的遮陽構築，為居民提供可自由使用的空間。
captions: 空中天橋鳥瞰。
新的活動公園。
街道與社區入口處的空中天橋。
兩座天橋交會之處。

sections.heading: Sky Garden - Raising a Park Above the Crossroads of an Old Community
sections.body: Field research and interviews with residents revealed three key problems in an old community: earlier planning left no room for a community park, three schools crowd a single intersection, and neighbours have no place to meet. The project proposes using the empty motor lanes and the free space above the intersection to create a community park. Most flyovers in such neighbourhoods carry only traffic, so the study asks whether a pedestrian bridge can become a place planned for people. The bridge is meant to raise living standards and give residents more room for activity. It is drawn through the important nodes of the community and connected to a renovated event venue. Stepped rest areas, ramps and an air platform are added step by step along the route. The sky bridge links the primary school, the old park, the bus station and a new event park that replaces cluttered flowerbeds with a stepped space for rest. Where the two bridges meet, a sunshade inspired by the flowers of the decades-old kapok tree of the community shelters a space that residents can use as they wish, so that the crossroads becomes a shared garden in the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 空中花園-在路口上方為老社區架起公園
zh-Hant.body: 田野調查與居民訪談，揭示了一處老舊社區的三個關鍵問題：早年的規劃沒有留下社區公園的空間，三所學校擠在同一個路口，鄰里之間也沒有相聚的地方。作品提議利用空出來的機動車道，以及路口上方的閒置空間，創造一座社區公園。多數社區裡的天橋只承載交通，研究因此追問：人行橋能否成為一處為人而規劃的場所？這座橋旨在提升生活品質，也為居民帶來更多活動的空間。橋身穿過社區的重要節點，並與一處翻新的活動場地相連；階梯式休憩區、坡道與空中平台沿著路線逐步加入。空中步橋串起小學、老公園、公車站，以及一座以階梯休憩空間取代雜亂花壇的新活動公園。在兩座橋交會之處，一頂以社區裡數十年木棉樹的花朵為靈感的遮陽棚，庇護著居民可以自由使用的空間。

pins.title: Toilet Revolution — Beijing Road Pedestrian Street Renovation
pins.description:
Foldable toilet and shop modules that bring public toilets back to Guangzhou's busiest pedestrian street.

Beijing Road, Guangzhou, China | Public toilets and pedestrian street renovation | Aug–Dec 2022 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 廁所革命——北京路步行街改造
zh-Hant.description:
以可折疊的廁所與商店模組，讓公共廁所重回廣州最繁華的步行街。

中國廣州北京路｜公共廁所與步行街改造｜2022 年 8–12 月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Toilet modules, a viewing platform and a business group combine into a mixed function group.
廁所模組、觀景平台與商業組合成一個複合機能群組。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Beijing Road has been a commercial centre of Guangzhou since ancient times, and today it is the city's most prosperous pedestrian street. On-site consultation and online surveys showed that its public toilets are hard to find, too few and not felt to be safe.
captions: Site axonometric of Beijing Road Pedestrian Street, Guangzhou.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 北京路自古以來就是廣州的商業中心，如今更是全市最繁華的步行街。現場訪談與網路問卷顯示，這裡的公共廁所難以找到、數量不足，也讓人覺得不夠安全。
captions: 廣州北京路步行街的基地軸測圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The strategy breaks the traditional detached and closed toilet into scattered and open units, joined by mutable stores, ecological toilets and transformable toilets. Analysis of the street, its available sites and its movement lines decides where the units can stand.
captions: Status of the site, available sites, movement lines and planning.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 策略將傳統獨立、封閉的廁所拆解為分散、開放的單元，並結合可變商店、生態廁所與可變形廁所。透過分析街道、可用基地與動線，決定這些單元的設置位置。
captions: 基地現況、可用基地、動線與規劃分析。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Folding walls, rotating wall panels and pop-up shops let each unit be stowed and unfolded by hand. Urinals, a barrier-free toilet and a folding store transform from one basic module, and the modules combine into business, restroom and mixed function groups.
captions: Structural details of the deformable units.
Transformation process of the modules.
Modular design and module groups.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 折疊牆、旋轉牆板與彈出式店舖，讓每個單元都能以人力收納與展開。小便斗、無障礙廁所與折疊商店都由同一個基本模組變化而來，模組再組合成商業、廁所與複合機能群組。
captions: 可變形單元的構造細部。
模組的變形過程。
模組設計與模組群組。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Toilet module groups, accessible toilets and double-layer modules with solar panels line the old pedestrian street. An excrement recycling system works with biogas power generation and solar energy so that the toilets can run themselves as much as possible.
captions: Aerial view of the modules along the street.
Floor plan with the gender-neutral toilet module.
Two systems enable a reuse cycle.
Street perspective.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 廁所模組群、無障礙廁所與設有太陽能板的雙層模組沿著老步行街排列。排泄物回收系統結合沼氣發電與太陽能系統，讓廁所盡可能自我循環運作。
captions: 沿街模組鳥瞰。
含性別友善廁所模組的平面圖。
兩套系統實現循環再利用。
街道透視。

sections.heading: Toilet Revolution - Scattering the Public Toilet Along a Pedestrian Street
sections.body: This street has been a commercial centre of the city since ancient times, and today it is the most prosperous pedestrian street of all. On-site consultation and online surveys showed that its public toilets are hard to find, too few, and not felt to be safe. The strategy breaks the traditional detached and closed toilet into scattered and open units, joined by mutable stores, ecological toilets and transformable toilets. Analysis of the street, its available sites and its lines of movement decides where the units can stand. Folding walls, rotating wall panels and pop-up shops let each unit be stowed away and unfolded by hand. Urinals, a barrier-free toilet and a folding store all transform from one basic module, and the modules combine into business, restroom and mixed groups. Toilet module groups, accessible toilets and double-layer modules with solar panels line the old pedestrian street. An excrement recycling system works with biogas power generation and solar energy so that the toilets can run themselves as far as possible. The most overlooked of everyday facilities becomes a visible and trusted part of the street.

zh-Hant.heading: 廁所革命-讓步行街的公廁化整為零
zh-Hant.body: 這條街自古便是城市的商業中心，如今更是最繁華的步行街。現場訪談與網路問卷顯示，街上的公廁難以尋找、數量太少，也讓人缺乏安全感。策略把傳統獨立而封閉的廁所，拆解為分散而開放的單元，再以可變的店鋪、生態廁所與可轉換的廁所相互串連；對街道、可用基地與動線的分析，決定了單元可以安放的位置。折疊牆、旋轉牆板與快閃店，讓每個單元都能以手動收起與展開；小便斗、無障礙廁所與折疊店鋪由同一個基本模組轉換而成，模組再組合為商業、如廁與混合機能的群組。廁所模組群、無障礙廁所，以及附有太陽能板的雙層模組，沿著老步行街排列。一套排泄物回收系統結合沼氣發電與太陽能，讓廁所盡可能自給自足。最不起眼的日常設施，就此成為街道上可以被看見、被信任的一部分。

pins.title: Urban Space Debris — An Urban Farm in Futian
pins.description:
Unused green space in Shenzhen becomes a modular urban farm.

Futian, Shenzhen, China | Urban farm and open space | Feb 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市空間碎片——福田城市農場
zh-Hant.description:
把深圳閒置的零碎綠地轉化為模組化城市農場。

中國深圳福田｜城市農場與開放空間｜2020 年 2 月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Exploded view of the farm: planting areas, greenhouses, fish ponds and work cells.
農場爆炸圖：種植區、溫室、魚塘與工作單元。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Futian in Shenzhen has many small pieces of green space that are left unused. Shenzhen imports most of its grain, and when Covid-19 cut food imports the project proposed to link urban space with food production.
captions: Scattered green space across Futian.
City growth, users and the site layers of green space, activity and route.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳福田區有許多零碎而閒置的綠地。深圳大部分糧食仰賴進口，當新冠疫情使糧食進口驟減，本案提出把城市空間與糧食生產結合起來。
captions: 福田區零散分布的綠地。
城市擴張、使用者分析，以及綠地、活動與動線的基地分層。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: People, environment and economy are treated as branches that feed one another in a cycle. An internal loop circulates material and energy inside the farm, while an external loop returns its benefits to the surrounding city.
captions: Internal and external systems of the urban farm.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案把人、環境與經濟視為彼此滋養的循環分支。內部循環在農場內流轉物質與能量，外部循環則把效益回饋給周邊城市。
captions: 城市農場的內部系統與外部系統。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A 2×2 m unit module becomes ground, plowland, fish pond, stair, greenhouse or operating room. The units are combined to suit each site and grouped into four blocks that each run a complete planting cycle.
captions: The unit module and the four steps of assembly.
Free combinations of modules with their harvest per year.
Connecting the farms with the surrounding buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以 2×2 公尺的單元模組，發展為地面、耕地、魚塘、樓梯、溫室或操作室。單元依各基地條件自由組合，並分成四個區塊，各自完成一個完整的種植循環。
captions: 單元模組與四個組裝步驟。
模組的自由組合與每年收成量。
把農場與周邊建築連接起來。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Overhead corridors link the fifth floor of fourteen buildings to the subway entrance and to the farms on two idle sites. Along the route, farming areas, a sunken purchase area, a green corridor and a planting base give office workers and residents new places to grow, buy and rest.
captions: Exploded view of the corridors.
The urban farm system across the district.
Sections along the corridor from rest space to planting base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 架空廊道串連十四棟建築的五樓、地鐵出入口與兩處閒置基地上的農場。沿線的種植區、下沉採購區、綠色廊道與種植基地，讓上班族與居民有了耕種、採買與休憩的新場所。
captions: 廊道爆炸圖。
橫跨街區的城市農場系統。
沿廊道從休憩空間到種植基地的剖面。

sections.heading: Urban Space Debris - Stitching Idle Green Scraps Into an Urban Farm
sections.body: This district is scattered with small pieces of green space that are left unused, while the city imports most of its grain. When the epidemic cut off food imports, the project proposed linking urban space with food production. People, environment and economy are treated as branches that nourish one another in a cycle. An internal loop circulates material and energy inside the farm, while an external loop returns its benefits to the surrounding city. A two-metre-square unit module can become ground, plowland, fish pond, stair, greenhouse or operating room. The units are combined to suit each site and grouped into four blocks, each running a complete planting cycle. Overhead corridors link the fifth floors of fourteen buildings to the subway entrance and to farms on two idle sites. Along the route, farming areas, a sunken purchase area, a green corridor and a planting base give office workers and residents new places to grow, buy and rest. Forgotten fragments of the city are pieced together into a web that can help feed it, and the daily commute passes through fields rather than around them.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市空間碎片-把閒置綠地串成都市農場
zh-Hant.body: 這片城區散落著許多閒置的小塊綠地，而城市的糧食大多仰賴外地輸入；當疫情切斷食物進口時，作品提出把城市空間與糧食生產連結起來。人、環境與經濟被視為相互滋養的分支，在循環中彼此供給：內部迴圈讓物質與能量在農場裡流轉，外部迴圈則把收益回饋給周遭的城市。一個兩米見方的單元模組，可以化為地面、耕地、魚池、樓梯、溫室或操作室；單元依各處基地的條件組合，並分成四個區塊，每一區都運行一套完整的種植循環。架空廊道把十四棟大樓的五樓連接到地鐵入口，以及兩處閒置基地上的農場。沿途的耕作區、下沉的採購區、綠色廊道與種植基地，讓上班族與居民有了種植、購買與休憩的新去處。被遺忘的城市碎片，就此拼合為一張能夠餵養城市的網。

pins.title: Inner Peace — A Memory Route on Kulangsu
pins.description:
A landscape route that turns the history of Kulangsu into a journey from depression to peace.

Kulangsu, Xiamen, China | Memorial landscape | Oct 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 內心平靜——鼓浪嶼記憶路徑
zh-Hant.description:
把鼓浪嶼的歷史轉化為從壓抑走向平靜的景觀路徑。

中國廈門鼓浪嶼｜紀念景觀｜2019 年 10 月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Master plan: Memory Slope, Thistles and Thorns, the Path of Exile and the Life Tree.
總平面圖：記憶坡、荊棘之地、流放之路與生命樹。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Kulangsu was once a public concession where 18 countries set up consulates, and its history still stirs different feelings in different groups of people. The project designs a route on the green space outside the former organ museum that leads visitors from depression to peace.
captions: Western-style buildings, consulates and the site on Kulangsu Island.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 鼓浪嶼曾是公共租界，有 18 個國家在島上設立領事館，這段歷史至今仍在不同群體心中激起不同的情緒。本案在舊風琴博物館外的綠地上設計一條路線，引導訪客從壓抑走向平靜。
captions: 鼓浪嶼上的西式建築、領事館與基地位置。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Historical events are analysed by the emotions they raise, using the PAD emotion model. These emotions are then translated into space elements such as a narrow road, a high wall, a mirror and glass debris.
captions: Story line of the route from start to end.
Morphology of the space elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案以 PAD 情緒模型，分析歷史事件所引發的情緒。再把這些情緒轉譯為空間元素，例如窄路、高牆、鏡子與玻璃碎片。
captions: 從起點到終點的路線故事線。
空間元素的形態。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The route passes through four spaces: Oppression, Assuage, Inner Peace and Wonderful World. Each space is built from layers such as a mirror and glass fragments, high walls along the main road, a mirror pool under a cherry tree, and a loop with a slope towards the exit.
captions: Exploded drawings of the four spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 路線依序穿過四個空間：壓迫、撫慰、內心平靜與美好世界。每個空間由不同層次構成，例如鏡子與玻璃碎片、主路兩側的高牆、櫻花樹下的鏡面水池，以及沿坡道通往出口的迴圈。
captions: 四個空間的爆炸圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the model, broken glass and mirror fragments made of plastic reflect a broken image of oneself in Thistles and Thorns. The route then opens onto Memory Slope and the Life Tree, where the feeling turns towards peace.
captions: Model views of Thistles and Thorns and Memory Slope.
Bird's-eye view of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在模型中，以塑膠製作的碎玻璃與鏡片，在荊棘之地映照出破碎的自我。路線隨後開向記憶坡與生命樹，情緒也在此轉向平靜。
captions: 荊棘之地與記憶坡的模型視角。
模型鳥瞰。

sections.heading: Inner Peace - A Memory Route From Oppression Toward Calm
sections.body: This island was once a public concession where eighteen countries set up consulates, and its history still stirs different feelings in different groups of people. The project designs a route across the green space outside the former organ museum that leads visitors from depression toward peace. Historical events are analysed by the emotions they raise, measured with the PAD emotion model. These emotions are then translated into spatial elements such as a narrow road, a high wall, a mirror and fragments of glass. The route passes through four spaces: Oppression, Assuage, Inner Peace and Wonderful World. Each is built from layers, such as mirrors and glass shards, high walls along the main path, a mirror pool beneath a cherry tree and a loop that slopes gently toward the exit. In the model, broken glass and mirror fragments made of plastic reflect a shattered image of oneself in Thistles and Thorns. The route then opens onto Memory Slope and the Life Tree, where feeling turns toward calm. The weight of history is not erased; it is walked through, seen step by step, and finally set down.

zh-Hant.heading: 內心平靜-從壓抑走向安寧的記憶路徑
zh-Hant.body: 這座島嶼曾是公共租界，十八個國家在此設立領事館，它的歷史至今仍在不同族群心中激起不同的感受。作品在昔日風琴博物館外的綠地上設計一條路徑，引領來訪者從抑鬱走向平靜。歷史事件依其引發的情緒被逐一分析，並採用 PAD 情緒模型加以量度；這些情緒再被轉譯為空間元素，例如狹窄的道路、高牆、鏡面與玻璃碎片。路徑穿越四個空間：壓抑、撫慰、內心平靜與美好世界。每個空間都由層層元素構成，例如鏡面與玻璃碎片、主路沿線的高牆、櫻花樹下的鏡池，以及一道朝出口緩升的迴圈。模型中，以塑膠製成的碎玻璃與鏡片，在荊棘之地映照出破碎的自我；路徑隨後開向記憶之坡與生命之樹，情緒在此轉向安寧。歷史的重量沒有被抹去，而是被一步步走過、看見，最終得以放下。

pins.title: City Respite — Furniture from Community Waste
pins.description:
Straws and plastic bags from take-out waste are woven into a resting canopy.

Liuyun Community, Guangzhou, China | City furniture | 2022 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市喘息——以社區垃圾打造的城市家具
zh-Hant.description:
把外帶垃圾中的吸管與塑膠袋編織成休憩頂棚。

中國廣州六運社區｜城市家具｜2022 年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A canopy woven from straws and plastic bags shades a resting space in the community.
以吸管與塑膠袋編織的頂棚，為社區遮蔽出一處休憩空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As the Liuyun neighbourhood became more commercial, the influx of visitors led to a large amount of take-out waste. The residents also lacked shade and seats, so people queued in the sun or sat on the ground.
captions: Waste from herbal shops, bubble tea shops, coffee shops, BBQ and homes.
Waste generated by the community.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 隨著六運社區日益商業化，湧入的遊客帶來大量外帶垃圾。居民也缺少遮蔭與座位，只能在烈日下排隊或席地而坐。
captions: 來自涼茶舖、手搖飲店、咖啡店、燒烤店與住家的垃圾。
社區產生的垃圾。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Following cradle-to-cradle principles, the waste was analysed to find materials that could be reused for spatial installations. Straws and plastic bags were chosen because they are the most frequent waste in the community.
captions: Straws and plastic bags as potential materials.
Ways to connect the plastic bags into strings and a roof.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案依循「從搖籃到搖籃」的原則分析垃圾，找出可再利用於空間裝置的材料。吸管與塑膠袋是社區最常見的垃圾，因此被選為設計材料。
captions: 吸管與塑膠袋作為潛在材料。
把塑膠袋連接成繩索與屋頂的方法。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Straws collected from coffee shops are spliced into barrels that form seats, plant containers and reclining benches, and residents and visitors can add their own straws to the frame. A part of the ceiling was then built at 1:1 with straws and woven plastic bags and tested for rain and light.
captions: Straw modules and the design process.
Physical model of the woven ceiling at 1:1.
Testing the model for rain and light.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 從咖啡店收集的吸管被拼接成筒狀單元，組成座椅、植栽容器與躺椅，居民與遊客也能把自己的吸管加入框架。接著以吸管與編織塑膠袋製作 1:1 的局部頂棚，並測試其防雨與透光表現。
captions: 吸管模組與設計流程。
1:1 編織頂棚實體模型。
測試模型的防雨與透光。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Vertical straws are spliced with curved straws into tree-like columns that connect the ceiling to the ground. The final canopy creates spaces for participatory design, private conversation and rest.
captions: Tree structure and physical model at 1:5.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 垂直吸管與彎曲吸管拼接成樹狀柱，把頂棚與地面連接起來。最終的頂棚營造出參與式設計、私密交談與休憩的空間。
captions: 樹狀結構與 1:5 實體模型。

sections.heading: City Respite - A Community Canopy Woven From Straws and Plastic Bags
sections.body: As the neighbourhood grew more commercial, the influx of visitors brought a large amount of take-out waste. Residents also lacked shade and seating, so people queued in the sun or sat on the ground. Following cradle-to-cradle principles, the waste was analysed to find materials that could be reused in spatial installations. Straws and plastic bags were chosen because they are the most frequent waste in the community. Straws collected from coffee shops are spliced into barrels that form seats, plant containers and reclining benches, and residents and visitors can add their own straws to the frame. A section of the ceiling was then built at full scale with straws and woven plastic bags and tested against rain and for the light it lets through. Vertical straws are joined with curved straws into tree-like columns that connect the ceiling to the ground. The finished canopy creates spaces for participatory design, private conversation and rest. Things thrown away without a thought are gathered again by many hands, raising over the street a patch of shade where the city can catch its breath and neighbours can linger together.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市喘息-以吸管與塑膠袋編織的社區遮蔭
zh-Hant.body: 隨著社區日漸商業化，湧入的遊客帶來大量外帶垃圾；居民也缺少遮蔭與座椅，人們只能在烈日下排隊，或直接坐在地上。依循從搖籃到搖籃的原則，作品分析這些垃圾，尋找可以再利用於空間裝置的材料；吸管與塑膠袋因為是社區裡最常見的廢棄物而被選中。從咖啡店收集來的吸管被拼接成桶狀單元，構成座椅、植栽容器與躺椅，居民與遊客也能把自己的吸管添進框架之中。接著，一部分頂棚以吸管與編織塑膠袋按一比一的尺度建造，並測試其遮雨與透光的表現。垂直的吸管與彎曲的吸管拼接成樹狀柱體，把頂棚與地面連接起來。最終的遮棚創造出可供參與式設計、私密交談與休憩的空間。被隨手丟棄的日常之物，在眾人手中重新聚合，為街道撐起一片可以喘息的陰涼。

pins.title: The Birth of Ginger Milk Curd — Learning Through Food
pins.description:
An old factory becomes a place where children learn by making ginger milk.

Shawan District, Guangzhou, China | Food and education centre | 6 weeks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 薑撞奶的誕生——從食物中學習
zh-Hant.description:
把舊工廠改造成讓孩子動手做薑撞奶、從中學習的場所。

中國廣州沙灣區｜飲食與教育中心｜6 週｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Model of the ginger milk making space, with a slide down to the tasting area.
薑撞奶製作空間的模型，以滑梯通往品嚐區。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Institutionalized schooling often limits the development and spontaneity of children. The project turns an old factory in Shawan District, Guangzhou, into a food and education centre focused on ginger milk, a local specialty.
captions: Exploded axonometric of the old factory.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 制式化的學校教育，往往限制了孩子的發展與自發性。本案把廣州沙灣區的一座舊工廠，改造為以在地特色小吃薑撞奶為主題的飲食與教育中心。
captions: 舊工廠的爆炸軸測圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The making of ginger milk is traced step by step, from getting buffalo milk and picking ginger to tasting the result. Each step becomes a chance for situational education through food.
captions: Production process of ginger milk.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案逐步拆解薑撞奶的製作過程，從取得水牛奶、採摘生薑到品嚐成品。每一個步驟都成為透過食物進行情境教育的機會。
captions: 薑撞奶的製作流程。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The programs follow the process: a cowshed, walking trails, a watch tower, a climbing area, a production area and a dining table. The making space is divided into three layers, from interactive projection on the first floor to preparing materials and art on the second and making ginger milk on the third.
captions: Programs along the ginger milk process.
Plan of the making ginger milk space.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 空間機能依製作流程配置：牛棚、步道、瞭望塔、攀爬區、製作區與餐桌。製作空間分為三層，一樓是互動投影，二樓用於備料與藝術創作，三樓則製作薑撞奶。
captions: 沿著薑撞奶製作流程配置的空間機能。
薑撞奶製作空間平面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: After making ginger milk, children slide down to the tasting area on the first floor. A folding truck that opens like a book can be pushed outside to sell ginger milk to the neighbourhood.
captions: Model of the stairs and tasting area.
Steps of heating, waiting and mixing the milk.
The folding truck for selling ginger milk.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 做完薑撞奶後，孩子們可沿滑梯滑到一樓的品嚐區。一輛像書本般展開的摺疊餐車，可推到戶外向街坊販售薑撞奶。
captions: 樓梯與品嚐區的模型。
加熱、等待與撞奶的步驟。
販售薑撞奶的摺疊餐車。

sections.heading: The Birth of Ginger Milk Curd - Learning at Every Step of a Recipe
sections.body: Institutional schooling often limits the growth and spontaneity of children. The project turns an old factory into a food and education centre devoted to ginger milk curd, a local speciality. The making of the dessert is traced step by step, from obtaining buffalo milk and picking ginger to tasting the result. Each step becomes a chance for situational learning through food. The programmes follow the process: a cowshed, walking trails, a watch tower, a climbing area, a production area and a dining table. The making space is arranged in three layers, with interactive projection on the first floor, preparing ingredients and making art on the second, and making ginger milk curd on the third. Once the dessert is made, children slide down to the tasting area on the first floor. A folding truck that opens like a book can be pushed outside to sell ginger milk curd to the neighbourhood. A single bowl of sweetness travels from pasture to table, and through making, watching and sharing, children rediscover the curiosity and joy of learning, as education returns to everyday life itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 薑撞奶的誕生-在食物的每一步中學習
zh-Hant.body: 制度化的學校教育，往往限制了孩子的發展與自發性。作品把一座老工廠改造為以薑撞奶為主題的食物與教育中心，這道點心正是當地的特產。薑撞奶的製作被一步步追溯，從取得水牛奶、採摘生薑，到品嚐成品；每一個步驟，都成為透過食物進行情境教育的機會。各項機能依循製作流程展開：牛棚、步道、瞭望塔、攀爬區、製作區與餐桌。製作空間分為三層，一樓是互動投影，二樓準備材料並從事藝術創作，三樓則動手製作薑撞奶。完成之後，孩子們順著滑梯滑到一樓的品嚐區；一輛像書本般展開的摺疊貨車，還能推到戶外，把薑撞奶賣給鄰里。一碗甜品從牧場走到餐桌，孩子們也在動手、觀察與分享之間，重新找回學習的好奇與樂趣，讓教育回到生活本身。

pins.title: The Stair to the Roof — Renovation of a Dormitory
pins.description:
Big stairs and rooftop modules give students the activity space their dormitory lacks.

Jinwan District, Zhuhai, China | Dormitory renovation | 2022 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 通往屋頂的階梯——宿舍改造
zh-Hant.description:
以大階梯與屋頂模組，為學生補足宿舍所缺的活動空間。

中國珠海金灣區｜宿舍改造｜2022 年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Activity spaces are fitted under the big stairs that climb the dormitory.
在沿宿舍攀升的大階梯下方嵌入活動空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In the dormitory, personal habits clash, and the long and narrow campus leaves students far from the places they need. Students lack space to move, study and gather outside their rooms.
captions: Location and the distance between units on campus.
The original dormitory.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 宿舍裡的個人生活習慣彼此衝突，狹長的校園也讓學生距離所需設施遙遠。學生在房間以外缺少活動、讀書與聚會的空間。
captions: 基地位置與校園各單元之間的距離。
原有的宿舍。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A survey of student life found needs for many kinds of activity, from discussion, music and study to games, exercise and parties. The roof is the closest unused space, so it is unlocked and linked to modules for these activities.
captions: Activity spaces that students need.
Strategies: unlock the roof and design different modules.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 對學生生活的調查顯示，他們需要從討論、音樂、讀書到遊戲、運動與派對等多種活動空間。屋頂是距離最近的閒置空間，因此本案開放屋頂，並連接容納這些活動的模組。
captions: 學生需要的活動空間。
策略：開放屋頂並設計多種模組。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Five grass mouldings were made to test how the roof could connect to the ground and become public. Like Tetris, the space under the big stairs is filled with modules shaped to each site.
captions: Conceptual model and hypotheses in grass.
Combination samples for different sites.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 本案製作五個草地模型，測試屋頂如何連接地面並成為公共空間。大階梯下方的空間如同俄羅斯方塊般，以順應各處基地的模組填滿。
captions: 以草地製作的概念模型與假設。
因應不同基地的組合方案。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Four different roofs are linked by bridges that connect the otherwise separate dormitories. The double-layer aluminium modules allow natural light and air while giving sound insulation and keeping heat.
captions: Rooftop activity space across the dormitories.
Module layout of the staircase interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 四種不同的屋頂以天橋相連，串起原本各自分離的宿舍。雙層鋁製模組引入自然光與通風，同時具備隔音與保溫效果。
captions: 橫跨宿舍的屋頂活動空間。
階梯內部的模組配置。

sections.heading: The Stair to the Roof - Returning Idle Rooftops to Dormitory Life
sections.body: In the dormitory, personal habits clash, and the long, narrow campus leaves students far from the places they need. Beyond their rooms, students lack space to move, study and gather. A survey of student life revealed needs for many kinds of activity, from discussion, music and study to games, exercise and parties. The roof is the nearest unused space, so it is unlocked and linked to modules that hold these activities. Five grass mouldings were made to test how the roof could meet the ground and become public. Like a game of Tetris, the space beneath the big stairs is filled with modules shaped to fit each site. Four different roofs are joined by bridges that connect dormitories which once stood apart. The double-layer aluminium modules let in natural light and air while providing sound insulation and keeping in heat. From the bedroom door up to the roof, a single stair extends crowded daily life beneath the open sky. Dormitory life gains a place to breathe, to gather and to linger at ease, and rooftops long locked away become the shared living room of the whole campus community.

zh-Hant.heading: 通往屋頂的階梯-把閒置屋頂還給宿舍生活
zh-Hant.body: 在宿舍裡，個人習慣彼此衝突，狹長的校園又讓學生與所需的場所相距遙遠；房間之外，學生缺少活動、讀書與聚會的空間。一份關於學生生活的調查，發現從討論、音樂、讀書到遊戲、運動與派對等多種活動的需求。屋頂是最近卻未被使用的空間，於是它被開啟，並與承載這些活動的模組相連。五個草地模型被製作出來，測試屋頂如何與地面相接，並轉化為公共空間；如同俄羅斯方塊一般，大階梯下方的空間被依各處基地形狀量身打造的模組填滿。四座不同的屋頂以橋相連，串起原本彼此分隔的宿舍。雙層鋁製模組引入自然光與空氣，同時兼具隔音與保溫。從房門走上屋頂，一道階梯把擁擠的日常延伸到天空之下，讓宿舍生活多出一片可以呼吸、相聚與自在停留的地方。

pins.title: A Carnival for the Terminally Ill Elderly — Healthcare Space
pins.description:
A healthcare space that turns the last stage of life into a journey of care and memory.

Shenzhen, China | Healthcare space for the elderly | 2021 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 臨終長者的嘉年華——安寧照護空間
zh-Hant.description:
把人生最後階段轉化為一段照護與追思旅程的安寧空間。

中國深圳｜長者安寧照護空間｜2021 年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Exploded views: the numbers show each function space and the arrows show the order of the visit.
爆炸圖：數字標示各機能空間，箭頭標示參訪順序。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: By 2035 there will be two elderly people to support for every young person, yet there is no special healthcare space for terminally ill people. The survey found that most of the elderly have a bad impression of current healthcare spaces and that many nursing workers lack experience.
captions: Status survey of the elderly, nursing homes and nursing workers.
Population imbalance and the prejudice against healthcare spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 到了 2035 年，每位年輕人將要扶養兩位長者，卻沒有專為臨終者設計的醫療照護空間。調查發現，多數長者對現有照護空間印象不佳，許多照護人員也缺乏經驗。
captions: 長者、養老院與照護人員的現況調查。
人口失衡與對照護空間的偏見。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project reads the needs of the elderly from physiological needs and safety to belonging, care and psychological comfort. The site is planned as a route from the entrance through residential and activity areas, a botanical garden, a memorial space and a meditation promenade.
captions: Plan of the residential, memorial and garden areas.
Design thinking sketches and types of wheelchair.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案從生理需求、安全，到歸屬、照護與心理慰藉，解讀長者的需求。基地規劃為一條路線，從入口經過居住區與活動區、植物園、紀念空間，再到冥想步道。
captions: 居住區、紀念區與花園的平面圖。
設計思考草圖與輪椅類型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The pool is divided into three areas: the deepest for swimming, the middle for people in wheelchairs to exercise, and the top for those who like to soak their feet. A smart armrest senses the sleep of the elderly and adjusts its position to keep them warm and safe at night.
captions: Detailed vertical section of the pool.
The smart armrest strategy.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 泳池分為三區：最深處供游泳，中間供輪椅使用者運動，最上層則給喜歡泡腳的長者。智慧扶手能感知長者的睡眠，並調整位置，在夜間為他們保暖與防護。
captions: 泳池的詳細垂直剖面。
智慧扶手策略。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Self-care rooms and shared balconies let the elderly decorate their own space and meet each other. After death, the body can become nutrient soil that grows into a tree in the garden, so that relatives have a living place to remember them.
captions: Sections of the self-care room and the shared balcony.
From nutrient soil to a mature tree.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 自理房與共享陽台，讓長者能布置自己的空間並彼此相聚。長者離世後，遺體可化為營養土，在花園中長成一棵樹，讓親人有一處充滿生命的追思之地。
captions: 自理房與共享陽台的剖面。
從營養土到長成大樹。

sections.heading: A Carnival for the Terminally Ill Elderly - Warmth at the End of Life
sections.body: By 2035 every young person will support two elderly people, yet there is no healthcare space designed especially for the terminally ill. A survey found that most older people hold a poor impression of current care spaces and that many nursing workers lack experience. The project reads the needs of the elderly from physiological needs and safety to belonging, care and psychological comfort. The site is planned as a route from the entrance through residential and activity areas, a botanical garden and a memorial space to a meditation promenade. The pool is divided into three areas: the deepest for swimming, the middle for people in wheelchairs to exercise, and the top for those who like to soak their feet. A smart armrest senses the sleep of the elderly and adjusts its position to keep them warm and safe at night. Self-care rooms and shared balconies let residents decorate their own space and meet one another. After death, the body can become nourishing soil that grows into a tree in the garden, so that relatives have a living place to remember. The end of life is no longer cold, but closes gently like a carnival among company and green.

zh-Hant.heading: 臨終長者的嘉年華-讓生命終點也有溫度
zh-Hant.body: 到二〇三五年，每一位年輕人將要扶養兩位長者，然而目前並沒有專為臨終者設計的照護空間。調查發現，多數長者對現有的照護空間印象不佳，許多照護人員也缺乏經驗。作品從生理需求、安全，到歸屬、關懷與心理慰藉，解讀長者的需要；基地被規劃為一條路線，從入口經過居住與活動區、植物園、紀念空間，直到冥想步道。水池分為三區：最深處供游泳，中段讓坐輪椅的人運動，最上層則給喜歡泡腳的人。智慧扶手能感知長者的睡眠，並調整位置，在夜裡保持溫暖與安全。自理房與共享陽台讓長者布置自己的空間，也彼此相遇。離世之後，遺體可化為滋養的土壤，在園中長成一棵樹，讓親人有一處活著的地方來懷念。生命的終點不再冰冷，而像一場溫柔的嘉年華，在陪伴與綠意中緩緩落幕。

pins.title: Reborn — A Space of Embryonic Growth
pins.description:
A cave-like space shaped by the growth of an embryo, for those who carry the pain of abortion.

China | Spatial installation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重生——胚胎成長的空間
zh-Hant.description:
依胚胎成長形塑的洞穴般空間，給承受流產之痛的人。

中國｜空間裝置｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Sectional elevation: a cave-like space drawn by hand, with figures to show its scale.
剖立面：手繪的洞穴般空間，以人物標示尺度。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: More than 13 million abortions are expected in China each year, and half of them are repeated abortions that are a serious public health problem. Behind the numbers are people who find it hard to talk about the physical and mental pain they go through.
captions: Preliminary investigation: rates, research fact sheets and reasons for abortion.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 中國每年預計發生超過 1300 萬例人工流產，其中一半是重複流產，是嚴重的公共衛生問題。數字背後，是一群難以說出身心痛苦的人。
captions: 初步調查：流產比例、研究資料與流產原因。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project studies how an embryo grows and turns its forms into single spatial units. These units are then joined along a route that moves from a narrow passage to a final room.
captions: Monomer morphogenesis.
Spatial morphology generation.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案研究胚胎如何成長，並把其形態轉化為單一的空間單元。這些單元再沿著一條路線串連，從狹窄的通道走向最後的房間。
captions: 單體形態生成。
空間形態生成。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The form is tested by hand with paper, wire mesh and gypsum cloth, then given texture. A sequence model sets the steps of the visit from falling in to lying down at the end.
captions: Manual attempt step by step.
Model study.
Adding texture and the sequence model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 形態以紙、鐵絲網與石膏布親手試做，再加上質感。序列模型定出參訪的步驟，從跌入到最後躺下。
captions: 逐步的手作嘗試。
模型研究。
加上質感與序列模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The space is a chain of winding, narrow and open moments for perception, exploration, movement and memory. Visitors walk through it as a slow passage of rebirth and can choose how to remember.
captions: Spatial sequence: winding, narrow passages, perception, movement and memorials.
Model and architectural drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 空間由蜿蜒、狹窄與開闊的片段串成，供人感知、探索、移動與追憶。參訪者緩緩穿越，如同一段重生之路，並能選擇如何記住。
captions: 空間序列：蜿蜒、狹窄通道、感知、移動與紀念。
模型與建築圖。

sections.heading: Reborn - A Passage Shaped by the Growth of an Embryo
sections.body: More than thirteen million abortions are expected each year, and half of them are repeated abortions, a serious public health problem. Behind the numbers are people who find it hard to speak of the physical and mental pain they go through. The project studies how an embryo grows and turns its forms into single spatial units. These units are then joined along a route that moves from a narrow passage toward a final room. The form is tested by hand with paper, wire mesh and gypsum cloth, and then given texture. A sequence model sets the steps of the visit, from falling in at the beginning to lying down at the end. The space becomes a chain of winding, narrow and open moments for perception, exploration, movement and memory. Visitors walk through it as a slow passage of rebirth and can choose how they wish to remember. The architecture does not speak on anyone's behalf; it simply keeps quiet company. Pain that resists words can be felt and held among light, shadow and turning walls, and those who stand outside that silence are given a way to come closer to it.

zh-Hant.heading: 重生-沿著胚胎成長走過的空間
zh-Hant.body: 每年預計有超過一千三百萬例人工流產，其中一半是重複流產，構成嚴重的公共衛生問題。在數字背後，是難以說出身心之痛的人們。作品研究胚胎如何生長，並把胚胎的形態轉化為一個個獨立的空間單元；這些單元再沿著一條路線串連起來，從狹窄的通道走向最後的房間。形態先以紙、鐵絲網與石膏布手工測試，再賦予質感；序列模型則設定參觀的步驟，從墜入開始，到最後躺下為止。整個空間是一連串蜿蜒、狹窄與開闊的片刻，分別對應感知、探索、移動與記憶。來訪者穿行其中，如同經歷一段緩慢的重生之旅，並且可以選擇如何記住。空間不替人訴說，只是安靜地陪伴；那些難以言說的痛，得以在光影與曲折之間被感受、被承接，也讓旁人得以靠近這份沉默。

pins.title: Memory of the Tower — Tower Shadow Building Renewal
pins.description:
A 1919 riverside tower studio reborn as a stage for Cantonese opera and morning tea.

Guangzhou, China | Heritage renewal | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 塔樓記憶——塔影樓活化
zh-Hant.description:
將 1919 年的江畔塔樓畫室，活化為粵劇與早茶的舞台。

中國廣州｜歷史建築活化｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower model at night, with its Chinese roof on a Western-style body.
夜色中的塔樓模型，西式樓身上覆著中式屋頂。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: This tower studio on the west bank of the Pearl River in Guangzhou was built in 1919 and is called the Tower Shadow Building because of its reflection in the water. It is a historical site with a strange mix of Chinese and Western looks, yet few people know what it is or what it is for.
captions: Exploded view of the tower.
Project status: viewing platform, living rooms and meeting rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座塔樓畫室位於廣州珠江西岸，建於 1919 年，因倒映在江水中而被稱為「塔影樓」。它是一處中西合璧、樣貌奇特的歷史建築，卻很少人知道它是什麼、做什麼用。
captions: 塔樓爆炸圖。
現況：觀景平台、起居室與會議室。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Provincial rules ask that a cultural relic be reused in a way that fits its heritage value, such as an exhibition hall or a place for leisure. The site study shows crowds by the river, large open spaces and views of both banks around the tower.
captions: Design strategy for the four storeys.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 省級規定要求文物的再利用須符合其文化遺產價值，例如作為展覽館或休閒場所。基地研究顯示，塔樓周邊有江邊人潮、大片開放空間，以及兩岸的景觀。
captions: 四個樓層的設計策略。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The storeys are staggered to make room for a stair and filled with Cantonese culture, from opera to morning tea. Each floor gets its own scene of the stage, the costumes, the orders and the tea.
captions: Design generation: Cantonese opera and morning tea.
Section of the design generation.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 各樓層錯動以留出樓梯空間，並注入從粵劇到早茶的廣府文化。每層樓各有一幕場景：舞台、戲服、點單與品茶。
captions: 設計生成：粵劇與早茶。
設計生成剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The handmade model shows a viewing deck on top, an opera stage, an exhibition floor and a tea and dining floor below. Laser-cut planks were glued together to test the stair and the light inside.
captions: The four sides of the model.
Model details.
Interior model views.
Floor plan with the memorial hall and the stair.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 手作模型呈現頂層的觀景台、粵劇舞台、展覽層，以及下方的茶飲與用餐層。雷射切割的板材黏合而成，用來測試室內的樓梯與光線。
captions: 模型的四個立面。
模型細部。
室內模型視角。
紀念廳與樓梯的平面圖。

sections.heading: Memory of the Tower - Layering Cantonese Culture Into a Century-Old Reflection
sections.body: This tower studio on a riverbank was built in 1919 and is called the Tower Shadow Building because of its reflection in the water. It is a historic site with a curious blend of Chinese and Western appearances, yet few people know what it is or what it is for. Regulations ask that a cultural relic be reused in a way that fits its heritage value, such as an exhibition hall or a place for leisure. The site study shows crowds along the river, large open spaces and views of both banks around the tower. The storeys are staggered to make room for a stair and filled with Cantonese culture, from opera to morning tea. Each floor receives its own scene: the stage, the costumes, the ordering of dishes and the tea. The handmade model shows a viewing deck on top, an opera stage, an exhibition floor, and a floor for tea and dining below. Laser-cut planks were glued together to test the stair and the light inside. A forgotten tower steps out of its reflection and back into everyday life, where opera, costume and tea can once again gather people along the water.

zh-Hant.heading: 塔樓記憶-把粵韻文化疊進一座百年塔影
zh-Hant.body: 這座河畔的塔樓畫室建於一九一九年，因倒映在水中的身影而被稱為塔影樓。它是一處中西風格奇特交融的歷史古蹟，卻少有人知道它是什麼、用來做什麼。相關規範要求文物的再利用須符合其遺產價值，例如作為展覽館或休閒場所；基地研究則顯示，塔樓周圍有河邊聚集的人潮、大片開放空間，以及眺望兩岸的視野。樓層被錯開，騰出設置樓梯的空間，並填入從粵劇到早茶的粵式文化；每一層樓各有自己的場景：舞台、戲服、點單與茶點。手作模型呈現頂層的觀景平台、粵劇舞台、展覽層，以及下方的茶點與用餐層；雷射切割的木板被黏合在一起，用以測試樓梯與室內的光線。一座被遺忘的塔，從倒影中重新走回人們的日常。

pins.title: Rabbit Hole — A Healing Underland
pins.description:
A sunken space of staggered floors, built from what the senses notice, to heal the stressed mind.

Healing architecture | Competition entry | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 兔子洞——療癒的地下世界
zh-Hant.description:
由感官所察覺之物構成的錯落下沉空間，療癒壓力下的心靈。

療癒建築｜競圖作品｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometric view: staggered floors and winding stairs lead down into the hole.
軸測圖：錯落的樓板與蜿蜒的樓梯通往洞穴深處。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The international competition Into the Rabbit Hole asks for architecture that can heal the stressed human mind. It calls for spaces beyond conditioned thinking, with a geometry, a volume and an underland of one's own.
captions: Perception map of each mark in the field.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 國際競圖「掉進兔子洞」要求設計能療癒壓力下人心的建築。它呼籲跳脫制式思考，創造屬於自己的幾何、量體與地下世界。
captions: 場域中各個標記的感知地圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project maps what the senses pick up on the street, from sounds to touch and the passing of time. These moments are drawn as lines and turned into a set of spatial forms.
captions: Spatial extraction.
Extracted forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案記錄感官在街道上接收到的一切，從聲音、觸感到時間的流逝。這些片刻被畫成線條，再轉化為一組空間形態。
captions: 空間萃取。
萃取出的形態。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The space sinks below the ground, and its layout is sketched as rings of rooms around a core. Models refine the floors, and the changing light and shadow of roots and trees reflect the passage of time.
captions: Sinking space and layout sketches.
Model refinement.
Time perception.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 空間沉入地下，平面以環繞核心的房間草擬。模型逐步修正樓板，樹根與樹木的光影變化映照出時間的流逝。
captions: 下沉空間與平面草圖。
模型修正。
時間感知。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Staggered floors with different heights and entrances give people different experiences in hearing and vision. A circular cloister, a rest area and a meditation root guide visitors through the hole at their own pace.
captions: The physical model.
Interior renderings of the staggered floors.
Section of the underground space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 錯落的樓板有不同的高度與入口，帶給人們不同的聽覺與視覺體驗。環形迴廊、休憩區與冥想之根，引導參訪者依自己的步調穿越洞穴。
captions: 實體模型。
錯落樓板的室內渲染圖。
地下空間剖面。

sections.heading: Rabbit Hole - A Healing World Sunk Below Ground
sections.body: The international competition Into the Rabbit Hole asks for architecture that can heal the stressed human mind. It calls for spaces beyond conditioned thinking, with a geometry, a volume and an underland of their own. The project begins by mapping what the senses pick up on the street, from sounds and touch to the passing of time. These moments are drawn as lines and then turned into a set of spatial forms. The space sinks below the ground, and its layout is sketched as rings of rooms gathered around a core. Models refine the floors, and the shifting light and shadow of roots and trees reflect the passage of time. Staggered floors with different heights and entrances give people different experiences of hearing and sight. A circular cloister, a rest area and a meditation root guide visitors through the hole at their own pace. Descending from the noise of the street, the senses are gathered and settled layer by layer, and a tense mind can slowly loosen among dim light and roots. Visitors recover a rhythm and a quiet of their own underground, then return to the surface with new eyes.

zh-Hant.heading: 兔子洞-沉入地下的療癒世界
zh-Hant.body: 一場名為「進入兔子洞」的國際競賽，徵求能療癒壓力下人心的建築；它呼喚超越慣性思維的空間，擁有屬於自己的幾何、體量與地下世界。作品首先描繪感官在街道上捕捉到的一切，從聲音、觸覺到時間的流逝；這些片刻被畫成線條，再轉化為一組空間形態。空間沉入地面之下，平面被勾勒為環繞核心的一圈圈房間；模型反覆推敲各層樓板，樹根與樹木變幻的光影，映照出時間的流轉。高低錯落的樓層各有不同的高度與入口，帶給人們在聽覺與視覺上相異的體驗。一座環形迴廊、一處休憩區與一道冥想之根，引導來訪者依自己的步調穿越這個洞穴。從喧囂的街面向下，感官被一層層收攏、沉澱，緊繃的心靈得以在幽微的光與根系之間慢慢鬆開，讓人在地底找回屬於自己的節奏與寧靜，再帶著新的眼光回到地面。

pins.title: Building Surround — A Park for Stress Relief
pins.description:
An unplanned square among office towers turned into a park where workers can take a break.

Tianhe, Guangzhou, China | Urban park | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 高樓環繞——紓壓城市公園
zh-Hant.description:
把辦公大樓間未經規劃的廣場，轉化為讓上班族喘息的公園。

中國廣州天河｜城市公園｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Site modification plan: paths, trees and pools, with a view of each area.
基地改造平面：步道、樹木與水池，並附各區的視角。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Walking along a road in Tianhe, Guangzhou, the designer saw slogans on mental health posted on hoarding boards. Office towers, crowds of workers and heavily regulated shopping areas during the epidemic left people nearby no place to take a break from work.
captions: Site conditions: tall buildings, height differences and a lack of open space.
The square between the towers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 走在廣州天河的路上，設計者看見工地圍板上貼滿心理健康的標語。辦公大樓、密集的上班人潮，加上疫情期間嚴格管制的商場，讓附近的人無處可以從工作中喘口氣。
captions: 基地現況：高樓環繞、高差與缺乏開放空間。
高樓之間的廣場。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: In the middle of this business district lies Guangzhou East Station Square, a large space that seems unplanned. The project lists what workers, residents, students and passengers each need from it, from rest to play and quick passage.
captions: Site requirements for each user group.
Site planning: routes, planting and functional areas.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 在這片商業區的中央，廣州東站廣場是一處看似未經規劃的大型空間。本案列出上班族、居民、學生與旅客各自的需求，從休息、遊玩到快速通行。
captions: 各使用群體的基地需求。
基地規劃：動線、植栽與功能分區。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The site is divided into areas for rest, play, dining and sports, and each is shaped by simple forms. These forms are then refined and generated into pavilions, ramps and seats for each group of users.
captions: Design partition.
Refinement of each area.
Design generation for each user group.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 基地劃分為休憩、遊玩、餐飲與運動等區域，各以簡單的形體塑造。這些形體再經修正，生成為給各使用群體的亭子、坡道與座椅。
captions: 設計分區。
各區的修正。
依使用群體的設計生成。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The square becomes an urban park with a raised ring path, wooden walls, water and dense planting. Surrounded by high-rise buildings, it offers people in the neighbourhood a place to take a break in the midst of their daily stress.
captions: Storyboard and layered view of the site.
Perspective views of six places in the park.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 廣場化為一座城市公園，有高架環形步道、木牆、水景與茂密植栽。在高樓環繞之中，它讓附近的人在日常壓力裡有一處能喘息的地方。
captions: 基地的分鏡與分層圖。
公園六處地點的透視圖。

sections.heading: Building Surround - A Park for Catching Breath Amid the Towers
sections.body: Walking along a road through the business district, the designer noticed slogans about mental health posted on hoarding boards. Office towers, crowds of workers and heavily regulated shopping areas during the epidemic left people nearby with no place to step away from work. In the middle of this district lies a large station square that seems never to have been planned. The project lists what workers, residents, students and passengers each need from it, from rest and play to quick passage. The site is divided into areas for rest, play, dining and sport, and each is shaped by simple forms. These forms are then refined and generated into pavilions, ramps and seats suited to each group of users. The square becomes an urban park with a raised ring path, wooden walls, water and dense planting. Surrounded by high-rise buildings, it offers people in the neighbourhood a place to take a break in the midst of daily stress. Between the gaps of steel and glass, a field of green lets hurried steps slow down and tight minds loosen a little, and the forgotten void at the centre of the district finally becomes a place to breathe.

zh-Hant.heading: 高樓環繞-在壓力之間留一座喘息的公園
zh-Hant.body: 沿著商業區的一條道路走去，設計者看見圍板上張貼著心理健康的標語。辦公大樓林立，上班族熙來攘往，疫情期間購物區又受到嚴格管制，附近的人們找不到一處能從工作中暫時抽離的地方。就在這片商業區的中央，有一座廣闊卻彷彿未經規劃的車站廣場。作品列出上班族、居民、學生與旅客各自的需求，從休憩、遊戲到快速通行。基地被劃分為休憩、遊戲、餐飲與運動等區域，每一區都以簡單的形體塑造；這些形體再經推敲，生成為各類使用者專屬的涼亭、坡道與座椅。廣場由此轉變為一座城市公園，擁有架高的環形步道、木牆、水景與茂密的植栽。被高樓環繞的公園，為鄰里的人們在日常壓力之中，提供一處喘息的空間；在鋼筋與玻璃的縫隙之間，一片綠意讓匆忙的腳步得以放慢，也讓緊繃的心緒稍稍鬆開。

pins.title: School Bully — The Black Sheep Effect
pins.description:
A game space of four levels that lets visitors play the victim, the bystander and the bully.

Interactive game space | Interior design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 校園霸凌——黑羊效應
zh-Hant.description:
一座四關的遊戲空間，讓參觀者扮演受害者、旁觀者與霸凌者。

互動遊戲空間｜室內設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The four game spots, linked by a main stem and a blind pass.
四個遊戲關卡，以主幹道與盲道相連。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Having been a bystander, a bully and a victim, the designer saw how school bullying works like the black sheep effect, where a group turns on one person while others watch. The project asks how a space could let visitors play all three roles and think about them.
captions: Level A: the purpose is to make players give up one person.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 設計者曾是旁觀者、霸凌者，也曾是受害者，她看見校園霸凌就像黑羊效應：一群人針對一個人，其他人在旁觀看。本案探問，空間能否讓參觀者親身扮演這三種角色並加以反思。
captions: 第一關：目的是讓玩家在困境中放棄一個人。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The three roles are turned into the order of the game: the first two levels create conflict and weed out victims, and the third lets each person discover their uniqueness. In Level A, a sponge blocks the way until one player is forced to stay and hold the lever.
captions: Rotating rocker and sponge blocks that turn into a staircase.
Cut view: the lifting platform and the secret door for the victim.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 三種角色被轉化為遊戲的關卡順序：前兩關製造衝突並淘汰受害者，第三關讓每個人發現自己的獨特。在第一關，海綿擋住去路，直到一名玩家被迫留下握住拉桿。
captions: 旋轉搖桿與化為階梯的海綿塊。
剖視：升降平台與受害者離開的密門。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In Level B, the machine cage, the door stays closed until one person explores a space full of fog and is sacrificed. Pedals, a connecting rod and a one-way card slot drive the door, and the roles are switched so that players learn inaction can make them the next one out.
captions: Level B model: the victim's route and the bystanders' route.
Sequence: four people arrive, one falls into the secret passage and the door opens.
Mechanism: pedals, connecting rod and one-way card slot.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二關「機械籠」的門一開始是關的，直到有人進入充滿霧氣的空間並被犧牲。踏板、連桿與單向卡槽驅動門的開啟，角色也隨之互換，讓玩家明白袖手旁觀也可能成為下一個被淘汰的人。
captions: 第二關模型：受害者與旁觀者的路線。
過程：四人抵達，一人落入密道，門隨之開啟。
機構：踏板、連桿與單向卡槽。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In Level C, players turn their own gears to find a path, and the victim decides whether to open the way for the one who once bullied them. In Level D, everyone pushes the walls of a rotating gear together to find the exit, then returns to the start to close the door on bullying.
captions: Level C: a space of reconciliation driven by gears.
The gear model before, during and after turning.
Level D: the unity rotate gear and the last level.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第三關中，玩家轉動各自的齒輪尋找路徑，受害者則決定是否為曾霸凌自己的人開啟通道。第四關裡，所有人一起推動旋轉齒輪的牆面找到出口，再回到起點關上霸凌重演的門。
captions: 第三關：以齒輪驅動的和解空間。
齒輪模型轉動前、轉動中與轉動後。
第四關：團結旋轉齒輪與最後一關。

sections.heading: School Bully - Playing All Three Roles of the Black Sheep Effect
sections.body: Having been a bystander, a bully and a victim, the designer saw how school bullying works like the black sheep effect, in which a group turns on one person while others watch. The project asks how a space might let visitors play all three roles and reflect on them. The three roles are turned into the order of a game: the first two levels create conflict and weed out victims, and the third lets each person discover their own uniqueness. In Level A, a sponge blocks the way until one player is forced to stay behind and hold the lever. In Level B, the machine cage, the door stays shut until one person explores a fog-filled space and is sacrificed. Pedals, a connecting rod and a one-way card slot drive the door, and the roles are switched so that players learn that inaction can make them the next one out. In Level C, players turn their own gears to find a path, and the victim decides whether to open the way for the one who once bullied them. In Level D, everyone pushes the walls of a rotating gear together to find the exit, then returns to the start to close the door on bullying.

zh-Hant.heading: 校園霸凌-在遊戲中輪流扮演三種角色
zh-Hant.body: 曾經身為旁觀者、霸凌者與受害者，設計者看見校園霸凌如同黑羊效應：一群人攻擊一個人，其餘的人在旁觀看。作品追問，空間能否讓來訪者親身扮演這三種角色。三種角色被轉化為遊戲的順序：前兩關製造衝突、淘汰受害者，第三關則讓每個人發現自己的獨特。在 A 關，一塊海綿擋住去路，直到有一名玩家被迫留下、握住拉桿。在 B 關的機械籠中，門始終緊閉，直到有人走進滿是霧氣的空間探索而被犧牲；踏板、連桿與單向卡槽驅動這扇門，角色也隨之互換，讓玩家明白袖手旁觀，可能使自己成為下一個出局者。在 C 關，玩家轉動自己的齒輪尋找路徑，受害者則決定是否為曾經欺負自己的人開路；在 D 關，所有人一起推動旋轉齒輪的牆面找到出口，再回到起點，親手關上霸凌之門。

pins.title: Urban Roaming — A Spa for the Neighbourhood
pins.description:
A vacant bus terminal turned into a spa where stressed office workers can unwind.

Tianhe, Guangzhou, China | Interior design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市漫遊——給鄰里的水療站
zh-Hant.description:
把閒置的客運站，轉化為讓壓力大的上班族放鬆的水療空間。

中國廣州天河｜室內設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Exploded view: roof seats, roof deck, original structure, air corridor and two spa pools.
爆炸圖：屋頂座椅、屋頂平台、原有結構、空中廊道與兩座水療池。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The once busy East Station bus terminal in Tianhe, Guangzhou, peaked in 2008, but since 2016 intercity buses have been replaced by other transport and its staff fell from 200 to only 20. Now the vacant station is for rent, while office workers in the nearby business district are under pressure and lack places to unwind.
captions: District analysis: a desolate edge beside a prosperous centre.
Why a spa: what people in cars and office workers want.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州天河曾經繁忙的東站客運站在 2008 年達到高峰，但自 2016 年起城際客運被其他交通方式取代，員工從 200 人減至僅 20 人。如今閒置的車站正在招租，而附近商業區的上班族承受壓力，卻缺乏放鬆的地方。
captions: 區域分析：繁華中心旁的冷清邊緣。
為何是水療：搭車旅客與上班族的需求。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site is close to the city centre but cut off from its surroundings by a long tunnel, and much of the station is functional waste. The strategy keeps the original transport use while adding spa healing, plant healing and a more attractive entrance.
captions: Testing the interactive wall with motion sensing.
Physical model, cut twice like a loaf of bread to show the structure and joints.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地鄰近市中心，卻因一條長隧道與周邊隔絕，車站內大量空間閒置浪費。策略是保留原有的交通功能，同時加入水療、植物療癒與更具吸引力的入口。
captions: 以動作感測測試互動牆。
實體模型，像切麵包一樣切兩刀以呈現結構與節點。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A flowing roof deck with seats sits above the original structure, linked by an air corridor to two spa pools. In the tunnel, an interactive wall lets its lines ripple with the movement of visitors' bodies.
captions: The visiting process as people get on and off the bus.
Plan of the spa along the station.
Pattern forms for the interactive wall.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 流動的屋頂平台與座椅位於原有結構之上，並以空中廊道連接兩座水療池。在隧道中，一道互動牆讓牆上的線條隨著參觀者的身體動作起伏。
captions: 乘客上下車之間的參觀流程。
沿車站配置的水療平面。
互動牆的圖案形式。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Travellers who cannot reach the spa before their bus can soak their feet in a pavilion, and seats for waiting cars sit under the canopy outside. A misty rainforest, a rain walk and hot spring pools give office workers a place to exercise and relax.
captions: Scenes of the spa pools for people escaping the city.
Detail section of the rain walking pool.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 趕不及泡湯就要上車的旅客，可以在亭子裡泡腳，戶外的候車座椅則位於頂棚之下。霧林、雨中步道與溫泉池，讓上班族有一處能運動與放鬆的地方。
captions: 為逃離城市的人們設計的湯池場景。
雨中步道水池的細部剖面。

sections.heading: Urban Roaming - Turning a Vacant Bus Terminal Into a Neighbourhood Spa
sections.body: This once busy bus terminal peaked in 2008, but since 2016 intercity buses have been replaced by other transport and its staff has fallen from two hundred to only twenty. Now the vacant station waits for a tenant, while office workers in the nearby business district live under pressure and lack places to unwind. The site is close to the city centre yet cut off from its surroundings by a long tunnel, and much of the station has become functional waste. The strategy keeps the original transport use while adding spa healing, plant healing and a more inviting entrance. A flowing roof deck with seating sits above the existing structure, linked by an air corridor to two spa pools. In the tunnel, an interactive wall lets its lines ripple with the movement of visitors' bodies. Travellers who cannot reach the spa before their bus can soak their feet in a pavilion, and seats for those waiting sit beneath the canopy outside. A misty rainforest, a rain walk and hot spring pools give office workers a place to exercise and relax. A forgotten station becomes once more a stop in the city where people can pause.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市漫遊-讓閒置客運站成為鄰里的水療站
zh-Hant.body: 這座客運站曾經繁忙，在二〇〇八年達到高峰；自二〇一六年起，城際巴士逐漸被其他交通方式取代，員工也從兩百人減少到僅剩二十人。如今閒置的車站正待出租，附近商業區的上班族則承受壓力，缺少放鬆的地方。基地鄰近市中心，卻被一條長長的隧道與周遭隔開。策略保留原有的交通用途，同時加入水療療癒、植物療癒，以及更具吸引力的入口。一片帶有座椅的流動屋頂平台架在原有結構之上，以空中廊道連接兩座水療池；隧道裡，一面互動牆的線條會隨來訪者身體的移動而起伏。趕不及在發車前泡湯的旅人，可以在涼亭裡泡腳，候車的座位則設在戶外的雨棚之下。霧氣繚繞的雨林、雨中步道與溫泉池，讓上班族有了運動與放鬆的去處。被遺忘的車站，重新成為城市裡可以停下腳步的一站。

pins.title: Cashmere in Bloom — A Flash Store for Cashmere
pins.description:
A flash store shaped from collaged sweater patterns, made by hand in wool.

Flash store | Interior design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 綻放的羊絨——羊絨快閃店
zh-Hant.description:
以拼貼的毛衣圖案塑形、用羊毛手工製作的快閃店。

快閃店｜室內設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The centre flower device: a pavilion that combines a fitting room and a resting place.
中央花朵裝置：結合試衣間與休憩處的展亭。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cashmere sweaters are often seen as traditional clothing, worn only as an inner layer. The project asks how a flash store could tear down that label and show the fashion style of young people.
captions: Elements of clothing taken from the sweaters.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 羊絨毛衣常被視為傳統服飾，只被當作內搭。本案探問，一間快閃店能否撕掉這個標籤，展現年輕人的時尚風格。
captions: 從毛衣中擷取的服裝元素。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The designer experimented with wool combined with other materials, from organza and fabric mesh to felt, yarn and iron gauze. Patterns were then extracted from the sweaters, cut and collaged together into a new shape.
captions: Extraction of shape from the sweater patterns.
The collaged pattern that becomes the floor plan and its functional areas.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 設計者以羊毛結合其他材料進行實驗，從歐根紗、網布到毛氈、毛線與鐵紗。接著從毛衣中擷取圖案，剪裁並拼貼成新的形狀。
captions: 從毛衣圖案中擷取形狀。
拼貼而成的圖案，成為平面與功能分區。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The collaged pattern evolves into the floor plan of the store, with a central device, cold and warm transition zones, coloured corridors and aisles. Each part is made by hand, from iron wire molding and wet felting to sewing wool on wire.
captions: Manufacturing steps: central device, transition zone, wool fence, strip felt and wool counter.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 拼貼圖案逐步演變為店鋪平面，配置中央裝置、冷暖過渡區、彩色廊道與走道。每個部分都以手工製作，從鐵絲塑形、濕氈到在鐵絲上縫製羊毛。
captions: 製作步驟：中央裝置、過渡區、羊毛圍籬、條狀毛氈與羊毛櫃台。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: From the entrance, visitors see the inside only through gaps in the plush, which adds a sense of mystery as they pick out clothes on the way to the centre. At the centre, a flower device holds a touch wall, a gallery wrapped in cashmere, a small fitting room and soft resting places.
captions: Two transition nodes that look at each other.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 從入口望去，參觀者只能透過絨毛的縫隙看見內部，在走向中心、挑選衣服的路上增添神秘感。中央的花朵裝置容納觸摸牆、包覆羊絨的展廊、小試衣間與柔軟的休憩處。
captions: 兩個彼此相望的過渡節點。

sections.heading: Cashmere in Bloom - A Flash Store That Tears Away a Traditional Label
sections.body: Cashmere sweaters are often seen as traditional clothing, worn only as an inner layer. The project asks how a flash store might tear away that label and show the fashion sense of young people. The designer experimented with combining wool and other materials, from organza and fabric mesh to felt, yarn and iron gauze. Patterns were then extracted from the sweaters, cut and collaged into a new shape. The collaged pattern evolves into the floor plan of the store, with a central device, cold and warm transition zones, coloured corridors and aisles. Each part is made by hand, from moulding iron wire and wet felting to sewing wool onto wire. From the entrance, visitors glimpse the interior only through gaps in the plush, which adds a sense of mystery as they pick out clothes on the way toward the centre. At the centre, a flower-like device holds a touch wall, a gallery wrapped in cashmere, a small fitting room and soft places to rest. Cashmere is no longer warmth hidden beneath a coat, but a material that blooms in space and becomes a fashion language to be seen and touched by the young.

zh-Hant.heading: 綻放的羊絨-撕下傳統標籤的快閃店
zh-Hant.body: 羊絨毛衣常被視為傳統服裝，只被當作內搭穿著。作品追問：一間快閃店能否撕下這樣的標籤，展現年輕人的時尚風格？設計者嘗試把羊毛與其他材料結合，從歐根紗、織物網布到毛氈、紗線與鐵紗；接著從毛衣中萃取圖案，剪裁並拼貼成全新的形狀。拼貼的圖案演變為店鋪的平面，包含中央裝置、冷暖過渡區、彩色廊道與走道；每個部分都以手工製作，從鐵絲塑形、濕氈到把羊毛縫在鐵絲上。從入口望去，來訪者只能透過絨毛的縫隙窺見內部，在走向中心、一路挑選衣服的過程中，平添幾分神祕感。抵達中心時，一座花朵般的裝置容納觸摸牆、包覆羊絨的展廊、小小的試衣間與柔軟的休憩處。羊絨不再只是藏在外套底下的溫暖，而是在空間中綻放，成為被看見、被觸摸的時尚語言。

pins.title: The Middle Income Trap — A Mall of Fast Consumption
pins.description:
A tower mall that leads visitors through five spaces until they see how consumerism steers them.

Shopping mall | Interior design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 中等收入陷阱——快速消費商場
zh-Hant.description:
一座塔狀商場，帶參觀者走過五個空間，直到看見消費主義如何操弄自己。

購物商場｜室內設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Overall effect: a tower mall that rises from the entrance to the top floor.
整體效果：從入口一路升至頂樓的塔狀商場。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The designer saw that in a middle-income economy, people tend to focus on short-term interests, spend most of their money on fast consumption and fall into a trap set by merchants. Shopping sites remember what you search for and push more, and in the end people discover they have spent a lot of money on useless things.
captions: Morphogenesis: from personality shapes to the trap.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 設計者觀察到，在中等收入的經濟處境中，人們傾向追求短期利益，把大部分的錢花在快速消費上，落入商家設下的陷阱。購物網站記住你搜尋的東西並不斷推送，最後人們才發現自己把大把的錢花在無用之物上。
captions: 形態生成：從個性形體到陷阱。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Key words used by consumerism, such as abundance of matter, commodity symbols, diversity and a delightful experience, are turned into forms. The forms are selected, classified, made individual, warped and finally become a trap.
captions: Research on the middle income trap and fast consumption.
A collage on consumerism and shopping habits.
Morphological evolution: select, classify, individuality, warp, trap.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 消費主義操弄的關鍵字，如物質豐富、商品符號、多樣性與愉悅體驗，被轉化為形體。這些形體經過挑選、分類、個性化、扭曲，最後成為陷阱。
captions: 關於中等收入陷阱與快速消費的研究。
關於消費主義與購物習慣的拼貼。
形態演變：挑選、分類、個性化、扭曲、陷阱。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The result is a trap mall of fast consumption, where visitors ride an elevator to the top floor and browse down through five spaces. In the option space they choose white clothes and one of four styles of space, and coloured lights in the projection space change the patterns on what they wear.
captions: Elevator route and browse route through the five spaces.
Option space: choose white clothes and a style of space.
Projection space and individuation space.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 成果是一座快速消費的陷阱商場，參觀者搭電梯到頂樓，再一路逛下五個空間。在選擇空間中，他們挑選白色衣服與四種空間風格之一，投影空間裡的彩色燈光則改變身上衣服的圖案。
captions: 電梯動線與逛街動線串起五個空間。
選擇空間：挑選白色衣服與空間風格。
投影空間與個性化空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the warp space, accessories that match the chosen style keep visitors buying, and a long slide carries them on to other stores. In the trap space, digital models and robotic arms bring every outfit to them, until they realise how much they bought before they knew it.
captions: Warp space: accessories and a slide to the next store.
Trap space: digital models and robotic arms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在扭曲空間中，與所選風格相配的配件讓參觀者不停購買，一條長滑道再把他們送往其他店鋪。在陷阱空間裡，數位模特兒與機械手臂把每套衣服送到眼前，直到他們發覺自己不知不覺買了多少。
captions: 扭曲空間：配件與通往下一間店的滑道。
陷阱空間：數位模特兒與機械手臂。

sections.heading: The Middle Income Trap - A Mall Where Everything Is Bought Before One Knows
sections.body: The designer observed that in a middle-income economy people tend to focus on short-term interests, spend most of their money on fast consumption and fall into a trap set by merchants. Shopping sites remember every search and push ever more, until people discover how much they have spent on useless things. Key words of consumerism, such as abundance of matter, commodity symbols, diversity and delightful experience, are turned into forms. These forms are selected, classified, individualised and warped until they finally become a trap. The result is a trap mall of fast consumption, where visitors ride an elevator to the top floor and browse downward through five spaces. In the option space they choose white clothes and one of four styles of space, and coloured lights in the projection space change the patterns on what they wear. In the warp space, accessories that match the chosen style keep visitors buying, and a long slide carries them on to other stores. In the trap space, digital models and robotic arms deliver every outfit to them, until they realise how much they bought before they knew it. The building makes the hidden choreography of consumption physically legible.

zh-Hant.heading: 中等收入陷阱-一座讓人不知不覺買下一切的商場
zh-Hant.body: 設計者觀察到，在中等收入的經濟體中，人們傾向著眼短期利益，把大部分的錢花在快速消費上，落入商家設下的陷阱。購物網站記住人們搜尋過的東西，不斷推送更多。消費主義慣用的關鍵詞，例如物質的豐盛、商品符號、多樣性與愉悅的體驗，被轉化為形體；這些形體經過篩選、分類、個別化與扭曲，最終成為一座陷阱。成果是一座快速消費的陷阱商場：來訪者搭電梯直上頂樓，向下瀏覽五個空間。在選擇空間裡，人們挑選白色衣服與四種空間風格之一，投影空間的彩色燈光則改變身上衣物的圖案。在扭曲空間中，與所選風格相配的配件讓人不斷購買，一道長長的滑梯把人送往其他店鋪；到了陷阱空間，數位模型與機械手臂把每一套服裝送到眼前，直到人們驚覺，自己早已在不知不覺中買下了那麼多。

pins.title: Macao Fisheries Museum — Echoes and Memories
pins.description:
A conch-like spiral museum in a retained harbour warehouse that keeps the memory of Macao's fishing industry.

Macao | Museum | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 澳門漁業博物館——回聲與記憶
zh-Hant.description:
在保留的港口倉庫中，以海螺般的螺旋博物館留存澳門漁業的記憶。

澳門｜博物館｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Physical section model of the museum.
博物館的實體剖面模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Macao's inner harbour sits right beside the historic district, yet its coastline is filled with passenger and cargo terminals, abandoned warehouses and parking lots, with almost no space where people can reach the water. Traffic and a jumble of buildings keep tourists away, while the culture of the fishing industry that shaped the harbour is fading.
captions: The original warehouse structure is kept: frame, facade, floor circulation and spatial elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 澳門內港緊鄰歷史城區，海岸線卻被客貨碼頭、廢棄倉庫與停車場佔據，幾乎沒有讓人親近水邊的空間。交通擁塞與雜亂的建築讓遊客卻步，而塑造這座港口的漁業文化也正逐漸淡去。
captions: 保留原有倉庫結構：框架、立面、樓層動線與空間元素。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The designer mapped the industry chain of fishing, from fishing boats and markets to processing, restaurants and tourists. Forms were then extracted from the shipyard, the ferry terminal, the fishing boats and the conch.
captions: Elements extracted from the shipyard, ferry terminal, fishing boats and conch.
Floor plan with the spiral core and the water walkway.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 設計者梳理漁業的產業鏈，從漁船、市場到加工、餐廳與遊客。接著從船廠、渡輪碼頭、漁船與海螺中提取形體。
captions: 從船廠、渡輪碼頭、漁船與海螺提取的元素。
平面圖：螺旋核心與水上步道。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A spiral inspired by the conch becomes the core of the museum, and visitors move from the shipyard entrance through the pier and market zone and the fishing zone to the core area. Light is studied for each zone, and canvas, water and glass, braided hemp rope mesh and metal are tested as materials.
captions: Interior node and light analysis from the entrance to the core area.
Test of materials: canvas, water and glass, hemp rope mesh, metal.
Aquatic life simulation space with boats on three levels.
The fishing net turned into places to rest.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 受海螺啟發的螺旋成為博物館的核心，參觀者從船廠入口，經過碼頭與市場區、捕魚區，走到核心區。設計者為每個區域研究光線，並以帆布、水與玻璃、麻繩編織網與金屬進行材料測試。
captions: 從入口到核心區的室內節點與光線分析。
材料測試：帆布、水與玻璃、麻繩網、金屬。
水生生活模擬空間，三層皆有漁船。
漁網轉化為休憩的場所。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the section, the spiral exhibition rises through the retained warehouse, and the materials of the top and bottom stand for the old and the new of the fishing industry. Like a conch that holds the sound of the sea, the building lets visitors listen to the past and future of fishing in Macao.
captions: Building east view section drawing.
Detail section drawing of the spiral.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 剖面中，螺旋展覽穿過保留的倉庫向上延伸，頂部與底部的材料代表漁業的新與舊。如同收藏海聲的海螺，這座建築讓參觀者聆聽澳門漁業的過去與未來。
captions: 建築東向剖面圖。
螺旋的細部剖面圖。

sections.heading: Fisheries Museum - Listening for the Echoes of a Harbour Within a Spiral
sections.body: This inner harbour sits right beside the historic district, yet its coastline is crowded with passenger and cargo terminals, abandoned warehouses and parking lots, leaving almost no place where people can reach the water. Traffic and a jumble of buildings keep visitors away, while the fishing culture that shaped the harbour is quietly fading. The designer mapped the industry chain of fishing, from boats and markets to processing, restaurants and tourists. Forms were then extracted from the shipyard, the ferry terminal, the fishing boats and the conch. A spiral inspired by the conch becomes the core of the museum, and visitors move from the shipyard entrance through the pier and market zone and the fishing zone toward the core. Light is studied for each zone, and canvas, water and glass, braided hemp rope mesh and metal are tested as materials. In section, the spiral exhibition rises through the retained warehouse, and the materials at the top and bottom stand for the old and the new of the fishing industry. Like a conch that holds the sound of the sea, the building lets visitors listen to the past and future of fishing, and a harbour falling silent begins to echo again.

zh-Hant.heading: 漁業博物館-在螺旋中聆聽漁港的回聲
zh-Hant.body: 這座內港緊鄰歷史城區，海岸線上卻擠滿了客運與貨運碼頭、廢棄倉庫與停車場，幾乎沒有讓人親近水岸的空間。車流與雜亂的建築讓遊客卻步，而塑造港口的漁業文化也逐漸淡去。設計者描繪出漁業的產業鏈，從漁船、魚市到加工、餐廳與遊客；形體再從船廠、渡輪碼頭、漁船與海螺中萃取而出。以海螺為靈感的螺旋成為博物館的核心，來訪者從船廠入口出發，經過碼頭與魚市區、捕撈區，抵達核心展區。每個區域的光線都經過研究，帆布、水與玻璃、編織麻繩網與金屬也被逐一測試。剖面中，螺旋展覽在保留下來的倉庫中盤旋上升，頂部與底部的材料分別象徵漁業的舊與新。就像一枚收藏著海潮聲的海螺，這座建築讓來訪者得以聆聽漁業的過去與未來，讓逐漸沉默的港口再度發出回聲。

pins.title: Neurotic Experience Center — A Space of Bubbles
pins.description:
A research project that turns neurotic personalities into inflatable bubble spaces visitors can feel from the inside.

Research project | Experience center | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 神經質體驗中心——泡泡空間
zh-Hant.description:
一項研究計畫，把神經質人格轉化為參觀者能從內部感受的充氣泡泡空間。

研究計畫｜體驗中心｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Physical model of the first floor.
一樓的實體模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: People with neurotic personalities often find it hard to communicate with the outside world and to fit into daily life, and others rarely see the world as they do. The designer asked how a space could let visitors feel this inner world from the first person's perspective.
captions: A collage on neuroticism and the inner world.
Space plans for four personalities: sensitive, anxiety, tanking and irritability.
A bubble space for each personality.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 具有神經質人格的人往往難以與外界溝通、融入日常生活，旁人也很少能以他們的方式看世界。設計者思考，空間如何讓參觀者以第一人稱的視角感受這個內在世界。
captions: 關於神經質與內心世界的拼貼。
四種人格的空間平面：敏感、焦慮、消沉與易怒。
為每種人格設計的泡泡空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Emotional paths from self doubt to anxiety and beyond were mapped, and each personality was given a bubble space that wraps, opens, deflates or expands. An interactive device built with Rhino, Grasshopper, Firefly and Arduino uses a motion sensor and an air pump to inflate a balloon according to changes in the visitor's expression.
captions: How the growth environment shapes character, and signs of neurological weakness.
Interaction device: sensor, Arduino and air pump.
The inflatable device from 5 % to 75 % expansion.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 設計者梳理從自我懷疑到焦慮之後的情緒路徑，並為每種人格設計包覆、開敞、洩氣或膨脹的泡泡空間。以 Rhino、Grasshopper、Firefly 與 Arduino 製作的互動裝置，透過動作感測器與氣泵，依參觀者表情的變化為氣球充氣。
captions: 成長環境如何塑造性格，以及神經脆弱的表現。
互動裝置：感測器、Arduino 與氣泵。
充氣裝置從 5% 到 75% 的膨脹。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Shapes, textures and lighting were tested for the feelings they bring, from the sense of rule to loneliness and hope. A balloon inflated inside a wire frame grows along the frame and is squeezed by it, and this became the method for generating the architectural form.
captions: Material, space and senses: shapes, textures and lighting atmosphere.
Concept development of the architectural form with the balloon.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計者測試形狀、質地與光線帶來的感受，從規則感到孤獨與希望。氣球在線框中充氣，沿著框架生長並被擠壓，這成為生成建築形體的方法。
captions: 材料、空間與感官：形狀、質地與光線氛圍。
以氣球推演建築形體的概念發展。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: On the first floor, soft bubble walls blur the outside world so that visitors see it as vague, real or imaginary. The second floor holds the ruins of the psychic and a light of hope, built with balloon, plastic and clay to express the struggles of the inner world.
captions: First floor layout and conceptual model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一樓以柔軟的泡泡牆模糊外在世界，讓參觀者看見模糊、真實或想像的景象。二樓安排心靈的廢墟與希望之光，以氣球、塑膠與黏土表達內心世界的掙扎。
captions: 一樓配置與概念模型。

sections.heading: Neurotic Experience Center - Entering an Inner World Through Bubbles
sections.body: People with neurotic personalities often find it hard to communicate with the outside world and to fit into daily life, and others rarely see the world as they do. The designer asked how a space might let visitors feel this inner world from a first-person perspective. Emotional paths from self-doubt to anxiety and beyond were mapped, and each personality was given a bubble space that wraps, opens, deflates or expands. An interactive device built with Rhino, Grasshopper, Firefly and Arduino uses a motion sensor and an air pump to inflate a balloon as the expression of the visitor changes. Shapes, textures and lighting were tested for the feelings they evoke, from a sense of rule to loneliness and hope. A balloon inflated inside a wire frame grows along the frame and is squeezed by it, and this became the method for generating the architectural form. On the first floor, soft bubble walls blur the outside world so that visitors see it as vague, real or imagined. The second floor holds the ruins of the psyche and a light of hope, built with balloon, plastic and clay to express the struggles of the inner world.

zh-Hant.heading: 神經質體驗中心-以泡泡進入他人的內在世界
zh-Hant.body: 具有神經質人格的人，往往難以與外界溝通、融入日常生活。設計者追問：空間能否讓來訪者以第一人稱的視角，感受這樣的內在世界？從自我懷疑到焦慮的情緒路徑被逐一描繪，每種人格都被賦予一個會包覆、開啟、洩氣或膨脹的泡泡空間。一件以參數化軟體與微控制器打造的互動裝置，透過動作感測器與氣泵，依來訪者表情的變化為氣球充氣。形狀、質地與燈光逐一被測試；在鐵絲框架中充氣的氣球沿著框架生長，又被框架擠壓，這成為生成建築形態的方法。一樓柔軟的泡泡牆模糊了外部世界，讓人看見的外界時而朦朧、時而真實、時而虛幻；二樓則以氣球、塑膠與黏土，構築心靈的廢墟與一道希望之光，表達內在世界的掙扎。

pins.title: Home for Left-behind Children in Shangri-La
pins.description:
A three-storey home in a Tibetan area where left-behind children can pray, learn and live close to their culture.

Shangri-La | Children's home | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 香格里拉留守兒童之家
zh-Hant.description:
位於藏區的三層之家，讓留守兒童貼近自身文化祈福、學習與生活。

香格里拉｜兒童之家｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Explosion diagram: prayer space, learning space and living space.
爆炸圖：祈福空間、學習空間與生活空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In the Tibetan areas around Shangri-La, many children grow up while their parents work far from home. The designer looked for a home where these left-behind children can learn, play and live together close to their own culture and nature.
captions: Building form generation from local construction to activity space with nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在香格里拉一帶的藏區，許多孩子在父母遠赴外地工作時成長。設計者希望為這些留守兒童打造一個家，讓他們能貼近自身文化與自然，一起學習、玩耍與生活。
captions: 建築形體生成：從在地構造到與自然結合的活動空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The form starts from local construction, raises the frame beams to adapt to seasonal changes, adds floors, enlarges the platform and divides the functions. Local customs such as the water prayer wheel turned by the river and the mani heaps of engraved stones are brought into the site.
captions: Spatial function on three floors with the water prayer wheel.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 形體從在地構造出發，抬高框架樑以適應季節變化，增加樓層、擴大平台並劃分機能。由河水推動的水轉經輪、刻經石堆成的瑪尼堆等在地習俗，也被帶進基地。
captions: 三層樓的空間機能與水轉經輪。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first floor is a space for prayer and nature, the second floor holds activity and learning, and the third floor is for living and public life. The plans include planting and playing spaces, classrooms, a handicraft room and dormitories for girls and boys.
captions: Ground, first and second floor plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一樓是祈福與親近自然的空間，二樓安排活動與學習，三樓則是生活與公共空間。平面中包含種植與遊戲空間、教室、手工藝室以及男生與女生宿舍。
captions: 一樓、二樓與三樓平面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The elevation uses a golden dome, Tibetan traditional windows, a vegetation wall and fragrant cloth. The detail section shows how the walls and floors are built, with a white wall mortar of lime mixed with milk, saffron and honey.
captions: Elevation and its elements.
Details, section B-B.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 立面運用金頂、藏式傳統窗、植生牆與香布。細部剖面呈現牆與樓板的構造，白牆灰泥以石灰混合牛奶、番紅花與蜂蜜製成。
captions: 立面及其元素。
細部剖面 B-B。

sections.heading: Home for Left-behind Children - Learning and Living Between Faith and Nature
sections.body: In this highland region many children grow up while their parents work far from home. The designer looked for a home where these left-behind children could learn, play and live together, close to their own culture and to nature. The form begins with local construction: the frame beams are raised to adapt to seasonal change, floors are added, the platform is enlarged and the functions are divided. Local customs are drawn into the site, such as the water prayer wheel turned by the river and the mani heaps of engraved stones.
