The bedroom and study are the most used rooms, at thirty and twenty-five percent, followed by the living room and kitchen. The resulting house gathers entrance, bedroom, living room, lounge, kitchen, study, toilets and back door into one curved plan, each room taking the shape of the bodies that use it.

zh-Hant.heading: 身體生成的空間-讓房間依循肢體的姿態成形
zh-Hant.body: 住宅空間的形成，通常是先劃出空間，再分配機能，最後才把人放進去。作品追問：這個順序能否倒轉過來，讓人體肢體的動態去生成室內的空間？一條生活時間軸記錄了每個房間在一天之中被使用的頻率，動作擷取則顯示，不同空間裡的不同活動，會改變身體對周遭的影響。站立的空間呈長形，上半部因手臂伸展而較寬；坐姿的空間由牆面的內凹與外凸塑形；躺臥的空間則扁平而修長，呈現M字形。以三種姿態的模型做出八組形狀組合，每個房間再依各自的比例混合，例如臥室由六成的躺臥空間與四成的站立空間構成。臥室與書房是使用最多的空間，分別占三成與兩成五，其次是客廳與廚房。最終的住宅把入口、臥室、客廳、休息區、廚房、書房、廁所與後門，納入一個彎曲的平面之中，每一個房間，都長成了使用者身體的形狀。

pins.title: Romain Vacation Home
pins.description:
A vacation home on the New Zealand waterfront whose interlocking curved floors bring nature inside.

Whakatane, New Zealand | December 2021 | Competition work | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Romain 度假屋
zh-Hant.description:
位於紐西蘭水岸的度假屋，以相互咬合的曲面樓層把自然帶進室內。

紐西蘭 Whakatane｜2021 年 12 月｜競圖作品｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Exploded axonometric of the house with new vegetation, rain arrangement and wind block.
住宅的爆炸軸測圖，包含新植栽、雨水配置與擋風。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: People busy with daily work in the industrial environment of the city sometimes wish to get away and return to nature for a moment of peace and relaxation. The site is a waterfront area near Whakatane on the North Island of New Zealand, away from the city and surrounded by pristine environments where people, plants, animals and water creatures are drawn to each other.
captions: Site analysis of the Whakatane waterfront and the users and nature around it.
Existing situation: the programme wheel from sleep at the centre to the kitchen, living room and garage at the edge.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在城市工業環境中忙於日常工作的人們，有時希望暫時離開，回到自然中享受片刻的平靜與放鬆。基地位於紐西蘭北島 Whakatane 附近的水岸，遠離城市，周圍是人、植物、動物與水中生物彼此吸引的原始環境。
captions: 華卡塔尼濱水基地分析，以及周邊的使用者與自然。
現況分析：以睡眠為核心，向外延伸至廚房、客廳與車庫的機能圓環。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The study researched the geographical characteristics and plant types around the whole site, since New Zealand is rich in natural resources. Local trees can build the structure of the house, and some fruits and plants attract birds, so placing birds and plants in the building plays a big role in the feeling of returning to nature.
captions: Concept development models of interlocking curved volumes.
Floor relationship: three curved floors overlapping into one plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究調查整個基地周邊的地理特徵與植物種類，因為紐西蘭擁有豐富的自然資源。當地樹木可以用來建造房屋結構，部分果實與植物則會吸引鳥類，因此如何在建築中安排鳥與植物，是營造回歸自然感受的關鍵。
captions: 相互咬合的曲面量體概念模型。
樓層關係：三層曲面樓板疊合為一個平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The building form overlaps from bottom to top as the site ramps from public to private space, and each floor interlocks to create a central internal outdoor space. Sections test how wind circulation, sunlight and rain move through the rooms.
captions: Top cutting section with the section lines.
Section B-B'.
Section D-D' with the climate analysis of wind circulation, sunlight and rain.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 建築形態隨著基地由公共到私密的坡度，自下而上層層疊合，各樓層相互咬合，圍出中央的室內戶外空間。剖面則檢驗通風、日照與雨水如何穿過各個房間。
captions: 俯視剖切圖與剖面線位置。
B-B' 剖面。
D-D' 剖面與氣候分析：通風、日照與雨水。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The walls use locally sourced natural materials with a reasonable combination of insulation, and the exterior wall carries a specially shaped facade made from two local woods popular for building houses in the area. The facade gives the house privacy while helping the sun and wind reach the interior.
captions: Explosion A: windows and hallway, from concrete and wood to the glass frame windows.
Explosion B: the facade layers, from light concrete to the exterior wood facade and the long curved windows.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 牆體採用在地取得的天然材料，並合理搭配隔熱層；外牆加上一層特殊造型的立面，以當地常用於建屋的兩種木材組合而成。這層立面為住宅帶來隱私，同時讓陽光與風進入室內。
captions: 爆炸圖 A：窗戶與走廊，從混凝土、木材到玻璃窗框。
爆炸圖 B：立面層次，從輕質混凝土到外層木立面與長條曲面窗。

sections.heading: Romain Vacation Home - A House Where Birds and Trees Come to Stay
sections.body: People busy with daily work in the industrial setting of the city sometimes long to slip away and return to nature for a moment of peace and rest. The site is a waterfront area far from the city, surrounded by pristine surroundings where people, plants, animals and creatures of the water are drawn to one another. The study researches the geography and plant types around the whole site. Local trees can form the structure of the house, and certain fruits and plants attract birds, so placing birds and plants within the building plays a large part in the feeling of returning to nature. The building form overlaps from bottom to top as the site ramps from public to private, and each floor interlocks to enclose a central indoor outdoor space. Sections test how wind, sunlight and rain move through the rooms. The walls use locally sourced natural materials with a sensible layer of insulation. The outer wall carries a specially shaped facade made from two local woods often used for building houses. It gives the house privacy while letting sun and wind reach the interior, so that the home becomes an extension of nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 度假之家-讓鳥與樹一同住進屋裡
zh-Hant.body: 在城市的工業環境裡忙於日常工作的人們，有時渴望暫時離開，回到自然之中，尋得片刻的寧靜與放鬆。基地是一片遠離城市的濱水地帶，四周環繞著原始的環境，人、植物、動物與水中生物在此彼此吸引。研究探查整片基地周邊的地理特徵與植物種類；在地的樹木可以構成房屋的結構，某些果實與植物能吸引鳥類，因此把鳥與植物安放進建築之中，對於回歸自然的感受至關重要。建築形體隨著基地從公共到私密的坡度，由下而上層層交疊，各層彼此咬合，圍出中央的室內戶外空間；剖面則測試風、陽光與雨水如何在房間之間流動。牆體採用在地取材的天然材料，並合理搭配隔熱層；外牆覆上一道造型特殊的立面，以兩種當地常用於建屋的木材製成。這道立面為房屋守住隱私，也讓陽光與風得以進入室內。一棟房子，從此成為自然的延伸。

pins.title: Club Hub
pins.description:
A century-old brick building in Toronto renovated into curved, shared floors for entrepreneurs and artists.

Toronto, Canada | Spring 2021 | Renovation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Club Hub 共創基地
zh-Hant.description:
將多倫多一棟百年磚造建築，改造為供創業者與藝術家共享的曲面樓層。

加拿大多倫多｜2021 年春｜建築改造｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Long section: staggered curved floors, stairs, ramps and slides inside the old brick building.
長向剖面：老磚造建築內交錯的曲面樓板、樓梯、坡道與滑梯。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project renovates a building more than 100 years old in downtown Toronto, which bears witness to the evolution of the city's architectural form, style and migration. Inside, each floor is a closed, narrow and independent space, and the rooms for cafe, performance, meeting and office work are cramped and monotonous.
captions: Space development: from clearly divided rooms to curved floors whose height differences separate events.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案改造多倫多市中心一棟超過百年的建築，它見證了城市建築形式、風格與移民歷史的演變。建築內部每層樓都是封閉、狹窄且各自獨立的空間，咖啡、表演、會議與辦公的空間都顯得擁擠而單調。
captions: 空間發展：從分隔明確的房間，到以高低差區分活動的曲面樓板。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: User research grouped the related people into academic, entrepreneurial and artistic ranges and filtered their needs for space and activities, such as young designers looking for a shared creative space. Ants, which act in groups and cooperate and communicate as they work, became the concept for a space that inspires good ideas.
captions: Retrofitting development: break the floor, adjust the curvature of the slabs, then adjust the spatial and visual links.
Explosion analysis: basement, three floors, the historic brick wall, a large glass frame ball and small air film balls.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 使用者研究將相關的人分為學術、創業與藝術等範疇，並篩選他們對空間與活動的需求，例如正在尋找共享創意空間的年輕設計師。成群行動、在工作中合作與溝通的螞蟻，成為打造能激發好點子的空間概念。
captions: 改造推演：打破樓板、調整樓板曲率，再調整空間與視覺的連結。
爆炸分析：地下室、三層樓、歷史磚牆、大型玻璃框架球與小型氣膜球。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The traditional layout was broken by staggering each floor and linking them with stairs, ramps and slides, while the historic brick wall facing the road is kept in its original state. A large glass frame ball holds pop-up events and planting, and small air film balls at different heights give private rest areas connected by slopes and stairs.
captions: Street view of the new brick facade, whose gaps and curvature bring in sunlight.
Interior scenes of the shared spaces for entrepreneurs and artists.
Open floors whose undulation and small spaces in the circulation provide privacy.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計打破傳統配置，讓各層樓板錯開，並以樓梯、坡道與滑梯相連，面向道路的歷史磚牆則維持原貌。大型玻璃框架球容納快閃活動與植栽，不同高度的小型氣膜球則成為私密的休憩區，以坡道與樓梯串連。
captions: 街景：新磚立面的縫隙與曲度引入陽光。
為創業者與藝術家設計的共享空間室內場景。
開放樓層的起伏與動線中的小空間提供隱私。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The new structures respect the red brick walls, combining glass bricks with historic red bricks to preserve the history while breaking the city's modular building form. The renovated building gives entrepreneurs and creators more space for communication and sharing, and platforms to express their specialties.
captions: Brick studies and physical models of the curved facade.
Detail sections: red brick structure, steel support frame, tempered glass and insulated glazing.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 新結構尊重原有的紅磚牆，以玻璃磚結合歷史紅磚，在保存歷史的同時打破城市模組化的建築形式。改造後的建築為創業者與創作者提供更多交流與分享的空間，以及展現專長的平台。
captions: 磚砌研究與曲面立面的實體模型。
細部剖面：紅磚結構、鋼支撐框架、強化玻璃與隔熱玻璃。

sections.heading: Club Hub - Housing Ant-Like Collaboration in a Century-Old Brick Building
sections.body: The project renovates a building more than a hundred years old in the city centre, one that bears witness to changes in the architectural form, style and migration of the city. Inside, each floor is a closed, narrow and separate space, and the rooms for café, performance, meetings and office work feel cramped and monotonous. User research groups the people involved into academic, entrepreneurial and artistic circles and sorts their needs for space and activity, such as young designers in search of a shared creative studio. Ants, which move in groups and cooperate and communicate as they work, become the concept for a space that sparks good ideas. The traditional layout is broken by staggering the floors and linking them with stairs, ramps and slides, while the historic brick wall facing the road is kept intact. A large glass-framed sphere holds pop-up events and planting, and small air film spheres at different heights offer private resting corners joined by slopes and stairs. Glass bricks combine with historic red brick, preserving the past while giving creators more room to share and to show their skills.

zh-Hant.heading: 俱樂部樞紐-在百年紅磚樓裡放進一場螞蟻般的協作
zh-Hant.body: 作品改造市中心一棟超過百年的建築，它見證了城市在建築形式、風格與移民上的演變。樓內每一層都是封閉、狹窄而獨立的空間，咖啡、表演、會議與辦公的房間顯得侷促而單調。使用者研究把相關的人分為學術、創業與藝術三個範疇，篩選各自對空間與活動的需求。螞蟻成群行動、邊工作邊合作與溝通，成為一個能激發好點子的空間概念。設計打破傳統的格局，讓各層錯落，並以樓梯、坡道與滑梯相連，面向街道的歷史磚牆則維持原貌；一顆大型玻璃框架球容納快閃活動與植栽，高低不一的小型氣膜球則提供私密的休息角落，以坡道與樓梯相互串連。新結構尊重紅磚牆，以玻璃磚結合歷史紅磚，在保存歷史的同時，也打破城市模組化的建築形式。改造後的建築，為創業者與創作者提供更多交流分享的空間，以及展現專長的舞台。

pins.title: Sunward Orphanage
pins.description:
An orphanage on the Ganges in Bihar that shelters and educates children and gives its ground floor to the seasonal floods.

Bihar, India | Orphanage and flood adaptation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 向陽孤兒院
zh-Hant.description:
位於比哈爾邦恆河畔的孤兒院，收容並教育孩子，並把一樓讓給季節性的洪水。

印度比哈爾邦｜孤兒院與防洪適應｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Explosion diagram: the grey space on the first floor, the reading stairs, the atrium and the roof.
爆炸圖：一樓的灰空間、二樓的閱讀階梯、三樓的中庭與屋頂。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In many parts of India, social injustices such as the death of parents, illness, son preference, child labour and child trafficking leave children displaced, illiterate and without social security, education or a safe place to live. Along the Ganges in Bihar, floods and lightning strikes make life even harder and easily destroy the buildings of poor people.
captions: A news collage on orphaned children, floods and the epidemic.
Concept and strategy: social issues, children's protection and the living environment problem.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在印度許多地區，父母離世、疾病、重男輕女、童工與兒童販運等社會不公，使孩子流離失所、無法識字，也缺乏社會保障、教育與安全的居所。在比哈爾邦的恆河沿岸，洪水與雷擊讓生活更加艱難，也輕易摧毀貧困居民的房屋。
captions: 關於孤兒、水災與疫情的新聞拼貼。
概念與策略：社會問題、兒童保護與居住環境問題。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The study mapped the social issues, the needs for children's protection and the problems of the living environment, such as messy functions, dangerous structures and a lack of space for children. It also followed the river through the dry and flood seasons to see how the site changes over the year.
captions: Site and location: historical legacy, geography and the lack of social care.
Design strategy for the grey space: sand-bar diversion, a modified river channel and planting to absorb water, in the dry and flood seasons.
Flooded section diagram: in the dry season the channel grows vegetables, and when the flood comes the children's activities move upstairs.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究梳理了社會問題、兒童保護的需求，以及居住環境的問題，例如機能混亂、結構危險與缺乏兒童空間。研究也追蹤河流在乾季與洪水季的變化，了解基地一年之中的轉變。
captions: 基地與區位：歷史背景、地理影響與社會照顧的不足。
灰空間的設計策略：乾季與洪水季的沙洲導流、河道調整與吸水植栽。
淹水剖面圖：乾季時河道用來種菜；洪水來臨時，孩子們的活動移到樓上。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The building form starts from local construction, raises its frame beams to adapt to seasonal changes, adds floors and platforms to expand the living space, and divides the functions around activity spaces with nature. New rivers and pools drain and store floodwater, while trees and plants in the zone help absorb it.
captions: Building form generation from local construction to activity space with nature.
Details of section A-A with the waterproof mortar and wall layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 建築形態從在地工法出發，抬高框架樑以適應季節變化，再增加樓層與平台以擴大生活空間，並圍繞親近自然的活動空間劃分機能。新設的河道與水池負責排水與蓄水，區內的樹木與植栽則協助吸收洪水。
captions: 從在地工法到親近自然活動空間的建築形態生成。
A-A 剖面細部，包含防水砂漿與牆體層次。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The orphanage shelters and educates children in a healthy and normal living environment, with a first floor grey space that can flood, reading stairs on the second floor and an atrium on the third. Its plans gather planting and playing spaces, a simulated river, classrooms, a handicraft room, dormitories and a water circulation system that lifts river water through the pillars.
captions: Ground floor plan with the planting and playing space, simulated river, water pond and play area.
First and second floor plans with classrooms, a handicraft room, the atrium and dormitories.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 孤兒院在健康而正常的生活環境中收容並教育孩子：一樓是可以淹水的灰空間，二樓設有閱讀階梯，三樓則是中庭。平面中包含種植與遊戲空間、模擬河道、教室、手工藝教室、宿舍，以及透過柱子將河水送上樓的水循環系統。
captions: 一樓平面：種植與遊戲空間、模擬河道、水池與遊戲區。
二、三樓平面：教室、手工藝教室、中庭與宿舍。

sections.heading: Sunward Orphanage - Raising a Home for Children Between Flood and Dry Season
sections.body: In many places social injustices such as the death of parents, illness, a preference for sons, child labour and trafficking leave children displaced and unable to read, without social security, schooling or a safe place to live. Along a great river, floods and lightning make life harder still and easily destroy the houses of the poor. The study maps these social issues, the needs of child protection and the problems of the living environment, such as muddled functions, dangerous structures and a lack of space for children. It also follows the river through the dry and flood seasons to see how the site changes across the year. The building form begins from local construction, lifting its frame beams to adapt to the seasons and adding floors and platforms to expand living space. Functions are divided around activity spaces connected with nature. New channels and pools drain and store floodwater, while trees and plants help to absorb it. The orphanage shelters and educates children in a healthy, ordinary environment, with a ground floor grey space that can flood, reading stairs above and an atrium at the top. Here children can grow toward the sun.

zh-Hant.heading: 向陽孤兒院-在洪水與旱季之間撐起孩子的家
zh-Hant.body: 在許多地方，雙親離世、疾病、重男輕女、童工與人口販運等社會不公，讓孩子流離失所、失去讀書的機會，也缺乏社會保障、教育與安全的住處。沿著大河而居的這片土地，洪水與雷擊更讓生活雪上加霜，窮人的房屋輕易便被摧毀。研究描繪出種種社會議題、兒童保護的需求，以及居住環境的問題，例如機能雜亂、結構危險、缺乏孩子的活動空間；研究也追隨河流走過旱季與汛期，觀察基地一年之中的變化。建築形體從在地的營造方式出發，抬高框架梁以適應季節的變化，加建樓層與平台以擴展生活空間，並圍繞著與自然相連的活動空間劃分機能；新開的水道與水池排放並蓄存洪水，區內的樹木與植物也協助吸收水量。孤兒院在健康而正常的環境中庇護並教育孩子，一樓的灰空間可以容許淹水，二樓設有閱讀階梯，三樓則是中庭。孩子在此向陽而生。

pins.title: Assimilate Plan
pins.description:
Stackable units in Toronto's unused spaces that help refugees find housing, work and a place in the city.

Toronto, Canada | Winter 2022 | Refugee housing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 融入計畫
zh-Hant.description:
在多倫多閒置空間中堆疊的居住單元，協助難民找到住所、工作，以及在城市中的位置。

加拿大多倫多｜2022 年冬｜難民住宅｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Corner space: circulation, triangular frame and blocks stacked over the site.
街角空間：動線、三角形框架與量體在基地上方層層堆疊。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Refugees forced from their countries by disasters and wars come to the city for safety, and they need to be resettled while easing their conflicts with the local population. After visiting the sites in Toronto, the student found that their temporary living and activity spaces affect the city's service system and take up a lot of social space.
captions: Nouns and verbs: models that mix, scatter, disarrange and expand.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 因災難與戰爭被迫離開家園的難民來到城市尋求安全，他們需要被安置，同時也需要化解與在地居民之間的衝突。學生走訪多倫多的基地後發現，難民臨時的居住與活動空間影響了城市的服務系統，也占用了大量社會空間。
captions: 名詞與動詞：混合、分散、打亂與擴張的模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Research on how refugees spread through the city over four months gave four words, to expand, to mix, to disarrange and to scatter, and an ink and water experiment showed drops gradually merging into the water. The project uses this to express Toronto as a diverse and inclusive city where refugees can become part of its lifestyle and environment.
captions: Floor plans of units in different sizes and forms for the number of people in each group.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究追蹤難民在四個月間如何在城市中擴散，歸納出擴張、混合、打亂與分散四個詞，並以墨水與水的實驗觀察水滴逐漸融入水中。本案以此表達多倫多是一座多元包容的城市，難民可以成為城市生活與環境的一部分。
captions: 依每個群體人數推演出的不同大小與形式的單元平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A variety of units with basic living functions can be stacked and combined in the city's grey spaces for markets, planting, education and outdoor activities, without affecting the local community. On a triangular corner, staggered triangles of different sizes become resting seats, planting areas, temporary selling spaces and event venues.
captions: Corner space programmes for green space, public, retail and entertainment, with pathways, stairs and stages.
Scenes of the corner market where people rest, meet and sell what they grow or make by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 各種具備基本生活機能的單元，可以在城市的灰空間中堆疊組合，作為市集、種植、教育與戶外活動之用，而不影響在地社區。在三角形的街角，大小不一的三角形錯落排列，成為休憩座椅、種植區、臨時攤位與活動場地。
captions: 街角空間的綠地、公共、零售與娛樂機能，以及步道、階梯與舞台。
街角市集的場景：人們在此休息、相聚，販售自己種植或手作的物品。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Between buildings the blocks stack upwards over unused aisles, an empty wall carries a new structure that spreads upwards on standard scaffolding, the lake side stacks blocks of different heights into platforms, and low roofs hold a staggered neighbourhood. Together they give refugees step-by-step help with housing, education, work and self-sufficiency in the city.
captions: Empty space between buildings: stacked blocks creating semi-outdoor shared spaces.
Building empty wall: a new structure spreading upwards on scaffolding, with the roof structure analysis.
Lake side: shape out, split, rotate, float, cut out cube and circulation.
Low building roof empty space: west elevation of the staggered neighbourhood.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在建築之間，量體沿著閒置的通道向上堆疊；一面空牆以標準鷹架承載向上擴展的新結構；湖畔以高低不一的量體堆疊出平台；低矮的屋頂則承載錯落的小社區。這些設計一起為難民在城市中的居住、教育、工作與自給自足，提供循序漸進的協助。
captions: 建築之間的空地：堆疊的量體形成半戶外的共享空間。
建築空牆：以鷹架向上擴展的新結構，以及屋頂結構分析。
湖畔：塑形、分割、旋轉、懸浮、切削與動線。
低矮建築屋頂空地：錯落小社區的西向立面。

sections.heading: Assimilate Plan - Letting Refugees Blend Into the City Like Ink in Water
sections.body: Refugees forced from their homelands by disaster and war come to the city in search of safety. They need to be resettled, and the tensions between newcomers and local residents need to be eased. After visiting the sites, the student found that the temporary living and activity spaces of refugees strain the service system of the city and occupy a great deal of social space. Research into how refugees spread through the city over four months produced four words: to expand, to mix, to disarrange and to scatter. An experiment with ink and water showed drops gradually merging into the water. The project uses this to express a diverse and inclusive city in which refugees can become part of its life and environment. Units with basic living functions can be stacked and combined in the grey spaces of the city for markets, planting, education and outdoor activity without disturbing local communities. On a triangular corner, staggered triangles of different sizes become seats, planting beds, temporary stalls and event venues. Growing over unused gaps, blank walls, the lakeside and low roofs, the units help refugees step by step toward housing, education, work and self-reliance.

zh-Hant.heading: 同化計畫-讓難民如墨入水般融入城市
zh-Hant.body: 因災難與戰爭被迫離開家園的難民，來到城市尋求安全；難民需要被安置，也需要化解與在地居民之間的衝突。走訪各處基地之後，學生發現難民暫時的居住與活動空間，牽動城市的服務系統，也占去不少社會空間。研究追蹤難民四個月來在城市中擴散的方式，歸納出四個詞：擴展、混合、錯置與散布；一場墨滴入水的實驗，則呈現墨滴如何逐漸融入水中。作品以此表達一座多元而包容的城市，讓難民成為城市生活與環境的一部分。具備基本生活機能的單元，可在城市的灰色空間中堆疊組合，作為市集、種植、教育與戶外活動之用；在一處三角形的街角，大小不一的三角形錯落排列，成為座椅、種植區、臨時攤位與活動場地。從建築縫隙、空牆、湖畔到低矮的屋頂，單元層層生長，一步步協助難民在城市中安居、受教、工作並自立。

pins.title: Reconstruction of Jiegui Street
pins.description:
A low-key renovation that turns an old street in Changsha into a lively market and community space.

Changsha, China | Street renovation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Jiegui 街改造
zh-Hant.description:
以最低限度的改造，讓長沙一條老街重新成為熱鬧的市場與社區空間。

中國長沙｜街道改造｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Fresh food market section: an archway entrance, colourful stalls and new planting along the street.
生鮮市場段：拱門入口、色彩繽紛的攤位，以及沿街新增的綠化。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Jiegui Street is an old street in the centre of Changsha that looks incongruous with the modern buildings around it, as if it had been swallowed up by the city. It faces ageing challenges such as limited space, damaged facilities and an outdated quality of life, and the sense of community nearby has declined.
captions: Methods of reconstruction: combining small blocks into courtyards, adding roof gardens and balconies, and broadening paths.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: Jiegui 街是長沙市中心的一條老街，與周圍的現代建築顯得格格不入，彷彿被城市吞沒。這條街面臨空間狹小、設施損壞與生活品質落後等老化問題，周邊社區的凝聚力也逐漸下降。
captions: 改造手法：把零散量體合併成院落、加入屋頂花園與陽台，並拓寬通道。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The study found that the shops along the street had mixed functions and were spread too far apart, so people were scattered without a focus. Daily problems such as rubbish were also traced step by step, from collection and sorting to transport and treatment.
captions: Garbage disposal improvement: inspection, sorting, cleaning and recycling shown as small scenes.
Process of rubbish disposal from homes, restaurants and shops to the sorting and treatment plants.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究發現，街上的店鋪機能混雜、分布過於分散，使人流四散而缺乏焦點。研究也逐步追蹤垃圾等日常問題，從收集、分類到運送與處理。
captions: 垃圾處理改善：以小場景呈現巡查、分類、清潔與回收。
垃圾處理流程：從住家、餐廳與商店，到分類廠與處理廠。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The strategy is to make the least invasive renovations to the public environment, so the street can blend in with its modern surroundings while keeping its own identity. The main shops are gathered along the street and planned in stages as a fresh food market, an entertainment section and a living facility section.
captions: Community improvement guide: the street plan before, during and after the renovation.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 策略是以最低限度的介入改造公共環境，讓老街融入周圍的現代環境，同時保留自身的特色。主要店鋪集中到街上，並分段規劃為生鮮市場段、娛樂段與生活設施段。
captions: 社區改善指南：改造前、改造中與改造後的街道規劃。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Outdoor teahouses, cinemas and planting give the entertainment section room for singing, dancing and small performances, while the living facility section adds trees, benches and spaces for outdoor dining. The street becomes both a better retail environment and a gathering place for the community.
captions: Entertainment section: outdoor teahouses and a stage where older residents meet and perform.
Living facility section: a one-lane street with trees, benches and outdoor seating for restaurants.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 戶外茶館、電影院與綠化讓娛樂段有了唱歌、跳舞與小型表演的空間；生活設施段則加入樹木、長椅與戶外用餐的空間。老街因此既是更好的商業環境，也成為社區的聚會場所。
captions: 娛樂段：長者相聚、表演的戶外茶館與舞台。
生活設施段：種有樹木、設有長椅與餐廳戶外座位的單線街道。

sections.heading: Jiegui Street Reconstruction - Gathering Life Back to an Old Street With the Lightest Touch
sections.body: This old street in the city centre looks out of place among the modern buildings around it, as if the city had swallowed it whole. It faces the challenges of age, from cramped space and damaged facilities to an outdated quality of life, and the sense of community nearby has faded. The study finds that shops along the street mix their functions and sit too far apart, so people scatter without a focus. Everyday problems such as rubbish are traced step by step, from collection and sorting to transport and treatment. The strategy is to make the least invasive changes to the public environment, so the street can blend with its modern surroundings while keeping its own identity. The main shops are gathered along the street and planned in stages as a fresh food market, an entertainment section and a section of living facilities. Outdoor teahouses, cinemas and planting give the entertainment section room for singing, dancing and small performances. The living section adds trees, benches and places for outdoor dining. The street becomes a better place to shop and a gathering place for the community once more.

zh-Hant.heading: 老街重構-以最輕的介入讓老街重新聚攏人氣
zh-Hant.body: 這條位於市中心的老街，與四周的現代建築顯得格格不入，彷彿被城市吞沒。它面臨空間有限、設施毀損、生活品質老舊等老化的挑戰，周邊的社區感也逐漸衰退。研究發現，沿街店鋪機能混雜、分布過於分散，人潮四散，缺乏聚焦；垃圾等日常問題也被逐步追溯，從收集、分類，到運輸與處理。設計的策略，是對公共環境做最少的侵入式改造，讓老街既能融入現代的周遭，又保有自身的特質。主要的店鋪被沿街集中，並分期規劃為生鮮市場、娛樂區段與生活設施區段。戶外茶館、電影院與植栽，為娛樂區段留出唱歌、跳舞與小型表演的空間；生活設施區段則增添樹木、長椅與戶外用餐的角落。老街由此成為更好的商業環境，也重新成為社區的聚會之所，在現代城市之中守住一段溫熱的日常。

pins.title: The Delirious Skyscraper
pins.description:
A skyscraper built from rock patterns and everyday doors and windows, where every floor is its own world.

China | Skyscraper design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 狂想摩天樓
zh-Hant.description:
以岩石紋理與日常門窗構成的摩天樓，每一層都是獨立的世界。

中國｜摩天樓設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The space dream: walls, windows and stairs from different cities joined into one dense landscape.
空間之夢：來自不同城市的牆、窗與樓梯，拼接成一片密集的地景。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project starts from engineering geology, a subject the student had long been fascinated by while researching different materials. It asks how the structures of rocks could be carried into a skyscraper built from the doors and windows of daily life.
captions: Observation of the surroundings: dense streets in three Chinese cities.
Stripe: a rock pattern turned into a series of block models.
Porosity and layer: rock patterns tested as surfaces and stacked timber strips.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案從工程地質出發，這是學生在研究各種材料時一直深深著迷的學科。它探問：岩石的結構能否轉化為一座由日常生活中的門與窗構成的摩天樓。
captions: 觀察周遭環境：三座中國城市的密集街景。
條紋：把岩石紋理轉化為一系列量體模型。
孔隙與層理：把岩石紋理發展成曲面與層疊的木條。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The porosity, layers and stripes of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks were studied and turned into patterns, then into three-dimensional forms through hand-made models. The student also observed three familiar cities, Shenzhen, Hong Kong and Changsha, and their very different streets and buildings.
captions: Combining the three patterns into an expanded block.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究岩漿岩、沉積岩與變質岩的孔隙、層理與條紋，把它們轉化為圖案，再透過手作模型發展成立體形式。學生也觀察了自己熟悉的三座城市：深圳、香港與長沙，以及它們截然不同的街道與建築。
captions: 把三種圖案組合成擴展的量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Walls and windows were collected as a catalogue, from brick, lattice and antique walls to sliding, round and hollow-out windows. Each floor works as its own world, so the tower can be read as a stack of separate floors with no symbolism shared between them.
captions: A catalogue of walls and windows used to build the floors.
Model and exploded axonometric of the stacked floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 牆與窗被整理成一份目錄，從磚牆、花格牆與古牆，到推拉窗、圓窗與鏤空窗。每一層都是獨立的世界，使這座塔可以被解讀為一疊彼此分離、互不共享象徵的樓層。
captions: 用來構成各樓層的牆與窗目錄。
層疊樓層的模型與爆炸軸測圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the vertical section each layer is independent and closely related at the same time, and different doors and windows combine to form a towering skyscraper. Each floor plan has its own character, and changeable stairways let routes across floors be explored and developed freely.
captions: Vertical section of the skyscraper.
Rendered exploded perspective with views of the first, third, seventh and twelfth floors.
Floor plans of the first, third, seventh and twelfth floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在垂直剖面中，每一層既獨立又緊密相連，不同的門與窗組合成一座高聳的摩天樓。每層平面都有自己的性格，多變的樓梯讓跨樓層的路線可以被自由探索與發展。
captions: 摩天樓的垂直剖面。
爆炸透視渲染圖，標示一、三、七與十二樓。
一、三、七與十二樓平面圖。

sections.heading: Delirious Skyscraper - Stacking Independent Worlds From Rock Strata and Windows
sections.body: The project begins from engineering geology, a subject that had long fascinated the student while researching different materials. It asks whether the structures of rock could be carried into a skyscraper built from the doors and windows of everyday life. The porosity, layers and stripes of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are studied and turned into patterns, then into three-dimensional forms through hand-made models. The student also observed three familiar cities and compared their very different streets and buildings. Walls and windows are gathered into a catalogue, from brick, lattice and antique walls to sliding, round and pierced windows. Each floor works as a world of its own, so the tower can be read as a stack of separate levels that share no common symbolism. In the vertical section every layer is independent yet closely related, and different doors and windows combine into a towering skyscraper. Each floor plan carries its own character, and changeable stairways let routes between levels be explored and developed freely. The deep order of the earth is overlaid upon the ordinary life of the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 譫妄的摩天樓-以岩層與門窗堆疊出各自獨立的世界
zh-Hant.body: 作品從工程地質學出發，這是學生在研究各種材料時長久著迷的一門學問；它追問，岩石的結構能否被帶進一座由日常門窗構成的摩天樓？火成岩、沉積岩與變質岩的孔隙、層理與紋路被一一研究，轉化為圖樣，再透過手作模型化為立體的形體；學生也觀察了三座熟悉的城市，比較它們截然不同的街道與建築。牆與窗被收集成一份目錄，從磚牆、花格牆、仿古牆，到推拉窗、圓窗與鏤空窗。每一層樓都是一個獨立的世界，塔樓因此可以被解讀為一疊彼此分離的樓層，之間不共享任何象徵。垂直剖面中，每一層既獨立又緊密相關，不同的門窗彼此組合，築成一座高聳的摩天樓。每一層平面各有性格，可變的樓梯讓跨越樓層的路徑得以自由探索與發展。大地深處的秩序，在此與城市的日常相互疊印。

pins.title: Taipei X-Site
pins.description:
A wavy installation that collects rain and turns it into mist, asking visitors to care for the ocean.

Taipei | Art installation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 台北 X-Site
zh-Hant.description:
收集雨水、化為細霧的起伏裝置，邀請參觀者關心海洋。

台北｜藝術裝置｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Scene display: the wavy installation in front of the museum, with the rain collecting system below.
場景展示：美術館前起伏的裝置，下方是雨水收集系統。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Global warming is becoming more serious, sea levels keep rising and marine ecosystems are being damaged, with problems such as coral bleaching. This art installation outside a museum in Taipei aims to raise people's awareness of protecting the ocean and to encourage practical action.
captions: Weather data: temperature, rainfall and humidity month by month.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 全球暖化日益嚴重，海平面持續上升，海洋生態也不斷遭到破壞，出現珊瑚白化等問題。這座位於台北一座美術館外的藝術裝置，希望喚起人們保護海洋的意識，並鼓勵實際的行動。
captions: 氣象數據：逐月的氣溫、降雨與濕度。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Within two kilometres of the museum there are many busy places, such as temples, restaurants, coastal parks and shopping malls, connected by routes. The study also recorded the museum's opening hours, its visitor flow through the week and the city's weather over the year.
captions: The plan form drawn from the data, with the highest and lowest climate figures of the year.
Form in four steps: meteorological data, combination, smooth connection and formation.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 美術館周邊兩公里內有許多人潮聚集的地方，如寺廟、餐廳、海濱公園與購物中心，彼此以路線相連。研究也記錄了美術館的開放時間、一週間的參觀人流，以及城市全年的氣候。
captions: 由數據推演出的平面形態，以及全年氣候的最高與最低數值。
四個步驟生成形態：氣象數據、組合、平滑連接與成形。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The form was generated from the weather data, combined and smoothly connected into a wavy surface. Its material was tested in a model and a composition of strips laid in different directions.
captions: Entity model of the woven surface.
1x1 material composition of strips in different directions.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 形態由氣象數據生成，再經組合與平滑連接形成起伏的曲面。材料則透過實體模型，以及不同方向排列的條狀構成來測試。
captions: 編織曲面的實體模型。
不同方向條狀材料的 1x1 構成。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The installation rises and falls so that visitors feel as if they were at sea, with views that open in some places and close in others, and edges for resting before visiting the museum. It collects rainwater on rainy days and turns it into a fine spray on sunny days, and at night layers of blue light make people feel as if they were at the bottom of the ocean.
captions: Elevations of the installation at different heights.
Plan of the installation.
Rainy day, bright day and dark night: collecting rain, playing and viewing the lights.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 裝置高低起伏，讓參觀者彷彿置身海上，有些位置視野開闊，有些則被遮擋，邊緣也適合在參觀美術館前休息。它在雨天收集雨水，晴天化為細霧，夜晚則以層層藍光讓人彷彿身處海底。
captions: 裝置在不同高度的立面。
裝置平面圖。
雨天、晴天與夜晚：收集雨水、遊玩與欣賞燈光。

sections.heading: X-Site Ocean Installation - Raising a Breathing Wave Outside the Museum
sections.body: Global warming grows more serious, sea levels keep rising, and marine ecosystems suffer harms such as coral bleaching. This art installation outside a museum hopes to raise awareness of protecting the ocean and to encourage practical action. The study finds that within two kilometres of the museum lie many busy places, such as temples, restaurants, coastal parks and shopping malls, all linked by routes. It also records the opening hours of the museum, its visitor flow through the week and the weather of the city across the year. The form is generated from weather data, combined and smoothly joined into a wave-like surface. Its material is tested in a model as strips laid in different directions. The installation rises and falls so that visitors feel as if they are at sea, with views that open in some places and close in others, and edges where people can rest before entering the museum. On rainy days it gathers rainwater, and on sunny days it releases that water as a fine mist. At night layers of blue light make people feel as though they have sunk to the ocean floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 海洋裝置-在美術館外掀起一片會呼吸的浪
zh-Hant.body: 全球暖化日益嚴重，海平面持續上升，海洋生態也正承受珊瑚白化等種種傷害。這件位於美術館外的藝術裝置，希望喚起人們守護海洋的意識，並鼓勵具體的行動。研究發現，美術館方圓兩公里內有廟宇、餐廳、濱海公園與購物中心等熱鬧的場所，彼此以路徑相連；研究也記錄了美術館的開放時間、一週之中的人流，以及城市全年的天氣。形體由天氣數據生成，經過組合與平滑的銜接，化為一片波浪般的曲面；材料則在模型中加以測試，以不同方向鋪排的條帶構成。裝置高低起伏，讓參觀者彷彿置身海上，視野時而開闊、時而收束，邊緣也可供人在參觀美術館之前稍事休息。雨天，它收集雨水；晴天，再把雨水化為細細的水霧；入夜後，層層藍光讓人恍如沉入海底。一道人造的浪，溫柔地提醒著遠方大海的處境。

pins.title: Second Nature 2060
pins.description:
A speculative cultural landmark for Shenzhen, seen from 2060, built from the blocks of its local cultures.

Shenzhen, China | Cultural landmark | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 第二自然 2060
zh-Hant.description:
從 2060 年回望的深圳文化地標，以在地文化的量塊構成。

中國深圳｜文化地標｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: VR experience venue: fireflies and glowing jellyfish fill a dark exhibition hall.
VR 體驗館：螢火蟲與發光的水母布滿幽暗的展廳。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project imagines how people in 2060 will look back on the new landmarks of Shenzhen built for the city's fortieth anniversary in 2020. Because of its short history and lack of cultural facilities, Shenzhen has long been called a cultural desert compared with the other first-tier cities.
captions: Design inspiration: local cultures that once ran in parallel begin to flow, meet and converge.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案想像 2060 年的人們，將如何回望深圳在 2020 年建城四十週年時所建造的新地標。由於歷史短、文化設施不足，深圳與其他一線城市相比，長期被稱為文化沙漠。
captions: 設計靈感：原本平行的各地文化開始流動、交會並匯聚。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Data on Shenzhen's population showed that most residents came from other provinces, and visits to bookstores, galleries and museums were lower than in the other three first-tier cities. Before the Special Economic Zone, the cultures of different regions were in sporadic contact, but afterwards they began to flow together and converge.
captions: Four architectural cultures turned step by step into building blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 深圳的人口數據顯示，大多數居民來自其他省份，而書店、美術館與博物館的人均造訪次數，也低於其他三座一線城市。在經濟特區成立之前，各地文化只是零星接觸，特區成立之後，它們開始交流並匯聚在一起。
captions: 把四種建築文化逐步轉化為建築量塊。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Four traditional architectural cultures of the city were simplified into outlines and turned into building blocks for the new landmark. Inside, the blocks hold cultural and recreational uses such as a viewing platform, a book corner, a history gallery, a VR experience venue and exhibition spaces, guided by a phone app.
captions: An exploded section shown through a phone guide, with the visiting pathways.
Functional partition of the cultural and recreational spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 城市中四種傳統建築文化被簡化成輪廓，轉化為新地標的建築量塊。量塊內部容納觀景台、書角、歷史展廊、VR 體驗館與展覽空間等文化與休閒機能，並以手機應用程式導覽。
captions: 透過手機導覽呈現的爆炸剖面，以及參觀動線。
文化與休閒空間的機能分區。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the VR venue, species that have disappeared, such as fireflies, flutter again, and the book corner asks whether paper books still have a place next to new technology. In the galleries visitors scan their phones to see the stories of each year of the city's forty-year history.
captions: The book corner, where a screen and a stack of books meet.
Gallery views of the history exhibition and the screens of the city's stories.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在 VR 體驗館中，螢火蟲等已消失的物種重新飛舞；書角則提問：在新科技旁，紙本書是否仍有一席之地。在展廊中，參觀者以手機掃描，就能看見城市四十年歷史中每一年的故事。
captions: 書角：螢幕與一疊疊書本在此相遇。
歷史展覽的展廊，以及呈現城市故事的螢幕。

sections.heading: Second Nature 2060 - Stacking a Landmark of Memory for a Cultural Desert
sections.body: The project imagines how people forty years from now will look back on the new landmarks built for the fortieth anniversary of this city. With its short history and few cultural facilities, the city has long been called a cultural desert. Population data show that most residents came from other provinces, and visits to bookshops, galleries and museums fall below those of the other first-tier cities. Before the special economic zone, the cultures of different regions touched only sporadically, but afterwards they began to flow together and converge. Four traditional architectural cultures of the city are simplified into outlines and turned into building blocks for the new landmark. Inside, the blocks hold a viewing platform, a book corner, a history gallery, a virtual reality venue and exhibition spaces, guided by a phone app. In the virtual reality venue, vanished species such as fireflies flutter once more, while the book corner asks whether paper books still have a place beside new technology. In the galleries, visitors scan their phones to see the story of each year of the city. A young city begins to write its own memory.

zh-Hant.heading: 第二自然2060-為文化沙漠堆疊出記憶的地標
zh-Hant.body: 作品想像四十年後的人們，將如何回望這座城市在建城四十週年時建造的新地標。由於歷史短暫、文化設施匱乏，這座城市長久以來被稱為文化沙漠。人口數據顯示，多數居民來自外地，書店、美術館與博物館的造訪次數也低於其他一線城市；在特區設立之前，各地的文化只是零星接觸，此後才開始匯流、交融。城中四種傳統的建築文化被簡化為輪廓，化為新地標的建築積木；積木內部容納觀景台、書角、歷史藝廊、虛擬實境體驗館與展覽空間等文化與休閒用途，並由手機應用程式引導參觀。在虛擬實境館裡，螢火蟲等已經消失的物種再度飛舞；書角則提出一個問題：在新科技旁，紙本書是否仍有一席之地？藝廊中，參觀者掃描手機，便能看見城市四十年來每一年的故事。年輕的城市，由此開始為自己書寫記憶。

pins.title: An Experiment in Empathy
pins.description:
An exhibition of five spaces that lets visitors feel how people with different senses may experience the world.

Experimental | Exhibition design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 同理心實驗
zh-Hant.description:
由五個空間組成的展覽，讓參觀者感受感官不同的人可能如何經驗這個世界。

實驗性｜展覽設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Five parts of the exhibition, each developed from small spatial components.
展覽的五個部分，各自由小型空間構件發展而來。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: It can be hard to empathise with people whose senses work differently, because their feelings are difficult to describe accurately. The project began with a mother who only understood her autistic son's fear of everyday sounds after seeing his world through a VR headset.
captions: A collage of the sounds and feelings a child with autism cannot express.
Background and inspiration: experiencing the world through someone else's senses.
Spatial components for each condition, such as barriers, memory fragments, an emotional abyss and boundless walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 感官運作方式與我們不同的人，他們的感受很難被準確描述，因此也不容易被同理。本案的起點是一位母親：她透過 VR 頭戴裝置看見自閉症兒子眼中的世界後，才真正理解他對日常聲音的恐懼。
captions: 自閉症兒童無法表達的聲音與感受拼貼。
背景與靈感：透過他人的感官體驗世界。
每一種狀況的空間構件，例如障礙、記憶碎片、情緒深淵與無邊之牆。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student looked into what we call common sense, the shared experiences of things that most people take as the default. Cases of sensory differences were collected for autism, Alzheimer's disease, depressive disorder, colour blindness and visual impairment, to understand how each might perceive daily life.
captions: Design strategy: spatial components drawn from five sensory conditions.
A circle of everyday questions asking what common sense means to them.
Physical model at 1:50 of the spatial components.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生探討我們所謂的常識，也就是大多數人視為理所當然的共同經驗。研究收集了自閉症、阿茲海默症、憂鬱症、色盲與視覺障礙等感官差異的案例，試著理解他們可能如何感知日常生活。
captions: 設計策略：從五種感官狀況提取的空間元件。
以日常提問構成的圓環，追問「常識」對他們的意義。
空間構件的 1:50 實體模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each experience was translated into small spatial components and tested in models. The exhibition is divided into five sections, so that visitors entering different areas can experience different sensations.
captions: Depressive disorder: a spiralling space developed from sketches of feeling lost and falling.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每一種經驗都被轉化為小型的空間構件，並以模型測試。展覽分為五個區域，讓參觀者走進不同區域時，能體驗到不同的感受。
captions: 憂鬱症：由迷失與墜落感的草圖發展出的螺旋空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Tubes, poles, spirals and spheres turn each condition into a space that can be walked through and felt. The student concludes that full empathy may not be possible, but trying to understand others' feelings is a positive and necessary gesture.
captions: Sketches of a tube passage and a forest of poles.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 管道、立柱、螺旋與球體，把每一種狀況轉化為可以走進、可以感受的空間。學生的結論是：完全的同理或許不可能，但嘗試理解他人的感受，是一個正向而必要的姿態。
captions: 管道通道與立柱森林的草圖。

sections.heading: An Experiment in Empathy - Turning Different Senses Into Spaces One Can Enter
sections.body: When the senses of a person work differently from those of most others, that experience is often hard to describe and therefore hard to empathise with. The project began with a parent who, only after seeing the world of a child through a virtual reality headset, finally understood why everyday sounds caused such fear. From there the student examined what we call common sense, the shared experiences most people take as the default. Cases of sensory difference were gathered for autism, Alzheimer's disease, depressive disorder, colour blindness and visual impairment, in an effort to understand how each might perceive daily life. Every experience was translated into small spatial components and tested in models. The exhibition is divided into five sections, so that visitors entering each area meet a different sensation. Tubes, poles, spirals and spheres turn every condition into a space that can be walked through and felt. The project concludes that complete empathy may lie out of reach, yet the attempt to understand the feelings of others remains a positive and necessary gesture.

zh-Hant.heading: 同理心的實驗-讓不同的感官成為可以走進的空間
zh-Hant.body: 當一個人的感官運作方式與眾不同，那份感受往往難以被準確描述，也就不容易被旁人同理。作品的起點，是一位家長透過虛擬實境頭盔看見孩子眼中的世界，才終於明白孩子為何害怕日常的聲響。學生由此探究所謂的常識，也就是多數人視為理所當然的共同經驗；研究蒐集自閉症、阿茲海默症、憂鬱症、色盲與視覺障礙等感官差異的案例，試著理解每一種狀況如何感知日常生活。每一種經驗都被轉譯為小小的空間構件，並在模型中加以測試；展覽分為五個區段，參觀者走進不同的區域，便能體會不同的感受。管道、立柱、螺旋與球體，把每一種狀況化為可以穿行、可以觸及的空間。作品最後承認，完全的同理或許無法達成，但試著理解他人的感受，本身就是一種積極而必要的姿態。

pins.title: A Midsummer Night’s Dream
pins.description:
A stage redesign for Shakespeare's comedy, with levels for reality, the dream and the change between them.

London, UK | Stage design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 仲夏夜之夢
zh-Hant.description:
為莎士比亞喜劇重新設計的舞台，以不同層次承載現實、夢境與兩者之間的轉換。

英國倫敦｜舞台設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Spiral double-staircase, ground floor and revolving stages, moving between reality and the dream.
螺旋雙梯舞台、地面舞台與旋轉舞台，在現實與夢境之間轉換。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: After reading the original script and seeing a stage production of A Midsummer Night's Dream, the student wanted to redesign the stage and offer a personal reading of this absurd comedy. In the play, the city and the forest stand for waking and sleeping, the real and the dream, and the change between them begins at moonrise and ends at dawn.
captions: Stills from a stage production that inspired the redesign.
The story told in seven scenes, from the palace to the forest and back to the wedding.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在讀過《仲夏夜之夢》的原著劇本、看過它的舞台製作後，學生希望重新設計舞台，提出自己對這齣荒誕喜劇的詮釋。劇中的城市與森林代表清醒與沉睡、現實與夢境，兩者之間的轉換始於月升，終於黎明。
captions: 啟發本次改造的舞台製作劇照。
以七個場景說明故事：從宮殿到森林，再回到婚禮。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The seven scenes of the story take place in only two places, the Athenian palace and the forest, which the student read as reality and the dream. The second concept is a dream within a dream, where a dreamcatcher holds the dreams while the audience outside watches the comedy as if they were also dreaming.
captions: Design concepts: reality and the dream, and a dream within a dream.
Concept sketch of two performance zones, the transition area and the audience around them.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 故事的七個場景只發生在兩個地方：雅典宮殿與森林，學生把它們解讀為現實與夢境。第二個概念是夢中之夢：捕夢網收住夢境，而外面的觀眾觀看這齣喜劇時，彷彿自己也在做夢。
captions: 設計概念：現實與夢境，以及夢中之夢。
概念草圖：兩個表演區、轉換區與環繞其外的觀眾。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The performance area of a famous round theatre in London was redesigned, with a new circular skylight, an added auditorium on the second floor terrace and a new middle section of the stage. The performance area is divided vertically into dreamland, reality and the transition between them.
captions: Design development: the stage layers above the round theatre in London.
Exploded layers: skylight, dreamcatcher, original beams, performance area and auditorium.
The inner layer of the performance area, from dreamland at the top to reality below.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 本案重新設計倫敦一座著名圓形劇場的表演區，加入新的圓形天窗、二樓露台上增設的觀眾席，以及舞台的新中段。表演區在垂直方向分為夢境、現實與兩者之間的轉換區。
captions: 設計發展：倫敦圓形劇場上方的舞台層次。
爆炸分層：天窗、捕夢網、原有樑架、表演區與觀眾席。
表演區的內層：上方是夢境，下方是現實。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A cyclorama of curtains projects forest scenes, a suspended stage becomes the dream world of the fairy king and queen, and a spiral double staircase carries the scenes from reality to the dream. The ground floor stage holds the scenes of reality, and a revolving stage for the forest fairies can move along a track and up and down on a lift.
captions: Cyclorama with front and rear projection, and the suspended stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 環形布幕投影出森林場景，懸吊舞台成為仙王與仙后的夢境世界，螺旋雙梯則把場景從現實帶入夢境。地面舞台承載現實的場景，而森林精靈的旋轉舞台可以沿軌道移動，並透過升降台上下升降。
captions: 可前投與背投的環形布幕，以及懸吊舞台。

sections.heading: A Midsummer Night's Dream - Building a Dream Within a Dream Between Moonrise and Dawn
sections.body: After reading the original script and seeing a stage production, the student set out to redesign the stage for this absurd comedy and offer a personal reading of it. In the play the city and the forest stand for waking and sleeping, the real and the dreamed, and the passage between them begins at moonrise and ends at dawn. The seven scenes unfold in only two places, the palace and the forest, which the student read as reality and dream. A second concept is the dream within a dream, in which a dreamcatcher holds every dream while the audience watches as though dreaming too. The performance area of a famous round theatre is reimagined with a new circular skylight, an added auditorium on the second floor terrace and a new middle section of stage. The space is divided vertically into dreamland, reality and the threshold between them. A cyclorama of curtains projects forest scenes, a suspended stage becomes the dream realm of the fairy king and queen, and a spiral double staircase carries the action from waking into dream. Even the act of watching becomes a kind of dream.

zh-Hant.heading: 仲夏夜之夢-在月升與黎明之間搭起夢中之夢
zh-Hant.body: 讀過原著劇本、也看過一場舞台演出之後，學生希望重新設計這部荒誕喜劇的舞台，提出屬於自己的詮釋。劇中的城市與森林，象徵清醒與沉睡、真實與夢境，兩者之間的轉換始於月升，終於黎明。故事的七幕只發生在宮廷與森林兩處，學生將它們解讀為現實與夢；第二個概念是夢中之夢，捕夢網承接著所有的夢，台下的觀眾觀看這齣喜劇，彷彿自己也在夢裡。一座著名圓形劇場的表演區被重新設計，新增圓形天窗、二樓露台上的觀眾席，以及舞台的中段；表演區在垂直方向上被劃分為夢境、現實與兩者之間的過渡。布幕構成的環形天幕投映出森林的景象，懸吊的舞台化為仙王與仙后的夢之國度，螺旋雙梯把場景從現實帶入夢中。一樓舞台承載現實的場景，森林精靈的旋轉舞台則能沿軌道移動，並隨升降機起落。觀看本身，也成了一場夢。

pins.title: New Toys for Kids
pins.description:
Building blocks made from leftover water bottles, sized for children aged three to seven.

Hubei, China | Installation | Recycling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 給孩子的新玩具
zh-Hant.description:
以剩下的水瓶做成的積木，尺寸依三到七歲兒童而設計。

中國湖北｜裝置｜回收再利用｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Blocks used alone or combined, so children can build their own small spaces.
積木可以單獨使用，也可以組合，讓孩子們搭建屬於自己的小空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The ageing water pipes at the student's university need frequent repairs, so students buy cases of drinking water whenever a notice comes, and around four to five hundred empty bottles piled up by the hostel after one stoppage. In China only about seven percent of mineral water bottles are recycled each year, and the rest is buried as rubbish.
captions: Boxes of empty bottled water piled up in the hostel, the starting point of the project.
Background: water pipe repairs at school and the low recycling rate of water bottles.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生就讀的大學水管老舊，需要經常維修，每次接到停水通知，學生們就會買一箱箱飲用水；一次停水之後，宿舍旁堆積了約四、五百個空瓶。在中國，每年只有約百分之七的礦泉水瓶被回收，其餘都被當作垃圾掩埋。
captions: 宿舍裡堆積的空瓶裝水紙箱，本案的起點。
背景：校內水管維修，以及瓶裝水的低回收率。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Instead of melting the bottles down, the student looked for a way to turn clean leftover bottles into simple but interesting crafts. The bottles were collected, their labels cut off, then washed and disinfected.
captions: Recycling process: collect bottles, cut off the labels, wash and get clean bottles.
The basic block: bottles pasted five in a row and five rows deep, 250 mm high.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生沒有選擇把瓶子熔化，而是尋找把剩下的乾淨瓶子做成簡單又有趣的手作的方法。瓶子經過收集、撕去標籤，再清洗與消毒。
captions: 回收流程：收集瓶子、撕除標籤、清洗並取得乾淨瓶子。
基本積木：瓶子每排五個、前後五排黏合而成，高 250 公釐。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The recycled bottles replace the wood and plastic building blocks of kindergarten toys, with bottles pasted five in a row and five rows deep as the basic block. Based on body sizes of children aged three to seven, three sizes of shelves can be built to hold light objects such as picture books, reaching to the calf, the waist or the top of the head.
captions: Ergonomic sizes for children aged three to seven, and shelves to the calf, the waist and the top of the head.
More combinations of the blocks into seats, steps and shelters.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 回收瓶取代幼兒園玩具中木頭與塑膠製的積木，以每排五個、前後五排的瓶子作為基本積木。依據三到七歲兒童的身體尺寸，可以搭出三種高度的書架，分別到小腿、腰部與頭頂，用來放繪本等輕的物品。
captions: 三到七歲兒童的人體尺寸，以及到小腿、腰部與頭頂的書架。
積木的更多組合：座椅、階梯與小屋。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each block can be combined in many ways, so children can create different small spaces according to their interests and needs. The blocks were tested at full scale, to be played with on the lawn, in the classroom or anywhere the children like.
captions: 1:1 model test of the bottle blocks with children at play.
Rendering: on the lawn or in the classroom, children play wherever they like.
Full-scale test of the bottle blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每塊積木都能以多種方式組合，讓孩子依自己的興趣與需要，創造出不同的小空間。積木以 1:1 比例實際測試，可以在草地上、教室裡，或任何孩子喜歡的地方遊玩。
captions: 瓶子積木的 1:1 模型測試與孩子們的遊戲。
渲染圖：在草地或教室裡，孩子們隨處自在遊戲。
瓶子積木的 1:1 實體測試。

sections.heading: New Toys for Kids - Stacking Empty Bottles Into Worlds of Play
sections.body: The ageing water pipes on campus need frequent repairs, so whenever a notice comes students buy drinking water by the case. After one stoppage, four to five hundred empty bottles piled up beside the hostel. Only a small share of mineral water bottles is recycled each year, and the rest is buried as rubbish. Rather than melting the bottles down, the student looked for a way to turn clean leftover bottles into crafts that are simple yet engaging. The bottles were collected, their labels cut away, then washed and disinfected. The recycled bottles take the place of the wooden and plastic blocks found among kindergarten toys, glued five in a row and five rows deep to form a basic block. Based on the body sizes of children aged three to seven, three heights of shelf can be built, reaching the calf, the waist or the top of the head, to hold light things such as picture books. Each block combines in many ways, so children can create small spaces to suit their own interests and needs. Tested at full scale, the blocks can be played with on a lawn, in a classroom or anywhere children like.

zh-Hant.heading: 孩子的新玩具-讓空瓶堆疊出遊戲的天地
zh-Hant.body: 校園老舊的水管需要頻繁維修，每逢停水通知，學生們便成箱購買飲用水；一次停水過後，宿舍旁堆起了四、五百個空瓶。礦泉水瓶每年只有極少比例被回收，其餘多被當作垃圾掩埋。學生沒有選擇把瓶子熔化重製，而是尋找一種方式，讓乾淨的剩餘瓶子化為簡單卻有趣的手作。瓶子被收集起來，割去標籤，清洗並消毒。回收的瓶子取代幼兒園玩具中的木頭與塑膠積木，以五瓶一列、五列為一組黏合成基本的積木；依據三到七歲孩子的身體尺寸，可以搭出三種高度的架子，分別及於小腿、腰部與頭頂，用來放置繪本等輕巧物品。每一塊積木都能以多種方式組合，讓孩子依自己的興趣與需要，創造出各式小小的空間。積木經過足尺測試，可以在草地上、教室裡，或任何孩子喜歡的地方玩耍。被丟棄的空瓶，從此成為想像力的材料。

pins.title: Rooftop Art Workshops in Dafen
pins.description:
Workshops and a corridor that join the isolated rooftops of an urban village into a space for art.

Shenzhen, China | Urban renewal | Art studios | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 大芬村屋頂藝術工作坊
zh-Hant.description:
以工作坊與廊道，把城中村裡孤立的屋頂串連成藝術空間。

中國深圳｜城市更新｜藝術工作室｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Section perspective: a corridor and art workshops linking the rooftops around a square.
剖透視：串連廣場周邊屋頂的廊道與藝術工作坊。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In Dafen, an urban village in Shenzhen, the ground floor is so crowded that there is not enough space for public events, and many artists have no studio of their own and work on the street. The rooftops of the old buildings are like a second ground where residents dry clothes, exercise and talk, but each roof is an isolated island.
captions: The skyscrapers of Shenzhen above the village and the cultural facilities around the site.
The rooftops of the village, each one cut off from its neighbours.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳的城中村大芬村，地面層非常擁擠，沒有足夠的空間舉辦公共活動，許多藝術家也沒有自己的工作室，只能在街上作畫。老建築的屋頂就像城市的第二層地面，居民在上面晾衣、運動、聊天，但每一片屋頂都是一座孤島。
captions: 深圳摩天大樓下的城中村，以及基地周邊的文化設施。
村裡的屋頂，彼此互不相連。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student compared activities on the rooftops and on the ground, and studied how artists, residents and visitors could meet through art. Three sites were selected, and the housing types were analysed because the heights of the roofs differ greatly.
captions: Art studio and market comparisons and how young artists earn a living.
Site selection: the square beside the ancestral temple.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生比較屋頂與地面上的活動，研究藝術家、居民與訪客如何透過藝術相遇。學生選定了三個基地，並分析住宅類型，因為屋頂的高度差異很大。
captions: 藝術工作室與市場的比較，以及年輕藝術家的謀生方式。
基地選擇：祠堂旁的廣場。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Depending on the height difference between neighbouring roofs, different building units are used to connect them, keeping the structure and facades of the original buildings. The column grid is extended for the additions, and the beams of the surrounding buildings act as structural support.
captions: Strategies for linking roofs surrounded on two, three or four sides.
Section detail of a studio pod hung beneath the structure.
Exploded axonometric drawing of the corridor and workshops.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 依相鄰屋頂的高度差，以不同形式的建築單元把它們連接起來，同時保留原有建築的結構與立面。新增的部分沿用延伸的柱網，並以周邊建築的樑作為結構支撐。
captions: 連接三面、四面或兩面被圍合之屋頂的策略。
懸掛於結構下方的工作室單元剖面細部。
廊道與工作坊的爆炸軸測圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A series of visual art workshops connects the residences like dots, and a large corridor on thin columns links the roofs around the square, where people can cycle or stop to enjoy the view. The painting workshop hangs beneath the corridor, and people reach the handicraft workshops by lift from a café and bookshop on the ground floor.
captions: Master plan, studio floor and corridor floor.
The workshops floating above the rooftops.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一系列視覺藝術工作坊以點狀方式串連各棟住宅，一條由細柱支撐的大型廊道連接廣場周邊的屋頂，人們可以在上面騎單車，或停下來欣賞景色。繪畫工作坊懸掛在廊道下方，人們則從地面層的咖啡館與書店搭電梯前往手作工作坊。
captions: 總平面圖、工作室層與廊道層平面。
漂浮在屋頂上方的工作坊。

sections.heading: Dafen Rooftop Art Workshops - Joining Island Roofs Into a Second Ground
sections.body: In an urban village known for painting, the ground floor is so crowded that public events have no room, and many artists without studios of their own work out on the street. The rooftops of the old buildings are like a second ground where residents dry clothes, exercise and chat, yet each roof is an isolated island. The student compared activity on the roofs and on the ground, and studied how artists, residents and visitors might meet through art. Three sites were chosen, and because roof heights differ greatly, the housing types were analysed one by one. Different building units bridge neighbouring roofs according to their difference in height, while the structure and facades of the original buildings are kept. The column grid is extended to carry the additions, and the beams of surrounding buildings lend structural support. A series of visual art workshops links the homes like scattered dots, and a large corridor on slender columns rings the roofs around the square, where people can cycle or pause to take in the view. The painting workshop hangs beneath the corridor, and art finds a home above the rooftops.

zh-Hant.heading: 屋頂藝術工坊-把孤島般的屋頂連成第二地面
zh-Hant.body: 在一座以繪畫聞名的城中村裡，地面擁擠得容不下公共活動，許多畫家沒有自己的工作室，只能在街頭作畫。老房子的屋頂就像第二層地面，居民在上面晾衣、運動與閒聊，但每一片屋頂都是一座孤島。學生比較屋頂與地面上的活動，研究畫家、居民與遊客如何透過藝術相遇；三處基地被選定，由於屋頂高度差異甚大，住宅類型也被逐一分析。設計依相鄰屋頂的高低差，採用不同的建築單元加以連接，同時保留原有建築的結構與立面；柱網被延伸以承載新增的部分，周邊建築的梁則成為結構的支撐。一系列視覺藝術工坊如同散落的點，把住家串連起來；細柱撐起的大型廊道環繞廣場周圍的屋頂，人們可以騎車穿行，或駐足眺望。繪畫工坊懸吊在廊道下方，手工藝工坊則經由地面咖啡書店的電梯抵達。藝術就此在屋頂之上找到了家。

pins.title: Modular Housing with Corridors in the Sky
pins.description:
Growing modular units joined by sky corridors, bringing neighbours back together in a dense city.

Shenzhen, China | Housing | Modular design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空中廊道模組化住宅
zh-Hant.description:
以空中廊道連接可生長的模組單元，在高密度城市裡讓鄰居重新相聚。

中國深圳｜住宅｜模組化設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Housing towers linked by curving corridors in the sky.
以曲線空中廊道串連的住宅塔樓。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In traditional villages, close neighbours make life more lively and the community safer, because they watch out for each other. As Shenzhen grows denser, copies of skyscraper apartments widen the gap between people, and neighbours rarely meet.
captions: Village life and skyscraper life compared, imagining 2040.
Planning analysis: the plot laid out to let the summer wind through the community.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在傳統村落裡，鄰居關係緊密，不僅讓生活更熱鬧，也讓社區更安全，因為大家會互相照應。隨著深圳越來越密集，一棟棟複製的高樓公寓拉大了人與人之間的距離，鄰居之間很少見面。
captions: 想像 2040 年：比較村落與高樓的生活。
規劃分析：依夏季風向配置基地，讓風吹進社區。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Set in a new development zone of Shenzhen, the project starts from a modular unit of 4.3 by 4.3 metres that can keep growing in six floors and duplexes. Windows, doors and public spaces are placed along people's lines of sight, and one-way glass keeps the apartments private.
captions: The continuously growing modular unit.
Unit plans with vision and privacy analysis.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 專案位於深圳的新開發區，以 4.3 × 4.3 公尺的模組單元為起點，能以六層樓與樓中樓的方式持續生長。窗、門與公共空間沿著人的視線配置，單向玻璃則保護公寓的隱私。
captions: 持續生長的模組單元。
單元平面與視線、隱私分析。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The functions of the city are gathered into the interlayer between apartment units, and rooms are combined in different ways for families and for young people. Each way of connecting the units through sky corridors was scored for residents' satisfaction to find the best solution.
captions: Function integration: reconstructing city functions between two units and the calculation of satisfaction.
Room combinations for families and for young people.
Interconnected corridors in the sky and their satisfaction scores.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 城市的各種機能被收進公寓單元之間的夾層，房間依家庭與年輕人的需要以不同方式組合。每一種以空中廊道連接單元的方式，都依住戶滿意度評分，以找出最佳方案。
captions: 功能整合：在兩個單元之間重構城市機能，並計算滿意度。
家庭與年輕人的房間組合。
相互連通的空中廊道與滿意度評分。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Between the apartments, a communal courtyard lets single people organise social events and families join festive gatherings. A multifunctional floor holds a gym, shops and pet boarding, so people can get what they need without leaving the community.
captions: Model of the communal courtyard and the public floor.
The assembled unit and the community centre.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 公寓之間的共享庭院，讓單身住戶可以舉辦社交活動，家庭也能參與節慶聚會。多功能樓層設有健身房、商店與寵物寄養，人們不必離開社區就能取得所需。
captions: 共享庭院與公共樓層的模型。
組合後的單元與社區中心。

sections.heading: Modular Housing - Recovering Neighbourly Watchfulness Through Sky Corridors
sections.body: In traditional villages close neighbours make life lively and keep the community safe, because people look out for one another. As the city grows denser, copied skyscraper apartments widen the distance between people, and neighbours rarely meet. Set in a new development zone, the project begins from a modular unit four point three metres square that can keep growing through six floors and duplexes. Windows, doors and public spaces are placed along lines of sight, while one-way glass protects the privacy of each home. The functions of the city are gathered into the interlayer between apartment units, and rooms are combined in different ways for families and for young people. Every way of linking the units through sky corridors is scored for resident satisfaction to find the best arrangement. Between the apartments, a shared courtyard lets single people organise social events and families join festive gatherings. A multifunctional floor holds a gym, shops and pet boarding, so daily needs can be met without leaving the community. Within the towers, the warmth of neighbourhood is woven back together.

zh-Hant.heading: 模組住宅-以空中廊道找回鄰里的守望
zh-Hant.body: 在傳統的村落裡，鄰居彼此靠近，生活因此熱鬧，社區也因相互守望而安全。城市日益稠密，一棟棟複製而來的摩天公寓卻拉開了人與人的距離，鄰里之間難得碰面。作品坐落於一處新開發區，從一個邊長四點三公尺的模組單元出發，可以在六個樓層與樓中樓之間持續生長；窗、門與公共空間沿著人們的視線安排，單向玻璃則守住各戶的隱私。城市的機能被收攏到公寓單元之間的夾層，房間依家庭與年輕人的不同需求組合；每一種以空中廊道串連單元的方式，都經過居民滿意度的評分，以找出最佳方案。公寓之間的共享庭院，讓獨居者能籌辦社交活動，家庭也能加入節慶聚會；多功能樓層容納健身房、商店與寵物寄養，不出社區便能滿足所需。高樓之中，鄰里的溫度被重新編織回來。

pins.title: Free Jazz Fabric Pavilion
pins.description:
A temporary pavilion that turns the improvisation of free jazz into fabric, walls, light and shadow.

Taipei | X-Site | Temporary pavilion | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自由爵士布幕展亭
zh-Hant.description:
把自由爵士的即興轉化為布幕、牆面與光影的臨時展亭。

台北｜X-Site｜臨時展亭｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A temporary pavilion of fabric and walls in the plaza in front of the museum.
美術館前廣場上，由布幕與牆面構成的臨時展亭。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: This temporary X-Site pavilion sits in the plaza in front of an art museum in Taipei, and it is aimed mainly at young people and students who come on foot, by bicycle or by public transport. The student asked how the improvisation of free jazz could be translated from music into architecture.
captions: Multi-reality analysis of reachable landmarks around the museum.
Site analysis and the layers of the multi-reality concept: dream, light, wind and architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座臨時的 X-Site 展亭位於台北一座美術館前的廣場，主要對象是步行、騎單車或搭大眾運輸前來的年輕人與學生。學生思考的是，如何把自由爵士的即興精神從音樂轉譯成建築。
captions: 美術館周邊可達地標的多重現實分析。
基地分析與多重真實概念的分層：夢境、光影、風與建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The human brain anticipates what comes next from what it has already heard, and repetition and variation in music can bring pleasure. The original 28 parts of a free jazz recording were reorganised into eight sections, and their spectrograms were overlaid to make dream-like images.
captions: The free jazz concept tree and the jazz musicians behind it.
Music data of the free jazz piece.
From the audio file to a 4D model of the song.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 人腦會依已經聽到的內容預想接下來的聲音，音樂中的重複與變奏能帶來愉悅。學生把一段自由爵士錄音原有的 28 個部分重新整理成八段，並疊合各段的頻譜圖，形成如夢般的影像。
captions: 自由爵士概念樹，以及背後的爵士樂手。
自由爵士樂曲的音樂數據。
從音訊檔到樂曲的 4D 模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The student built a physical model to simulate shifting shadows, and recorded their own sleep while listening to jazz to link the depth of sleep to the space. Fabric, a material missing on the way to the museum, was chosen because it is soft, light and slightly transparent, like walking through fog.
captions: Shadow simulation and the section of the installation.
Sleep and dream analysis shaping the fabric surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生製作實體模型模擬變化的光影，也記錄自己聽爵士樂入睡時的睡眠數據，把睡眠深度與空間連結起來。前往美術館的路上看不到布料這種材料，因此選用它，因為它柔軟、輕盈又帶點透明，走在其中就像穿過霧氣。
captions: 光影模擬與裝置剖面。
以睡眠與夢境分析塑造布幕曲面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The floor-to-ceiling and overhanging walls match the height of the fabric, which is set by the depth of sleep, and visitors pass up the staircase twice under more and more skylights. Like jazz, the space starts with a quiet solo and builds up to an improvised climax, as the shadows of the walls layer on the fabric.
captions: Exploded axonometric drawing of the pavilion.
Spatial analysis drawing combining views from different angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 落地與懸吊的牆面對應布幕的高度，而布幕高度由睡眠深度決定；參觀者會兩次走上樓梯，頭頂的天窗也越來越多。空間就像爵士樂，從安靜的獨奏開始，逐步堆疊到即興的高潮，牆面的影子也層層落在布幕上。
captions: 展亭的爆炸軸測圖。
結合多個角度視圖的空間分析圖。

sections.heading: Free Jazz Fabric Pavilion - Weaving Improvised Melody Into Light and Shadow
sections.body: This temporary pavilion stands in the plaza before an art museum and welcomes mainly young people and students who arrive on foot, by bicycle or by public transport. The student asked how the improvising spirit of free jazz could be translated from music into architecture. The brain anticipates what comes next from what it has already heard, which is why repetition and variation in music can bring pleasure. The original twenty-eight parts of a free jazz recording were regrouped into eight sections, and their spectrograms were overlaid into dreamlike images. The student built a physical model to simulate shifting shadows and recorded a night of sleep while listening to jazz, linking the depth of sleep to space. Fabric, absent along the route to the museum, was chosen for its softness, lightness and slight transparency, so that moving through it feels like walking through fog. Floor-to-ceiling and hanging walls follow the height of the fabric, and visitors climb the stairs twice beneath a growing number of skylights. Like jazz, the space begins with a quiet solo and builds toward an improvised climax, as the shadows of the walls layer across the fabric.

zh-Hant.heading: 自由爵士布幕展亭-把即興的旋律織進光影
zh-Hant.body: 這座臨時展亭坐落於美術館前的廣場，主要迎接步行、騎單車或搭乘大眾運輸前來的年輕人與學生。學生追問的是：自由爵士的即興精神，如何從音樂轉譯為建築？人腦會依據已經聽見的聲音預想接下來的旋律，音樂中的重複與變奏因此帶來愉悅。一段自由爵士錄音原有的二十八個部分被重新整理為八段，各段的頻譜圖彼此疊合，生成如夢似幻的影像。學生製作實體模型模擬變幻的光影，也記錄自己伴著爵士樂入睡時的睡眠，把睡眠的深淺與空間相連。前往美術館的路上不見布料，於是選用它的柔軟、輕盈與微透，讓穿行其中如同走過霧氣。落地與懸吊的牆面對應布幕的高度，參觀者兩度登上樓梯，頭頂的天窗逐漸增多。空間如爵士樂般從安靜的獨奏起始，層層堆疊至即興的高潮，牆影也一層層落在布幕之上。

pins.title: Changeable Public Space in Guangzhou
pins.description:
Small changeable spaces in the corners of the city, where locals and African migrants can meet through play.

Guangzhou, China | Public space | Community | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 廣州的可變公共空間
zh-Hant.description:
在城市角落裡的小型可變空間，讓本地居民與非洲移民透過遊戲相遇。

中國廣州｜公共空間｜社區｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Modular units forming a lively landscape for music, rest and play.
以模組單元組成的活力地景，供音樂、休憩與遊戲使用。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An estimated 30,000 to 50,000 African migrants live in Guangzhou, where they come to do business, study and live. The student felt that mutual acceptance between locals and newcomers still had a long way to go, and that the language barrier was the biggest problem.
captions: Users analysis of the African community and its gathering areas in Guangzhou.
Construction steps: set up the columns, hang the frames, place the bamboo and lay the ropes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 估計有三萬到五萬名非洲移民在廣州經商、求學與生活。學生認為，本地居民與新移民之間的相互接納仍有很長的路要走，而語言隔閡是最大的問題。
captions: 廣州非洲社群及其聚集區域的使用者分析。
施工步驟：立柱、掛上框架、放置竹管，再鋪設繩網。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Through street questionnaires and fieldwork, the student found where African residents pass through or gather, and which corners of the area were underused. Small sites were chosen in a residential community near a university, in front of a supermarket and beside a bus stop.
captions: Rope frames that can be pulled down for football, table tennis or shuttlecock.
Bamboo tubes hung by ropes drop lower as more people sit together.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生透過街頭問卷與田野調查，找出非洲居民經過或聚集的地點，以及區內未被善用的角落。最後選定幾處小基地：大學附近的住宅社區、超市前方，以及公車站旁。
captions: 可以拉下來踢足球、打桌球或踢毽子的繩網框架。
以繩索懸吊的竹管，坐的人越多就垂得越低。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In the gaps between homes, a pavilion offers shade and chat by day, and its ropes can be pulled down for sports so that people of different backgrounds can play together. In a hair and nail corner, bamboo tubes on the ceiling drop lower as more people use the seats, inviting people to sit together.
captions: Sites and forms chosen around the gathering points of the area.
Dining room and dance studio boxes rotate between day and night, with wooden joint study models.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在住宅之間的縫隙裡，一座小亭白天可以乘涼聊天，繩索拉下後也能運動，讓不同背景的人一起玩。在美髮美甲角落，座位上的人越多，天花板的竹管就垂得越低，吸引大家坐在一起。
captions: 依區內聚集點選定的基地與形式。
餐廳與舞蹈教室的盒子可在日夜之間旋轉，並附木構接頭研究模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In front of the supermarket, the dining room and dance studio can be rotated by hand to free a larger outdoor space at night. Triangular modular units form a landscape where people can rest, sell their art, picnic or perform on small stages.
captions: The bamboo ceiling unit, its plan and the 1:1 model.
Structure of the timber frame, stores and dance room.
Triangular traffic and functional units, with a section.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在超市前方，餐廳與舞蹈教室可以用手推動旋轉，在夜間釋放出更大的戶外空間。三角形的模組單元組成一片地景，人們可以在這裡休息、販售自己的作品、野餐，或在小舞台上表演。
captions: 竹天花單元、平面與 1:1 模型。
木構框架、商店與舞蹈教室的結構。
三角形的動線單元與功能單元，以及剖面。

sections.heading: Changeable Public Space - Crossing the Language Barrier Through Play
sections.body: Tens of thousands of African migrants come to this city to trade, study and live. The student sensed that mutual acceptance between locals and newcomers still had a long way to go, and that the language barrier was the greatest obstacle. Through street questionnaires and fieldwork, the student traced where African residents pass through or gather, and which corners of the area were overlooked. Small sites were then chosen in a housing community near a university, in front of a supermarket and beside a bus stop. In the gaps between homes, a pavilion offers shade and conversation by day, and its ropes pull down to make a place for sport where people of different backgrounds can play together. In a hair and nail corner, bamboo tubes in the ceiling hang lower as more people take a seat, inviting everyone to sit closer. In front of the supermarket, a dining room and a dance studio can be turned by hand to free a wider outdoor space at night. Triangular modular units form a landscape for resting, selling art, picnicking or performing on small stages. Where words fall short, play and shared presence open the conversation first.

zh-Hant.heading: 可變公共空間-以玩耍跨越語言的隔閡
zh-Hant.body: 數以萬計的非洲移民在這座城市經商、求學與生活；學生感受到，本地居民與新來者之間的相互接納仍有漫長的路要走，而語言的隔閡是最大的難題。透過街頭問卷與田野調查，學生找出非洲居民經過或聚集的地點，以及區內被忽略的角落，最後選定大學附近的住宅社區、超市前方與公車站旁的幾處小基地。在住宅之間的縫隙裡，一座小亭白天供人乘涼閒聊，拉下繩索便成了運動的場地，讓不同背景的人一起遊戲；在美髮美甲的角落，坐下的人越多，天花板的竹管就垂得越低，邀請大家靠得更近。超市前方的餐廳與舞蹈教室可以徒手推動旋轉，在夜晚釋放出更寬闊的戶外空間；三角形的模組單元組成一片地景，供人休息、販售作品、野餐，或在小舞台上表演。言語難以抵達之處，遊戲與共處率先開啟了對話。

pins.title: Behind the Wall
pins.description:
Turning a walled-off riverside site into a park of lawns, wetland, forest and orchard.

Saint Petersburg, Russia | Landscape | Park renovation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 藍牆之後
zh-Hant.description:
把被圍牆封閉的河畔基地，改造成擁有草坪、濕地、森林與果園的公園。

俄羅斯聖彼得堡｜景觀｜公園改造｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Master plan of the park by the river, from the green wall to the orchard farm.
河畔公園的總平面圖，從綠牆到果園農場。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: For many years this riverside site was surrounded by blue iron walls and went through a lot of construction and demolition. People in the surrounding communities knew little about what lay behind the wall, but they still hoped it could become a green, comfortable and beautiful park.
captions: Site and surrounding analysis with visitor routes from home, hotel and work.
Public transport, current planting, the coastal water situation and circulation.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 多年來，這塊河畔基地一直被藍色鐵皮圍牆包圍，經歷了多次興建與拆除。周邊社區的居民對牆後的土地所知甚少，卻仍希望它能成為一座綠意盎然、舒適又美麗的公園。
captions: 基地與周邊分析，以及從住家、旅館與工作地點出發的訪客路線。
大眾運輸、現況植栽、沿岸水域狀況與動線。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The analysis showed that the site sits at a fork in the road with convenient transport, which makes it suitable for people to walk and go sightseeing. The student also planned sustainable programmes for outdoor comfort, materials, emissions, climate resilience and social life.
captions: Sustainable programme planning and development.
Design process sketches, from zoning bubbles to the latest draft.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 分析顯示，基地位於道路分岔處，交通便利，適合人們散步與觀光。學生也針對戶外舒適度、材料、排放、氣候韌性與社會生活，規劃了永續計畫。
captions: 永續計畫的規劃與發展。
設計過程草圖：從分區泡泡圖到最新草案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Through the design process, the student found that plants shape a park through their height, density, light and darkness, and seasons, and used these to divide its spaces. The original blue iron wall on one side was turned into a green ornamental slope with progressive plants.
captions: The green wall replacing the old iron wall, with its construction detail.
Section and plan of the quiet dance palace garden.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在設計過程中，學生發現植物會透過高度、密度、明暗與季節影響公園，並以此劃分公園的空間。基地一側原有的藍色鐵皮牆，被改造成種植層次植物的綠色觀賞斜坡。
captions: 取代舊鐵皮牆的綠牆與構造細部。
安靜的舞蹈宮花園剖面與平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The park links a green wall, great lawn, grassland slope, wetland, boat-shaped platform, dance palace garden, forest walk and orchard farm. Two squares beside the dance palace show different scenery in each season, from blossoms in late spring to warm colours in mid autumn.
captions: The wetland landscape and the boat-shaped platform by the river.
The south square in late spring and the north square in mid autumn.
Vegetation analysis of tree heights across the park.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 公園串連了綠牆、大草坪、草坡、濕地、船形平台、舞蹈宮花園、森林步道與果園農場。舞蹈宮兩側的兩座廣場在不同季節呈現不同景色，從晚春的花開到仲秋的暖色。
captions: 濕地景觀與河畔的船形平台。
晚春的南廣場與仲秋的北廣場。
公園樹木高度的植栽分析。

sections.heading: Behind the Wall - Growing a Riverside Park of Four Seasons Behind the Fence
sections.body: For many years this riverside site was closed off by blue iron walls and passed through round after round of building and demolition. People in the surrounding communities knew little about the land behind the wall, yet they still hoped it could become a green, comfortable and beautiful park. The analysis shows that the site sits at a fork in the road with easy transport, which suits walking and sightseeing. The student also planned sustainable programmes for outdoor comfort, materials, emissions, climate resilience and social life. Through the design process the student found that plants shape a park through height, density, light and shade, and the seasons, and used these qualities to divide its spaces. The original blue iron wall on one side is turned into a green ornamental slope planted in layers. The park links a green wall, a great lawn, a grassy slope, a wetland, a boat-shaped platform, a dance palace garden, a forest walk and an orchard farm. Two squares beside the dance palace change with the seasons, from blossom in late spring to warm colour in mid autumn. Where the wall once stood, the seasons now walk in.

zh-Hant.heading: 藍牆之後-讓圍籬後的河岸長成四季的公園
zh-Hant.body: 多年來，這塊河畔基地一直被藍色的鐵皮圍牆包圍，歷經一次又一次的興建與拆除。周邊社區的居民對牆後的土地所知甚少，卻仍盼望它能成為一座綠意盎然、舒適而美麗的公園。分析顯示，基地位於道路的分岔處，交通便利，適合散步與觀光；學生也針對戶外舒適度、材料、排放、氣候韌性與社會生活，規劃了一系列永續的計畫。在設計的過程中，學生發現植物會透過高度、密度、明暗與季節塑造一座公園，並以此劃分公園的空間；基地一側原有的藍色鐵皮牆，則被轉化為種滿層次植物的綠色觀賞斜坡。公園串起綠牆、大草坪、草坡、濕地、船形平台、舞蹈宮花園、森林步道與果園農場；舞蹈宮旁的兩座廣場隨季節變換景致，從晚春的繁花到仲秋的暖色。圍牆倒下之處，四季從此走了進來。

pins.title: Beauty & Beast
pins.description:
A children's outdoor teaching park where Chinese culture blends with the landscape.

Shenzhen, China | Landscape | Outdoor teaching park | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 美與野
zh-Hant.description:
一座讓中華文化融入地景的兒童戶外教學公園。

中國深圳｜景觀｜戶外教學公園｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Master plan of the teaching park beside a primary school, wrapped by hills on three sides.
緊鄰小學、三面環山的教學公園總平面圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Some schools in China value the teaching of Chinese culture, but children mostly learn it from classrooms and books and do not enjoy it. The site, surrounded by mountains on three sides, sits next to a primary school and nearby residential communities.
captions: Design concept: the overall plan built from plant communities, water collection nodes, paths, key nodes and terrain drops.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 中國有些學校重視中華文化教育，但孩子們多半只從教室與課本中學習，並不快樂。基地三面環山，緊鄰一所小學與周邊的住宅社區。
captions: 設計概念：由植物群落、集水節點、路徑、重要節點與地形落差組成的整體配置。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Starting from an experiment of dropping ink into water, the student saw how culture and wildness can blend with each other. The site analysis was then divided into five parts, giving the plan a streamlined form from top to bottom.
captions: Section A-A: a children's hillside forms a soft border between the school and the park.
Section B-B with vignettes of the landscape pockets along the route.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從把墨滴入水中的實驗出發，看見文化與野性可以彼此交融。接著把基地分析分成五個部分，讓整體配置呈現由上而下的流線形態。
captions: A-A剖面：兒童山坡在學校與公園之間形成柔和的邊界。
B-B剖面與沿線各景觀節點的小透視。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The biggest change in level, between the campus and the park, was shaped into a children's hillside that gives the two a gentle border. Cultural areas let children try printing, archaeology, clay sculpture and wall engraving, and read ancient Chinese inscriptions on a mural wall.
captions: The archaeological excavation area, a cultural activity area for children.
The mural rest area, where visitors can sit on the platform and read the inscriptions.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 校園與公園之間最大的高低落差，被塑造成兒童山坡，為兩者形成柔和的邊界。文化區讓孩子體驗拓印、考古、陶土雕塑與牆面刻畫，並在壁畫牆上閱讀古代中文銘文。
captions: 考古挖掘區，為孩子設計的文化活動區。
壁畫休憩區，訪客可坐在平台上閱讀牆上銘文。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: An ecological swimming pool protects the natural environment while letting children swim and play, and a puzzle play area adds to their campus life. A research building in the woods serves as an outdoor class where students observe natural species.
