captions: The ecological swimming pool and its section elevation.
The children's entertainment area with its puzzle activities.
Section elevations of the research building with its winding wooden ramps.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 生態泳池在保護自然環境的同時，讓孩子游泳與玩耍，益智遊戲區則豐富了他們的校園生活。林中的研究建築是一間戶外教室，讓學生觀察自然物種。
captions: 生態泳池與其剖立面。
設有益智活動的兒童遊戲區。
研究建築剖立面與蜿蜒的木構坡道。

sections.heading: Beauty and Beast - Letting Culture Be Learned Through Play in the Wild
sections.body: Some schools value teaching traditional culture, yet children mostly meet it in classrooms and textbooks and find little joy in it. The site is ringed by mountains on three sides and sits beside a primary school and the housing communities around it. The project begins with an experiment of dropping ink into water, revealing how culture and wildness can bleed into one another and blend. The site analysis is then divided into five parts, giving the plan a flowing form that runs from top to bottom. The steepest change in level, between campus and park, is shaped into a children's hillside that draws a soft border between the two. Cultural areas let children try rubbing prints, archaeology, clay sculpture and wall carving, and read ancient inscriptions on a mural wall. An ecological swimming pool protects the natural setting while letting children swim and splash, and a puzzle play area adds delight to campus life. A research building in the woods serves as an outdoor classroom for observing living species. Culture is no longer only words on a page, but something touched and joyfully played in the wild.

zh-Hant.heading: 美與野-讓文化在山野之間被玩出來
zh-Hant.body: 有些學校重視傳統文化的教育，孩子卻多半只能從教室與課本裡學習，並不覺得快樂。基地三面環山，緊鄰一所小學與周邊的住宅社區。作品從一個把墨滴入水中的實驗出發，看見文化與野性如何彼此暈染、交融；基地分析隨後被分為五個部分，讓整體配置呈現由上而下流動的形態。校園與公園之間最大的高低落差，被塑造成一座兒童山坡，為兩者劃出柔和的邊界。文化區讓孩子動手嘗試拓印、考古、陶土雕塑與牆面刻畫，也能在壁畫牆上辨讀古老的銘文。生態泳池在守護自然環境的同時，讓孩子游泳玩水，益智遊戲區則為校園生活增添樂趣；林間的研究建築化身為一間戶外教室，讓學生觀察自然中的物種。文化不再只是書本上的文字，而是在山野之間被親手觸摸、被歡快地玩出來的經驗。

pins.title: Festival Village
pins.description:
Bringing festivals, play and markets back into the public spaces of an old village.

Xiamen, China | Urban renewal | Ancient village reconstruction | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 節慶村落
zh-Hant.description:
讓節慶、遊戲與市集重回老村落的公共空間。

中國廈門｜城市更新｜古村落改造｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometric of the festival village, from the theatre stage to the rainbow hill.
節慶村落軸測圖，從戲台到彩虹山丘。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Since the late 1980s many ancient buildings in China have been demolished, and uniform concrete buildings have gradually weakened local culture and traditional public space. In this old village in Xiamen, the space under the ancient trees is piled with rubbish, the stage in front of the ancestral hall is abandoned and children have nowhere to play.
captions: Site analysis, development process, problems and daily activity timelines of the village.
Development process, from a poorly used site to a cultural exchange platform.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 自1980年代末以來，中國許多古建築遭到拆除，整齊劃一的混凝土建築也逐漸削弱了地方文化與傳統公共空間。在這座廈門的老村落裡，古樹下堆滿垃圾，祠堂前的戲台被廢棄，孩子們也沒有地方玩耍。
captions: 村落的基地分析、發展過程、問題與日常活動時間軸。
發展進程：從低度利用的基地，到文化交流平台。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied the village's festivals and turned them into three ideas: dice-shaped play devices, lanterns that create a festive atmosphere and a movable stage. The eave forms of the ancient houses, read through the five elements, became the starting point for new structures.
captions: Festival activities development: Mid-Autumn dice game, lanterns and opera.
Initial concept: dice conversion, festive atmosphere and stage reconstruction.
The eaves of the ancient houses, read through water, wood, gold, earth and fire.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究村落的節慶活動，並轉化為三個構想：骰子造型的遊戲裝置、營造節慶氣氛的燈籠，以及可移動的戲台。古厝屋簷的形式透過五行來解讀，成為新構造的起點。
captions: 節慶活動發展：中秋博餅、燈籠與戲曲。
初步概念：骰子轉化、營造氛圍與戲台改造。
以水、木、金、土、火解讀古厝屋簷。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The village is divided into three areas: a historical introduction area with a movable stage in front of the ancestral hall, a square with a rest area and market, and an entertainment area for children. Beside the old tree at the entrance, movable dice chairs and flowers form a sinking rest area.
captions: Process and before/after plans of the sinking rest area.
The seats are removed, stacked and joined into a movable stage with a screen that can be raised and lowered.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 村落被分為三個區域：祠堂前設有可移動戲台的歷史介紹區、設有休憩區與市集的廣場，以及兒童遊樂區。入口的老樹旁，可移動的骰子座椅與花卉構成一處下沉式休憩區。
captions: 下沉式休憩區的推演與改造前後平面。
座椅被移出、堆疊並組成可移動的戲台，配有可自由升降的屏幕。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the busiest open area, mobile carts can be taken apart and put together again, forming a long market by day. At night the same carts are regrouped into sheltered booths for the barbecue restaurant.
captions: Market plans before and after renovation, from morning to night.
The cart evolves from the five-element eaves and changes from a long market to night shelters.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在人潮最多的開放區，可拆裝的移動推車白天能組成一條長長的市集。到了晚上，同樣的推車重新組合，成為燒烤餐廳的遮蔽攤位。
captions: 改造前後從早到晚的市集平面。
推車由五行屋簷演變而來，從長市集轉變為夜間遮棚。

sections.heading: Festival Village - Reviving an Ancient Village With Dice, Lanterns and a Stage
sections.body: For decades many ancient buildings have been torn down, and uniform concrete blocks have slowly weakened local culture and traditional public space. In this old village the ground beneath the ancient trees is heaped with clutter, the stage before the ancestral hall stands abandoned, and children have nowhere to play. The student studied the festivals of the village and turned them into three ideas: dice-shaped play devices, lanterns that create a festive mood and a stage that can move. The eave forms of the old houses, read through the five elements, became the starting point for new structures. The village is divided into three areas: a historical introduction area with a movable stage before the ancestral hall, a square for rest and a market, and a play area for children. Beside the old tree at the entrance, movable dice seats and flowers form a sunken resting corner. In the busiest open area, carts that come apart and fit back together form a long market by day. At night they regroup into sheltered booths for a barbecue restaurant, and the joy of festival returns to daily life.

zh-Hant.heading: 節慶村落-以骰子燈籠與戲台喚回古村的熱鬧
zh-Hant.body: 數十年來，許多古建築相繼被拆除，整齊劃一的混凝土樓房逐漸削弱了地方文化與傳統的公共空間。在這座老村落裡，古樹下堆滿雜物，祠堂前的戲台被棄置一旁，孩子也沒有地方玩耍。學生研究村落的節慶活動，把它們轉化為三個構想：骰子造型的遊戲裝置、營造節慶氣氛的燈籠，以及可以移動的戲台；古厝屋簷的形式透過五行加以解讀，成為新構造的起點。村落被分為三區：祠堂前設有活動戲台的歷史介紹區、容納休憩與市集的廣場，以及兒童遊樂區；入口老樹旁，可移動的骰子座椅與花卉圍出一處下沉的休憩角落。在人潮最多的開放區，可拆裝的推車白天組成一條長長的市集，入夜後又重新組合，化為燒烤餐廳的遮蔽攤位。節慶的熱鬧，由此重新回到日常。

pins.title: Child Living in the Rivers
pins.description:
A narrative landscape that rebuilds a remembered journey into the kingdom of a river child.

Experimental | Landscape | Narrative landscape design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 住在河裡的孩子
zh-Hant.description:
以敘事景觀重建一段走進河童國度的記憶旅程。

實驗性｜景觀｜敘事景觀設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The mysterious kingdom between the mountains and the lake, wrapped in forest and mist.
山與湖之間神秘的國度，被森林與霧氣包圍。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: This narrative landscape begins with a story: one summer the narrator meets a child of the river, a kappa, follows it and accidentally falls into an isolated place. The path to that kingdom no longer exists, so the design has to rebuild the journey from memory.
captions: Ink line drawing of the kappa, the child who lives in the rivers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個敘事景觀從一個故事開始：某個夏天，敘事者遇見一個住在河裡的孩子——河童，跟著牠走，意外跌入一處與世隔絕的地方。通往那個國度的路已不復存在，因此設計必須憑記憶重建這段旅程。
captions: 河童的墨線繪圖，那個住在河裡的孩子。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student drew the whole story as a storyboard, moving from bare winter trees to walls, stairs, water and forest. The kingdom was then mapped as a route between the mountains and the lake, with each feeling noted along the way.
captions: Storyboard of the journey into the kappa's world.
Plan of the kingdom, with the feelings noted along the route.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把整個故事畫成分鏡，從冬日的枯樹一路走到牆、階梯、水與森林。接著把這個國度描繪成山與湖之間的一條路徑，並沿途標記每一種感受。
captions: 進入河童世界的旅程分鏡。
國度平面圖，沿途標記各段感受。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: From the entrance, a wooden bridge sinks into the distance, the stream slowly floods up to the walker's shoes and the walls on both sides gradually drop. The path then divides into three roads: one climbs up, one leads to a small hole and one is blocked by tall trees and a dense forest.
captions: At the entrance, the wooden bridge sinks and the water rises.
The three roads: climbing, going down into a hole and meeting the forest.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 從入口開始，木橋向遠方下沉，溪水慢慢漫上行人的鞋子，兩側的牆也逐漸降低。接著路徑分成三條：一條向上攀升，一條通往一個小洞，另一條則被高大的樹木與茂密的森林擋住。
captions: 入口處木橋下沉、水面上升。
三條路：向上攀升、下探洞口與遇見森林。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: An elastic net laid over the water lets visitors bounce and play like the kappa jumping in the creek. The ponds, bridges and paths are set within the forest so that the walk feels like entering and then leaving a dream.
captions: The elastic net laid out over the water.
Section A-A along the route from the entrance into the forest.
Aerial render of the ponds and bridges seen when leaving.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 鋪在水面上的彈性網，讓訪客像在溪中跳躍的河童一樣彈跳玩耍。池塘、橋與步道都安置在森林之中，讓這段散步就像走進又走出一場夢。
captions: 鋪在水面上的彈性網。
從入口到森林的A-A剖面。
離開時看見的池塘與橋的鳥瞰圖。

sections.heading: Child Living in the Rivers - Rebuilding a Dreamlike Journey From Memory
sections.body: This narrative landscape begins with a story. One summer the narrator meets a child of the river, a kappa, follows it and stumbles into an isolated kingdom by accident. The road to that place no longer exists, so the design must rebuild the journey from memory. The student drew the whole story as a storyboard, moving from bare winter branches toward walls, stairs, water and forest. The kingdom was then mapped as a route between the mountains and the lake, with each feeling noted along the way. From the entrance a wooden bridge sinks slowly into the distance, the stream creeps up over the shoes of the walker, and the walls on either side gradually fall away. The path then divides into three. One road climbs upward, one leads to a small opening, and one is blocked by tall trees and dense forest. An elastic net stretched across the water lets visitors bounce and play like the kappa leaping in the creek. Ponds, bridges and paths lie hidden in the forest, so that a single walk feels like entering a dream and then stepping out of it again.

zh-Hant.heading: 住在河裡的孩子-憑記憶重建一段夢境之旅
zh-Hant.body: 這處敘事景觀從一個故事開始：某個夏天，敘事者遇見一個住在河裡的孩子，一隻河童，跟著牠走，竟意外跌入一處與世隔絕的國度。通往那裡的路早已不復存在，設計因此必須憑著記憶，重新建構這段旅程。學生把整個故事畫成分鏡，從冬日的枯枝，一路走向牆、階梯、水與森林；這個國度接著被描繪為山與湖之間的一條路徑，沿途標記著每一種感受。從入口出發，木橋向遠方緩緩下沉，溪水慢慢漫上行人的鞋面，兩側的牆也漸次降低；路徑隨後分岔為三條，一條向上攀升，一條通往小小的洞口，另一條則被高大的樹木與茂密的森林擋住。鋪展在水面上的彈性網，讓訪客像在溪中跳躍的河童般彈跳嬉戲。池塘、橋與步道藏身林間，一趟散步，便如走進又走出一場夢。

pins.title: New Corridor
pins.description:
An elevated promenade that helps new and old villagers meet in an urban village.

Xiamen, China | Urban design | Urban village promenade | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 新廊道
zh-Hant.description:
一條讓城中村新舊村民相遇的架高步道。

中國廈門｜都市設計｜城中村步道｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial plan of the new corridor linking the community school, creative center, game, sports and music zones.
新廊道鳥瞰平面，串連社區學校、創意中心、遊戲區、運動區與音樂區。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An urban village in Xiamen was about to be demolished, leaving new villagers who had moved in and old villagers living side by side with little contact. The project set out to create a cultural and artistic promenade that would break down these barriers and build mutual understanding.
captions: The invisible boundary between young migrants and local villagers.
Scheme generation: places for education, games, music, sports, food and art.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廈門一座城中村即將拆除，搬進來的新村民與原有的老村民比鄰而居，卻少有往來。這個專案希望打造一條文化與藝術的步道，打破隔閡，增進彼此的理解。
captions: 年輕移居者與在地村民之間的無形邊界。
方案生成：教育、遊戲、音樂、運動、飲食與藝術的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied cases of leftover space, transformed old buildings and stepped circulation, then sketched six kinds of activity spaces within the village. Massing studies tested how a path could weave through the dense blocks.
captions: Path generation through the dense village blocks.
Section A-A through the existing village buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究了閒置空間、舊建築改造與階梯式動線等案例，接著在村中構想六種活動空間。量體研究則測試一條路徑如何穿梭於密集的街區之間。
captions: 穿梭於密集村落街區的路徑生成。
穿過既有村落建築的A-A剖面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The design stacks three layers: public activity spaces on the ground, a living folk promenade on the second layer and a top layer that connects floating migrants. The elevated corridor threads between houses and over rooftops, tying the new activity spaces together.
captions: Exploded axonometric of the three layers.
Sectional perspective of the elevated promenade and roof terraces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計疊合了三個層次：地面的公共活動空間、第二層的生活民俗步道，以及連結流動人口的頂層。架高的廊道穿梭於房屋之間、跨越屋頂，把新的活動空間串連起來。
captions: 三個層次的分解軸測圖。
架高步道與屋頂平台的剖透視。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Old houses become a community school, with new stairs and joints inserted into the traditional timber roofs. A game zone and a creative center with rentable rooms for chatting, exhibitions, workshops and salons give new and old villagers reasons to meet.
captions: The community school, with insertion, combination, column and division details.
Section of the game zone along the corridor.
Section of the creative center around a planted courtyard.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 老房子被改造成社區學校，在傳統木構屋頂中嵌入新的樓梯與接頭。遊戲區，以及設有可租用的聊天室、展覽、工作坊與沙龍空間的創意中心，讓新舊村民有了相遇的理由。
captions: 社區學校，以及嵌入、結合、柱與分隔的構造細部。
沿廊道的遊戲區剖面。
圍繞植栽中庭的創意中心剖面。

sections.heading: New Corridor - A Promenade Over the Rooftops Linking New and Old Villagers
sections.body: An urban village is about to be demolished, and the new villagers who have moved in live side by side with the old villagers yet rarely meet. The project sets out to build a cultural and artistic promenade that breaks down these barriers and slowly leads both groups toward mutual understanding. The student studied cases of leftover space, transformed old buildings and stepped circulation, then sketched six kinds of activity space within the village. Massing studies tested how one path might weave through the dense blocks. The design stacks three layers: public activity spaces on the ground, a lively folk promenade on the second level and a top layer that connects the floating population. The raised corridor threads between houses and over rooftops, tying the new activity spaces together one by one. Old houses become a community school, with new stairs and joints set into their traditional timber roofs. A game zone and a creative centre with rentable rooms for chatting, exhibitions, workshops and salons give new and old villagers reasons to meet. A single corridor draws strangers together as neighbours.

zh-Hant.heading: 新廊道-在屋頂之間牽起新舊村民的步道
zh-Hant.body: 一座城中村即將拆除，搬進來的新村民與原有的老村民比鄰而居，彼此卻少有往來。作品希望打造一條文化與藝術的步道，打破隔閡，讓雙方慢慢走向相互理解。學生研究閒置空間、舊建築改造與階梯式動線的案例，在村中構想出六種活動空間，再以量體研究測試一條路徑如何穿梭於密集的街區之間。設計疊合了三個層次：地面是公共活動空間，第二層是充滿生活氣息的民俗步道，頂層則連結流動的人口。架高的廊道在房屋之間穿行、跨越屋頂，把新的活動空間一一串起。老房子被改造為社區學校，新的樓梯與接頭嵌入傳統的木構屋頂；遊戲區與設有可租用聊天室、展覽、工作坊與沙龍的創意中心，為新舊村民創造了相遇的理由。一條廊道，就這樣把陌生的鄰居牽到了一起。

pins.title: Danan Eco-Park
pins.description:
An eco-park that resists urban erosion and shelters birds, plants and stormwater.

Taoyuan, Taiwan | Landscape | Eco-park | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 大湳生態公園
zh-Hant.description:
一座抵抗都市侵蝕、庇護鳥類、植物與雨水的生態公園。

台灣桃園｜景觀設計｜生態公園｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Master plan of the eco-park, with a central detention pond, woodland, bird reserve and community buildings.
生態公園總平面圖，包含中央滯洪池、林地、鳥類保護區與社區建築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site lies where urban and non-urban land meet in Bade District, and rapid urbanization has severely eroded the area's ecological resources. The park was asked to resist this erosion and give plants and animals a place to thrive.
captions: Green structure of the district: the central green network is missing.
Population density around the site, where demand for park space is high.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於八德區都市與非都市土地的交界，快速的都市化使當地的生態資源嚴重流失。這座公園被賦予抵抗侵蝕的任務，為動植物提供生長棲息的空間。
captions: 區域綠色結構：中央的綠色網絡是缺失的。
基地周邊的人口密度，對公園綠地的需求很高。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Map studies showed that the district's natural ponds had shrunk sharply as the city grew. The former military base on the site had meanwhile grown into a rich ecosystem that now attracts endangered orioles.
captions: Bubble diagram linking entrance squares, playgrounds, birdwatching and elderly care.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 地圖研究顯示，隨著城市擴張，區內的自然埤塘大幅減少。基地上原有的軍事基地則逐漸發展出豐富的生態系統，如今吸引了瀕危的黃鸝棲息。
captions: 泡泡圖，連結入口廣場、遊戲場、賞鳥區與長照中心。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Two main entrances in the north and south are tied by one main road, and only a single road crosses the park to limit disturbance to the ecological core. Retained buildings are reused as a community center, a children's library, an elderly care center and a birdwatching post.
captions: Circulation analysis with the two main entrances and activity spots.
Building character: retained buildings and their new uses.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 南北兩個主要入口以一條主要道路串連，僅有一條道路穿越公園，以減少對生態核心的干擾。保留下來的建築被改造成社區中心、兒童圖書館、長照中心與賞鳥據點。
captions: 動線分析，標示兩個主要入口與活動節點。
建築性格：保留建築與其新用途。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Dense woodland, light woodland, grassland and a detention basin each shelter different birds, insects and small animals. The lawn at the center of the park is lowered into a basin that stays dry for recreation most of the year and holds stormwater during heavy rain.
captions: Sections of the four habitats: dense woodland, light woodland, grassland and detention basin.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 密林、疏林、草地與滯洪池，各自為不同的鳥類、昆蟲與小動物提供棲地。公園中央的草坪下降成一處滯洪池，平時保持乾燥供休閒使用，豪雨時則暫時蓄存雨水。
captions: 四種棲地的剖面：密林、疏林、草地與滯洪池。

sections.heading: Danan Eco-Park - Guarding a Habitat for Orioles at the Edge of the City
sections.body: The site lies where urban and non-urban land meet, and rapid urbanisation has badly eroded the ecological resources of the area. The park is asked to resist this erosion and to give plants and animals a place to grow and shelter. Map studies show that the natural ponds of the district have shrunk sharply as the city expanded. Meanwhile the former military base on the site has quietly grown into a rich ecosystem over the years, and it now draws endangered orioles. The design ties the northern and southern entrances together with one main road, and only a single road crosses the park so that disturbance to the ecological core is kept to a minimum. Retained buildings are reused as a community centre, a children's library, an elderly care centre and a birdwatching post. Dense woodland, light woodland, grassland and a detention basin each shelter different birds, insects and small animals. The central lawn is lowered into a basin that stays dry for recreation most days and holds stormwater in heavy rain. Human activity and the rhythm of nature learn to live gently together.

zh-Hant.heading: 大湳生態公園-為黃鸝守住一片都市邊緣的棲地
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於都市與非都市土地的交界，快速的都市化嚴重侵蝕了這一帶的生態資源；這座公園被賦予抵抗侵蝕的任務，讓動植物有地方生長與棲息。地圖研究顯示，隨著城市擴張，區內的天然埤塘大幅減少；而基地上的舊軍事基地，卻在歲月中悄悄發展出豐富的生態系統，如今更吸引了瀕危的黃鸝前來。設計以一條主要道路串連南北兩個入口，且只讓單一道路穿越公園，把對生態核心的干擾降到最低；保留下來的建築被改造為社區中心、兒童圖書館、長照中心與賞鳥據點。密林、疏林、草地與滯洪池，分別為不同的鳥類、昆蟲與小動物提供棲身之處。公園中央的草坪下降為一處滯洪池，平日乾燥可供休憩，豪雨時則暫存雨水。人的活動與自然的節奏，在此學會溫柔地共處。

pins.title: Community Rescue Program
pins.description:
Urban acupuncture that reconnects a community about to be split by a new road.

Zhangzhou, China | Urban design | Community renewal | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 社區拯救計畫
zh-Hant.description:
以城市針灸重新串連一個即將被新道路切開的社區。

中國漳州｜都市設計｜社區更新｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometric of the community blocks opened up to the commercial street.
社區街廓向商業街打開的軸測圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A community in Zhangzhou, already split into three neighborhoods by its waterways, was about to be cut in two by a planned new road. The project set out to rescue the community by reconnecting its villages across the road.
captions: Current communities and the future split caused by the new road.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 漳州一處社區原本就被水系分成三個鄰里，如今又將被一條規劃中的新道路一分為二。這個專案希望透過跨越道路、重新串連各個村落，來拯救這個社區。
captions: 現況社區，以及新道路將造成的分割。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student mapped circulation and shop types along the old Shimei Street, where catering and food dominate and many stalls spill out in front of the shops. Commercial vitality fades toward the southern end once the morning market disperses.
captions: New commercial form: retail and catering in the north, the fresh market in the middle and new uses in the south.
Typology of shop fronts, stalls and courtyards.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生調查了這條老街沿線的動線與店鋪類型，餐飲是主要業態，許多攤位擺到了店面前方。早市散去後，街道南端的商業活力明顯減弱。
captions: 新的商業形態：北段零售與餐飲、中段生鮮市場、南段注入新用途。
店面、攤位與院落的類型學。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Using urban acupuncture, the design works at several scales along two lines: a commercial line on the old street and an ecological line along the river. Local houses, self-built houses and verandas are transformed and combined so that buildings share their interfaces with the community.
captions: Sections of the commercial street and the life street.
Original and new architectural types: optimizing, sharing and connecting buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計以城市針灸的方法，在不同尺度上沿兩條主線展開：老街上的商業線，以及沿河的生態線。在地古厝、自建房與騎樓被轉化與組合，讓建築與社區共享介面。
captions: 商業街與生活街的剖面。
原有與新的建築類型：優化、共享與連結建築。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Where the new road crosses the old street, a sunken underpass plaza lets people keep walking and hosts stalls, steps and daily leisure. Along the river, landscape bridges and a raised pedestrian park over an urban wetland reconnect the divided neighborhoods.
captions: Underpass commercial plaza with flexible venues for steps, stalls and a sunken plaza.
Eco theme line along the river, with three landscape bridges.
Pedestrian raised park with wooden decks over an urban wetland.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在新道路與老街交會處，下沉的地下通道廣場讓人們可以繼續步行，並容納攤位、階梯與日常休閒。沿著河岸，景觀橋與架高於都市濕地之上的步行公園，重新連結被分隔的鄰里。
captions: 地下通道商業廣場，設有階梯、臨時攤位與下沉廣場等彈性場地。
沿河的生態主題線，以及三座景觀橋。
架高的步行公園，木棧道橫跨都市濕地。

sections.heading: Community Rescue Program - Stitching Villages Divided by a Road Through Urban Acupuncture
sections.body: A community already split into three neighbourhoods by its waterways was about to be cut in two by a planned new road. The project sets out to reach across that road and reconnect the villages, giving the community back its wholeness. The student surveyed circulation and shop types along the old street. Food and catering prove to be the main trade, with many stalls spilling out in front of the shops. Once the morning market disperses, commercial life at the southern end of the street fades noticeably. Using urban acupuncture, the design works at several scales along two lines: a commercial line on the old street and an ecological line along the river. Local old houses, self-built houses and verandas are transformed and recombined so that buildings share their edges with the community. Where the new road meets the old street, a sunken underpass plaza lets people keep walking and holds stalls, steps and everyday leisure. Along the river, landscape bridges and a pedestrian park raised above a wetland stitch the divided neighbourhoods back together.

zh-Hant.heading: 社區拯救計畫-以城市針灸縫合被道路切開的村落
zh-Hant.body: 一處社區原本就被水系分成三個鄰里，如今又將被一條規劃中的新道路一分為二。作品希望跨越這條道路，重新串連各個村落，為社區找回完整。學生調查老街沿線的動線與店鋪類型，發現餐飲是主要的業態，許多攤位一路擺到店面前方；早市散去之後，街道南端的商業活力便明顯消退。設計以城市針灸的方法，在不同尺度上沿兩條主線展開：一條是老街上的商業線，一條是沿著河岸的生態線。在地的古厝、自建房與騎樓被轉化與重組，讓建築與社區共享彼此的介面。在新道路與老街交會之處，一座下沉的地下通道廣場讓人們得以繼續步行，容納攤位、階梯與日常的休閒；沿著河岸，景觀橋與架高於濕地之上的步行公園，把分隔的鄰里重新縫合在一起。

pins.title: Tank Hsinchu
pins.description:
A tank recreation park with a red skywalk on a former military site.

Hsinchu, Taiwan | Landscape | Recreation park | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 新竹儲槽公園
zh-Hant.description:
一座在舊軍事用地上、以紅色空中步道串連的儲槽休閒公園。

台灣新竹｜景觀設計｜休閒公園｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Master plan of the tank park, wrapped by a raised running track.
儲槽公園總平面圖，由一條架高的跑道環繞。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site in Hsinchu was a former military site long closed to the public, while the surrounding area lacked open space and suffered from ecological fragmentation. The project set out to turn it into a public, multifunctional park for sports and leisure that benefits the whole neighborhood.
captions: Urban open space: the site is covered with soil and lush vegetation.
Landuse around the site, mainly education and residential land.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 新竹的基地是一處長期不對外開放的舊軍事用地，而周邊地區缺乏開放空間，生態也呈現破碎化。這個專案希望把它轉變為一座公共、多功能的運動與休閒公園，讓整個鄰里受益。
captions: 都市開放空間：基地覆蓋著土壤與茂密植被。
基地周邊的土地使用，以教育與住宅用地為主。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Surveys of space attributes showed that nearby residents and students had a specific demand for open venues. Terrain studies found a T-shaped depression and many trees worth preserving, and all four tanks on the site are covered with soil.
captions: Space attribute and residents' need for activity spaces.
Energy value of people, elevation and preserved trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 空間屬性調查顯示，周邊居民與學生對開放場地有明確的需求。地形研究發現了T字形的凹地與許多值得保留的樹木，基地上的四座儲槽也都覆蓋著土壤。
captions: 空間屬性與居民對活動空間的需求。
人群活力值、地形高程與保留樹木。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The four tanks become a children's activity center, a restaurant and cafe, a climbing gym and a service center. Functional, planting, sports zone and elevation studies arrange running, walking, playground and training areas around them.
captions: Ground and upper floor plans of the tanks.
Functional analysis, plants design, sports zone analysis and elevation design.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 四座儲槽分別轉化為兒童活動中心、餐廳與咖啡館、攀岩館與服務中心。機能、植栽、運動分區與高程的研究，則在它們周圍安排了跑步、散步、遊戲場與訓練區。
captions: 儲槽的地面層與上層平面圖。
機能分析、植栽設計、運動分區分析與高程設計。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Half-buried tanks open into sunlit rooms beneath a green landscape, while a red skywalk loops above the trees and touches the ground in four places. A spiral staircase at the entrance plaza connects the levels and doubles as a viewing platform.
captions: Sectional axonometric through the tanks and the skywalk.
Sections of the four tanks: children's center, restaurant and cafe, climbing gym and service center.
Elevation of the skywalk across the site.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 半埋於地下的儲槽在綠色地景下開出明亮的空間，紅色的空中步道則在樹梢上環繞，並在四處落地。入口廣場的螺旋樓梯串連上下層，也是一處觀景平台。
captions: 穿過儲槽與空中步道的剖軸測圖。
四座儲槽的剖面：兒童中心、餐廳與咖啡館、攀岩館與服務中心。
橫跨基地的空中步道立面。

sections.heading: Tank Hsinchu - Opening a Closed Military Ground to Its Neighbourhood
sections.body: A former military site has long been closed to the public, while the area around it lacks open space and suffers from broken ecological links. The project sets out to turn it into a public, multifunctional park for sport and leisure that benefits the whole neighbourhood. Surveys of spatial qualities show that nearby residents and students have a clear need for open venues. Terrain studies find a T-shaped hollow, many trees worth keeping and four tanks on the site, all covered in soil. The four tanks are transformed into a children's activity centre, a restaurant and café, a climbing gym and a service centre. Studies of function, planting, sports zones and levels arrange running, walking, play and training areas around them. The half-buried tanks open into sunlit rooms beneath a green landscape. A red skywalk loops above the treetops and touches the ground in four places. A spiral staircase at the entrance plaza joins the levels and doubles as a viewing platform. A once forbidden ground finally becomes an oasis that everyone can approach.

zh-Hant.heading: 儲槽公園-讓封閉的軍事用地向鄰里敞開
zh-Hant.body: 一處長年不對外開放的舊軍事用地，周邊地區既缺乏開放空間，生態也呈現破碎的狀態。作品希望把它轉化為一座公共而多功能的運動與休閒公園，讓整個鄰里都能受益。空間屬性的調查顯示，附近的居民與學生對開放場地懷有明確的需求；地形研究則發現一處丁字形的凹地、許多值得保留的樹木，以及四座覆土的儲槽。這四座儲槽分別被轉化為兒童活動中心、餐廳與咖啡館、攀岩館與服務中心；機能、植栽、運動分區與高程的研究，則在它們周圍安排跑步、散步、遊戲與訓練的場地。半埋於地下的儲槽，在綠色地景之下開出明亮的空間，紅色的空中步道在樹梢之上環繞，並於四處落地。入口廣場的螺旋樓梯串連上下，也是一座觀景台。昔日的禁地，終於成為人人可以親近的綠洲。

pins.title: "New" Community Activity Center
pins.description:
A community center that reconnects neighbors through shared activities.

Architecture | Community center | Neighborhood relations | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 「新」社區活動中心
zh-Hant.description:
一座以共享活動重新連結鄰里的社區中心。

建築設計｜社區中心｜鄰里關係｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Section perspective showing activities inside and outside the center.
剖透視，呈現中心內外的活動。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many communities surround the site, yet neighborhood relationships have grown increasingly thin. Residents have some free time, but the activity spaces in the community are not enough for them to use it well.
captions: Links between residential areas, the study area and event venues.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地周邊有許多社區，鄰里關係卻日漸淡薄。居民雖然有一些空閒時間，社區裡的活動空間卻不足以讓他們好好運用。
captions: 住宅區、研究區與活動場地之間的連結。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A survey of residents' interests and favorite activity sites showed what children, students, commuters and the elderly each wanted to do. The activities were then combined and the size of each space was estimated.
captions: Strategy 1: block cutting and a matrix linking user groups to activities.
Strategy 2: preset layouts for yoga, hydrotherapy, gym, free, bookshop, music and KTV spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 透過調查居民的興趣與常去的活動地點，了解兒童、學生、通勤族與長者各自想做的事。接著把這些活動加以組合，並估算每個空間的大小。
captions: 策略一：量體切割，以及連結使用族群與活動的矩陣。
策略二：瑜伽、水療、健身、自由空間、書店、音樂與KTV空間的預設配置。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The building volume was pushed, pulled and cut to let in sunlight and open views between residents and students. A second strategy lets people check space information on their phones and other devices before they arrive.
captions: Form generation through pushing, cutting and opening sightlines.
Axonometric rendering of user groups and the devices they use.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 建築量體經過推、拉與切割，引入陽光，並在居民與學生之間打開視線。第二項策略讓人們在抵達前，就能透過手機等裝置查看空間資訊。
captions: 透過推拉、切割與開放視線的形體生成。
使用族群與其所用裝置的軸測渲染圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The center stacks a DIY exhibition hall, a coffee restaurant, resident activity areas and a square on stepped levels with a steel frame above a concrete base. A physical section model tested the scale of people's activities so that the spaces would be reasonable to use.
captions: Section nodes of the steel and concrete structure.
Physical section model with node and perspective models.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 活動中心在階梯式的樓層上疊合了DIY展覽廳、咖啡餐廳、居民活動區與廣場，以鋼構架在混凝土基座之上。實體剖面模型檢驗了人們活動的尺度，讓空間更合理好用。
captions: 鋼構與混凝土結構的剖面節點。
實體剖面模型，以及節點與透視模型。

sections.heading: New Community Activity Center - Rebuilding a Gathering Place for Distant Neighbours
sections.body: Many communities surround the site, yet the ties between neighbours have grown steadily thinner. Residents have some free time, but the community lacks enough activity space for that time to be well spent. The project begins with a survey of residents' interests and favourite places, setting out what children, students, commuters and older people each wish to do. These activities are then combined, and the size of each space is estimated. The building volume is pushed, pulled and cut to let in sunlight and to open views between residents and students. A second strategy lets people check information about the spaces on their phones and other devices before they arrive. The finished centre stacks a do-it-yourself exhibition hall, a coffee restaurant, resident activity areas and a square on stepped levels, with a light steel frame rising above a concrete base. A physical section model tests the scale of human activity so that the spaces are reasonable to use. Reasons to gather are found again one by one, and warmth slowly returns to the neighbourhood.

zh-Hant.heading: 新社區活動中心-為淡薄的鄰里重新搭起相聚之所
zh-Hant.body: 基地四周環繞著許多社區，鄰里之間的關係卻日漸淡薄；居民雖有空閒的時光，社區裡卻沒有足夠的活動空間可供善用。作品從一份調查開始，了解居民的興趣與常去的活動地點，釐清兒童、學生、通勤族與長者各自想做的事，再把這些活動加以組合，估算每一處空間的大小。建築量體經過推、拉與切割，引入陽光，也在居民與學生之間打開彼此的視線；另一項策略讓人們在抵達之前，就能透過手機等裝置查看空間的使用資訊。最終的活動中心在階梯式的樓層上，疊合自己動手的展覽廳、咖啡餐廳、居民活動區與廣場，鋼構架輕盈地立於混凝土基座之上。實體剖面模型檢驗了人們活動的尺度，讓空間合理而好用。相聚的理由被一一找回，鄰里的溫度也隨之回升。

pins.title: Natural Media Funeral Parlour
pins.description:
A funeral parlour where light, water, life and wind guide grief toward calm.

Architecture | Funeral parlour | Natural media | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然媒介殯儀館
zh-Hant.description:
一座以光、水、生命與風引導哀傷走向平靜的殯儀館。

建築設計｜殯儀館｜自然媒介｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Perspective section tracing how emotions change along the route through the building.
剖透視圖，追溯情緒沿著建築動線的轉變。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As life expectancy grows and land for burial shrinks, the city faces a tense shortage of places for funerals. The local demand for funeral buildings keeps rising, while traditional funerals offer few ways to comfort the people left behind.
captions: Site and district analysis: the resident, temple and path photos, waiting time, mortality rate and usable land.
Light and water: forms in the building, sun paths, rainfall and water speed.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 隨著平均壽命延長、可用於安葬的土地縮減，城市面臨喪葬空間緊張的處境。當地對殯葬建築的需求持續上升，而傳統喪禮卻少有方式能撫慰留下來的人。
captions: 基地與區域分析：住宅、寺廟與道路照片，以及等候時間、死亡率與可用土地。
光與水：建築中的形式、日照路徑、降雨與水流速度。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project studied four natural media on the site: light, water, life and wind. Sunshine, rainfall, wind speed and the surrounding landscape were analysed to see how each medium could shape people's emotions.
captions: From traditional to modern funerals: the lack of media, and the moods and emotions of the bereaved.
Life and wind: energy fields, landscape framing, mountain-valley breezes and sensory design.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案研究基地上的四種自然媒介：光、水、生命與風。透過分析日照、降雨、風速與周邊地景，了解每種媒介如何影響人的情緒。
captions: 從傳統到現代的喪禮：媒介的缺乏，以及喪親者的心情與情緒。
生命與風：能量場、地景取景、山谷風與感官設計。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Concept sketches brought in the infinity symbol to express the eternity of life, and the plan was shaped to follow the lake around the site and the sunlight. The surface was then studied for light channels, courtyards, a wind corridor and flowing water.
captions: Concept drawing linking the living and the departed through infinity symbols.
Form generation from the site, the lake edge and sunlight intensity.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 概念草圖引入無限符號，表達生命的永恆，平面則依循基地周邊的湖岸與日照塑形。接著研究建築表皮，安排光之通道、中庭、風廊與流動的水。
captions: 以無限符號連結生者與逝者的概念圖。
由基地、湖岸與日照強度推導的形體生成。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The flowing building guides visitors through reception, waiting, mourning and funeral spaces, each tuned by light, water, life and wind. Its outline and its reflection in the water together form the infinity symbol.
captions: Scene rendering: the building wraps around water, trees and the misty hills.
Form sequence from required area to a wind-shaped roof and light openings.
Underground plan of the service level.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 流動的建築引導來訪者依序經過接待、等候、追思與告別空間，每一處都以光、水、生命與風調和。建築輪廓與水中倒影共同構成無限符號。
captions: 場景渲染：建築環繞著水、樹木與雲霧中的山丘。
從需求面積到風塑屋頂與採光開口的形體序列。
服務層的地下平面圖。

sections.heading: Natural Media Funeral Parlour - Consoling the Living Through Light, Water, Wind and Life
sections.body: As people live longer and land for burial shrinks, the city faces a tense shortage of space for funerals. Demand for funeral buildings keeps rising, yet traditional ceremonies offer few ways to truly comfort those who are left behind. The project studies four natural media found on the site: light, water, life and wind. Sunshine, rainfall, wind speed and the surrounding landscape are analysed to understand how each medium can move human emotion. Concept sketches bring in the infinity symbol as a sign of the eternity of life. The plan is shaped by the lakeshore around the site and by the path of the sun, and the surface is studied closely for light channels, courtyards, a wind corridor and flowing water. The flowing building leads visitors in turn through reception, waiting, mourning and farewell spaces, each one tempered by light, water, life and wind. The outline of the building and its reflection in the water together draw the infinity symbol. Farewell becomes not only an ending, but a journey in which grief can slowly settle.

zh-Hant.heading: 自然媒介殯儀館-以光水風與生命撫慰生者
zh-Hant.body: 平均壽命延長，可供安葬的土地日益縮減，城市面臨喪葬空間緊張的處境；殯葬建築的需求持續上升，傳統的喪禮卻少有方式能真正撫慰留下來的人。作品研究基地上的四種自然媒介：光、水、生命與風，並分析日照、降雨、風速與周邊地景，理解每一種媒介如何牽動人的情緒。概念草圖引入無限的符號，象徵生命的永恆；平面則依循環繞基地的湖岸與日照而塑形，建築表皮再被細細推敲，安排光的通道、中庭、風廊與流動的水。流動的建築引領來訪者依序經過接待、等候、追思與告別的空間，每一處都由光、水、生命與風加以調和。建築的輪廓與水中的倒影，共同構成一個無限的符號；告別因此不只是終點，也是一段讓哀傷緩緩沉澱的旅程。

pins.title: Revive the Lijia Alley
pins.description:
A phased street renewal that brings green space and daily life back to a historic alley.

Changsha, China | Urban design | Street renewal | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重振 Lijia 巷
zh-Hant.description:
一項分期街道更新，為歷史巷弄帶回綠意與日常生活。

中國長沙｜都市設計｜街道更新｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Phase one: the renewed commercial stretch of the alley.
第一期：更新後的巷弄商業段。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Lijia Alley, next to the city center of Changsha, is one of the few historic streets left in the city, yet it is poorly protected. The growing city center has taken over outdoor space, the population is ageing, and many homes still follow an unreasonable layout from the 1950s.
captions: The alley seen from above, squeezed between the skyscrapers and the urban villages.
Space making keeps the main body of two- and three-storey buildings while adding new frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: Lijia 巷緊鄰長沙市中心，是城內少數留存的歷史街道之一，卻缺乏妥善保護。市中心擴張侵占了戶外空間，人口持續老化，許多住宅仍沿用1950年代不合理的格局。
captions: 從高處俯瞰的巷弄，夾在摩天大樓與城中村之間。
空間營造保留二層與三層建築的主體，並加入新的構架。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Data on unemployment, age and income showed that the alley lags behind both its district and the city. Site observation found many run-down two- and three-storey buildings that no longer suit daily life.
captions: Unemployment, street features and the history timeline of the alley.
Exploded view of routes for vehicles, pedestrians, residents and business, with building heights.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 失業率、年齡與收入的數據顯示，這條巷子落後於所在的區與整座城市。現地觀察則發現許多破舊的二、三層建築已不再適合日常居住。
captions: 失業率、街道特色與巷弄的歷史時間軸。
分解圖：車行、步行、居民與商業動線，以及建築高度。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: New frames add parks, stages, markets and planting spaces along the street without erasing the old buildings. The alley is then planned in three phases: a commercial phase near the business district, a living phase for residents and a green phase toward the river.
captions: Strategy: three phases for business, residents and greening along the alley.
Phase two: the living stretch with a stage, homes and local shops.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 新的構架沿街加入公園、舞台、市集與種植空間，同時保留舊建築。巷弄接著分為三期規劃：靠近商業區的商業期、為居民而設的生活期，以及朝向河岸的綠化期。
captions: 策略：沿巷弄分為商業、居民與綠化三個階段。
第二期：設有舞台、住宅與在地小店的生活段。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The renewed alley mixes shops, homes, a stage and small parks along a greener walking street. Each phase uses its own planting strategy with vines, osmanthus and camphor trees.
captions: Street renderings with the residents' own words about the renewed alley.
Phase three: the green stretch toward the river.
Planting strategies: vertical planting, plant frames and mixed blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 更新後的巷弄沿著更綠意的步行街，混合了商店、住宅、舞台與小公園。每一期各有種植策略，運用藤蔓、桂花與樟樹。
captions: 街道渲染圖，以及居民對更新後巷弄的心聲。
第三期：朝向河岸的綠化段。
種植策略：垂直綠化、植栽架與混合街區。

sections.heading: Revive the Lijia Alley - Growing Greenery Between Old Houses in Phases
sections.body: This alley lies next to the city centre and is one of the few historic streets left in the city, yet it has been poorly protected. The growing centre has taken over outdoor space, the population is ageing, and many homes still follow an awkward layout from half a century ago. Data on unemployment, age and income show the alley lagging behind both its district and the city as a whole. Observation on site finds many run-down low-rise buildings that no longer suit daily life. The design does not erase the old houses. Instead new frames add parks, stages, markets and planting spaces along the street. The alley is then planned in three phases: a commercial phase near the business district, a living phase for residents and a green phase reaching toward the river. The renewed walking street grows greener, with shops, homes, a stage and small parks woven together. Each phase follows its own planting strategy, as vines, osmanthus and camphor trees take root in turn. The memory of the old street is kept, and daily life unfolds again through gradual renewal.

zh-Hant.heading: 重振歷史巷弄-在舊屋之間分期長出綠意
zh-Hant.body: 這條巷弄緊鄰市中心，是城裡少數留存的歷史街道之一，卻缺乏妥善的保護。擴張的市中心侵占了戶外空間，人口持續老化，許多住宅仍沿用半世紀前並不合理的格局。失業率、年齡與收入的數據，顯示這條巷子落後於所在的城區乃至整座城市；現地觀察則發現大量破舊的低層建築，早已不適合日常起居。設計沒有抹去舊屋，而是以新的構架沿街加入公園、舞台、市集與種植空間。巷弄接著被分為三期：靠近商業區的商業期、為居民而設的生活期，以及朝向河岸的綠化期。更新後的步行街更添綠意，商店、住宅、舞台與小公園彼此交錯；每一期各有種植的策略，藤蔓、桂花與樟樹依序生長。老街的記憶得以留存，日常生活也在漸進的更新中重新舒展開來。

pins.title: Accelerate the City
pins.description:
A replaceable vertical complex that lets the city renew itself as fast as technology.

Guangzhou, China | Architecture | Future city | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 加速城市
zh-Hant.description:
一座可替換的垂直綜合體，讓城市能與科技同步自我更新。

中國廣州｜建築設計｜未來城市｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Traditional and accelerated skyscraper forms, with the form exploration of stacked functions.
傳統與加速摩天樓形式，以及堆疊機能的形體探索。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Behind the rapid growth of Guangzhou lie population, environmental and traffic problems, and fast construction has eaten into green space. Buildings change far more slowly than technology, so people still live and work in spaces designed for a past era.
captions: Industrial metabolism: how fast each sector changes, leading to a vertical future complex.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州快速發展的背後，存在人口、環境與交通問題，加速興建也蠶食了綠地。建築的演變遠比科技緩慢，人們仍在為過去時代設計的空間中生活與工作。
captions: 產業代謝：各產業的變化速度，進而推導出垂直的未來綜合體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project compared the pace of change in science, transport, commerce, finance and building renewal. It proposed a super complex that absorbs many building types and grows upward, so the ground can return to green space.
captions: Theoretical illustration of the complex growing upward above a green ground floor and transport lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案比較科技、交通、商業、金融與建築更新的變化速度。進而提出吸納多種建築類型、向上生長的超級綜合體，讓地面得以回歸綠地。
captions: 理論圖解：綜合體在綠色地面層與交通路線之上向上生長。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The tower is built from a core tube with stacked rings of living space, gears for kinetic energy and fan blades for wind energy. Replaceable units can be lifted, rotated and swapped by cranes, robotic arms and drones as the needs of the city change.
captions: Detailed structure of the core tube, rings and gears, with phases of uplift and replacement.
Drone transport, robotic arms, the space update system and rail transport.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塔樓由核心筒構成，疊加居住空間環、動能齒輪與風能扇葉。可替換單元能隨城市需求改變，由吊車、機械手臂與無人機吊升、旋轉與更換。
captions: 核心筒、圓環與齒輪的細部構造，以及吊升與更換的階段。
無人機運輸、機械手臂、空間更新系統與軌道運輸。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A physical model shows how the rings turn around the spindle to adjust position, view and light. The model makes the idea of a building that renews itself easier to read than computer drawings alone.
captions: Model sequence: before, rotating and after.
Physical model of the rings and gears, with a node detail.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 實體模型展示圓環如何繞著主軸轉動，以調整位置、視野與採光。模型讓這座自我更新的建築構想，比單靠電腦圖面更容易理解。
captions: 模型序列：轉動前、轉動中與轉動後。
圓環與齒輪的實體模型，以及節點細部。

sections.heading: Accelerate the City - A Super Tower That Renews Itself
sections.body: Behind the rapid growth of a city lie pressures of population, environment and traffic, and hurried construction has eaten into its green space bit by bit. Buildings change far more slowly than technology, so people still live and work in spaces designed for an earlier era. The project compares the pace of change in science, transport, commerce, finance and building renewal. From this it proposes a super complex that absorbs many building types and grows upward, so that the ground can be returned to green space. The tower turns on a core tube, stacking rings of living space, gears that gather kinetic energy and blades that capture the wind. Replaceable units can be lifted, rotated and swapped by cranes, robotic arms and drones as the needs of the city shift. A physical model shows how the rings turn around the spindle to adjust position, view and light. It makes the idea of a self-renewing building easier to grasp than computer drawings alone. Architecture is no longer still here, but breathes in step with its time.

zh-Hant.heading: 加速城市-一座能自我更新的超級塔樓
zh-Hant.body: 一座城市的快速成長，背後隱藏著人口、環境與交通的壓力，急促的興建也一點一滴蠶食了綠地。建築演變的速度遠遠落後於科技，人們至今仍在為過去時代設計的空間裡生活與工作。作品比較了科學、交通、商業、金融與建築更新各自的變化節奏，進而提出一座超級綜合體：它吸納多種建築類型，向上生長，讓地面重新歸還給綠地。塔樓以核心筒為軸，疊加起居住空間的環、轉換動能的齒輪與擷取風能的扇葉；可替換的單元能隨城市需求改變，由吊車、機械手臂與無人機吊升、旋轉與更換。實體模型展示圓環如何繞著主軸轉動，調整位置、視野與採光，讓一座自我更新的建築，比單憑電腦圖面更容易被理解。建築由此不再靜止，而是與時代同步呼吸。

pins.title: The Artistic Rebirth of the Harbor
pins.description:
Art is woven into a working port so that an old industrial area can regain its vitality.

Lyon, France | Urban renewal | 163.5 ha | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 港口的藝術重生
zh-Hant.description:
將藝術織入運作中的港口，讓舊工業區重獲活力。

法國里昂｜都市更新｜163.5 公頃｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The renovated factory facade, with slender vertical fins along the port.
改造後的工廠立面，沿港口排列細長的垂直鰭片。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Old industrial areas built on the edge of western cities have gradually been surrounded by new blocks and become part of the city. Port de Lyon at the southern end of Lyon once flourished, but as the city grew around it, its industrial development was held back.
captions: Aerial view of the port, with the warehouse, sheds and tanks chosen for renovation.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 西方城市邊緣興建的舊工業區，逐漸被新街區包圍，成為城市的一部分。位於里昂南端的里昂港曾經繁榮，但城市在周圍擴張後，其工業發展受到阻礙。
captions: 港區鳥瞰，標示選定改造的倉庫、棚架與儲槽。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project studied the port's existing production chain and the gap left by the lack of art spaces in the south of the city. It kept the industrial character of the site and inserted exhibition, studio, business and service functions into the existing buildings.
captions: Operation diagrams: art packaging is added to the original production line.
Scheme generation from site factors, with the resulting master plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案研究港口既有的生產鏈，以及城市南部缺乏藝術空間的空缺。設計保留基地的工業特色，並在既有建築中植入展覽、工作室、商業與服務機能。
captions: 運作圖解：在原有生產線中加入藝術包裝環節。
從基地要素推導的方案生成，以及最終總平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In the factory, artist studios join the production line through an overpass and a light freight track. The original steel frame is kept, while balconies and railings strengthen the relationship between inside and outside.
captions: Factory design: roof, frame, living floors, art studio and transport layers.
Long section through the exhibition, office, packaging line and storage.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在工廠中，藝術家工作室透過天橋與輕型貨運軌道接入生產線。原有鋼構架被保留，陽台與欄杆則加強了室內外的關係。
captions: 工廠設計：屋頂、構架、居住樓層、藝術工作室與運輸層。
貫穿展覽、辦公、包裝生產線與倉儲的長剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Over time, artists settle in the port and more people come for leisure, work and living. The port is expected to become an art centre and a new symbol of Lyon.
captions: Diversification in time: workers, artists and the public gradually share the port.
Axonometric drawing of the renewed port and its streets.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 隨著時間推移，藝術家進駐港口，更多人前來休閒、工作與生活。港口可望成為一座藝術中心，以及里昂的新象徵。
captions: 隨時間多元化：工人、藝術家與大眾逐漸共享港口。
更新後港區與街道的軸測圖。

sections.heading: The Artistic Rebirth of the Harbor - Joining Studios to the Production Line
sections.body: Industrial areas once built on the edges of western cities have slowly been surrounded by new blocks and drawn into the city itself. This harbour once flourished, yet as the city grew around it, its industry was held back. The project studies the existing production chain of the port and notes the gap left by the lack of art spaces in the south of the city. The design therefore keeps the industrial character of the site and inserts exhibition, studio, business and service functions into the existing buildings. Inside the factory, artist studios join the production line through an overpass and a light freight track. The original steel frame is kept, while new balconies and railings bring inside and outside into closer relation. Over time artists settle in, and more and more people arrive for leisure, work and daily life. The port is expected to become an art centre and a new symbol for the city. Production and creation run side by side on the same ground, and the old industrial memory gains a new life.

zh-Hant.heading: 港口的藝術重生-讓工作室接上生產線
zh-Hant.body: 昔日建在西方城市邊緣的工業區，逐漸被新的街區包圍，成為城市的一部分。這座港口曾經繁榮，城市在四周擴張之後，工業的發展卻受到了阻礙。作品研究港口既有的生產鏈，也注意到城市南部缺乏藝術空間的空白；設計因此保留基地的工業特質，把展覽、工作室、商業與服務機能植入既有的建築之中。在工廠裡，藝術家的工作室透過天橋與輕型貨運軌道，直接接上生產線；原有的鋼構架被保留下來，新增的陽台與欄杆則拉近了室內與室外的關係。隨著時間推移，藝術家陸續進駐，越來越多人前來休閒、工作與生活。港口可望成為一座藝術中心與城市的新象徵，生產與創作在同一片場域中並肩運轉，舊的工業記憶也因此獲得新的生命。

pins.title: Typological Exploration
pins.description:
A new university campus built from a meta-language drawn from local vernacular buildings.

Kunming, China | Urban design | University campus | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 類型學探索
zh-Hant.description:
以在地傳統民居提煉的後設語言，構築一座新的大學校園。

中國昆明｜都市設計｜大學校園｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A section through campus life, with drawn students meeting across the floors.
穿越校園生活的剖面，以手繪學生在各樓層間相遇。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As college enrolment grows year by year, universities in China are expanding and the old campus can no longer meet the needs of a new one. This graduation project designed the unbuilt north campus of a university in Kunming, Yunnan.
captions: Background: national and provincial strategies and the trend of interdisciplinary work.
Concept analysis of the site location and its surroundings.
Extracting the type from three local vernacular buildings, then combining basic prototypes into an object.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 隨著大學招生逐年增加，中國各地大學正在擴建，舊校區已無法滿足新校區的需求。本畢業設計以雲南昆明一所大學尚未開發的北校區為對象。
captions: 背景：國家與省級策略，以及跨學科發展的趨勢。
基地位置與周邊環境的概念分析。
從三種在地傳統民居中提取類型，再將基本原型組合成單體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Typology describes a group of objects that share the same formal structure. The project drew a meta-language from local vernacular buildings, so that the regional memory could carry on in the new campus.
captions: Quota distribution of the functional areas based on student numbers.
Meta-language design, unit module deformation, and the library and dormitory built from the modules.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 類型學描述具有相同形式結構的一組物件。本案從在地傳統民居中提煉出一套後設語言，讓地域記憶得以延續到新校區。
captions: 依學生人數推算各功能區的配額分布。
後設語言設計、單元模組變形，以及由模組組成的圖書館與宿舍。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Teaching, research and living spaces were sized from a quota study of each discipline. The disciplines were set as islands around a central library to encourage exchange between them.
captions: Strategy and concept: interdisciplinarity, typology, landscape and participation.
Strategy, concept, master plan and axonometric view of the new campus.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 教學、研究與居住空間的規模，依各學科的配額研究而定。各學科被安排成圍繞中央圖書館的島嶼，以促進彼此交流。
captions: 策略與概念：跨學科、建築類型、地景與參與。
新校區的策略、概念、總平面與軸測圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The library section shows how the courtyard type stacks into reading rooms and shared terraces. The campus offers a way to renew and expand a university while keeping its regional character.
captions: Library section with reading rooms and terraces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 圖書館剖面呈現合院類型如何疊合成閱覽室與共享露台。這座校園提供了一種在延續地域特色的同時，更新與擴建大學的方式。
captions: 圖書館剖面，包含閱覽室與露台。

sections.heading: Typological Exploration - Carrying Regional Memory Into a New Campus
sections.body: University enrolment grows year after year, campuses everywhere are expanding, and old grounds can no longer meet the new demand. This graduation project takes up the unbuilt north campus of one university and asks how a new campus might grow without breaking from the past of its land. Typology describes a group of objects that share the same formal structure. The student drew a meta-language out of local vernacular houses so that regional memory could live on in the new campus. Teaching, research and living spaces were sized through a quota study of each discipline. The disciplines were then placed as islands around a central library to encourage exchange among them. The library section shows how the courtyard type stacks up into reading rooms and shared terraces. Expansion here no longer means erasure. It becomes an act of translation, and the campus offers a path by which a university can renew and grow while keeping the character of its own ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 類型學探索-讓地域記憶延續到新校園
zh-Hant.body: 大學招生逐年增加，各地校園紛紛擴建，舊有校區已無法回應新的需求。這份畢業設計以一所大學尚未開發的北校區為對象，探問一座全新的校園，如何不與土地的過去斷裂？類型學描述的是一組共享相同形式結構的物件；學生從在地的傳統民居中提煉出一套後設語言，讓地域的記憶能在新校園裡延續。教學、研究與居住空間的規模，依各學科的配額研究而定；各學科被安排為一座座島嶼，環繞著中央的圖書館，鼓勵彼此之間的交流。圖書館的剖面呈現合院的類型如何層層疊合，化為閱覽室與共享露台。擴建不再意味著抹去，而是一種轉譯；這座校園提出了一條路徑，讓大學在更新與成長之際，仍保有屬於自身土地的性格。

pins.title: Village Paradise in the City
pins.description:
Activity platforms lifted into the air turn a village beside a new overpass into a paradise for its residents.

Chuxiong, China | Urban village renewal | 1.2 ha | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城中村樂園
zh-Hant.description:
抬升至空中的活動平台，讓新高架橋旁的村落成為居民的樂園。

中國楚雄｜城中村更新｜1.2 公頃｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial view of the village, with the new overpass curving past its edge.
村落鳥瞰，新建高架橋沿其邊緣彎曲而過。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In Chinese cities, many villages are surrounded by urban construction and are often ignored as the city develops. A viaduct built high above this village in Chuxiong, Yunnan brings heavy traffic noise and pollution to its residents.
captions: Location: the village in the city, with the overpass being built in front of it.
Usage demand: user groups, main activities and the spaces they need.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在中國城市中，許多村落被城市建設包圍，在發展過程中常被忽視。一座高架橋從雲南楚雄這座村落上方高高跨過，為居民帶來嚴重的交通噪音與污染。
captions: 區位：城市中的村落，以及正在村前興建的高架橋。
使用需求：使用族群、主要活動與所需空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Most young people work far away, so most residents are elderly people and children, and the village lacks public space and facilities. The plan answers the traffic and parking problems and the missing public space, turning the area into a place for many activities.
captions: Key findings: traffic noise and the lack of activity space, facilities and planning.
Design concept: an ecological barrier, new green space and an overhead ground.
Platform strategy: materials and activities combined along the platform.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 多數年輕人在外地工作，居民多為老人與兒童，村內缺乏公共空間與設施。規劃回應交通、停車與公共空間不足的問題，將此地轉化為容納多種活動的場所。
captions: 主要發現：交通噪音，以及活動空間、設施與規劃的缺乏。
設計概念：生態屏障、新增綠地與架空地面。
平台策略：沿平台組合材料與活動。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Woods are planted along the overpass as an ecological barrier, and activity platforms are lifted into the air to save the scarce ground for vegetable plots. Corridors and stairs link the platforms so residents can reach each activity space easily.
captions: Column forest, spatial interaction, continuous space and band attachment.
Platform composition: furniture, building, gravel, platform and farm layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 沿高架橋種植樹林作為生態屏障，並將活動平台抬升至空中，把稀缺的地面留給菜地。廊道與樓梯串連各平台，讓居民能輕鬆抵達每個活動空間。
captions: 柱林、空間互動、連續空間與帶狀附著。
平台構成：家具、建築、礫石、平台與農地等層次。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The master plan brings together a forest park, a village square, a sports park, a cooperative farm and the activity platform. The village, its architecture and its landscape become a lively sky paradise for the residents.
captions: Master plan of the renewed village.
Long section across the village and its platforms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 總平面整合森林遊樂園、村落廣場、運動公園、合作農場與活動平台。村落、建築與地景共同成為屬於居民的活力空中樂園。
captions: 更新後村落的總平面。
橫跨村落與平台的長剖面。

sections.heading: Village Paradise in the City - Lifting a Sky Garden Beneath the Viaduct
sections.body: As cities spread outward they surround many villages, which are often forgotten as development moves on. A viaduct passes high above this village, bringing heavy traffic noise and pollution to the people below. Most young people work far away, so the residents are mainly elderly people and children, and the village has little public space or facilities. The plan begins from the problems of traffic, parking and missing public space, hoping to make room for many kinds of activity. A belt of woodland planted along the overpass forms an ecological barrier. Activity platforms are lifted into the air so that the scarce ground can be kept for vegetable plots. Corridors and stairs then tie the platforms together, letting residents reach each activity space with ease. The master plan joins a forest park, a village square, a sports park, a cooperative farm and the raised platforms, so that village, architecture and landscape merge into one. A corner once wrapped in noise is transformed into a lively paradise in the sky, belonging to those who live there every day.

zh-Hant.heading: 城中村樂園-在高架橋下抬升一片空中天地
zh-Hant.body: 城市擴張的腳步包圍了許多村落，它們卻常在發展中被遺忘。一座高架橋從這座村落上方高高跨過，為居民帶來沉重的車聲與污染；年輕人多在遠方工作，留下的多是老人與孩子，村裡也缺少公共空間與設施。規劃從交通、停車與公共空間的不足著手，希望讓這裡容納更多樣的活動。沿著高架橋種下的林帶，成為一道生態屏障；活動平台被抬升至半空，把稀缺的地面留給菜園，廊道與樓梯再把各個平台串連起來，讓居民輕鬆抵達每一處活動空間。總體規劃整合森林遊樂園、村落廣場、運動公園、合作農場與空中平台，村落、建築與地景彼此交融。被噪音籠罩的角落，因此轉化為一座生氣勃勃的空中樂園，屬於每天在此生活的人。

pins.title: Urban Dwelling: Residing in the City
pins.description:
Six light parasite structures fill the gaps of a post-war London housing estate with spaces for artists and visitors.

London, UK | Parasitic architecture | Artist spaces | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市棲居：寄居於城
zh-Hant.description:
六座輕量寄生結構填補倫敦戰後住宅社區的縫隙，為藝術家與訪客提供空間。

英國倫敦｜寄生建築｜藝術家空間｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Site axonometric of the post-war housing estate and its surroundings.
戰後住宅社區及其周邊的基地軸測圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The Golden Lane Estate is a 1950s council housing complex in the City of London, built on land devastated by wartime bombing. Business had become the main use of land in the City, and the project looks for the negative urban space left between its buildings.
captions: Site analysis: the history of the area and its post-war housing estate.
Six spaces for artists and visitors: gallery, square, gardens, office, studio and park.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: Golden Lane Estate 是倫敦金融城一座建於 1950 年代的公共住宅，坐落在戰時遭轟炸摧毀的土地上。商業已成為金融城的主要用地，本案尋找建築之間被遺留的負空間。
captions: 基地分析：區域的歷史及其戰後住宅區。
為藝術家與訪客設計的六個空間：藝廊、廣場、花園、辦公室、工作室與公園。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Parasitic architecture attaches to an existing larger structure to answer high rents and the lack of space in big cities. It is cheap to build, uses space efficiently and stays socially inclusive, so it suits the gaps of this estate.
captions: Users analysis: the artists, curators and makers behind an exhibition.
Why designers create parasite architecture, and the workshop, shop, gallery and rooftop bar.
Floating gallery: workshop, terrace shop, gallery and rooftop bar along one section.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 寄生建築依附於既有的大型結構，回應大城市高租金與空間不足的問題。它造價低、空間利用有效率且具社會包容性，適合填補這座社區的縫隙。
captions: 使用者分析：展覽背後的藝術家、策展人與製作者。
設計師為何創造寄生建築，以及工作坊、商店、藝廊與屋頂酒吧。
漂浮藝廊：工作坊、露台商店、藝廊與屋頂酒吧沿同一剖面展開。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: For the air studio, the centre point between the existing buildings fixes the location, and Voronoi geometry is generated within the defined space. The dancing office uses a spring-based form-finding script to balance the mesh between its connection points.
captions: Air studio section, hung between two existing blocks.
Air studio plan and the parametric script that shapes it.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 空中工作室以既有建築之間的中心點決定位置，並在限定空間內生成 Voronoi 幾何。舞動辦公室以彈簧力學的找形腳本，平衡網格與各連接點之間的關係。
captions: 懸掛於兩棟既有建築之間的空中工作室剖面。
空中工作室平面與塑造其形體的參數化腳本。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Six light structures for studios, exhibitions, offices, gardens and a bar connect to the ground, open to the sky and lean on existing walls. They show that there is no need to build heavily to bring artists back into the city.
captions: Dancing office section with its flowing shell.
Dancing office plan between the existing buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 六座輕量結構容納工作室、展覽、辦公、花園與酒吧，連接地面、向天空開放並倚靠既有牆面。它們說明不必大興土木，也能讓藝術家重回城市。
captions: 具流動外殼的舞動辦公室剖面。
位於既有建築之間的舞動辦公室平面。

sections.heading: Urban Dwelling - Light Structures Living in the Gaps Between Buildings
sections.body: A post-war council housing estate stands on land once devastated by bombing, and business districts have long since closed in around it. The project searches the spaces between its buildings for the negative urban space that was left behind. Parasitic architecture attaches itself to an existing larger structure, answering high rents and the shortage of room in big cities. It is cheap to build, uses ground efficiently and remains socially inclusive, which suits the gaps of this estate well. For the air studio, the centre point between existing buildings fixes the location, and Voronoi geometry is generated within the defined space. The dancing office uses a spring-based form-finding script to balance its mesh between the connection points. In the end six light structures hold studios, exhibitions, offices, gardens and a bar. They touch the ground, open toward the sky and lean on the walls that are already there. Artists can return to the city without heavy construction, and the overlooked gaps of the city become shelters for a new way of living.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市棲居-寄生於建築縫隙的輕盈結構
zh-Hant.body: 一座建於戰後廢墟之上的公共住宅社區，四周早已被商業用地包圍；作品在建築與建築之間，尋找那些被遺留下來的負空間。寄生建築依附於既有的大型結構，回應大城市高昂的租金與空間的匱乏；它造價低廉、用地有效率，也保有社會的包容性，正適合填補這座社區的縫隙。空中工作室以既有建築之間的中心點決定位置，在限定的範圍內生成泰森多邊形的幾何；舞動辦公室則借助模擬彈簧的找形腳本，在各個連接點之間求得網格的平衡。最終，六座輕量的結構容納工作室、展覽、辦公、花園與酒吧，它們觸及地面、向天空敞開，並倚靠著既有的牆面。不必大興土木，藝術家也能重新回到城市，城市的縫隙由此成為新生活的棲身之所。

pins.title: Polyver: Vector Exploration of Polyline
pins.description:
Hand-made timber nodes without nails or glue grow from a polyline into a pedestrian bridge in Hyde Park.

London, UK | Timber structure | Pedestrian bridge | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Polyver：折線的向量探索
zh-Hant.description:
不用釘子或膠的手作木節點，從一條折線發展成海德公園裡的人行橋。

英國倫敦｜木構造｜人行橋｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A structure grown from polylines, the starting point of the study.
由折線生長而成的結構，是這項研究的起點。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explores how a simple polyline can become a structure, first as a built timber object and then as architecture. It asks how pieces can hold together without nails, ropes or glue.
captions: Site analysis of the park, its galleries and points of attraction.
Material chart comparing fabrication, strength, workability and cost.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案探索簡單的折線如何成為結構，先做成實體木構物件，再發展為建築。它追問構件如何在不用釘子、繩索或膠的情況下彼此固定。
captions: 公園、藝廊與周邊景點的基地分析。
比較加工方式、強度、可加工性與成本的材料圖表。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Materials and wood types are compared for strength, workability and cost, and eucalyptus and camphor wood are chosen. The joint follows the traditional Chinese interlocking burr puzzle, which stands up through the connection of its own parts.
captions: Node 2 making: cutting, drilling and assembling the timber pieces by hand.
Node decomposition and the two connection ways: cuboid and triangular insertion.
Node 1 made by hand in nine steps.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案比較各種材料與木種的強度、可加工性與成本，最後選用尤加利木與樟木。節點借鑑中國傳統的榫卯鎖，僅靠構件彼此咬合便能自立。
captions: 節點二製作：以手工裁切、鑽孔並組裝木構件。
節點拆解與兩種接合方式：方形插接與三角插接。
以九個步驟手工製作節點一。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wood is cut to three lengths and drilled with cube and triangle holes about 2.5 cm deep, so each node grips the sticks without glue. The parts close into one loop, so the nodes cannot fall loose.
captions: The finished timber model, indoors and outdoors.
3D model of the same node system.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木料裁成三種長度，並鑽出約 2.5 公分深的方形與三角形孔，讓節點不用膠也能卡住木桿。所有構件組成一個封閉迴圈，使節點不會鬆脫。
captions: 完成的木構模型，室內與戶外。
同一節點系統的 3D 模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the second part the polyline system becomes a pedestrian bridge over a lake in Hyde Park, London. The bridge keeps a distance from the nearby galleries so walkers can see them in full, and it doubles as a rest area and a scenic spot.
captions: Aerial render of the bridge over the lake.
Renders of the polyline pedestrian bridge.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第二部分將折線系統發展為倫敦海德公園湖上的一座人行橋。橋與鄰近藝廊保持距離，讓行人能看見其全貌，同時也是休憩區與觀景點。
captions: 橫跨湖面的橋梁鳥瞰渲染圖。
折線人行橋的渲染圖。

sections.heading: Polyver - A Timber Bridge That Stands Without Nails or Glue
sections.body: Can a simple polyline become a structure? The project first makes it into a physical timber object and then carries it toward the scale of architecture. Along the way it asks how pieces might hold together without nails, ropes or glue. Materials and wood types are compared for strength, workability and cost, and eucalyptus and camphor are chosen. The joint borrows from the traditional interlocking burr puzzle, which stands up only through the grip of its own parts. Timber is cut to three lengths and drilled with square and triangular holes about two and a half centimetres deep, so each node holds its sticks firmly without any glue. All the parts finally close into a single loop, leaving the nodes no way to fall loose. In the second stage the polyline system becomes a footbridge across a lake in a park. It keeps its distance from nearby galleries so walkers can see them whole, and it doubles as a place to rest and take in the view. An old wisdom of interlocking is reinterpreted, and the strength of the structure comes from the trust of each piece in the next.

zh-Hant.heading: 折線的向量-不靠釘膠自立的木構橋
zh-Hant.body: 一條簡單的折線，能否成為結構？作品先把它做成一件實體的木構物件，再將它推向建築的尺度，並追問構件如何在沒有釘子、繩索與膠的情況下彼此固定。各種材料與木種在強度、可加工性與成本上被逐一比較，最後選定尤加利木與樟木；節點借鑑傳統的榫卯鎖，僅憑構件之間的咬合便能自立。木料被裁成三種長度，鑽出約兩公分半深的方孔與三角孔，讓每個節點不需膠合也能緊緊握住木桿；所有構件最終閉合成一個迴圈，節點因此無從鬆脫。第二階段，這套折線系統化為一座跨越公園湖面的人行橋，刻意與鄰近藝廊保持距離，讓行人得以望見其全貌，橋身同時也是休憩與觀景之處。古老的咬合智慧在此被重新演繹，結構的力量來自構件彼此的信任。

pins.title: Guangdong Cultural Centre
pins.description:
A truss-framed cultural centre on a hillside gives travellers on a mountain highway a place to rest, read and look at the view.

Guangdong, China | Cultural centre | Truss structure | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 廣東文化中心
zh-Hant.description:
以桁架構成的山坡文化中心，讓山區公路上的旅客有地方休息、閱讀與看風景。

中國廣東｜文化中心｜桁架結構｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The cultural centre stretched across a hillside in the mountains.
橫跨山坡的文化中心。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: This cultural centre sits in a mountainous village in Guangdong, close to a highway, where hills rise in the middle of the site. It should serve local culture and also give drivers and tourists a place to rest and read.
captions: Form steps: the figure-eight shape, the added triangles and the extra levels.
Ground floor plan with the reading room, court and exhibition.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座文化中心位於廣東山區的村落，靠近高速公路，基地中央是起伏的丘陵。它既要承載在地文化，也要讓駕車旅客有地方休息與閱讀。
captions: 形體步驟：「8」字形、增加的三角形與加高的樓層。
地面層平面，含閱覽室、庭院與展覽空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The initial form comes from the number eight, with the two rectangles at its ends as the main entrances. Triangular rest areas are added beside the shape to respond better to the site.
captions: First and second floor plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 最初的形體來自數字「8」，兩端的矩形是主要入口。形體兩側再加入三角形休憩區，更好地回應基地。
captions: 二樓與三樓平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: More levels are added above, and one main entrance extends down into a court on the basement level. A truss of rigid triangles carries the overhangs and spans, while columns support the reading space.
captions: The truss structure lifts the building over the slope.
Section through the levels, with courtyard and semi-outdoor spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 上方再加入更多樓層，其中一個主入口向下延伸為地下層的庭院。由剛性三角形組成的桁架承載懸挑與跨距，閱讀空間則以柱子支撐。
captions: 桁架結構讓建築跨越坡地。
穿越各層的剖面，含庭院與半戶外空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The building offers exhibition spaces, reading lounges and a small court along a route that follows the hills. Its open floors frame views of the mountains for visitors who stop on their journey.
captions: Axonometric drawing on the terrain and interior views.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 建築沿著順應丘陵的動線，提供展覽空間、閱讀休息區與一座小庭院。開放的樓層為途中停留的旅客框出山景。
captions: 地形上的軸測圖與室內視角。

sections.heading: Mountain Village Cultural Centre - A Pause Between the Hills and the Highway
sections.body: A village sits among the mountains beside a highway, and a stretch of rolling hills rises in the middle of its site. The cultural centre carries two hopes at once. It should hold local culture, and it should also give passing drivers and travellers a place to stop, rest and read. The first form is drawn from the number eight, with the rectangles at its two ends serving as the main entrances. Triangular rest areas are then added along its sides so that the shape settles more closely into the land. More floors gather above, and one entrance reaches downward to become a court on the basement level. A truss of rigid triangles carries the overhangs and spans, while columns hold up the reading space. The building unfolds along a route that follows the hills, linking exhibition rooms, reading lounges and a small court. Its open floors frame the distant mountains again and again. A hurried journey is gently slowed here, and the highway and the village meet through a page of a book and a window onto the hills.

zh-Hant.heading: 山村文化中心-在丘陵與公路之間停駐
zh-Hant.body: 群山之間的一座村落，緊鄰高速公路，基地中央隆起一片起伏的丘陵。這座文化中心肩負兩種期待：既要承載在地的文化，也要讓途經的駕駛與旅人有一處歇腳、閱讀的地方。最初的形體取自數字「8」，兩端的矩形成為主要入口，兩側再添上三角形的休憩區，讓形體更貼合基地的起伏。上方的樓層逐漸增加，其中一個入口向下延伸，化為地下層的一座庭院；由剛性三角形構成的桁架承托懸挑與跨距，閱讀空間則由柱列穩穩撐起。建築沿著順應丘陵的動線展開，串起展覽空間、閱讀休息區與小小的庭院，開放的樓層一再為旅人框出遠山。匆匆的旅途在此被輕輕放慢，公路與山村也在一頁書、一扇窗之間，找到彼此相遇的方式。

pins.title: Santo Domingo School of Music
pins.description:
A small site in a crowded capital becomes a vertical school city with open spaces carved into its red blocks.

Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic | School | Vertical campus | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聖多明哥音樂學校
zh-Hant.description:
擁擠首都中的小基地，化為在紅色量體中挖出開放空間的垂直校園城市。

多明尼加聖多明哥｜學校｜垂直校園｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The school tower and its low red wings around the playground.
學校高塔與環繞操場的低矮紅色側翼。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Santo Domingo is a dense seaside capital that lacks efficient public facilities, and the site for this music school is small. The school should evoke students' interest in learning and keep them engaged in school life.
captions: Site analysis: the city grid, transport and beach, and the site location.
Social structure: the dense, overlapping structures of the old city.
Open spaces carved into the dense red blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 聖多明哥是一座密集的濱海首都，缺乏有效率的公共設施，而這所音樂學校的基地也很小。學校需要激發學生的學習興趣，並讓他們持續投入校園生活。
captions: 基地分析：城市街廓、交通與海灘，以及基地位置。
社會結構：老城區密集而交疊的結構。
在密集紅色量體中挖出的開放空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The study reads the city's culture of crowdedness, where dense, layered structures leave creative gaps between walls and masses. Three questions guide the design: how to make the best campus on a small site, how to serve teenage students and how to answer the climate.
captions: First floor plan with the playground at the centre.
Site axonometric and the life, study and exhibition programme blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究解讀這座城市的「擁擠文化」，層層堆疊的密集結構在牆與量體之間留下富創意的縫隙。設計由三個問題引導：如何在小基地上創造最好的校園、如何服務青少年學生，以及如何回應氣候。
captions: 以操場為中心的二樓平面。
基地軸測圖，以及生活、學習與展覽的機能量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Because the site is limited but the allowed floor area is generous, the school stacks its rooms into a small vertical school city. Open spaces inside the building create organised space for study, life and exhibition.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 由於基地有限但容積率寬裕，學校將教室堆疊成一座小型的「垂直校園城市」。建築內部的開放空間，為學習、生活與展覽創造有秩序的空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A tall tower rises beside low red wings that hold halls and courts, linked by stairs and terraces. The long section shows how study, life and performance stack into one compact campus.
captions: Long section through the tower and the performance spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 高塔矗立在容納大廳與庭院的低矮紅色側翼旁，以樓梯與露台相連。長剖面呈現學習、生活與演出如何疊合成一座緊湊的校園。
captions: 穿越高塔與演出空間的長剖面。

sections.heading: Santo Domingo School of Music - Stacking a City of Music on a Small Site
sections.body: This dense seaside capital lacks efficient public facilities, and the site for the music school is small. The school must spark students' interest in learning and keep them engaged in the life of the campus. The study reads the culture of crowdedness found across the city, where dense and layered structures leave creative gaps between walls and masses. Three questions guide the design: how to make the best possible campus on a small site, how to serve teenage students and how to respond to the climate. Because the site is limited while the permitted floor area is generous, the school stacks its rooms upward into a small vertical city of learning. Open spaces inside the building create organised places for study, daily life and exhibition. A tall tower rises beside low red wings that hold halls and courts, all linked by stairs and terraces. The long section shows how study, life and performance stack into one compact campus. Crowdedness is transformed into energy here, and melodies echo from one floor to the next.

zh-Hant.heading: 聖多明哥音樂學校-在小基地上疊起一座音樂之城
zh-Hant.body: 這座濱海首都人口稠密，缺乏有效率的公共設施，音樂學校的基地也相當狹小；學校需要喚起學生的學習興趣，並讓學生持續投入校園生活。研究閱讀城市中的擁擠文化，密集而層疊的結構，在牆體與量體之間留下富有創意的縫隙。三個問題引導著設計：如何在小基地上打造最好的校園、如何服務青少年學生，以及如何回應氣候。由於基地有限，容許的樓地板面積卻相當充裕，學校把各種房間向上堆疊，形成一座小型的垂直校園城市；建築內部的開放空間，為學習、生活與展演組織出有序的場所。一座高塔矗立在低矮的紅色翼樓旁，翼樓容納禮堂與球場，以樓梯與露台相互連接；長剖面呈現學習、生活與表演如何疊合為一座緊湊的校園。擁擠在此被轉化為活力，旋律也在層層樓板之間迴盪。

pins.title: Plants and Architecture in Symbiosis
pins.description:
Boundary models are divided and recombined into a timber building that weaves between existing trees.

Taipei, Taiwan | Architecture | Individual project | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 植物與建築的共生
zh-Hant.description:
邊界模型經拆解與重組，成為一座穿梭於既有樹木之間的木構建築。

台灣台北｜建築｜個人專案｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Timber volumes rising between the existing trees.
在既有樹木之間升起的木構量體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project explores how plants and architecture can live together in daily life. It asks how a building can relate to the surrounding buildings and existing plants through its boundaries.
captions: Site and behaviour analysis: plants around the building, the boundary studies and how different people use the space.
Sections of the open boundary, light edge and selected penetration.
Drawing of different plants living in harmony above and below ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個專案探討植物與建築如何在日常生活中共生。它追問建築如何透過自身的邊界，與周邊建築及既有植物建立關係。
captions: 基地與行為分析：建築周邊的植物、邊界研究，以及不同人群如何使用空間。
開放邊界、輕盈邊緣與選擇性穿透的剖面。
不同植物在地上與地下和諧共生的圖面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Three boundary types were tested in models: open boundary, light edge and selected penetration. The models were then divided, and small blocks were used to form sixteen new building blocks.
captions: Models testing how each boundary filters light and shadow.
The sixteen blocks and the nine combined blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以模型測試三種邊界類型：開放邊界、輕盈邊緣與選擇性穿透。接著將模型拆解，再以小量體組成十六種新的建築量體。
captions: 測試各種邊界如何過濾光影的模型。
十六種量體與九種組合量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The sixteen blocks were combined into nine new blocks, which were superimposed a second time into one large building body. Timber joints from node to node and plane to plane hold the pieces together.
captions: Four detail blocks with their plans.
Node and plane joints in two steps.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 十六種量體組合成九種新量體，再次疊合成一個大型建築體。從節點到節點、從板到板的木構接合，將各部分固定在一起。
captions: 四個細部量體及其平面。
分兩步驟的節點與板件接合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The generated modules connect along the stairs into a porous timber building. From above, the building weaves between the existing trees, linking interior space, plants and paths.
captions: Generated modules connected to form the building.
Roof plan weaving between the trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 生成的模組沿著階梯相連，成為一座多孔的木構建築。從上方看，建築穿梭於既有樹木之間，串連室內空間、植物與通道。
captions: 生成的模組相連形成建築。
穿梭於樹木之間的屋頂平面。

sections.heading: Plants and Architecture in Symbiosis - A Timber Building Woven Among the Trees
sections.body: The project explores how plants and architecture can live together in everyday life. It asks how a building might relate to the surrounding buildings and to existing plants through the nature of its boundaries. Three boundary types are tested in models: an open boundary, a light edge and selected penetration. The models are then divided, and their small blocks are used to form sixteen new building blocks. These sixteen blocks are combined into nine new ones, which are superimposed a second time into one large building body. Timber joints, from node to node and from plane to plane, hold all of the pieces firmly together. The generated modules connect along the stairs into a porous timber building. Seen from above, the building weaves its way between the existing trees, closely linking interior space, plants and paths. Architecture no longer draws a hard line against nature. It learns to step back, to let things pass through and to share ground, so that trees and people can each find their place within the same space.

zh-Hant.heading: 植物與建築的共生-在樹林間編織的木構建築
zh-Hant.body: 作品探索植物與建築如何在日常生活中共同存在，並追問一棟建築能如何透過它的邊界，與周圍的建築和既有植物建立關係。研究以模型測試三種邊界類型：開放的邊界、輕盈的邊緣與有選擇的穿透。這些模型隨後被切分，再以小塊體組合出十六個新的建築塊體。十六個塊體接著被組合為九個新塊體，經過第二次疊加，形成一個完整的大型建築量體；從點到點、面到面的木構接頭，把各個部分牢牢固定在一起。生成的模組沿著樓梯彼此連接，構成一棟多孔的木構建築。從上方俯瞰，建築在既有的樹木之間穿梭編織，把室內空間、植物與步道緊密相連。建築不再與自然劃清界線，而是學會退讓、穿透與共處，讓樹與人在同一片空間裡各得其所。

pins.title: Coming Home
pins.description:
A fragmented riverside district in Brisbane is planned around daily activities, a cultural belt and public space nodes.

Brisbane, Australia | Urban design | Sep–Dec 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 回家
zh-Hant.description:
布里斯本破碎的河畔街區，以日常活動、文化帶與公共空間節點重新規劃。

澳洲布里斯本｜都市設計｜2020年9–12月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial view of the new urban building areas by the river.
河畔新城市建築區的鳥瞰圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Brisbane is a fast-growing riverside city, and this site sits between the river, a park and busy roads and bridges. The design asks how a fragmented riverside district can become a place where people feel at home.
captions: Site analysis of edges, function, traffic, green space, heritage and public places.
District conditions: function, traffic, flood issues, subareas and activity.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 布里斯本是一座快速成長的河畔城市，而基地位於河流、公園與繁忙道路及橋梁之間。設計追問破碎的河畔街區，如何成為讓人有歸屬感的地方。
captions: 基地分析：周邊、機能、交通、綠地、文化資產與公共場所。
街區現況：機能、交通、淹水問題、分區與活動。

sections.heading: Research
