sections.body: The study maps economics, public realm, transport, social and cultural life and built form as layers of the city. Everyday activities such as walking, cooking, studying and dancing are linked into a network for the new district.
captions: Community research: where people live and play, local customs, outdoor activities and the history of the site.
Five planning steps from platforms to local natural elements.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究將經濟、公共領域、交通、社會文化生活與建成形態，視為城市的不同圖層加以分析。走路、烹飪、讀書與跳舞等日常活動，被串連成新街區的活動網絡。
captions: 社區研究：人們居住與休閒的地方、在地習俗、戶外活動與基地歷史。
從平台到在地自然元素的五個規劃步驟。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A cultural belt and two axes fix the central square, and each parcel then grows its own blocks and vertical cues. The grey space under the bridge is partitioned, cross-linked and streamlined into a lively public route.
captions: Strategy and planning steps for the space under the bridge.
Planning and axis generation for the building parcels.
Generation of key buildings such as the farm, school, market and apartments.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 文化帶與兩條軸線確立了中央廣場，各街廓再生成各自的量體與垂直線索。橋下的灰色空間經過分區、串連與流線整理，成為充滿活力的公共路徑。
captions: 橋下空間的策略與規劃步驟。
建築街廓的規劃與軸線生成。
農場、學校、市場與公寓等關鍵建築的生成。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Public space nodes host gatherings, rest and performance between the new buildings. The section shows low, layered blocks stepping down to the river in front of the city towers.
captions: Public space nodes for gathering and performance.
A-A section from the city towers down to the river.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 公共空間節點在新建築之間容納聚會、休憩與表演。剖面呈現低矮而層疊的量體，在城市高樓前方向河岸逐步降低。
captions: 供聚會與表演的公共空間節點。
從城市高樓延伸至河岸的A-A剖面。

sections.heading: Coming Home - Turning a Fragmented Riverside District Into a Place of Belonging
sections.body: This is a fast-growing riverside city, and the site sits squeezed between the river, a park and busy roads and bridges. The design asks how a fragmented riverside district could become a place where people truly feel at home. The study maps the city as a set of layers covering economics, the public realm, transport, social and cultural life and built form. Everyday activities such as walking, cooking, studying and dancing are linked into a network for the new district. A cultural belt and two axes fix the position of the central square, and each parcel then grows its own blocks and vertical cues. The grey space beneath the bridge is partitioned, cross-linked and streamlined into a lively public route. Public space nodes host gatherings, rest and performance between the new buildings. The section shows low, layered blocks stepping gently down toward the river in front of the city towers. The feeling of home is not imposed by a single gesture here. It is woven slowly, thread by thread, out of these ordinary daily connections.

zh-Hant.heading: 回家-讓破碎的河岸街區成為歸屬之地
zh-Hant.body: 這是一座快速成長的河岸城市，基地夾在河流、公園與繁忙的道路和橋梁之間。設計探問，一片破碎的河岸街區，能否成為讓人感到回家的地方？研究把城市拆解為經濟、公共領域、交通、社會與文化生活，以及建成形態等多個圖層；散步、烹飪、讀書與跳舞等日常活動，則被連結為新街區的一張網絡。一條文化帶與兩條軸線確立了中央廣場的位置，每個地塊再各自生長出街廓與垂直的指引；橋下的灰色空間經過分隔、交錯連結與流線化的處理，轉化為一條熱鬧的公共路徑。公共空間節點散布在新建築之間，容納聚會、休憩與表演；剖面呈現低矮而層疊的街廓，在城市高樓之前一路向河岸緩緩跌落。家的感覺，由這些日常的連結一點一滴編織而成。

pins.title: Herbal Garden
pins.description:
An abandoned herb-growing school plot becomes an art gallery and garden about traditional Chinese medicine.

Macau, China | Art gallery | Mar–May 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 草藥花園
zh-Hant.description:
曾種植草藥的廢棄校地，化為一座關於中醫藥的藝術館與花園。

中國澳門｜藝術館｜2020年3–5月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Planting rings and a sunken amphitheatre in the herbal garden.
草藥花園中的種植圓環與下沉劇場。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site is an abandoned school plot in Macau that was once used to grow traditional Chinese medicine herbs. Hospitals and dormitories for medical students now surround it, so the project continues the old use with an art gallery about traditional Chinese medicine.
captions: The site on the map of Macau, and the street views around the abandoned school site.
Site map with the planting area marked.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地是澳門一處曾用來種植中草藥的廢棄校地。周邊如今有醫院與醫學生宿舍，因此專案延續原本的用途，打造一座關於中醫藥的藝術館。
captions: 澳門地圖上的基地位置，以及廢棄校地周邊的街景。
標示種植區的基地圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Interviews with people around the site and a questionnaire showed that most people have only heard of traditional Chinese medicine. Most of those who have learned about it did so through exhibitions, which points to a gallery with several ways to learn.
captions: Research on traditional Chinese medicine and the questionnaire about how people know it.
Function areas for exhibition, discussion, projection, experience, light food and planting.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 對周邊居民的訪談與問卷顯示，多數人只聽過中醫藥而不甚了解。曾經學習過的人大多透過展覽認識它，這指向一座提供多種學習方式的展館。
captions: 中醫藥研究，以及人們如何認識中醫的問卷調查。
展覽、討論、投影、體驗、輕食與種植等機能區。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The S-shaped curve of Tai Chi becomes the flow line of the site, and the foot acupoint map divides the site into areas. A round floor is cut along the curve, divided into two parts, linked again and opened with an atrium.
captions: Concept drawn from the Tai Chi curve and the foot acupoint map.
Five steps from an ordinary floor to an open atrium.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 太極的S形曲線成為基地的動線，腳底穴位圖則用來劃分基地區塊。圓形樓板沿著曲線切開、分為兩半，再重新連結並開出中庭。
captions: 取自太極曲線與腳底穴位圖的概念。
從普通樓板到開放中庭的五個步驟。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Two vaulted buildings hold exhibition, projection, office and history areas across a basement and a first floor. Planting areas, sunken spaces and an experience area for making herbal tea let visitors learn by doing.
captions: Master plan of the buildings and planting areas.
Section A-A through the two vaulted halls.
Experience area for making herbal tea.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩棟拱形建築在地下層與一樓容納展覽、投影、辦公與歷史區。種植區、下沉空間與製作草本茶的體驗區，讓參觀者在動手中學習。
captions: 建築與種植區的總平面圖。
穿越兩座拱形大廳的A-A剖面。
製作草本茶的體驗區。

sections.heading: Herbal Garden - Continuing a Tradition of Healing on a Former Herb Plot
sections.body: The site is an abandoned school plot that was once used to grow herbs for traditional Chinese medicine. Hospitals and dormitories for medical students now surround it, so the project continues the old use of the land with an art gallery devoted to that medical tradition. The student interviewed people around the site and handed out a questionnaire, discovering that most people had only heard of it in passing. Most of those who had truly learned about it did so through exhibitions, which points toward a gallery offering several ways to learn. The S-shaped curve of Tai Chi becomes the flow line of the site, while a map of foot acupoints divides the ground into areas. A round floor is cut along the curve, separated into two parts, joined again and opened up with an atrium. Two vaulted buildings hold exhibition, projection, office and history areas across a basement and a first floor. Planting areas, sunken spaces and a hands-on area for making herbal tea let visitors learn by doing, turning ancient knowledge into something touched and tasted.

zh-Hant.heading: 草藥花園-在昔日藥圃上延續一門醫藥智慧
zh-Hant.body: 基地是一塊廢棄的學校用地，過去曾用來種植中草藥；如今周圍環繞著醫院與醫學生宿舍，作品因此延續這塊地的舊有用途，設計一座以中醫為主題的藝廊。學生訪談基地周邊的人們並發放問卷，發現多數人只是聽說過中醫；而真正學習過的人，大多是透過展覽認識它，這指向一座提供多種學習方式的藝廊。太極的 S 形曲線成為基地的動線，足部穴位圖則把基地劃分為不同區域；一個圓形樓板沿著曲線被切開、分為兩半，再重新連接，並以中庭打開。兩棟拱頂建築跨越地下室與一樓，容納展覽、投影、辦公與歷史區；種植區、下沉空間與製作草本茶的體驗區，讓參觀者在動手之中學習。古老的醫藥智慧在此不再遙遠，而成為可以觸摸、品嚐與親身體會的知識。

pins.title: The Home of Pottery
pins.description:
A sunken building in a ceramics village follows the steps of making porcelain to give young makers a place to work and show.

Jingdezhen, China | Culture and studios | Jun–Aug 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 陶瓷之家
zh-Hant.description:
陶瓷村落中的下沉建築，依循瓷器的製作步驟，為年輕創作者提供創作與展示的場所。

中國景德鎮｜文化與工作室｜2020年6–8月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The sunken building glowing on the hillside at night.
夜晚在山坡上發光的下沉建築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site sits on the edge of a village in Jingdezhen, the hometown of ceramics, where many artists have set up studios. Young makers from outside who cannot fit into local life need a place to show their work, a good place to create and a way into the community.
captions: Site layout: the new road links the new and old buildings, and the sunken building keeps the mountain views.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於陶瓷之鄉景德鎮一座村落的邊緣，附近有許多藝術家設立工作室。無法融入在地生活的外來年輕創作者，需要展示作品的地方、良好的創作環境，以及融入社區的途徑。
captions: 基地配置：新道路連結新舊建築，下沉的建築保留了望向山的視野。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The design follows the order in which ceramics are made, from china clay and moulding to glazing, firing and the finished piece. Each step is matched with an element such as water, sun or tree and turned into a space.
captions: Location in Jingdezhen and the user groups: the Jingpiao makers, visitors, artists and locals.
Concept: each step of making ceramics becomes a space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 設計依循陶瓷的製作順序，從瓷土、成型到上釉、燒製與成品。每個步驟都對應水、陽光或樹木等元素，並轉化為空間。
captions: 景德鎮的區位與使用者群體：景漂創作者、訪客、藝術家與在地居民。
概念：陶瓷製作的每個步驟化為一個空間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A sunken entrance, a courtyard fed by the stream, a zigzag corridor and a sunny open space follow the making process in sequence. Two sunken courtyards, a water yard and a sun yard, stand for the water and fire that porcelain needs.
captions: Water yard and sun yard in section and axonometric.
Study models of the sunken building.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 下沉入口、引入溪水的庭院、曲折的廊道與陽光充足的開放空間，依序呼應製作流程。水院與日院兩座下沉庭院，象徵瓷器所需的水與火。
captions: 水院與日院的剖面與軸測圖。
下沉建築的研究模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The building links production, tourism and communication so that artists, locals and visitors can share space. Sections and elevations show a low building tucked into the slope beneath the mountain.
captions: Programme axonometric for production, tourism and communication.
Ground floor plan.
Master plan between the stream, the mountain and the old building.
Elevations C-C and D-D.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 建築串連生產、觀光與交流，讓藝術家、在地居民與遊客共享空間。剖面與立面呈現一座嵌入山坡、低伏於山下的建築。
captions: 生產、觀光與交流的機能軸測圖。
一樓平面圖。
位於溪流、山與老建築之間的總平面圖。
C-C與D-D立面。

sections.heading: The Home of Pottery - Welcoming Outside Makers Through the Order of Firing
sections.body: The site sits on the edge of a village in a famous hometown of ceramics, where many artists have already set up studios. Young makers from elsewhere who struggle to fit into local life still need a place to show their work, a good environment in which to create and a path into the community. The design follows the order in which ceramics are made, from china clay and moulding to glazing, firing and the finished piece. Each step is matched with an element such as water, sun or tree and turned into a space. A sunken entrance, a courtyard fed by the stream, a zigzag corridor and a sunny open space follow the making process in sequence. Two sunken courtyards, a water yard and a sun yard, stand for the water and fire that porcelain needs. The building links production, tourism and communication so that artists, locals and visitors can share space. Sections and elevations show a low building tucked quietly into the slope beneath the mountain, where the journey of making becomes a journey through space and a place of belonging.

zh-Hant.heading: 陶瓷之家-依循燒製的次序安放外來的創作者
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於瓷都一座村落的邊緣，許多藝術家已在此設立工作室；然而來自外地、難以融入在地生活的年輕創作者，仍需要一處展示作品的地方、一個良好的創作環境，以及一條通往社區的途徑。設計依循陶瓷製作的次序展開，從瓷土、塑形到上釉、燒製與成品，每一個步驟都對應一種元素，例如水、陽光或樹，並轉化為一處空間。下沉的入口、引溪水而成的庭院、曲折的廊道與向陽的開放空間，依製作的過程依序排列；兩座下沉庭院，一為水院，一為陽院，象徵瓷器所需要的水與火。建築把生產、觀光與交流連結起來，讓藝術家、在地居民與遊客能夠共享空間；剖面與立面呈現一棟低矮的建築，安靜地嵌入山腳的坡地。創作的歷程在此化為空間的旅程，也為異鄉人留下一處歸屬。

pins.title: Port of Culture
pins.description:
A damaged building in Mariupol becomes a cultural landmark whose routes weave collective memory and migration under a planted membrane roof.

Mariupol, Ukraine | Culture and exhibition | Feb–Apr 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 文化之港
zh-Hant.description:
馬立波一棟受損建築化身為文化地標，在植栽膜屋頂下交織集體記憶與遷徙的路徑。

烏克蘭馬立波｜文化與展覽｜2019年2–4月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The green membrane roof rises from the ground over the new cultural building.
綠色膜結構屋頂自地面升起，覆蓋新的文化建築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A damaged historic building beside a church square in Mariupol is to become a new landmark for the city. The brief asks for an open space where residents can meet, share local stories and rebuild a sense of pride.
captions: The destroyed building inside and out, and the history of the city from the Civil War to 2014.
Site analysis: the building in its dense low-rise block, with land use, height and road maps.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 馬立波教堂廣場旁一棟受損的歷史建築，將被轉化為城市的新地標。任務要求一處開放空間，讓居民相聚、分享在地故事，並重建對城市的認同。
captions: 被摧毀建築的內外狀況，以及城市從內戰到2014年的歷史。
基地分析：位於密集低層街廓中的建築，以及土地使用、高度與道路圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: String models pulled by hand test how the old volume can be split, dragged, rotated and reconnected. Four urban effects guide the form: a landmark, a public ramp, beams of light and a place of remembrance.
captions: String model steps: split, drag, rotate, adjust, connect and end.
Location impact: special landmark, public space, lighthouse and commemoration.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以手拉動的線材模型，測試舊量體如何被分割、拉伸、旋轉與重新連接。四種城市效應引導形體：地標、公共坡道、光束與紀念場所。
captions: 線材模型步驟：分割、拉伸、旋轉、調整、連接與完成。
區位影響：特殊地標、公共空間、燈塔與紀念。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The city history is read as four themes, fortress, wharf, industry and war, and each theme becomes a set of space elements. Two routes, one of collective memory and one of migration, weave through the exhibition levels.
captions: Model studies of space elements for the four themes.
Space elements and the linked routes of migration and collective memory.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 城市歷史被解讀為要塞、碼頭、工業與戰爭四個主題，每個主題轉化為一組空間元素。集體記憶與遷徙兩條路徑，交織穿越各個展覽樓層。
captions: 四個主題空間元素的模型研究。
空間元素，以及遷徙與集體記憶相互連結的路徑。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Two floors above ground and two below sit under one inflatable membrane roof with planted ridges. Interior views follow the routes from the children's entrance through spaces of memory and migration.
captions: Exploded axonometry from the roof outline down to the second basement.
Interior renderings along the memory and migration routes.
Structure of the tensile roof with light and structural columns.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 地上兩層與地下兩層，覆蓋在一片帶有植栽脊線的充氣膜屋頂之下。室內視角沿著路徑，從兒童入口穿越記憶與遷徙的空間。
captions: 從屋頂輪廓到地下二層的爆炸軸測圖。
沿記憶與遷徙路徑的室內渲染。
張拉屋頂的結構，以及採光與結構柱。

sections.heading: Port of Culture - Rebuilding Pride in a City After War
sections.body: A damaged historic building beside a church square is to become a new landmark for the city. The brief asks for an open space where residents can meet, share local stories and rebuild a sense of pride in their home. String models pulled by hand test how the old volume can be split, dragged, rotated and reconnected. Four urban effects guide the form: a landmark, a public ramp, beams of light and a place of remembrance. The history of the city is read through four themes, fortress, wharf, industry and war, and each theme becomes a set of spatial elements. Two routes, one of collective memory and one of migration, weave through the exhibition levels. Two floors above ground and two below sit beneath a single inflatable membrane roof whose ridges are planted with greenery. Interior views follow the routes from the children's entrance through spaces of memory and migration. The wounds of the past are not hidden away. Instead they become the starting point from which a community can begin again, together and with dignity.

zh-Hant.heading: 文化之港-在戰後的城市重建驕傲
zh-Hant.body: 教堂廣場旁一棟受損的歷史建築，將成為這座城市新的地標。任務書要求一處開放的空間，讓居民在此相聚、分享在地的故事，並重新建立對城市的驕傲。研究以手拉的線模型，測試舊有量體如何被拆分、拖曳、旋轉與重新連接；四種城市效應引導著形態的生成：地標、公共坡道、光束與紀念之地。城市的歷史被解讀為四個主題，堡壘、碼頭、工業與戰爭，每個主題都轉化為一組空間元素；兩條路線，一條關於集體記憶，一條關於遷徙，交織穿過各個展覽樓層。地上兩層與地下兩層，共同覆蓋於一片充氣膜屋頂之下，屋脊上種滿植栽。室內視景沿著路線展開，從兒童入口出發，穿越記憶與遷徙的空間。傷痕沒有被掩蓋，而成為重新出發的起點。

pins.title: The Past and Future of KaoLao Pier
pins.description:
A silted fishing pier in Qingdao is revived with markets, timber jetties and a round history museum built on local memory.

Qingdao, China | Waterfront regeneration | Apr–Jul 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: KaoLao 碼頭的過去與未來
zh-Hant.description:
青島一座淤積的漁港，以市場、木棧道與一座承載在地記憶的圓形歷史博物館重獲新生。

中國青島｜濱水再生｜2019年4–7月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Cabin section: a timber seaside cabin on piles over the water.
小屋剖面：架於水面樁柱上的木構海邊小屋。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An old fishing pier in Qingdao has silted up, and village fishing no longer brings a steady income. The group set out to revive the wharf through fishing, mariculture, processing, tourism and a seafood market.
captions: Changes in fishing places, nets, storage, materials, power and food from the 1950s to the 2010s.
Income ranges of village occupations, from external contractors to manufacture workers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 青島一座老漁港逐漸淤積，村裡的捕魚已無法帶來穩定收入。小組希望透過捕撈、海水養殖、加工、觀光與海鮮市場，讓碼頭重新活絡。
captions: 從1950年代到2010年代，捕魚地點、漁網、保存、材料、動力與食物的變化。
村中各種職業的收入範圍，從外部承包商到製造工人。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Interviews with a long-time villager traced how boats, nets and work changed over the decades. The findings showed that income was the key, so the plan links fishing, culture and ecology to draw visitors back.
captions: Market way: buying at the wharf, transport and take-away, aiming at a clean, energy-saving and well-routed flow.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 與長年居住的村民訪談，追溯船隻、漁網與工作數十年來的轉變。研究發現收入是關鍵，因此計畫串連漁業、文化與生態，重新吸引訪客。
captions: 市場動線：碼頭購買、運輸與外帶，目標是乾淨、節能且分流的動線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Timber jetties tie the old concrete wharf to new market and leisure decks above the tidal flat. Each joint stacks layers of waterproofing, anti-damp mats and anti-corrosion paint to last by the sea.
captions: Node detail of the timber jetty meeting the concrete wharf.
Timber jetty section with fishing, walking and resting along the deck.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棧道將舊混凝土碼頭與潮間帶上的新市場及休閒平台相連。每個接點疊加防水、防潮墊與防腐塗層，以適應海邊環境。
captions: 木棧道與混凝土碼頭交接的節點詳圖。
木棧道剖面，沿線有垂釣、散步與休憩。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A round history museum takes its plan from the lines of the nearby sea bridge, with a ramp circling the rooms. Its sections show seaweed roofs, oyster shell walls and white shell floors as the water and mud rise over time.
captions: Masterplan of the pier on the aerial photo, with the new programmes along the wharf.
Section 1:100 of a round wharf unit, showing sunlight, low-e glass, moisture and waste flows.
Museum plans with the circling ramp and the bridge-derived grid.
Museum sections for three stages of water and mud levels.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 圓形的歷史博物館以鄰近跨海大橋的線條為平面依據，坡道環繞各個展間。剖面呈現海草屋頂、蚵殼牆與白貝殼地面，回應水位與淤泥隨時間上升。
captions: 在航拍底圖上的碼頭總平面，標示沿碼頭配置的新機能。
1:100剖面，呈現圓形碼頭單元的日照、低輻射玻璃、濕氣與廢水流向。
博物館平面，坡道環繞並以大橋線條劃分。
博物館三個水位與淤泥階段的剖面。

sections.heading: The Past and Future of KaoLao Pier - Restoring a Livelihood to a Silted Fishing Harbour
sections.body: An old fishing pier has slowly silted up, and village fishing no longer brings a steady income. The group set out to revive the wharf through fishing, mariculture, processing, tourism and a seafood market. Interviews with a long-time villager trace how boats, nets and ways of working changed over the decades. The findings show that income is the key, so the plan links fishing, culture and ecology to draw visitors back. Timber jetties tie the old concrete wharf to new market and leisure decks raised above the tidal flat. Each joint stacks layers of waterproofing, anti-damp mats and anti-corrosion paint so that it can endure life by the sea. A round history museum takes its plan from the lines of a nearby sea bridge, with a ramp circling the rooms inside. Its sections show seaweed roofs, oyster shell walls and white shell floors as water and mud rise around them over time. Memory and livelihood are carried forward together here, so that the pier can belong once more to both its past and its future.

zh-Hant.heading: KaoLao碼頭的過去與未來-為淤積的漁港找回生計
zh-Hant.body: 一座老漁港逐漸淤積，村裡的漁業也不再帶來穩定的收入。小組希望透過漁撈、海水養殖、加工、觀光與海鮮市場，讓這座碼頭重新活起來。研究訪談了一位久居村中的居民，追溯船隻、漁網與勞動方式在數十年間的變化；結果顯示，收入才是關鍵，因此規劃把漁業、文化與生態串連起來，吸引遊客回流。設計以木棧道把舊有的混凝土碼頭，連接到灘塗上方新的市集與休閒平台；每一處接合都層層疊加防水層、防潮墊與防腐塗料，以抵禦海邊的侵蝕。一座圓形的歷史博物館，從附近跨海大橋的線條取得平面，坡道環繞各個展室；剖面呈現海草屋頂、蠔殼牆與白色貝殼地坪，如何隨著海水與泥灘的上升而變化。碼頭的記憶與生計，在此被一併接續下去。

pins.title: Jinan Spring Pulse Remodeling
pins.description:
The old town of Jinan is reconnected to its springs through ditches, rain-collecting chimes and canopies, and devices that show how a spring forms.

Jinan, China | Urban renewal | May–Aug 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 濟南泉脈重塑
zh-Hant.description:
以水渠、集雨風鈴與頂棚，以及展示泉水成因的裝置，讓濟南老城重新與泉水相連。

中國濟南｜城市更新｜2020年5–8月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Masterplan: open and closed ditches link the spring groups across the old town.
總平面：明渠與暗渠串連老城中的各泉群。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The old town of Jinan grew around four groups of springs, which long shaped daily life in the city. Industrial growth and the loss of vegetation at the sources have lowered the flow, and some springs have even stopped.
captions: Landform, land use, transport and the blue and green network of the old town.
Spring origin: a geological section from the recharge mountains to the springs.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 濟南老城圍繞四大泉群發展，泉水長久以來塑造了城市的日常生活。工業化與泉源植被的破壞使水量下降，部分泉水甚至曾經斷流。
captions: 老城的地形、土地使用、交通與藍綠網絡。
泉水成因：從補給山區到泉口的地質剖面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Small models recreated scenes of daily life with the springs, from washing vegetables to playing by the water. A strategy chart then weighed how far each move should revive the spring veins and how far it should bring water back into daily life.
captions: Models of life and leisure with spring water.
Strategy chart weighing each move between the spring veins and daily life.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以小模型重現人們與泉水共處的日常，從洗菜到在水邊玩耍。策略圖再衡量每項操作在恢復泉脈與讓水回到生活之間的比重。
captions: 泉水生活與娛樂的模型。
衡量各策略在泉脈與日常生活之間比重的圖表。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rain wind chimes hang on gables and partition walls, ringing on sunny days and collecting rain on wet ones. Woven canopies in hexagon and quadrangle forms shelter squares and parking while gathering rainwater.
captions: Rain wind chime: pipe section and its use on gables and partition walls.
Parking canopy forms and section.
Public space section under a rain-collecting canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 雨水風鈴掛在山牆與隔牆上，晴天作為風鈴，雨天收集雨水。六邊形與四邊形的編織頂棚為廣場與停車場遮蔽，同時收集雨水。
captions: 雨水風鈴：管件剖面及其在山牆與隔牆上的應用。
停車場頂棚形式與剖面。
集雨頂棚下的公共空間剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Valve devices modelled on the heart show how a spring forms, with a large voice-controlled type for squares and a small push-button type for narrow streets. A ferry route along the old moat ties the spring nodes into one network.
captions: Moat park section with the ferry route.
Spring valve device: valve details, sections and working principle.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 仿照心臟瓣膜的裝置讓人理解泉水如何形成，大型聲控款適用於廣場，小型按鈕款適用於窄巷。沿舊護城河的遊船路線將各泉水節點串成一個網絡。
captions: 護城河公園與遊船路線剖面。
泉水瓣膜裝置：瓣膜細部、剖面與運作原理。

sections.heading: Jinan Spring Pulse Remodeling - Letting Spring Water Flow Back Into Daily Life
sections.body: The old town grew around four groups of springs, which long shaped the rhythm of daily life in the city. Industrial growth and the loss of vegetation at the sources have lowered the flow, and some springs have stopped altogether. Small models recreate scenes of life lived alongside the springs, from washing vegetables to playing by the water. A strategy chart then weighs how far each move should revive the spring veins and how far it should bring water back into everyday life. Rain wind chimes hang on gables and partition walls, ringing on sunny days and collecting rain on wet ones. Woven canopies in hexagonal and quadrangular forms shelter squares and parking while gathering rainwater. Valve devices modelled on the heart demonstrate how a spring forms, with a large voice-controlled type for squares and a small push-button type for narrow streets. A ferry route along the old moat ties the spring nodes into one network. The pulse of the city begins to beat again, carried by water that returns to the hands and ears of its residents.

zh-Hant.heading: 濟南泉脈重塑-讓泉水重新流回日常
zh-Hant.body: 這座老城圍繞著四組泉群生長，泉水長久以來塑造著城市的日常生活；然而工業發展與水源地植被的流失，使泉水流量下降，有些泉眼甚至已經停止湧出。研究以小型模型重現人們與泉水相伴的生活場景，從洗菜到在水邊嬉戲；一張策略圖再權衡每一項操作，應在多大程度上恢復泉脈，又應在多大程度上讓水重新回到生活之中。設計在山牆與隔牆上懸掛雨水風鈴，晴天時叮噹作響，雨天時收集雨水；六邊形與四邊形的編織頂篷為廣場與停車處遮蔭，同時匯集雨水。仿照心臟構造的閥門裝置，展示泉水如何形成，廣場上設置大型的聲控款，窄巷則配置小型的按鈕款。一條沿著舊護城河的渡船路線，把各個泉水節點串成網絡，讓城市的脈搏重新跳動。

pins.title: Melbourne Affordable Housing
pins.description:
Mixed groups of residents share homes that grow over the roofs of central Melbourne, using space that the city has left unused.

Melbourne, Australia | Affordable housing | Jun–Oct 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 墨爾本可負擔住宅
zh-Hant.description:
不同居民群體共享的住宅，沿墨爾本市中心的屋頂生長，利用城市閒置的空間。

澳洲墨爾本｜可負擔住宅｜2020年6–10月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Room configurations for each group, combined into nine household tribes.
各群體的房型配置，組合成九種家戶族群。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Melbourne's population keeps growing, and rising house prices and rents have pushed many families out of the city centre. Land in the centre is tight on the ground, yet much usable space above existing buildings is left unused.
captions: Site analysis: the city-centre site near the Treasury Gardens, block sections and site photos.
House and flat price changes across the city's districts.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 墨爾本人口持續成長，房價與租金上漲使許多家庭被迫離開市中心。市中心的地面土地有限，但既有建築上方仍有大量可用空間未被利用。
captions: 基地分析：鄰近財政花園的市中心基地、街廓剖析與基地照片。
城市各區的獨棟與公寓房價變化。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A daily time loop traced when different groups of residents use shared space, from early work hours to late evening rest. The groups were then paired by how well they can help one another, mixing natives, families, students, skilled workers and newcomers.
captions: Population life time loop over twenty-four hours.
Mixed habitation groups and options beside housing indicator charts.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以一日時間循環追蹤不同居民群體使用共享空間的時段，從清晨上班到深夜休息。再依彼此能否互相幫助來配對群體，混合在地居民、家庭、學生、技術工作者與新移民。
captions: 二十四小時的人口生活時間循環。
混居群體與組合方式，以及住宅相關指標圖表。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A nine-metre dwelling unit is divided into rooms of different sizes to suit each group and budget. Tribes are joined into four clusters, with crowd flow weaving through living, business and public areas.
captions: Four clusters combining tribes, with living, business and public areas.
Cluster IV with rooftops, ramps and shared spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以九公尺見方的住宅單元，依群體需求與經濟能力分割成不同大小的房間。各族群再組合成四個聚落，人流穿梭於居住、商業與公共空間之間。
captions: 四個由族群組合而成的聚落，含居住、商業與公共區。
聚落四的屋頂、坡道與共享空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The building spreads up from a park over existing roofs, with public space at the base, dense homes in the middle and many small shared spaces at the top. Wind and solar powered clocks on the roofs show the daily change in house prices and rents as a gentle public reminder.
captions: Section details: middle floors, balcony ventilation and a passive solar house.
Models of the building units.
Warning clock: parts, dial and gear drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 建築從公園沿既有屋頂向上蔓延，底部是公共空間，中段為密集住宅，頂部則有許多小型共享空間。屋頂上以風力與太陽能驅動的時鐘，每日顯示房價與租金的變化，作為溫和的公共提醒。
captions: 剖面細部：中段樓層、陽台通風與被動式太陽能住宅。
建築單元模型。
警示時鐘：構件、錶盤與齒輪圖。

sections.heading: Melbourne Affordable Housing - Tribes of Neighbours Built Above Existing Roofs
sections.body: The population of the city keeps growing, and rising house prices and rents have pushed many families out of the centre. Ground in the centre is tight, yet a great deal of usable space above existing buildings is left empty. A daily time loop traces when different groups of residents use shared space, from early working hours to rest late in the evening. The groups are then paired according to how well they can help one another, mixing long-time locals, families, students, skilled workers and newcomers. A nine-metre dwelling unit is divided into rooms of different sizes to suit each group and budget. These tribes are joined into four clusters, with flows of people weaving through living, business and public areas. The building spreads upward from a park and over existing roofs, with public space at the base, dense homes in the middle and many small shared spaces at the top. Clocks on the roofs, powered by wind and sun, display the daily change in house prices and rents, offering the city a gentle public reminder.

zh-Hant.heading: 墨爾本可負擔住宅-在既有屋頂之上共築部落
zh-Hant.body: 城市人口持續增長，攀升的房價與租金把許多家庭推離市中心；中心區的地面土地緊缺，既有建築上方卻仍有大量可用的空間閒置著。研究以一條日常時間環，追蹤不同居民群體使用共享空間的時段，從清晨的上班時間到深夜的休息；再依彼此互助的程度為群體配對，混合在地居民、家庭、學生、技術工作者與新移民。設計以九公尺的居住單元為基礎，切分為大小不同的房間，以符合各群體的需求與預算；這些部落再組合為四個群落，人流穿梭於居住、商業與公共區域之間。建築從公園向上延伸，越過既有的屋頂，底部是公共空間，中段是密集的住宅，頂部則散布許多小型共享空間。屋頂上以風能與太陽能驅動的時鐘，每天顯示房價與租金的變化，成為一則溫和的公共提醒。

pins.title: Cambodian Restaurant and Cookery School
pins.description:
A restaurant and cookery school in Brisbane draws on Cambodian cuisine, shared meals and green gardens.

Brisbane, Australia | Restaurant and cookery school | 2018 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 柬埔寨餐廳與烹飪學校
zh-Hant.description:
一座位於布里斯本的餐廳與烹飪學校，以柬埔寨料理、共享餐食與綠色花園為設計起點。

澳洲布里斯本｜餐廳與烹飪學校｜2018年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Sectional model of the restaurant and cookery school.
餐廳與烹飪學校的剖面模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The brief asked for a restaurant and cookery school in Brisbane that carries the taste of one food culture. The project starts from Cambodian cuisine and the way people share a meal.
captions: The steps of a traditional noodle dish, from preparation and cooking to serving.
Table drawings of a small family, a group of friends and a couple, during and after meals.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 題目要求在布里斯本設計一座承載單一飲食文化的餐廳與烹飪學校。本案從柬埔寨料理以及人們共享一餐的方式出發。
captions: 一道傳統米線料理的步驟，從備料、烹煮到上菜。
小家庭、朋友聚餐與兩人用餐時，餐中與餐後的桌面圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site sits where a secondary road meets a primary road, a spot that can draw in passers-by. A wide set of massing studies tested how the volumes could open to the street and to light.
captions: Massing model on the site at the corner of the two roads.
Massing studies comparing different ways of carving and stacking the volume.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於次要道路與主要道路的交會處，能吸引往來行人。大量量體研究測試建築如何向街道與光線打開。
captions: 位於兩條道路轉角的基地量體模型。
比較不同切削與堆疊方式的量體研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A central garden, a roof garden and planted shelves bring green space into a crowded neighbourhood. Dining sits on the lower levels and the cookery school above, with a basement for service.
captions: Green spaces: roof garden, dining area, central garden, shelves and social space.
Sections 1 and 2 through the dining floors and the central garden.
Exploded levels from the basement to the cookery school.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 中央花園、屋頂花園與種植層架，為擁擠的街區帶來綠意。用餐空間位於下層，烹飪學校在上層，地下室作為後勤使用。
captions: 綠色空間：屋頂花園、用餐區、中央花園、層架與社交空間。
穿過用餐樓層與中央花園的剖面一與剖面二。
從地下室到烹飪學校的分層爆炸圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The street façade becomes a colourful billboard, while the side facing the garden stays clear and simple. A section perspective shows people cooking, eating and resting across the floors.
captions: Section perspective with the stairs, terraces and planting.
Façade design: glass panel sets, colour studies and elevations.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 面向街道的立面成為一面繽紛的看板，面向花園的一側則保持清透簡潔。剖透視呈現人們在各樓層烹飪、用餐與休憩。
captions: 呈現樓梯、露台與植栽的剖透視。
立面設計：玻璃面板組合、色彩研究與立面圖。

sections.heading: Cambodian Restaurant and Cookery School - A Shared Table Connecting the Neighbourhood
sections.body: The brief asked for a restaurant and cookery school that carries the flavour of one particular food culture. The project starts from a Southeast Asian cuisine and from the way people gather around a table to share a meal. The site sits where a secondary road meets a primary road, a spot well placed to draw in passers-by. A wide set of massing studies tests how the volumes could open toward the street and toward the light. A central garden, a roof garden and planted shelves bring green space into a crowded neighbourhood. Dining sits on the lower levels, the cookery school occupies the floors above, and a basement holds the service spaces. The street facade becomes a colourful billboard, while the side facing the garden remains clear and simple. A section perspective shows people cooking, eating and resting across the floors. Food is more than something to taste here. It becomes a culture that is taught and shared, allowing unfamiliar flavours to grow into a new common memory for neighbours living side by side.

zh-Hant.heading: 柬埔寨餐廳與烹飪學校-以一桌共享的餐點連結街區
zh-Hant.body: 任務書要求設計一間承載某種飲食文化滋味的餐廳與烹飪學校。作品從一種東南亞料理，以及人們圍坐分享一餐的方式出發。基地位於次要道路與主要道路交會之處，是一個能吸引路人駐足的位置；大量的量體研究測試各個體塊如何向街道與光線打開。中央花園、屋頂花園與植栽架，為擁擠的街區帶進綠意；用餐空間位於較低的樓層，烹飪學校在上，地下室則作為後勤服務。臨街立面化身為一面色彩繽紛的看板，面向花園的一側則保持清晰而簡潔。剖透視呈現人們在各個樓層烹煮、用餐與休息的情景。料理在此不只是被品嚐的食物，更是一種被傳授、被分享的文化，讓陌生的味道成為街坊之間新的共同記憶。

pins.title: Meerkat Mansion and Entrance Building
pins.description:
A zoo enclosure in Brisbane where visitors and meerkats watch each other along interlocking ramps.

Brisbane, Australia | Zoo enclosure and entrance | 2017 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 狐獴屋與入口建築
zh-Hant.description:
位於布里斯本的動物園展區，遊客與狐獴沿著交錯的坡道彼此觀看。

澳洲布里斯本｜動物園展區與入口｜2017年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Model of the meerkat mansion: interlocking ramps under a light roof.
狐獴屋模型：輕盈屋頂下相互交錯的坡道。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Brisbane once had zoos, but they closed amid growing concern for animals kept in poor enclosures under the constant gaze of the public. The brief asked for a new zoo layout where one enclosure and its entrance rethink how visitors and animals meet.
captions: Zoo zoning, with the meerkat mansion and entry building at the heart of the plan.
From the conventional zoo to new strategies: interlocking levels, switched roles and spaces fitted to each animal.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 布里斯本曾有動物園，但因外界日益關注圈養動物的福祉而關閉，這些動物常處於簡陋的圍欄中、承受大眾不斷的注視。題目要求規劃一座新的動物園，以其中一個展區與入口建築重新思考遊客與動物的相遇方式。
captions: 動物園分區圖，狐獴屋與入口建築位於規劃核心。
從傳統動物園到新策略：交錯的樓層、互換的角色，以及依動物習性設計的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two assigned precedent buildings were taken apart and recombined into a set of hybrid forms. These forms were then matched to the habits of meerkats, which love to run, jump and watch moving things.
captions: Hybrid forms drawn from transforming the two precedent buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 將兩座指定的參考建築拆解、重組，發展出一系列混合形體。再將這些形體對應狐獴的習性：喜愛奔跑、跳躍，並好奇地觀察移動的事物。
captions: 由兩座參考建築轉化而來的混合形體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Spiral ramps for visitors and meerkats wrap around each other, so both sides watch one another. Towers, a roof terrace and an underground maze give each viewpoint its own place.
captions: Connection, transformation and event program for the mansion.
Mansion plans from the roof terrace down to the underground maze.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 遊客與狐獴的螺旋坡道彼此纏繞，讓雙方互相觀看。塔樓、屋頂平台與地下迷宮，為每一種觀看方式提供各自的位置。
captions: 狐獴屋的連結、轉化與活動計畫。
狐獴屋平面，從屋頂平台到地下迷宮。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The entrance building holds ticketing, a recreation area and a café beside the woodland paths. Sections show visitors climbing the ramps while the meerkats run and dig below.
captions: Exploded axonometric of the entrance building and the meerkat mansion, with the activity spaces.
Site plan of the mansion and the entrance building among the trees.
Ground and first level plans of the entrance building.
Three sections through the entrance building and the mansion.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 入口建築容納售票、休閒區與咖啡廳，緊鄰林間步道。剖面呈現遊客沿坡道上行，狐獴則在下方奔跑與挖掘。
captions: 入口建築與狐獴宅邸的分解軸測圖，以及各活動空間。
狐獴屋與入口建築在樹林中的配置圖。
入口建築一樓與二樓平面。
穿過入口建築與狐獴屋的三道剖面。

sections.heading: Meerkat Mansion and Entrance Building - Turning the Gaze Into a Two-Way Exchange
sections.body: The city once had zoos, but they closed amid growing concern for animals kept in poor enclosures under the constant gaze of the public. The brief asked for a new zoo layout in which one enclosure and its entrance rethink how visitors and animals meet. Two assigned precedent buildings are taken apart and recombined into a set of hybrid forms. These forms are then matched to the habits of meerkats, which love to run, jump and watch anything that moves. Spiral ramps for visitors and for meerkats wrap around each other, so that each side can watch the other. Towers, a roof terrace and an underground maze give every viewpoint a place of its own. The entrance building holds ticketing, a recreation area and a café beside the woodland paths. Sections show visitors climbing the ramps while the meerkats run and dig beneath them. Looking is no longer a one-way display of captive creatures. It becomes a mutual and more equal exchange of attention, in which the animals are as free to observe as the people who come to see them.

zh-Hant.heading: 狐獴屋與入口建築-讓觀看成為雙向的凝視
zh-Hant.body: 這座城市曾經有過動物園，卻在人們日益關注動物被關在簡陋圍欄、時時暴露於眾人目光之下的處境中相繼關閉。任務書要求一個新的動物園配置，透過一處圍欄與其入口，重新思考參觀者與動物如何相遇。兩棟指定的先例建築被拆解並重新組合，生成一系列混合形態；這些形態再對應狐獴的習性，牠們喜愛奔跑、跳躍，並注視移動的事物。設計讓供參觀者與狐獴使用的螺旋坡道彼此纏繞，雙方因此能互相觀望；塔樓、屋頂露台與地下迷宮，為每一種視角提供專屬的位置。入口建築容納售票處、休閒區與咖啡館，緊鄰林間步道；剖面呈現參觀者沿坡道攀升，狐獴則在下方奔跑挖掘。觀看不再是單向的展示，而成為一場彼此對等的凝視。

pins.title: Skate Park Training Facility
pins.description:
A skate park in Brisbane where a looping roof grows out of the slope and links outdoor and indoor skating.

Brisbane, Australia | Skate park | 2017 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 滑板公園訓練設施
zh-Hant.description:
位於布里斯本的滑板公園，環狀屋頂自坡地生長而出，串連戶外與室內的滑板空間。

澳洲布里斯本｜滑板公園｜2017年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Street view of the skate park, its curved roof rising out of the slope.
滑板公園街景，彎曲的屋頂自坡地中升起。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The brief asked for a training facility for elite skateboarders in a park in Brisbane. The site is bumpy, crossed by random footpaths and surrounded by busy roads and dense housing.
captions: Site analysis: surroundings, transport and access, trees and footpaths.
Who the park serves: older people, children, families, skaters and animals.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 題目要求在布里斯本一座公園內設計菁英滑板選手的訓練設施。基地地形起伏，雜亂的步道穿越其間，周邊是繁忙道路與密集住宅。
captions: 基地分析：周邊環境、交通與出入、樹木與步道。
公園的使用者：長者、孩童、家庭、滑板者與動物。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project reads site as a sense of place and surface as the ground where building and landscape meet. Studies of site, daily life and program set out how the park could welcome all ages.
captions: Site, life and program: placing the building where the footpaths cross.
Skate elements from ramps and bowls to rails and pipes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案將「基地」理解為場所精神，將「表面」視為建築與地景交會的地面。透過基地、日常生活與機能的研究，探討公園如何迎接各個年齡層。
captions: 基地、生活與機能：將建築置於步道交會處。
從坡道、碗池到扶手與管道的各種滑板元素。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Drawings of skaters in motion show the dynamic, fluent and curvy lines of the sport. These lines shape a looping roof that links the outdoor skating platform with the indoor training hall below.
captions: Skater movement studies that lead to the curved forms.
Site plan, with vehicle access from the north-west and pedestrian access from two sides.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 描繪滑板者動作的圖面，呈現這項運動動態、流暢而彎曲的線條。這些線條塑造出環狀屋頂，串連戶外滑板平台與下方的室內訓練館。
captions: 引出曲線形體的滑板動作研究。
配置圖，車輛由西北側進入，行人則可從兩側進出。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The building uses the height difference of the site, so the indoor skating area sits partly below ground. Above it lie a function room, a roof terrace and a skating platform on the roof.
captions: Cutaway and sectional perspectives: skaters on the roof platform and in the indoor skating area.
Exploded axonometric from the indoor skating area up to the outdoor facilities.
Roof, first level, ground level and basement plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 建築利用基地的高低差，使室內滑板區部分位於地面以下。其上依序是多功能室、屋頂露台與屋頂滑板平台。
captions: 剖切透視與剖面透視：屋頂平台與室內滑板區中的滑板者。
從室內滑板區到戶外設施的分解軸測圖。
屋頂、二樓、一樓與地下室平面。

sections.heading: Skate Park Training Facility - Turning the Curves of Skating Into a Roof
sections.body: The brief asked for a training facility for elite skateboarders within a public park. The site is uneven, crossed by random footpaths and surrounded by busy roads and dense housing. The project reads the site as a sense of place, and the surface as the ground where building and landscape meet. Studies of the site, of daily life and of the programme set out how the park could welcome people of all ages. Drawings of skaters in motion capture the dynamic, fluent and curving lines of the sport. These lines shape a looping roof that links the outdoor skating platform with the indoor training hall below. The building makes use of the height difference across the site, so the indoor skating area sits partly below ground. Above it lie a function room, a roof terrace and a skating platform set right on the roof. The trajectory of movement is frozen into architecture, and the freedom of gliding extends beyond the training floor to spread out across the whole surrounding landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 滑板公園訓練設施-把滑行的曲線化為屋頂
zh-Hant.body: 任務書要求在一座公園中，為精英滑板選手設計一處訓練設施。基地地勢起伏，被隨意的小徑穿越，四周則是繁忙的道路與密集的住宅。作品把基地理解為一種場所感，把地表視為建築與地景相遇的地面；對基地、日常生活與機能的研究，說明公園如何能迎接各個年齡層的人。學生描繪滑板者運動中的姿態，捕捉這項運動動感、流暢而充滿曲線的線條；這些線條塑造出一個迴旋的屋頂，把戶外滑板平台與下方的室內訓練館連結起來。建築利用基地的高低差，讓室內滑板區部分沉入地下，上方則是多功能室、屋頂露台，以及設在屋頂上的滑板平台。運動的軌跡就此凝固為建築，滑行的自由也從場地延伸到整片地景之上。

pins.title: Residing in the City
pins.description:
An urban park, a pixel landscape and a temporary artwork station slip new public space into dense Oakland.

Oakland, USA | Urban public space | 2018 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 棲居城市
zh-Hant.description:
城市公園、像素地景與臨時藝術站，將新的公共空間置入高密度的奧克蘭。

美國奧克蘭｜城市公共空間｜2018年｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Pixel landscape: greenery, pools, paving and pavilions broken into pieces between the towers.
像素地景：綠地、水池、鋪面與亭子被拆解成碎片，置入高樓之間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Oakland is already a high-density, well-developed city, and most of its land is taken by buildings. The project looks for ways to improve daily life and the look of the city while keeping its original structure.
captions: Pattern plan for the pixel landscape in the central office zone.
Land use map of commercial, residential and public space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 奧克蘭已是高密度且高度開發的城市，大部分土地都已被建築占據。本案在保留原有城市紋理的前提下，尋找改善市民生活品質與城市景觀的方法。
captions: 中央辦公區像素地景的圖案平面。
商業、住宅與公共空間的土地使用圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The city has many museums and galleries, but most are indoor and small, and outdoor gathering spots are few. Underused car parks and leftover gaps between buildings became the chances for new public space.
captions: Urban park sections: a stage, an entrance, a platform and two chairs.
Urban park site plan on a former car park.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 城市裡有許多博物館與藝廊，但多為室內小型空間，戶外聚集場所十分有限。閒置的停車場與建築之間的零碎空隙，成為新公共空間的契機。
captions: 城市公園剖面：舞台、入口、平台與兩處座椅。
建於原停車場上的城市公園配置圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A rectangular basic form was reshaped into an organic shell that shelters a stage and a theatre. Gaps between the ribs let sunlight and rain reach the planting below.
captions: Form studies: from a basic box to an organic shell that lets sunlight through.
Three options for an artwork station on a rooftop, between buildings or over a car park.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 從長方形的基本形體出發，逐步修改成有機的殼體，庇護舞台與劇場。肋條之間的縫隙讓陽光與雨水落到下方的植栽。
captions: 形體研究：從基本方盒到讓陽光穿透的有機殼體。
藝術站的三種方案：屋頂、建築之間或停車場上方。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A temporary artwork station plugs into the gap between a group of apartment buildings and a store beside a freeway. Its sections show a light, porous structure climbing above and around the existing buildings.
captions: Render of the urban park with its curved shell structures.
Site of the artwork station between apartments and a store.
Sections A and B through the artwork station.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 臨時藝術站嵌入高速公路旁一群公寓與一家商店之間的空隙。剖面呈現輕盈多孔的結構，在既有建築之上與周圍攀升。
captions: 都市公園的彩現，呈現曲面殼體結構。
位於公寓與商店之間的藝術站基地。
穿過藝術站的剖面A與剖面B。

sections.heading: Residing in the City - Planting Art Into the Gaps of a Dense City
sections.body: This is a high-density, well-developed city, and most of its land has long been taken by buildings. The project looks for ways to improve daily life and the appearance of the city while keeping its original structure intact. The study finds that although the city has many museums and galleries, most are indoors and small, and outdoor gathering spots are few. Underused car parks and leftover gaps between buildings therefore become opportunities for new public space. A rectangular basic form is reshaped into an organic shell that shelters a stage and a theatre. Gaps between the ribs let sunlight and rain fall through to the planting below. A temporary artwork station plugs into the gap between a group of apartment buildings and a store beside a freeway. Its sections show a light, porous structure climbing above and around the existing buildings. The leftover spaces of the city are seen anew, and art steps out of the gallery to become part of everyday life for the people who already live there.

zh-Hant.heading: 棲居城市-在城市縫隙裡植入藝術
zh-Hant.body: 這是一座高密度、發展成熟的城市，大部分土地早已被建築占據。作品尋找一種方式，在保留原有城市結構的前提下，改善日常生活與城市的面貌。研究發現，城裡雖有許多博物館與畫廊，卻多半位於室內、規模不大，戶外的聚集場所更是稀少；未被充分利用的停車場與建築之間的零碎空隙，於是成為新公共空間的契機。設計把矩形的基本形體重塑為有機的殼體，為舞台與劇場提供遮蔽，肋條之間的縫隙讓陽光與雨水落到下方的植栽。一座臨時的藝術工作站，插入一組公寓與高速公路旁商店之間的空隙；剖面呈現輕盈而多孔的結構，如何在既有建築的上方與周圍攀升。城市的剩餘空間由此被重新看見，藝術也走出室內，融入居民的日常。

pins.title: Inspired by Structure
pins.description:
Folded models and joint tests grow into a modular tower that is both structure and home.

Architecture | Modular tower | Structure study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 從結構出發
zh-Hant.description:
從摺疊模型與接點實驗出發，發展成一座兼具結構與居所的模組化高塔。

建築｜模組化高塔｜結構研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Forming a building: a tower wrapped in a repeating structural frame.
形成建築：以重複結構框架包覆的高塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how a structure can be both beautiful and useful at the same time. It starts from small material tests rather than from a given site or program.
captions: Exploded figure: a hand-made model pulled apart into its parts.
Models formed by folding and transforming triangles, cast in a cardboard mould.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案探討結構如何同時兼具美感與實用性。它從小型材料實驗出發，而非從既定的基地或機能開始。
captions: 爆炸模型：將手作模型拆解成各個部件。
以三角形連續摺疊與變形而成的模型，以紙板模具澆鑄。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Different joint types were compared for strength, stiffness, complexity and reliability. Physical models then tested which joint could be repeated and assembled.
captions: Comparing joint types by strength, stiffness, complexity, reliability and stress mode.
Exploring the physical model, from single joints to a final assembled unit.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 比較不同接點類型的強度、剛度、複雜度與可靠度。再以實體模型測試哪一種接點可以重複組裝。
captions: 依強度、剛度、複雜度、可靠度與受力方式比較接點類型。
探索實體模型，從單一接點到最終組裝單元。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chosen joint grows from a tetrahedron into a three-way node. A stress analysis shows that the frame is fairly even in stress, which suits modular building in many directions.
captions: Joints constructed from a tetrahedron, step by step.
Stress analysis of the frame, with drawings of the repeated structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 選定的接點由四面體發展為三向節點。應力分析顯示整體框架受力相當均勻，適合向多個方向進行模組化建造。
captions: 由四面體逐步建構而成的接點。
框架的應力分析，以及重複結構的圖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The frame becomes a tower that holds single rooms, lofts and family units in triangular plans. A derivative tower stacks a commercial base, apartments, lofts and penthouses inside the same structure.
captions: Planar graph of room types in a triangular plan.
Room models: loft, single room, compact and continuity.
Derivative building: commercial complex, apartment, loft and penthouse.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 框架發展成一座高塔，在三角形平面中容納單人房、樓中樓與家庭單元。衍生出的高塔在同一結構內，依序疊放商業基座、公寓、樓中樓與頂層住宅。
captions: 三角形平面中各種房型的平面圖。
房間模型：樓中樓、單人房、緊湊型與連續型。
衍生建築：商業綜合體、公寓、樓中樓與頂層住宅。

sections.heading: Inspired by Structure - A Tower Grown From a Single Joint
sections.body: The project asks whether a structure can be beautiful and useful at the same time. Rather than starting from a given site or programme, it begins with small material tests. Different joint types are compared for strength, stiffness, complexity and reliability. Physical models then test which joint can be repeated and assembled with confidence. The chosen joint grows from a tetrahedron into a three-way node. A stress analysis shows that the frame carries load fairly evenly, which suits modular building that extends in many directions. The frame then becomes a tower that holds single rooms, lofts and family units within triangular plans. A derivative tower stacks a commercial base, apartments, lofts and penthouses inside the very same structure. The logic of the design runs from the bottom up, and patient refinement of one small node ends up determining the character of an entire building. Structure proves itself capable of being the very source of space and form, rather than a hidden skeleton added once the architecture has already been imagined.

zh-Hant.heading: 從結構出發-由一個節點生長出的塔樓
zh-Hant.body: 作品追問，結構能否同時兼具美感與實用？它沒有從既定的基地或機能開始，而是從小小的材料測試出發。研究比較了多種接頭類型的強度、剛度、複雜度與可靠性，再以實體模型檢驗哪一種接頭能夠重複製作並組裝。被選中的接頭從四面體發展為三向節點；應力分析顯示，整個框架的受力相當均勻，適合朝多個方向延伸的模組化建造。這個框架隨後成為一座塔樓，在三角形平面中容納單人房、樓中樓與家庭單元。衍生出的另一座塔樓，則在同一套結構裡疊合商業基座、公寓、樓中樓與頂層住宅。設計的邏輯自下而上，一個節點的細心推敲，最終決定了整座建築的樣貌，證明結構本身就足以成為空間與形式的源頭。

pins.title: New Urban Life
pins.description:
A greenway and roof gardens turn a former racetrack neighbourhood into a place to walk, play and meet.

Guangzhou, China | Urban design | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 新都市生活
zh-Hant.description:
以綠廊與屋頂花園，把舊賽馬場街區轉化為步行、運動與相聚的地方。

中國廣州｜都市設計｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A green running track threads through the rebuilt neighbourhood and its roof gardens.
一條綠色跑道穿過重建後的街區與屋頂花園。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Daily life spent on screens has made many people sedentary. The project rebuilds a former racetrack neighbourhood in Guangzhou so that people walk outside and meet face to face.
captions: Urban change around the site, from farmland and villages to high-rise blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 日常生活被螢幕佔據，讓許多人習慣久坐。本案重建廣州一處舊賽馬場街區，讓人們走到戶外、面對面交流。
captions: 基地周邊的都市變遷，從農地與村落轉為高樓街廓。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site is ringed by busy roads on three sides and has only two gates. That makes it hard for people to walk in, even though subway and bus lines are close by.
captions: Circulation analysis: public transport, traffic and accessibility.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地三面被繁忙道路包圍，且只有兩個出入口。即使地鐵與公車就在附近，人們仍難以步行進入。
captions: 動線分析：大眾運輸、交通與可及性。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A north-south greenway runs through the middle of the site, and a tunnel below it takes cars off the surface. Most buildings carry roof gardens that link people with nature.
captions: Future development plan: form, edge, orientation and place.
Schematic layers: circulation, roads, buildings, greenway and roof gardens.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一條南北向綠廊貫穿基地中央，其下的隧道把車流移出地面。多數建築設有屋頂花園，讓人與自然相連。
captions: 未來發展計畫：形態、邊界、方向與場所。
設計分層：動線、道路、建築、綠廊與屋頂花園。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The master plan mixes offices, a sports field, an art centre, homes and a central park along the greenway. Work, green space and community life overlap so that the old sporting spirit of the site lives on.
captions: Master plan of the neighbourhood along the greenway.
Work life, green life and human life across the plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 總體配置沿綠廊混合辦公、運動場、藝術中心、住宅與中央公園。工作、綠地與社區生活彼此交疊，讓基地原有的運動精神得以延續。
captions: 沿綠廊展開的街區總體配置。
整體配置中的工作生活、綠色生活與人的生活。

sections.heading: New Urban Life - Setting an Old Racetrack Neighbourhood in Motion Again
sections.body: Daily life spent more and more in front of screens has left many people sedentary. The project replans a former racetrack neighbourhood so that people step outdoors and meet one another face to face. The site is ringed by busy roads on three sides and has only two gates. Even though subway and bus lines are close by, it remains hard for people to walk in. The design runs a north-south greenway through the middle of the site, while a tunnel beneath it takes cars off the surface. Most buildings carry roof gardens that reconnect people with nature. The master plan mixes offices, a sports field, an art centre, homes and a central park along the greenway, so that work, green space and community life overlap. The spirit of the old racing track does not vanish. It is transformed into the daily walks, games and gatherings of the people who live there. The neighbourhood is set in motion once again, and city life moves away from the screen and back into sunlight and shared company.

zh-Hant.heading: 新都市生活-讓舊賽馬場重新跑動起來
zh-Hant.body: 日常生活越來越多耗在螢幕前，讓許多人變得久坐少動。作品重新規劃一處昔日的賽馬場街區，希望人們走到戶外，面對面地相遇。基地三面被繁忙的道路包圍，只有兩個出入口；即使地鐵與公車路線近在咫尺，人們仍難以步行進入。設計以一條南北向的綠廊貫穿基地中央，下方的隧道把車流移出地面；大多數建築配有屋頂花園，讓人與自然重新建立連結。總體規劃沿著綠廊混合配置辦公室、運動場、藝術中心、住宅與中央公園，工作、綠地與社區生活彼此交疊。昔日奔馳的賽道精神並未消失，而是轉化為人們每日的散步、運動與相聚。這片街區因此重新跑動起來，城市生活也從螢幕前，回到陽光與彼此之間。

pins.title: Building a Prison
pins.description:
Models and drawings test how a prison can balance privacy and security around one control tower.

Architecture | Prison | Privacy study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 建構一座監獄
zh-Hant.description:
以模型與圖面，探討監獄如何圍繞一座控制塔，在隱私與安全之間取得平衡。

建築｜監獄｜隱私研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A hand-drawn labyrinth of towers, bridges and stairs.
手繪的迷宮，由高塔、橋與樓梯交織而成。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks how privacy and security can be balanced inside a prison. It treats the building as a study of how walls, distance and paths decide what people can see and reach.
captions: A collage of film stills that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案探討監獄內部如何在隱私與安全之間取得平衡。它把建築當作一項研究，觀察牆、距離與路徑如何決定人能看見與抵達的範圍。
captions: 啟發本案的電影劇照拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Early drawings imagine a maze of towers and stairs that is easy to enter and hard to leave. Three prototype models then test hanging cells, a vertical maze of stairs and an open grid.
captions: Reference stills sorted by exposure, surveillance and accessibility.
Three prototype models that recombine the earlier elements.
Prototype sections, each rated for privacy and security.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 早期的圖面想像一座由高塔與樓梯構成、易進難出的迷宮。接著以三個原型模型，測試懸吊的房間、垂直的樓梯迷宮與開放格架。
captions: 依曝光、監視與可達性分類的參考劇照。
三個重新組合先前元素的原型模型。
原型剖面，各自標示隱私與安全的程度。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The prototypes are combined into one block of stacked layers around a central control tower. Common cell rooms sit on the outer layer, with more isolated rooms toward the centre.
captions: Axonometric and exploded view of the layered block.
Plan with a single entrance and the cell rooms on the outer ring.
Plan with the guard office and control tower at the centre.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些原型被整合成一座圍繞中央控制塔、層層堆疊的量體。一般房間位於外層，隔離程度較高的房間則往中心配置。
captions: 分層量體的軸測圖與爆炸圖。
單一入口、房間位於外圈的平面。
警衛辦公室與控制塔位於中心的平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Renders show a light, open frame where stairs and bridges cross through the courtyard. The sections show how vertical circulation and the cell rooms stack around the tower.
captions: Views from a common cell room and from an isolated section.
Sections of the vertical circulation and the common cell rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 渲染圖呈現一座輕盈開放的框架，樓梯與天橋穿越中庭。剖面則說明垂直動線與房間如何圍繞高塔堆疊。
captions: 從一般房間與隔離區看出去的視角。
垂直動線與一般房間的剖面。

sections.heading: Building a Prison - Weighing Privacy Through Walls, Distance and Paths
sections.body: The project asks how privacy and security might be balanced inside a prison. It treats the building as a study of how walls, distance and paths decide what people can see and where they can reach. Early drawings imagine a maze of towers and stairs that is easy to enter yet hard to leave. Three prototype models then test hanging cells, a vertical maze of stairs and an open grid. These prototypes are finally combined into one block of stacked layers gathered around a central control tower. Ordinary cell rooms sit on the outer layer, and rooms become more isolated the closer they lie to the centre. Renders show a light, open frame in which stairs and bridges cross through the courtyard. The sections explain how vertical circulation and the cell rooms stack up around the tower. A space of confinement becomes a kind of mirror here, inviting reflection on how architecture draws the line between seeing and being seen, and on how much of freedom is shaped by the arrangement of walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 建構一座監獄-在牆與距離之間衡量隱私
zh-Hant.body: 作品探問，在監獄之中，隱私與安全能如何取得平衡？它把建築當作一項研究，觀察牆體、距離與路徑如何決定人們能看見什麼、能抵達哪裡。早期的圖面想像一座由塔與樓梯構成的迷宮，容易進入，卻難以離開。三個原型模型隨後分別測試懸吊的囚室、垂直的樓梯迷宮與開放的格網。這些原型最終被整合為一個層層堆疊的量體，圍繞著中央的控制塔；一般的囚室位於外層，越往中心，房間就越加隔離。渲染圖呈現一個輕盈而開敞的框架，樓梯與天橋在中庭中交錯穿行；剖面則說明垂直動線與囚室如何圍繞塔樓堆疊。監禁的空間在此被當作一面鏡子，讓人重新思考，看見與被看見之間，界線究竟如何被建築所劃定。

pins.title: Implantation of Changeable Wall
pins.description:
Corridors, balconies and moving walls let a city housing block switch between shop and home.

Guangzhou, China | Residential | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 可變牆的植入
zh-Hant.description:
以走廊、陽台與可移動的牆，讓都市住宅量體在店面與住家之間切換。

中國廣州｜住宅｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Cutaway view of the block, with staggered balconies and changeable rooms.
量體剖切透視，可見錯落的陽台與可變的房間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: During a lockdown, a residential community in central Guangzhou saw many shops left empty while residents could not live normally. The project asks how one building can serve both everyday trade and safe home life when that happens.
captions: The dense city and the residential blocks of the Liuyun community in Guangzhou.
Site history: the central axis of Guangzhou and how commerce spread through the community from 1900 to 2020.
Site location and site condition analysis in the city centre.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在封控期間，廣州市中心一處住宅社區的許多店面閒置，居民也無法正常生活。本案探討一棟建築如何在這種情況下，同時支持日常商業與安全的居家生活。
captions: 廣州六運社區的高密度城市與住宅街廓。
基地歷史：廣州中軸線，以及1900至2020年間商業如何在社區中擴張。
位於市中心的基地位置與現況分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied which activities each group in the community lost during the lockdown. Three needs came out of this, and each one led to a strategy, starting with managing the district in different periods.
captions: Demands and strategies: the activities limited during the epidemic, the users' needs and three possible strategies.
Strategy one: the district before, during and after a lockdown.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究社區中各族群在封控期間失去了哪些活動。由此歸納出三項需求，每一項都對應一個策略，首先是依不同時期管理街區。
captions: 需求與策略：疫情期間受限的活動、使用者需求與三種可能策略。
策略一：封控前、封控期間與解除後的街區。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Outside corridors and staggered balconies act as a separate route and a social space in a lockdown, and as shop frontage in normal times. Inside, walls that move let a room change between shop, home and mixed use.
captions: Strategy two: corridors and balconies keep sightlines between neighbours.
Strategy three: generating interior layouts from private to public.
Interior forms shown in perspective plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 外部走廊與錯落的陽台，在封控時作為獨立動線與社交空間，平時則成為店面的延伸。室內則以可移動的牆，讓房間在店面、住家與混合用途之間轉換。
captions: 策略二：走廊與陽台保留鄰里之間的視線。
策略三：從私密到公共生成室內配置。
以透視平面呈現的室內形式。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The floor plan and section show the changeable wall across the whole building. An entrance bathroom works as a buffer, so people who need to stay apart and other residents use separate routes.
captions: Floor plan, section and three ways the wall can change.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 平面與剖面呈現可變牆在整棟建築中的應用。入口浴室作為緩衝區，讓需要隔離的人與其他住戶使用不同的動線。
captions: 平面、剖面與牆體的三種變化方式。

sections.heading: Implantation of Changeable Wall - One Building Shifting Between Lockdown and Everyday Life
sections.body: During a lockdown, a residential community saw many of its shops fall empty while residents could not live their lives normally. The project asks how one building might serve both everyday trade and safe home life if such a time comes again. The student studied which activities each group in the community lost during the lockdown. Three needs emerged from this study, and each one led to a strategy, beginning with managing the district differently in different periods. Outside corridors and staggered balconies act as a separate route and a social space during a lockdown, and as shop frontage in ordinary times. Inside, walls that move allow a room to change between shop, home and mixed use. The floor plan and section show the changeable wall running through the whole building. An entrance bathroom works as a buffer, so that people who need to stay apart and other residents follow separate routes. The building gains a quiet resilience, protecting daily life in exceptional times and becoming lively again once ordinary days return.

zh-Hant.heading: 可變牆的植入-讓同一棟樓在封控與日常間切換
zh-Hant.body: 封控期間，一處住宅社區的許多商店人去樓空，居民的生活也無法正常進行。作品提問，當類似情況再度發生時，同一棟建築能否同時支持日常的商業與安全的居家生活？學生研究了社區中每一個群體在封控期間失去了哪些活動，從中歸納出三項需求，每一項都引出一個策略，首先是依不同時期分別管理街區。外廊與錯落的陽台在封控時成為獨立的動線與社交空間，平時則轉化為店舖的門面；室內可移動的牆，讓房間在商店、住家與混合使用之間自由轉換。平面與剖面呈現可變牆如何貫穿整棟建築；入口處的浴室作為緩衝，讓需要隔離的人與其他住戶各走不同的路線。建築由此具備一種韌性，在非常時期守護生活，在尋常日子裡重新熱鬧起來。

pins.title: Implantation of Welfare Index
pins.description:
A welfare index built from residents' needs guides the renewal of a dense urban village.

Guangzhou, China | Urban village renewal | 2018 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 福祉指數的植入
zh-Hant.description:
以居民需求建立的福祉指數，引導一座高密度城中村的更新。

中國廣州｜城中村更新｜2018｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The renewed village, with roof terraces, planting and residents drawn around it.
更新後的城中村，屋頂露台、綠化與周圍手繪的居民。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Urban villages give low-income residents and new arrivals a cheap place to start, but they are crowded and short of light, air and open space. The project asks how one village in central Guangzhou can become livable while keeping its own texture and scale.
captions: Aerial view of a dense urban village in Guangzhou.
The distribution of urban villages in the built-up district of Guangzhou.
Village types and the ways villages cluster in the city.
How the village grew, period by period.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 城中村為低收入居民與外來者提供低門檻的落腳處，但也擁擠、缺乏採光、通風與開放空間。本案探討廣州市中心的一座城中村，如何在保留原有肌理與尺度的同時變得宜居。
captions: 廣州高密度城中村的鳥瞰。
廣州建成區中城中村的分布。
城中村的類型，以及它們在城市中聚集的方式。
城中村逐期成長的過程。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student ran a field survey and interviews with residents, then drew the village layer by layer. Hand-made section models show how people actually live inside the dense buildings.
captions: The historical development stages of urban villages in Guangzhou.
Exploded analysis of the village, from ground to roofs.
Hand-made section models of villagers' activities inside buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生對居民進行實地問卷與訪談，再逐層繪製這座城中村。手作的剖面模型呈現人們如何在密集的建築中實際生活。
captions: 廣州城中村的歷史發展階段。
城中村的爆炸分析，從地面到屋頂。
呈現村民室內活動的手作剖面模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Using capability theory, the student built a welfare index from living, environment and leisure indicators. Each weak indicator is turned into a design move, such as better room layouts, planting that cleans the air and new leisure space.
captions: Welfare indicators compared against the living environment.
From present situation to improvement direction and strategy.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生運用可行能力理論，以居住、環境與休閒等指標建立福祉指數。每一項偏弱的指標都轉化為設計手法，例如改善房間配置、以植栽淨化空氣，以及增加休閒空間。
captions: 福祉指標與居住環境的對照。
從現況、改善方向到設計策略。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Roof terraces, enclosed courtyards and new interior layouts are implanted into the existing blocks. The village keeps its dense grain but gains greenery, safer lanes and more places to gather.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 屋頂露台、圍合中庭與新的室內配置被植入既有的街廓中。城中村保有原本緊密的紋理，同時多了綠意、更安全的巷道與更多聚集的場所。

sections.heading: Implantation of Welfare Index - Measuring and Mending Life in an Urban Village
sections.body: Urban villages give low-income residents and new arrivals an affordable place to begin, yet they are crowded and short of light, air and open space. The project asks how one village in a city centre could become more livable while keeping its own texture and scale. The student carried out a field survey and interviewed residents, then drew the village layer by layer. Hand-made section models show how people truly live inside the dense buildings. Drawing on capability theory, the design builds a welfare index from indicators of living, environment and leisure. Each weak indicator is turned into a concrete design move, such as better room layouts, planting that cleans the air and new space for leisure. Roof terraces, enclosed courtyards and new interior layouts are then implanted into the existing blocks. The village keeps its tight grain but gains greenery, safer lanes and more places where neighbours can gather. Improvement does not come from tearing everything down. It comes instead from a patient series of careful adjustments, each one answering a measured need.

zh-Hant.heading: 福祉指數的植入-以指標為城中村量身調養
zh-Hant.body: 城中村為低收入居民與新來者提供了低廉的起點，卻也擁擠不堪，缺乏光線、空氣與開放空間。作品探問，市中心的一座城中村，能否在保有自身肌理與尺度的同時，變得更宜居？學生進行田野調查並訪談居民，再把村落一層層繪製出來；手作的剖面模型呈現人們如何在密集的樓房中真實地生活。設計借助可行能力理論，以居住、環境與休閒三類指標建立一套福祉指數，每一項偏弱的指標都被轉化為具體的設計動作，例如改善房間配置、種植能淨化空氣的植物，以及增設休閒空間。屋頂露台、圍合庭院與新的室內配置被植入既有樓房之中，村落保有原本緊密的紋理，同時多了綠意、更安全的巷弄與更多相聚的地方。改善不靠推倒重來，而是一次次細緻的調養。

pins.title: Implantation of City Canopy
pins.description:
An umbrella taken apart becomes a folding canopy for an old shopping street.

Guangzhou, China | Commercial street | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市頂篷的植入
zh-Hant.description:
把雨傘拆解後，轉化為老商業街上可摺疊的頂篷。

中國廣州｜商業街｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A folding canopy spans the street from wall to wall.
可摺疊的頂篷從牆到牆橫跨街道。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Busy old shopping streets have little room, yet they need shade and shelter from the rain. The project asks whether a flexible device, folded into the corner of a building, can open over the street when needed.
captions: Shangxiajiu commercial street: location, street views and site history.
Taking an umbrella apart: opening process and raindrop paths.
The umbrella frame drawn as a pattern.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 熱鬧的老商業街空間有限，卻需要遮陽與避雨。本案探討一種收在建築轉角的彈性裝置，能否在需要時展開覆蓋街道。
captions: 上下九商業街：區位、街景與基地歷史。
拆解雨傘：開啟過程與雨滴軌跡。
以圖案形式繪製的傘骨。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The umbrella frame is reduced to two parts, a node and a fixture, and each is tested in study models. A movement study shows how the parts fold in and stretch out along a wall.
captions: Node design, fixture design and how the parts move.
Physical models of the node fixed to a wall, with and without a cover.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 傘骨被簡化為節點與固定件兩個部分，並各自以研究模型測試。一系列動作研究呈現這些部件如何沿著牆面收合與伸展。
captions: 節點設計、固定件設計與部件的運動方式。
固定在牆上的節點實體模型，有覆面與無覆面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The device is placed along an arcade shopping street in Guangzhou with many shops and visitors. Zoom views show where the canopy meets corners, junctions and wider parts of the street.
captions: Axonometric of the shopping street, with the canopy shown in pink.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 裝置被置入廣州一條商店與遊客眾多的騎樓商業街。放大視圖呈現頂篷與轉角、路口及街道較寬處的關係。
captions: 商業街軸測圖，頂篷以粉紅色標示。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Four canopy strategies grow from one wall bracket to frames that link both sides and turn corners. Each one changes how open or sheltered the street feels, from public to semi-private.
captions: Strategy one: a single bracket covers one side of the street.
Strategy two: two brackets join in the middle to cover the whole street.
Strategy four: a cross-shaped frame covers an intersection.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 四種頂篷策略從單一牆面支架，發展到連接兩側並轉過路口的框架。每一種都改變街道的開放或遮蔽程度，從公共到半私密。
captions: 策略一：單一支架覆蓋街道一側。
策略二：兩側支架在中央相接，覆蓋整條街。
策略四：十字形框架覆蓋路口。

sections.heading: Implantation of City Canopy - An Umbrella Folded Into the Corners of an Arcade
sections.body: Busy old shopping streets have little room to spare, yet they still need shade from the sun and shelter from the rain. The project asks whether a flexible device, folded away into the corner of a building, could open out over the street whenever it is needed. The umbrella frame is reduced to two parts, a node and a fixture, and each is tested in study models. A movement study shows how these parts fold inward and stretch out along a wall. The device is then placed along an arcade shopping street lined with many shops and crowded with visitors. Zoomed views show where the canopy meets corners, junctions and the wider stretches of the street. Four canopy strategies grow from this, ranging from a single wall bracket to frames that link both sides of the street and turn around corners. Each one changes how open or sheltered the street feels, shifting it between public and semi-private. The light intervention keeps the old street at its original scale while offering walkers a shelter that is always close at hand, in sunshine or in rain.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市頂篷的植入-在騎樓轉角收摺一把傘
zh-Hant.body: 熱鬧的老商業街空間有限，卻同樣需要遮陽與避雨。作品提問，能否設計一種靈活的裝置，平時收摺在建築轉角，需要時再向街道展開？研究把傘的骨架簡化為節點與固定件兩個部分，分別在研究模型中測試；一項運動研究則呈現這些構件如何沿著牆面收合與伸展。裝置被放置在一條商店林立、遊人如織的騎樓商業街上，局部放大圖說明頂篷如何回應轉角、交叉口與街道較寬的段落。四種頂篷策略由此發展，從單一的牆面支架，到連接街道兩側、並能轉過街角的框架；每一種都改變了街道的開放與遮蔽程度，讓空間在公共與半私密之間游移。輕巧的介入讓老街保有原有的尺度，也在晴雨之間，為行人撐起一片隨時可得的庇護。

pins.title: Heretical Intervention
pins.description:
One photo is read in many ways and grows into a folded space between two buildings.

Guangzhou, China | Cultural building | 2018 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 異質介入
zh-Hant.description:
一張照片被多角度解讀，生長為兩棟建築之間的摺疊空間。

中國廣州｜文化建築｜2018｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Light falls through folded planes inside the building.
光線穿過建築內部的摺疊面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project starts from one photo the student took and asks how many design ideas a single image can hold. Each way of looking at it, from shape to colour to density, could lead to a different space.
captions: The flower photo the concepts were extracted from.
Drawings that pull outlines, geometry and density out of the photo.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案從學生自己拍攝的一張照片出發，探問一張影像能容納多少設計概念。從形狀、色彩到密度，每一種觀看方式都可能導向不同的空間。
captions: 萃取概念所用的花卉照片。
從照片中抽取輪廓、幾何與密度的圖面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The extracted ideas are sorted into three themes: outline, geometry and density. Each theme is then tested with its own material in small study models.
captions: Study models for each theme.
Wire models that turn outlines into volume.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 抽取出的概念被歸納為輪廓、幾何與密度三個主題。每個主題再以各自的材料，在小型研究模型中測試。
captions: 各主題的研究模型。
把輪廓轉化為量體的線材模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The outline theme and the triangle theme are combined into a space of lines, surfaces and volume. This growth is drawn in section as it climbs between the floors of two blocks.
captions: Close views of the folded paper model.
Section showing the structure growing between floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 輪廓主題與三角形主題被結合為由線、面與量體構成的空間。剖面圖呈現這個構造如何在兩棟量體的樓層之間向上生長。
captions: 摺紙模型的近景。
呈現構造在樓層間生長的剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model sets a cluster of folded triangles between two plain boxes. The folded mass works as a medium that links the two buildings and casts changing light inside.
captions: Physical model, top view.
Physical model, front view.
Physical model, overall view.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型在兩個素淨的方盒之間置入一團摺疊三角形。這個摺疊量體作為媒介連接兩棟建築，並在室內投下變化的光影。
captions: 實體模型俯視。
實體模型正面。
實體模型整體。

sections.heading: Heretical Intervention - A Space Folded Out of a Single Photograph
sections.body: The project begins with a single photograph taken by the student and asks how many design ideas one image can actually hold. Each way of looking at it, whether through shape, colour or density, could lead toward an entirely different space. The ideas drawn out of the photograph are sorted into three themes: outline, geometry and density. Each theme is then tested in small study models using a material suited to it. Next, the outline theme and the triangle theme are combined into a space woven from lines, surfaces and volume. This growth is drawn in section as it climbs between the floors of two separate blocks. The final model sets a cluster of folded triangles between two plain boxes. The folded mass works as a medium that links the two buildings, and it casts constantly shifting light into the rooms inside. The heretical intervention does not destroy the existing order. Instead it allows an unexpected conversation to unfold between two ordinary boxes, proving how much a careful way of seeing can generate.

zh-Hant.heading: 異質介入-一張照片裡摺疊出的空間
zh-Hant.body: 作品從學生親手拍下的一張照片出發，追問：單一影像究竟能容納多少設計想法？每一種觀看方式，無論是形狀、色彩或密度，都可能通往截然不同的空間。從照片中萃取出的想法被整理為三個主題：輪廓、幾何與密度；每個主題再以各自合適的材料，在小型研究模型中反覆測試。接著，輪廓主題與三角形主題被結合起來，生成一個由線、面與體量交織而成的空間，並以剖面描繪它如何在兩棟量體的樓層之間攀升生長。最終模型在兩個素樸的方盒之間，置入一簇摺疊的三角形群體；這個摺疊量體成為連結兩棟建築的媒介，也在室內投下不斷變化的光影。異質的介入沒有破壞原有的秩序，反而讓平凡的盒子之間，生出一段意想不到的對話。

pins.title: Modern Garden Architecture
pins.description:
Principles of the classical garden shape a new commercial complex.

Suzhou, China | Commercial complex | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 現代園林建築
zh-Hant.description:
古典園林的原則塑造一座新的商業綜合體。

中國蘇州｜商業綜合體｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A long section shows shops, offices and courtyards under layered roofs.
長剖面呈現層疊屋頂下的商店、辦公與庭院。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project asks whether the classical Chinese garden still has something to teach modern architecture. It tests this question on a new commercial complex in Suzhou.
captions: Hand sketches of how garden buildings mix daily uses.
Rockery, plants and water taken apart in sketches.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 本案探問中國古典園林是否仍能為現代建築帶來啟發。這個問題在蘇州一座新的商業綜合體中被檢驗。
captions: 手繪速寫：園林建築如何混合日常機能。
以速寫拆解假山、植栽與水景。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Seven principles are drawn out of the garden, from free function and asymmetry to winding routes and borrowed scenery. Each one is turned into simple building forms and roof studies.
captions: Rich functions in the commercial complex: landscape, office, leisure, business and accommodation spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 從園林中歸納出七項原則，包括自由的機能、不對稱、曲折的路徑與借景。每一項都被轉化為簡單的建築形體與屋頂研究。
captions: 商業綜合體中的多元機能：景觀、辦公、休閒、商業與住宿空間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The complex is stacked as layers of shops, public rooms, offices and roof gardens. Curved roofs and broken volumes keep the garden feeling of many small buildings.
captions: Exploded axonometric of the spaces and roofs.
Line elevation of the complex.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 綜合體被堆疊為商業、公共活動、辦公與屋頂花園等層次。彎曲的屋頂與錯落的量體，保留了園林中眾多小建築的感受。
captions: 空間與屋頂的爆炸軸測圖。
綜合體的線稿立面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Low garden buildings sit at the base while a tower rises to meet the city. Inside, a maker space opens floor by floor for different groups of people.
captions: Street renders of the square boxes, irregular spaces and tortuous roads of the complex.
Sections at the four entrances.
The complex set against the city.
Sectional perspective of the maker space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 低矮的園林建築位於基座，塔樓則向上與城市對話。內部的創客空間逐層展開，服務不同的人群。
captions: 綜合體中方盒、不規則空間與曲折道路的街景彩現。
四個入口的剖面。
綜合體與城市的關係。
創客空間的剖透視。

sections.heading: Modern Garden Architecture - Carrying the Classical Garden Into a Contemporary Complex
sections.body: The project asks whether the classical garden still has something to teach modern architecture, and it tests that question on a new commercial complex. Seven principles are drawn out of the garden, ranging from free function and asymmetry to winding routes and borrowed scenery. Each principle is translated into simple building forms and a series of roof studies. The complex is stacked in layers of shops, public rooms, offices and roof gardens. Curved roofs and broken volumes preserve the garden's feeling of many small buildings gathered loosely together. Low garden pavilions sit at the base, while a tower rises to meet the city above them. Inside, a maker space opens floor by floor for different groups of people. The classical garden is not copied here as a style. Instead it is understood as a body of spatial wisdom about shifting views and the interplay of solid and void. Within the scale of commerce, it keeps alive a sense of leisurely wandering and quiet discovery for everyone who passes through.

zh-Hant.heading: 現代園林建築-讓古典園林走進當代綜合體
zh-Hant.body: 作品探問，古典園林是否仍能為現代建築帶來啟發？這個問題被放在一座新的商業綜合體上加以檢驗。研究從園林中提煉出七項原則，從自由的功能、不對稱的布局，到迂迴的路徑與借景，每一項原則都被轉化為簡單的建築形體與屋頂研究。設計把綜合體堆疊為商店、公共空間、辦公室與屋頂花園等層次；曲線屋頂與破碎的量體，保留了園林中許多小建築錯落並置的感受。低矮的園林建築安置在基部，塔樓則向上升起，迎向城市；室內的創客空間逐層開放，服務不同的人群。古典園林在此並非被複製的樣式，而是一套關於移步換景、虛實相生的空間智慧，在商業的尺度中，為人們保留了一份漫遊與發現的從容。

pins.title: Wind, Always With Me
pins.description:
Ventilation towers bring cool air and shared space to an urban village.

Guangzhou, China | Ventilation tower | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 風，與我同在
zh-Hant.description:
通風塔為城中村帶來涼風與共享空間。

中國廣州｜通風塔｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A new ventilation tower rises between dense village blocks.
新的通風塔在密集的村落樓房之間升起。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Homes in a dense urban village in Guangzhou are hot, dark and poorly ventilated. Residents also lack shared space for daily activities.
captions: Site analysis: the urban village on the aerial map, the rise of garment factories and the changes in village population.
A profile of the village with its new towers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州一處密集城中村的住宅炎熱、昏暗且通風不良。居民也缺少日常活動的共享空間。
captions: 基地分析：航拍圖上的城中村、成衣工廠的興起與村落人口變化。
加入通風塔後的村落輪廓。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The project studies the traditional wind-catching tower, which pulls cool air down like a chimney in reverse. Several air-trap shapes and duct layouts are compared before one is chosen.
captions: A comic of daily life in the stifling lanes and the ventilation tower.
Air trap shapes, duct design and staged cooling.
How the tower is generated.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 本案研究傳統的捕風塔，它像反向的煙囪般把涼風引入室內。設計比較了多種捕風口形狀與風道配置後才確定方案。
captions: 描繪悶熱巷弄日常生活與通風塔的漫畫。
捕風口形狀、風道設計與分段降溫。
通風塔的生成過程。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Towers come in large, medium and small sizes to fit wide plots and narrow lanes. Light modules for living, work and leisure are stacked around the central duct.
captions: Strategies for large, medium and small towers.
Exploded view of the tower.
Floor plans and functional modules.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 通風塔分為大、中、小三種尺度，以適應寬地塊與窄巷。居住、工作與休閒的輕量模組圍繞中央風道堆疊。
captions: 大、中、小型通風塔的策略。
通風塔的爆炸圖。
平面與機能模組。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A timber model tests the tower, its stairs and its stacked homes. It shows how one structure can cool rooms and add shared space at the same time.
captions: Physical model of the ventilation tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 木構模型檢驗了通風塔、樓梯與堆疊的居住空間。它展示一個結構如何同時為室內降溫並增加共享空間。
captions: 通風塔的實體模型。

sections.heading: Wind, Always With Me - A Tower That Draws Cool Air Into Stifling Lanes
sections.body: Homes in a dense urban village are hot, dark and poorly ventilated, and residents have little shared space for their daily activities. The project studies the traditional wind-catching tower, which works like a chimney in reverse and pulls cool air down into the rooms below.
