Several shapes of air trap and several duct layouts are compared before one combination is finally chosen. The towers come in large, medium and small sizes so that they can fit both wide plots and narrow lanes. Light modules for living, working and leisure are stacked around the central duct. A timber model tests the tower, its stairs and the stacked homes that cling to it. It shows how a single structure can cool rooms and add shared space at the same time. Wind is no longer just weather that happens to pass by. It is carefully caught, guided and shared out until it becomes part of everyday life for residents. Old wisdom answers contemporary crowding, bringing a steady breath of coolness into the lanes.

zh-Hant.heading: 風與我同在-為悶熱巷弄引入涼風的塔
zh-Hant.body: 高密度城中村裡的住宅悶熱、昏暗而通風不良，居民也缺乏進行日常活動的共享空間。研究從傳統的捕風塔出發，它像一座反向的煙囪，把涼爽的空氣引導下來；設計比較了多種集風口的形狀與風道的配置，最後選定其中一種。捕風塔依尺寸分為大、中、小三種，以適應寬闊的地塊與狹窄的巷弄；居住、工作與休閒的輕量模組，則圍繞中央風道層層堆疊。木構模型測試塔體、樓梯與疊合的住宅，呈現同一個構造如何同時為房間降溫，並增添共享的空間。風在這裡不再只是偶然吹過的天氣，而被細心地捕捉、引導與分配，成為居民日常生活的一部分。古老的智慧回應當代的擁擠，為巷弄帶來一縷持續的清涼。

pins.title: Climate Adaptive Architecture
pins.description:
A museum learns from vernacular houses to stay cool without machines.

Guangzhou, China | Museum | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 氣候適應性建築
zh-Hant.description:
一座向傳統民居學習、不靠機械也能保持涼爽的博物館。

中國廣州｜博物館｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Ring-shaped halls of the museum sit under a sweeping arch.
環形展廳坐落在一道大弧形屋頂之下。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Guangzhou is hot, humid and rainy for much of the year. The project asks how a museum can stay comfortable without relying on heavy machines.
captions: Elements in climate adaptive design, from landscapes to traditional buildings and devices.
Research on physical comfort in Guangzhou, the site climate evaluation and the exhibition vision.
Climate elements drawn from vernacular buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州一年中大部分時間炎熱、潮濕且多雨。本案探問一座博物館如何不依賴大量機械也能保持舒適。
captions: 氣候適應設計中的元素，從地景到傳統建築與裝置。
廣州體感舒適度研究、基地氣候評估與展覽願景。
從傳統民居中提取的氣候元素。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Round earth houses, stilt houses, cave dwellings, rain corridors and arcades are studied as climate tools. Each one shows a simple way to shade, ventilate or keep out rain.
captions: Hand sketch of a round earth house as a case study.
Vernacular elements turned into new building parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圓形土樓、干欄式建築、窯洞、風雨廊與騎樓都被視為應對氣候的工具來研究。每一種都展示了遮陽、通風或防雨的簡單方法。
captions: 以圓形土樓為案例的手繪速寫。
傳統元素轉化為新的建築構件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The museum is split into a mountain zone and a water zone across the site. Ring halls, raised floors and covered walks are layered into one landscape.
captions: Axonometric of the mountain and river zones.
Exploded layers of the water pavilion.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 博物館在基地上分為山區與水區兩部分。環形展廳、架空樓板與有頂步道被層疊成一片完整的地景。
captions: 山區與河區的軸測圖。
水上展館的分層爆炸圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the water pavilion, visitors turn wheels that pump water and drive fans to cool the hall. A timber model tests the ring structure and its details.
captions: Water-wheel cooling equipment.
Physical model of the museum.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在水上展館中，參觀者轉動水車抽水並帶動風扇，為展廳降溫。木構模型檢驗了環形結構與其細部。
captions: 水車驅動的降溫裝置。
博物館的實體模型。

sections.heading: Climate Adaptive Architecture - A Cool Museum That Learns From Vernacular Homes
sections.body: The city is hot, humid and rainy for much of the year. The project asks whether a museum could stay comfortable without relying on heavy machinery. Round earth houses, stilt houses, cave dwellings, rain corridors and arcades are each studied as tools for dealing with climate. Every one of them reveals a modest kind of wisdom for shading, ventilating or keeping out the rain. The design splits the museum into a mountain zone and a water zone that stretch across the site. Ring halls, raised floors and covered walks are layered into a single continuous landscape. In the water pavilion, visitors turn wheels that drive pumps and fans, cooling the hall with their own hands, so that viewing the exhibition becomes an act of bodily participation. A timber model tests the ring structure and its details. Traditional building experience is understood afresh here. It is not treated as nostalgic form but as a design method that remains effective in the face of heat, damp and heavy rain.

zh-Hant.heading: 氣候適應性建築-向傳統民居學習的涼爽博物館
zh-Hant.body: 這座城市一年之中大半時間炎熱、潮濕而多雨。作品提問，博物館能否在不依賴大型機械的情況下保持舒適？研究把圓形土樓、干欄式住屋、窯洞、雨廊與騎樓視為應對氣候的工具，逐一分析；每一種都展現出遮陽、通風或擋雨的樸素智慧。設計將博物館分為山區與水區，橫跨整個基地；環形展廳、架高樓板與有頂步道層層疊合，構成一片完整的地景。在水的展亭中，參觀者轉動輪盤，推動水泵與風扇，親手為展廳帶來涼意，觀展也因此成為一次身體力行的參與。木構模型則測試環形結構及其細部。傳統的營造經驗在此被重新理解，不再只是懷舊的形式，而是面對氣候時依然有效的設計方法。

pins.title: Container Kindergarten
pins.description:
Seven containers give a crowded neighbourhood a kindergarten with play on every roof.

Xiangtan, China | Kindergarten | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 貨櫃幼兒園
zh-Hant.description:
七個貨櫃量體，讓擁擠的社區擁有一座屋頂也能遊戲的幼兒園。

中國湘潭｜幼兒園｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Physical model of the kindergarten and its courtyards.
幼兒園與庭院的實體模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The kindergarten sits in a dense residential community in Xiangtan with little open ground. Children lack space to play and the old building gives them little to enjoy.
captions: Father and child's day, site photos and the existing problems of the community, with the proposed solutions.
General layout of the site.
Axonometric of the container buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這所幼兒園位於湘潭一個密集的住宅社區，開放用地很少。孩子缺少遊戲的空間，舊建築也難以帶給他們樂趣。
captions: 親子日常、基地照片與社區現有問題，以及提出的解決方案。
基地總平面。
貨櫃式建築群的軸測圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site plan is first divided by function and then rotated to add interest. A corridor is set up to tie each part together.
captions: Steps of the plane generation.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 總平面先依功能劃分，再加以旋轉以增加趣味。接著設置一條廊道把各部分串連起來。
captions: 平面生成的步驟。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A U-shaped layout holds seven containers around an inner and an outer courtyard. Classrooms, dining and play rooms are stacked and linked by ramps and terraces.
captions: Exploded layout with the floor plans.
Elevations and a section through the courtyard.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: U 形布局把七個貨櫃量體圍繞內外兩個庭院排列。教室、餐廳與活動室層層疊放，並以坡道和平台相連。
captions: 分層布局與各層平面。
立面與穿過庭院的剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: An air trail lets children walk from the ground up to the roof and lets parents watch over them. The playground rises across the roofs so the small site gains more room for activity.
captions: Render of the kindergarten entrance.
Render of the outdoor parent trail.
Overview of the physical model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一條空中步道讓孩子能從地面走上屋頂，也讓家長能從旁看顧。遊戲場沿屋頂抬升，使小小的基地獲得更多活動空間。
captions: 幼兒園入口的彩現。
戶外家長步道的渲染圖。
實體模型全景。

sections.heading: Container Kindergarten - An Air Trail Laid Across the Roofs for Children
sections.body: The kindergarten sits within a dense residential community where open ground is scarce. Children lack room to play, and the old building offers them little to enjoy. The site plan is first divided by function and then rotated to add variety, while a corridor is introduced to tie all of the parts together. A U-shaped layout holds seven containers arranged around an inner courtyard and an outer one. Classrooms, dining spaces and playrooms are stacked on top of one another and linked by ramps and terraces. An air trail lets children walk all the way from the ground up to the roof, while parents can keep watch over them from nearby. The playground climbs across the roofs, so the small site gains a great deal more room for activity. Containers, once cold boxes made for shipping goods, are transformed here into vessels for childhood. Limited land does not become a constraint. It instead gives rise to a vertical way of playing, in which children run, climb and explore among the rising and falling levels.

zh-Hant.heading: 貨櫃幼兒園-在屋頂上為孩子鋪一條空中小徑
zh-Hant.body: 這所幼兒園位於高密度的住宅社區之中，開放地面十分有限；孩子缺乏遊戲的空間，老舊的建築也難以帶來樂趣。設計先依功能劃分基地，再將配置旋轉以增添變化，並設置一條走廊串起各個部分。U 形的配置容納七個貨櫃，圍合出內外兩座庭院；教室、餐廳與遊戲室層層堆疊，以坡道與露台相互連接。一條空中步道讓孩子從地面一路走上屋頂，也讓家長能在旁照看；遊戲場跨越各個屋頂向上延伸，小小的基地因此多出了許多活動的餘地。貨櫃原本是運輸貨物的冰冷盒子，在此被轉化為承載童年的容器。有限的土地沒有成為限制，反而促成一種立體的遊戲方式，讓孩子在高低起伏之間奔跑、攀爬與探索。

pins.title: Museum of Intimate Relationship
pins.description:
A riverside museum turns water, wind and light into a walk through the parts of love.

Guangzhou, China | Museum | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 親密關係博物館
zh-Hant.description:
一座河岸博物館，把水、風與光化為穿越愛情各個面向的散步。

中國廣州｜博物館｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Sections along the visitor route, from dark rooms to open water.
沿參觀路線的剖面，從幽暗空間走向開闊水面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: When love fades, both partners are affected. The museum asks whether walking through different spaces can help couples understand love and keep it alive.
captions: Background: why couples break up, with statistics on marriages and divorces, and a map of the facets of love.
Map of the riverside site.
Analysis of the site, its natural conditions and the route.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 當愛情逐漸消退，雙方都會受到影響。這座博物館探問，走過不同的空間能否幫助伴侶理解愛並讓它延續。
captions: 背景：伴侶分手的原因、婚姻與離婚統計，以及愛的面向關係圖。
河岸基地的地圖。
基地、自然條件與路線的分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Love is read as three parts, intimacy, passion and commitment, which mix into eight types. Each type is matched with a mix of water, wind and light and the mood it creates.
captions: Conditions, space feelings and mood swings for each type of love.
Comparison of two ground conditions on the site.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 愛被解讀為親密、激情與承諾三個部分，並組合出八種類型。每一種類型都對應一組水、風與光的條件，以及它帶來的情緒。
captions: 各種愛情類型對應的環境條件、空間感受與情緒起伏。
基地上兩種地面狀態的比較。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The museum opens to the city instead of closing itself off from it. Small spaces test wind corridors, underwater galleries and rooms with strong or weak light.
captions: Design concept and plane generation.
Studies of wind, water and light spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 博物館向城市開放，而不是自我封閉。一系列小空間分別測試風廊、水下展廊，以及光線強弱不同的房間。
captions: 設計概念與平面生成。
風、水與光的空間研究。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Three routes, light for commitment, water for intimacy and wind for passion, lead visitors from dark spaces to the open river. Along the way the feeling of each space changes step by step.
captions: Function nodes and the three routes.
Section perspective along the water.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三條路線分別以光代表承諾、以水代表親密、以風代表激情，引導參觀者從幽暗空間走向開闊的河面。沿途每個空間的感受都逐步轉變。
captions: 功能節點與三條路線。
沿水面的剖透視。

sections.heading: Museum of Intimate Relationship - Rereading Love Through Water, Wind and Light
sections.body: When love begins to fade, both partners feel its loss. The museum asks whether walking through different spaces could help couples understand love and keep it alive. Love is read as three parts, intimacy, passion and commitment, which combine into eight distinct types. Each type is matched with a particular mix of water, wind and light, together with the mood that mix creates. The museum opens itself to the city instead of closing itself away. A series of small spaces tests wind corridors, underwater galleries and rooms where light is either strong or faint. Three routes then guide visitors forward, with light standing for commitment, water for intimacy and wind for passion, leading from dark interiors out toward the open river. Along the way the feeling of each space shifts step by step, much like the rise and settling of a long relationship. Abstract emotion is given a temperature that can be felt on the skin, and partners walking side by side may come to see each other anew.

zh-Hant.heading: 親密關係博物館-以水、風與光重讀愛
zh-Hant.body: 當愛情逐漸褪色，兩個人都會受到影響。這座博物館提問，穿行於不同的空間，能否幫助伴侶理解愛，並讓它延續下去？研究把愛解讀為親密、激情與承諾三個部分，三者交織出八種類型；每一種類型再對應一組水、風與光的組合，以及它所營造的情緒。博物館向城市敞開，而非把自己封閉起來；一系列小空間分別測試風的廊道、水下展廊，以及光線強弱不同的房間。三條路線引導參觀者前行：光代表承諾，水代表親密，風代表激情，從幽暗的空間一路走向開闊的河岸。沿途每個空間的感受一步步轉變，像一段關係中的起伏與沉澱。抽象的情感因此有了可以觸摸的溫度，伴侶也得以在同行之中，重新看見彼此。

pins.title: Urban Street Renovation and Flyover
pins.description:
A kapok-shaped flyover and three new street styles give walkers room in a busy district.

Guangzhou, China | Flyover and street | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市街道改造與天橋設計
zh-Hant.description:
一座木棉造型的天橋與三種新街道風格，為繁忙地區的行人留出空間。

中國廣州｜天橋與街道｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial render of the diamond-shaped flyover and its central spire.
菱形天橋與中央尖塔的鳥瞰渲染圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Busy roads in the Tianhe District cut the area apart and leave walkers with little room to stop. The streets also lack a clear local character.
captions: Site analysis: the Tianhe district, historical changes to the site and streets, demographic demand and local elements.
Analysis of traffic flow at the junction.
Activities the flyover should hold.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 天河區繁忙的道路把地區切割開來，行人幾乎沒有停留的空間。街道也缺少鮮明的在地特色。
captions: 基地分析：天河區、基地與街道的歷史變遷、人口需求與在地元素。
路口交通流線分析。
天橋需要容納的活動分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The plan starts from a diamond that follows the edges of the road. It then takes the petals of the kapok, the city flower, as its shape.
captions: Steps of the plane generation.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 平面從一個貼合道路邊緣的菱形開始。接著以市花木棉的花瓣作為形態。
captions: 平面生成的步驟。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: An outer ring keeps walkers moving while an inner ring gives them places to stay and rest. A central spire holds the deck and links it to the skyline of the district.
captions: Exploded view of the flyover.
Section through the flyover.
General layout at the junction.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 外環讓行人順暢通行，內環則提供停留與休息的地方。中央尖塔拉起橋面，並與地區的天際線呼應。
captions: 天橋的分層爆炸圖。
穿過天橋的剖面。
路口的總平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Below the flyover, the old roads are moved and planted to make streets for walking. Three street styles, classical garden, local flower and future frame, give each part its own feel.
captions: Plan of the renovated street.
Three street styles.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在天橋下方，舊道路被調整並加以綠化，成為適合步行的街道。古典園林、在地花卉與未來框架三種街道風格，讓每一段都有自己的氛圍。
captions: 改造後街道的平面。
三種街道風格。

sections.heading: Urban Street Renovation and Flyover - A Kapok Blossom Opening Above the Traffic
sections.body: Busy roads cut the district apart and leave walkers with almost nowhere to stop, while the streets themselves lack any clear local character. The design begins with a diamond that follows the edges of the road. It then takes the petals of the kapok, the flower of the city, as the source of its shape. An outer ring keeps pedestrians moving, while an inner ring gives them places to linger and rest. A central spire holds up the deck and links the flyover to the skyline of the district. Beneath the flyover, the old roads are shifted and planted to create streets made for walking. Three street styles, a classical garden, a local flower and a future frame, give each stretch its own atmosphere and personality. Movement and pause are arranged in separate layers. Traffic is no longer only a force that divides the city, and the flyover grows from a simple crossing into a public place to stand, look out and feel the identity of the city, like a flower opening quietly above the traffic.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市街道改造與天橋-在車流之上綻放一朵木棉
zh-Hant.body: 繁忙的道路把整個區域切割開來，行人幾乎沒有可以停下的地方，街道也缺乏清晰的在地特色。設計從一個順應道路邊緣的菱形出發，再以市花木棉的花瓣作為形態的來源。外環讓行人持續通行，內環則提供停留與休憩的空間；中央的塔尖承托橋面，並把天橋與區域的天際線連結起來。天橋之下，原有道路被調整並種植綠意，轉化為適合步行的街道。三種街道風格，分別是古典園林、在地花卉與未來框架，讓每一段街道擁有各自的氛圍與性格。通行與停駐在此被分層安排，交通不再只是切割城市的力量，天橋也從單純的過街設施，蛻變為一處可以駐足、眺望與感受城市身分的公共場所，像一朵在車流之上靜靜綻放的花。

pins.title: Residential in Green Space
pins.description:
Stepped green housing offers affordable homes to people who move to the city for work.

Shenzhen, China | Housing | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 綠色空間中的住宅
zh-Hant.description:
層層退台的綠色住宅，為到城市工作的人提供負擔得起的家。

中國深圳｜住宅｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Layers of the green roof over the housing blocks.
住宅群上方綠色屋頂的分層圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many people who move to Shenzhen for work cannot afford homes in the city centre. Low-income families, new graduates, people looking for work and people with disabilities all need a place to live.
captions: Site status on the aerial map, the living conditions of migrants over time and the end-user requirements.
Building program and links to the city.
Ways to combine buildings with green space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 許多到深圳工作的人負擔不起市中心的住房。低收入家庭、應屆畢業生、正在求職的人與行動不便者都需要一個安身之處。
captions: 航拍圖上的基地現況、外來人口居住條件的演變與使用者需求。
建築計畫與城市的連結。
建築與綠地結合的方式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Green space and buildings in the city are often kept apart. The project tests balconies, roof gardens, courtyards and green walls as ways to bring them together.
captions: Steps of the block generation.
Apartment types and the functional partition.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 城市中的綠地與建築往往彼此分離。本案測試陽台、屋頂花園、庭院與綠牆，作為讓兩者結合的方法。
captions: 量體生成的步驟。
各種戶型與功能分區。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The blocks are divided by function and stepped so that ramps and green terraces run through them. Several apartment types serve the different groups of residents.
captions: Standard floor plans of the two blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 量體依功能劃分並層層退台，讓坡道與綠色平台貫穿其中。多種戶型對應不同的居民群體。
captions: 兩棟住宅的標準層平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Solar panels, sun visors, green roofs and vertical planting help lower the energy use of the homes. Ramps let residents with disabilities walk through the whole building.
captions: Solar panel and building section model.
Roof structure, sun visor and wetland section.
Vertical greening model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 太陽能板、遮陽板、綠色屋頂與垂直綠化幫助降低住宅的能耗。坡道讓行動不便的居民也能走遍整棟建築。
captions: 太陽能板與建築剖面模型。
屋頂構造、遮陽板與濕地剖面。
垂直綠化模型。

sections.heading: Residential in Green Space - Homes for Newcomers Woven Into Greenery
sections.body: Many people who move to a large city for work cannot afford homes near its centre. Low-income families, new graduates, people looking for work and people with disabilities all need somewhere to live. The study finds that green space and buildings in the city are usually kept apart, so it tests balconies, roof gardens, courtyards and green walls as ways of bringing the two back together. The blocks are divided by function and stepped, allowing ramps and green terraces to run right through them. Several apartment types answer the needs of different groups of residents. Solar panels, sun visors, green roofs and vertical planting work together to lower the energy use of the homes. Continuous ramps let residents with disabilities walk through the entire building without barriers. Housing becomes more than a room that keeps out wind and rain. It becomes a green landscape open to everyone, where those who have only just arrived in the city can still find a sense of ease, dignity and belonging.

zh-Hant.heading: 綠色空間中的住宅-讓城市新來者住進綠意
zh-Hant.body: 許多為了工作而來到這座城市的人，負擔不起市中心的住宅；低收入家庭、應屆畢業生、求職者與身心障礙者，都需要一處安身之所。研究發現，城市中的綠地與建築往往彼此分離，因此逐一測試陽台、屋頂花園、庭院與綠牆，作為把兩者重新結合的方式。設計依功能把量體分區，並以階梯狀錯落配置，讓坡道與綠色露台貫穿其間；多種公寓類型則分別回應不同住戶的需求。太陽能板、遮陽板、綠屋頂與垂直植栽共同降低住宅的能源消耗；連續的坡道讓行動不便的住戶也能走遍整棟建築。住宅因此不只是一個遮風避雨的房間，而是一片向所有人敞開的綠色地景，讓初來乍到的人，也能在城市裡找到一份從容與歸屬。

pins.title: The City Dehumidifier
pins.description:
A stepped building on a slope cools and dries the air through ground pipes and plant roots.

Xiangtan, China | Wellness building | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市除濕機
zh-Hant.description:
一座沿坡地退台的建築，透過地下管道與植物根系為空氣降溫除濕。

中國湘潭｜養生建築｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Model of the building with its timber grille.
帶有木格柵的建築模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In the humid south of China, many people feel that damp air weighs on the body. The project asks whether a building itself can work as a dehumidifier.
captions: What the damp 'Shi Qi' does to the organs, and four common ways of removing it.
Moist wind comes in and dry air flows out.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在潮濕的中國南方，許多人覺得濕氣會加重身體的負擔。本案探問建築本身能否像除濕機一樣運作。
captions: 「濕氣」對器官造成的疾病，以及四種常見的祛濕方式。
潮濕的風進入，乾燥的空氣流出。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Local habits for removing damp were grouped into four ways: sweating in a sauna, massage, exercise and diet. Each way became one type of space for its own group of users.
captions: User relationship analysis linking the four ways of removing damp to spaces and user groups.
Section model showing the paths of the air.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 在地祛濕的習慣被歸納為四種方式：桑拿出汗、按摩、運動與飲食。每一種方式都成為一類空間，服務各自的使用者。
captions: 使用者關係分析：將四種祛濕方式對應到空間與使用族群。
呈現空氣路徑的剖面模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Outside air is first drawn through pipes in the ground, where it cools and loses water. It then passes a layer of plant aerial roots, which take up more of the moisture.
captions: Floor plans from the ground floor up.
Sections A and B across the sloping site.
Exploded view of the four kinds of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 室外空氣先被引入地下管道，在其中降溫並除去水分。接著空氣通過植物氣根層，進一步吸收濕氣。
captions: 由地面層往上的各層平面。
橫跨坡地的A、B剖面。
四類空間的爆炸圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The building steps up the slope, so visitors pass the four kinds of space in turn along one route. Wall and roof details show how the grilles, green roof and root layer handle the air.
captions: Detailed vertical section of the pool wall.
Wall section with the aerial-root layer.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 建築沿坡地層層升起，訪客沿著一條動線依序經過四類空間。牆身與屋頂的細部說明格柵、綠屋頂與氣根層如何處理空氣。
captions: 池畔牆身的詳細剖面。
帶有氣根層的牆身剖面。

sections.heading: The City Dehumidifier - A Building That Lifts the Damp From the Body
sections.body: In the humid south, many people feel that damp air sits heavily on the body. The project asks whether a building could itself work as a dehumidifier. Local habits for driving out damp are grouped into four ways, namely sweating in a sauna, massage, exercise and diet. Each way becomes one type of space serving its own group of users. Outside air is first drawn through pipes buried in the ground, where it cools and releases water as it passes through the soil. It then moves through a layer of plant aerial roots, which take up still more of the moisture. The building steps up the slope, so visitors pass through the four kinds of space in turn along one continuous route, almost like completing a course of care from outside to inside. Wall and roof details show how grilles, a green roof and the root layer work together to treat the air. A burden of climate becomes the starting point of design, and the building enters into a gentle, attentive relationship of care with the body.

zh-Hant.heading: 城市除濕機-一座替身體卸下濕氣的建築
zh-Hant.body: 在潮濕的南方，許多人都覺得濕氣沉沉地壓在身上。作品提問，建築本身能否成為一台除濕機？研究把在地人祛除濕氣的習慣歸納為四種方式：在蒸氣房裡出汗、按摩、運動與飲食，每一種方式都轉化為一類空間，服務各自的使用者。設計讓室外空氣先經由埋在地下的管道導入，在土壤中降溫並凝結出水分；接著再穿過一層植物氣根，讓根系吸收更多濕氣。建築沿著山坡層層升起，參觀者沿著同一條路線，依序經過四種空間，彷彿完成一趟由外而內的調養。牆體與屋頂的細部則說明格柵、綠屋頂與氣根層如何協同處理空氣。氣候的困擾在此被轉化為設計的出發點，建築也因此與身體建立起一種細膩而溫和的照護關係。

pins.title: Listening to the Sound
pins.description:
A noisy green square in the city becomes a quiet place for five groups of users.

Guangzhou, China | Public square | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聆聽聲音
zh-Hant.description:
城市中一處嘈雜的綠色廣場，成為五類使用者的安靜去處。

中國廣州｜公共廣場｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial view of the square and its activity zones.
廣場與各活動區的鳥瞰圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site is a green square in busy central Guangzhou, with many trees but little to do. Noise from the roads around it also keeps people from staying.
captions: Noise levels from the roads around the site.
Survey of five groups of users on the site.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地是廣州繁忙市中心的一處綠色廣場，樹木很多，卻少有可以做的事。周邊道路的噪音也讓人們不願停留。
captions: 周邊道路的噪音分布。
基地上五類使用者的調查。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The survey found five main groups of users, from office workers to local residents and people without stable homes. A shared management system links shops, studios, a museum and housing to keep the square alive over time.
captions: Management system that ties the uses together.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 調查找出五類主要使用者，從上班族、在地居民到沒有穩定住處的人。一套共同的管理系統串連商店、工作室、博物館與住宿，讓廣場長久保持活力。
captions: 串連各種用途的管理系統。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The routes were redrawn into curving paths that open a large central space among the trees. Small activity modules give each group of users a place to play, rest or perform.
captions: Masterplan of the square.
From the original routes to the refined design.
Activity modules for the five groups of users.
Eight scenes the central square can host.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 動線被重新繪製成彎曲的路徑，在樹林中打開一處大型中央空間。小型活動模組讓每一類使用者都有遊戲、休息或表演的地方。
captions: 廣場總平面圖。
從原有動線到深化設計。
對應五類使用者的活動模組。
中央廣場可容納的八種場景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Buildings on the edge use green walls, laminated glass and soundproof walls to block the noise of the city. The central museum is cut open in section so that air and light move through it.
captions: Green wall sections of the edge buildings.
Section of the central museum.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 邊界建築以綠牆、夾層玻璃與隔音牆阻擋城市噪音。中央博物館在剖面上被打開，讓空氣與光線貫穿其中。
captions: 邊界建築的綠牆剖面。
中央博物館剖面。

sections.heading: Listening to the Sound - Inviting People Back Into a Green Square Amid the Noise
sections.body: The site is a green square in a busy city centre, full of trees yet offering very little to do. Noise from the roads around it also keeps people from staying for long. A survey identifies five main groups of users, ranging from office workers and local residents to people without stable homes. A shared management system then links shops, studios, a museum and housing, so that the square can stay lively over time rather than for a single season. The design redraws the existing routes as curving paths that open up a large central space among the trees. Small activity modules give each group of users a place to play, rest or perform. Buildings along the edge use green walls, laminated glass and soundproof walls to hold back the noise of the city. The central museum is cut open in section so that air and light can move freely through it. The square is no longer a green backdrop to hurry past. It becomes a public place that has been listened to carefully, and where people may begin to listen to one another.

zh-Hant.heading: 聆聽聲音-讓喧囂中的綠地重新有人停留
zh-Hant.body: 基地是繁忙市中心的一處綠色廣場，樹木茂密，卻沒有什麼可做的事；周邊道路的噪音，也讓人們難以停留。調查歸納出五個主要的使用族群，從上班族、在地居民，到沒有穩定居所的人；一套共享的管理系統再把商店、工作室、博物館與住宅串連起來，讓廣場能長久保持活力。設計把原有路線重新繪製為曲線步道，在樹林之間打開一片寬闊的中央空間；小型活動模組則為每一群使用者提供遊戲、休息或表演的場所。邊緣的建築以綠牆、夾層玻璃與隔音牆阻擋城市的噪音；位於中央的博物館在剖面上被切開，讓空氣與光線得以穿流其中。廣場不再只是穿越的綠色背景，而成為一處被細心聆聽、也讓人願意傾聽彼此的公共場所。

pins.title: Signals of the Heart
pins.description:
Five themed spaces turn a meeting between strangers into a slow route of finding each other.

Guangzhou, China | Interactive pavilion | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 心的訊號
zh-Hant.description:
五個主題空間，讓陌生人之間的相遇成為一條慢慢找到彼此的路線。

中國廣州｜互動展亭｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The ice-breaking dance space under the glass dome.
玻璃穹頂下的破冰舞蹈空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In many city parks in China, parents look for partners for their grown children, while young people want to choose love freely. The project looks for a new way to balance the wishes of both sides.
captions: A timeline of courtship and marriage customs in China, from ancient times to today's dating apps.
Ramp, glowing pillars and dome in layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在中國許多城市公園裡，父母為成年子女尋找對象，而年輕人則希望自由選擇愛情。本案尋找一種平衡雙方期望的新方式。
captions: 中國求偶與婚俗的時間軸，從古代到今日的交友軟體。
坡道、發光柱與穹頂的分層。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Data and field research traced how these meeting customs began and why they still exist. The design turns one meeting into a route of five themed spaces for eight participants.
captions: A comic of the app guiding a couple to the pavilion in Haizhu Park.
The wall of memories with pictures and videos.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 透過資料與田野研究，追溯這些相親習俗的起源與至今仍存在的原因。設計把一次相遇轉化為一條由五個主題空間組成、供八位參與者體驗的路線。
captions: 交友軟體引導情侶前往海珠公園展亭的漫畫。
放置照片與影片的記憶之牆。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: After a dance, participants learn about each other at a wall of boxes and then search for coloured pillars among metal curtains. Each colour stands for one person, so choosing becomes a slow game of finding.
captions: Layers of the choosing device.
Metal curtain and pillars among the trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一場舞蹈之後，參與者在盒子之牆前認識彼此，接著在金屬簾幕間尋找彩色光柱。每一種顏色代表一個人，讓選擇成為一場慢慢尋找的遊戲。
captions: 選擇裝置的分層。
樹林中的金屬簾幕與光柱。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Pairs then share a small cinema with quiet spaces for two under the stairs. In a final maze, a phone app signals when two people who chose each other come close.
captions: Stepped cinema space for the pairs.
Layers of glass, mirror and concrete in the maze.
The heartbeat maze.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 配對者接著共享一座小型電影院，階梯下設有兩人的安靜空間。在最後的迷宮中，當互相選擇的兩人靠近時，手機應用程式會發出訊號。
captions: 供配對者使用的階梯電影空間。
迷宮中玻璃、鏡面與混凝土的分層。
心跳迷宮。

sections.heading: Signals of the Heart - Turning Courtship Into a Slow Game of Finding
sections.body: In many city parks, parents search for partners on behalf of their grown children, while young people long to choose love freely for themselves. The project looks for a new way to balance the wishes of both sides. Data and field research trace how these meeting customs began and why they still persist today. The design turns a single meeting into a route of five themed spaces shared by eight participants. After a dance, participants learn about one another at a wall of boxes and then search for coloured pillars among shimmering metal curtains. Each colour stands for one person, so that choosing becomes a slow and playful game of finding. Pairs who match then share a small cinema, with quiet spaces for two tucked beneath the stairs. In a final maze, a phone app sends a signal when two people who have chosen each other come close. Space intervenes gently here, giving both the hopes of the older generation and the feelings of the young a place where they can be heard.

zh-Hant.heading: 心的訊號-讓相遇成為一場緩慢的尋找
zh-Hant.body: 在許多城市公園裡，父母為成年子女尋找伴侶，年輕人卻渴望自由地選擇愛情。作品試圖為雙方的心願找到一種新的平衡。研究透過數據與田野調查，追溯這種相親習俗如何興起，又為何延續至今。設計把一次相遇轉化為一條路徑，由五個主題空間組成，供八位參與者共同經歷。一場舞蹈之後，參與者在一面盒子牆前認識彼此，再於金屬簾幕之間尋找彩色的柱子；每一種顏色代表一個人，選擇因此成為一場緩慢的尋找遊戲。配對成功的兩人接著共享一座小型影院，樓梯下方另有安靜的雙人空間。在最後的迷宮裡，當兩位互相選擇的人彼此靠近時，手機應用程式便會發出訊號。空間溫柔地介入，讓長輩的期盼與年輕人的心意都有被聽見的位置。

pins.title: Animal Box
pins.description:
Stacked habitat boxes invite people to meet animals again, with respect.

Guangzhou, China | Exhibition building | 2020 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 動物盒子
zh-Hant.description:
層層堆疊的棲地盒子，邀請人們以尊重重新認識動物。

中國廣州｜展覽建築｜2020｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The Animal Box at night.
夜晚的動物盒子。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Most people know animals only in a simple way, through zoos, school and the internet. The project asks how a building can help people see animals as complex lives that deserve respect.
captions: Background and a timeline of the human-animal relationship, from hunting to modern zoos.
How people come to know animals.
Sketches of boxes stacked and shifted to make cross views.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 多數人只透過動物園、學校與網路，以簡單的方式認識動物。本案探問建築如何幫助人們把動物看作值得尊重的複雜生命。
captions: 背景與人和動物關係的時間軸，從狩獵到現代動物園。
人們認識動物的途徑。
堆疊錯位的盒子形成交錯視野的草圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each animal habitat is set out as a box with its own sound, light, terrain and humidity. Some boxes use virtual reality, while others offer real experiences such as a bat cave or a snake maze.
captions: Arrangement of the virtual and real systems.
Expected scenes inside the animal boxes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每一種動物棲地都被設定為一個盒子，各有其聲音、光線、地形與濕度。有些盒子使用虛擬實境，另一些則提供蝙蝠洞或蛇迷宮等真實體驗。
captions: 虛擬與真實系統的配置。
動物盒子內預期的場景。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The boxes are grouped into virtual reality, real experience, education and office areas around a central core. A few times a month, a blind box day opens rooms whose content visitors do not know in advance.
captions: Functional areas of the building.
Interior on a blind box day.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 盒子被分為虛擬實境、真實體驗、教育展示與行政四區，環繞中央核心配置。每月數次的盲盒日，會開放訪客事先不知道內容的房間。
captions: 建築的各功能分區。
盲盒日的室內場景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The section shows how the boxes of different heights stack around stairs and open floors. Visitors move from habitat to habitat and meet each animal in its own setting.
captions: VR rooms and real blind-box experiences inside the building.
Long section through the boxes.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 剖面呈現不同高度的盒子如何圍繞樓梯與開放樓層堆疊。訪客從一處棲地走到另一處，在各自的環境中與每一種動物相遇。
captions: 建築內的虛擬實境房間與實體盲盒體驗。
穿越各盒子的長剖面。

sections.heading: Animal Box - Meeting Animals Anew, One Room at a Time
sections.body: Most people know animals only in a simple way, through zoos, classrooms and the internet. The project asks how a building might help people see animals as complex lives that deserve respect. Each animal habitat is set out as a box with its own sound, light, terrain and humidity. Some boxes use virtual reality, while others offer real experiences such as a bat cave or a snake maze. The boxes are grouped around a central core into four areas devoted to virtual reality, real experience, education and offices. A few times each month a blind box day opens rooms whose contents visitors do not know in advance, turning each visit into a small adventure of discovery. A section shows how boxes of different heights stack around stairs and open floors. Visitors move from habitat to habitat and meet each animal within its own setting, attentive to conditions that are not their own. Looking is gradually transformed into understanding, and simple curiosity slowly grows into something closer to respect for other forms of life.

zh-Hant.heading: 動物盒子-在一個個房間裡重新認識生命
zh-Hant.body: 多數人對動物的認識，僅止於動物園、課堂與網路上的簡單印象。作品探問，一棟建築能否幫助人們把動物視為值得尊重的複雜生命？設計把每一種動物的棲地設定為一個盒子，各自擁有獨特的聲音、光線、地形與濕度；有些盒子運用虛擬實境，有些則提供真實的體驗，例如蝙蝠洞穴或蛇類迷宮。盒子圍繞中央核心，分組為虛擬實境、真實體驗、教育與辦公四個區域。每個月有幾天是盲盒日，開放一些內容事先未知的房間，讓參觀帶有探索的驚喜。剖面呈現高低不一的盒子如何沿著樓梯與開放樓層堆疊，參觀者從一個棲地走到下一個棲地，在各自的環境中與每一種動物相遇。觀看由此轉化為體會，好奇也慢慢長成一份敬意。

pins.title: The Bridging
pins.description:
Light new units bridge over an old block so new and old neighbours can stay together.

Guangzhou, China | Community renewal | 2019 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 橋接
zh-Hant.description:
輕量的新單元跨越舊街區，讓新舊鄰里得以共同生活。

中國廣州｜社區更新｜2019｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The new units laid over the old blocks.
新單元疊置於舊街區之上。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Large-scale demolition of old city blocks pushes residents out and breaks long-standing community life. The project asks whether a gentler, embedded way of renewal can let new and old communities live together.
captions: First sketch of units bridging the old houses.
Model of two stacked units.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 舊城街區的大規模拆除迫使居民離開，也打斷了長久以來的社區生活。本案探問一種更溫和的嵌入式更新，能否讓新舊社區共同生活。
captions: 新單元跨越舊屋的初步草圖。
兩層疊置單元的模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The survey traces how open space in the courtyard houses shrank over time as land prices rose. The narrow tube houses that remain were then catalogued as a set of types.
captions: Courtyard houses and their shrinking open space.
Survey of existing house types.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 調查追溯合院住宅的開放空間如何隨地價上漲而逐漸縮減。留存下來的狹長竹筒屋被整理成一組類型。
captions: 合院住宅與逐漸縮減的開放空間。
既有住宅類型調查。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Light modules are set on top of retained structures, with a shared middle layer for public activities. Youth apartments sit above, while original residents keep their homes below.
captions: Steps of the embedding strategy.
Section through the old and new community.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 輕量模組被架設在保留的結構之上，中間層作為公共活動的共享空間。青年公寓位於上方，原有居民則保留下方的住所。
captions: 嵌入策略的步驟。
新舊社區的剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Roof walkways tie the new units together across the block and lead down to an open square. The model shows how the added construction rests lightly on the existing house.
captions: Model detail of the added construction.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 屋頂步道將街區中的新單元串連起來，並通往一處開放廣場。模型呈現加建部分如何輕巧地落在既有住宅之上。
captions: 加建部分的模型細部。

sections.heading: The Bridging - New and Old Communities Living Side by Side in One Block
sections.body: Large-scale demolition of old city blocks pushes residents out and breaks apart community life that has grown over many years. The project asks whether a gentler, embedded way of renewal could let new and old communities live together. A survey traces how open space within the courtyard houses shrank over time as land prices climbed. The narrow tube houses that remain are then catalogued as a set of types. The design places light modules on top of the retained structures, with a shared middle layer reserved for public activities. Youth apartments sit above, while the original residents keep their own homes below. Roof walkways tie the new units together across the whole block and lead down to an open square. A model shows how the added construction rests lightly on the existing house without overwhelming it. Renewal no longer means replacement. It becomes a gesture of layering and companionship, through which different rhythms of life find ways to look after one another beneath shared eaves.

zh-Hant.heading: 橋接-讓新舊社區在同一街廓共存
zh-Hant.body: 大規模拆除舊城街廓，迫使居民遷離，也打斷了長久累積的社區生活。作品探問，一種更溫和、嵌入式的更新方式，能否讓新舊社區共同生活？調查追溯合院住宅中的開放空間，如何隨著地價上漲而逐漸縮小；留存下來的狹長竹筒屋，則被整理為一套類型目錄。設計將輕量模組置於保留的結構之上，中間設置一層共享的公共活動空間；青年公寓位於上方，原有居民則繼續住在下方自己的家中。屋頂步道把新的單元跨越整個街廓串連起來，並引導人們走向一處開放廣場；模型呈現新增構造如何輕巧地落在既有房屋之上。更新不再意味著取代，而是一種疊加與陪伴，讓不同的生活節奏在同一片屋簷下，找到彼此照應的方式。

pins.title: Another Sustainable
pins.description:
A community building that changes shape as residents earn points for green habits.

Architecture | Community building | Participatory design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 另一種永續
zh-Hant.description:
一座隨居民累積環保點數而改變形態的社區建築。

建築｜社區建築｜參與式設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The community building seen from the square.
從廣場望向社區建築。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Sustainable design is often reduced to technology alone, while the habits of the people using a building are left out. The project asks whether a building can encourage residents to act sustainably themselves.
captions: Site plan of the community building.
Points earned for saving water, saving power and sorting waste.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 永續設計常被簡化為技術問題，使用建築的人的習慣卻被忽略。本案探問建築能否鼓勵居民自己採取永續的行動。
captions: 社區建築的配置圖。
節水、節電與垃圾分類所累積的點數。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Residents earn points on a phone app for everyday green actions, and the community level rises as the points add up. With these points they vote on which functions and forms the building should take.
captions: Illustration of the scheme and its spaces.
Possible forms the building can take.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 居民透過手機應用程式，為日常的環保行動累積點數，社區等級也隨之提升。他們再以這些點數投票，決定建築應有的功能與形式。
captions: 方案及其空間的圖解。
建築可能呈現的各種形式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Floors are built from modular components that can be rotated, reversed or added as needs change. The plan groups a tea hall, reading, fitness and game rooms around a shared platform.
captions: Assembly and disassembly of the components.
Steps of a transforming floor in the model.
Third floor plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 樓層由可旋轉、翻轉或增加的模組構件組成，以回應不同需求。平面將茶室、閱讀、健身與遊戲空間環繞一處共享平台配置。
captions: 構件的組裝與拆卸。
模型中樓層轉換的步驟。
三樓平面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The facade panels unfold, half fold or fold depending on sun and wind, and their pattern follows the residents' votes. The section shows how farm, reading, fitness and public spaces stack around a central core.
captions: Section through the stacked functions.
How votes and weather shape the facade.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 立面板依日照與風況而展開、半折或收合，其圖樣也隨居民的投票而改變。剖面呈現農園、閱讀、健身與公共空間如何圍繞中央核心堆疊。
captions: 穿越堆疊功能的剖面。
投票與天氣如何塑造立面。

sections.heading: Another Sustainable - A Green Building Shaped by the Hands of Its Residents
sections.body: Sustainable design is often reduced to technology alone, while the habits of the people who actually use a building are left out of the picture. The project asks whether a building could encourage its residents to act sustainably themselves. A phone app lets residents earn points for everyday green actions, and the community level rises as the points add up. These points then become votes, allowing residents to decide together which functions and forms the building should take. Floors are built from modular components that can be rotated, reversed or added as needs change over time. The plan gathers a tea hall, reading rooms, a fitness space and game rooms around a shared platform. Facade panels unfold, half fold or close according to sun and wind, and their pattern follows the results of the residents' votes. A section shows how farm, reading, fitness and public spaces stack around a central core. Sustainability is no longer a figure written into a specification. It becomes a way of living that residents shape together, one small action at a time.

zh-Hant.heading: 另一種永續-讓住戶親手參與的綠色建築
zh-Hant.body: 永續設計常被簡化為單純的技術問題，使用者的生活習慣卻被排除在外。作品提問，一棟建築能否鼓勵住戶自己採取永續的行動？研究設計了一套手機應用程式，住戶透過日常的綠色行為累積點數，社區等級也隨之提升；這些點數更成為投票的依據，讓住戶共同決定建築應具備哪些功能與形態。樓層以模組化構件建造，可依需求旋轉、翻轉或增加；平面則圍繞共享平台，配置茶廳、閱讀室、健身房與遊戲室。立面板依日照與風向展開、半摺或收合，圖案也隨住戶的投票結果而變化；剖面呈現農園、閱讀、健身與公共空間如何圍繞中央核心層層堆疊。永續於是不再只是寫在規格書裡的數字，而成為住戶一點一滴參與、共同塑造的生活方式。

pins.title: The Rhapsody of Future Office
pins.description:
Robotic arms build and remove rooms inside an open frame, following each worker's space rights.

Guangzhou, China | Office building | Future work | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 未來辦公狂想曲
zh-Hant.description:
機械手臂依每位工作者的空間權利，在開放框架中建造與拆除房間。

中國廣州｜辦公建築｜未來工作｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Section through the office and its customised rooms.
辦公室及其客製房間的剖面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Long working hours have pulled many people's lives apart from their work. The project asks whether a future office can be humane enough that people want to come to work.
captions: The frame filling up as more users arrive.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 長工時讓許多人的生活與工作逐漸脫節。本案探問未來的辦公室能否足夠人性化，讓人們願意前來工作。
captions: 隨使用者增加而逐漸填滿的框架。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each person has a set right to space for working, furniture and shared use. These rights become the rules that decide how large each office can grow.
captions: Rules for personal, furniture and public space.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個人都擁有一定的工作、家具與公共空間使用權。這些權利成為決定每間辦公室能擴展多大的規則。
captions: 個人、家具與公共空間的規則。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Inside an open steel frame, robotic arms pick components, stretch floor slabs and close each room to suit the program. Before a room is made, users can preview it in a virtual view and decide whether to build it.
captions: Steps of room generation.
Previewing a room before it is built.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在開放的鋼構框架中，機械手臂挑選構件、延展樓板，並依需求圍合出每個房間。房間生成之前，使用者可先在虛擬畫面中預覽，再決定是否建造。
captions: 房間生成的步驟。
建造前預覽房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each zone has two robotic arms that work along set tracks to make and remove rooms. Offices, a lobby, a bar, a restaurant and a fitness room share one changing frame.
captions: Robotic arm zones in the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個分區配有兩支機械手臂，沿既定軌道建造與拆除房間。辦公室、大廳、酒吧、餐廳與健身房共享同一個可變的框架。
captions: 框架中的機械手臂分區。

sections.heading: The Rhapsody of Future Office - A Workplace Assembled by Robotic Arms
sections.body: Long working hours have gradually pulled many people's lives apart from their work. The project asks whether a future office could be humane enough that people genuinely want to come in to work. Each person is given a set right to space covering working area, furniture and shared use, and these rights become the rules that decide how large each office may grow. Inside an open steel frame, robotic arms pick up components, stretch out floor slabs and close each room to suit its programme. Before a room is built, users can preview it in a virtual view and decide whether it should be made at all. Each zone has two robotic arms that run along set tracks, constructing rooms and taking them away again. Offices, a lobby, a bar, a restaurant and a fitness room all share one ever-changing frame. The workplace stops being a fixed grid of cubicles. It becomes a rhapsody that rises and falls with the wishes of its users, answering a widespread longing for a kinder balance between work and life.

zh-Hant.heading: 未來辦公狂想曲-一座由機械手臂生成的工作場所
zh-Hant.body: 漫長的工時，讓許多人的生活與工作逐漸斷裂。作品提問，未來的辦公室能否足夠人性，讓人們真心願意走進來工作？研究為每個人設定一份空間權利，涵蓋工作、家具與共享使用的面積，這些權利進而成為規則，決定每間辦公室能夠生長到多大。設計在開放的鋼構框架之中，以機械手臂揀取構件、延展樓板，並依照需求封閉每一個房間；房間建造之前，使用者可以先在虛擬視景中預覽，再決定是否動工。每個分區配有兩支機械手臂，沿著既定軌道建造與拆除房間，辦公室、大廳、酒吧、餐廳與健身房共享同一個持續變化的框架。工作空間因此不再是固定的格子，而是一首隨使用者意願起伏的狂想曲，回應人們對工作與生活平衡的渴望。

pins.title: Family Unit
pins.description:
Folding living units slot into idle city spaces as a new kind of council house.

London, United Kingdom | Council housing | Modular design | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 家庭單元
zh-Hant.description:
可折疊的居住單元嵌入城市閒置空間，成為新型公共住宅。

英國倫敦｜公共住宅｜模組化設計｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Exploded section of the family unit.
家庭單元的爆炸剖面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In a dense, high-priced city, council housing is slow to build and costly to rent. The project looks for a new type of council house that fits into narrow and rarely used spaces.
captions: Traditional and new council houses compared.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在高密度、高房價的城市中，公共住宅興建緩慢且租金昂貴。本案尋找一種能嵌入狹窄或少用空間的新型公共住宅。
captions: 傳統與新型公共住宅的比較。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Idle plots in the city were sorted by shape into rectangles, trapezoids and triangles. A scheme was then drawn for each shape, with standard and ground floor plans.
captions: Three schemes for different idle spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 城市中的閒置地塊依形狀被分為矩形、梯形與三角形。再針對每種形狀繪製方案，包含標準層與地面層平面。
captions: 針對不同閒置空間的三種方案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each living unit folds like a small tent and stretches down when in use, with a shared living room below. Units are made in a standard set that fits on a medium truck and is spliced together on site.
captions: How the units are moved and assembled.
Model of a unit unfolding.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每個居住單元像小帳篷一樣折疊，使用時向下展開，下方則是共享客廳。單元以標準組件製作，可裝上中型貨車，並在現場拼接。
captions: 單元的運輸與組裝方式。
單元展開的模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The structure goes up first and the units are then hung inside, which saves time and cost. Louvres and rain shields fold with the weather to keep air moving and rain out.
captions: Construction details of the unit.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 先建立結構，再將單元吊掛其中，節省時間與成本。百葉與遮雨板隨天氣折疊，保持通風並阻擋雨水。
captions: 單元的構造細部。

sections.heading: Family Unit - Council Housing That Unfolds Within the Gaps of the City
sections.body: In a dense city where prices are high, council housing is slow to build and costly to rent. The project looks for a new type of council house that can slip into narrow spaces that are rarely used. Idle plots across the city are first sorted by shape into rectangles, trapezoids and triangles. A scheme is then drawn for each shape, complete with standard and ground floor plans. Each living unit in the design folds like a small tent and stretches downward when in use, with a shared living room set beneath it. The units are produced as a standard set that fits on a medium-sized truck and is spliced together on site. The structure goes up first and the units are then hung inside it, saving both time and cost. Louvres and rain shields fold and open with the weather, keeping air moving while holding the rain outside. Housing no longer needs a single perfect site. Instead it can unfold in the corners and leftovers of the city, giving families an affordable place to settle and belong.

zh-Hant.heading: 家庭單元-在城市縫隙中展開的公屋
zh-Hant.body: 在高密度、高房價的城市裡，公共住宅興建緩慢，租金也不低。作品尋找一種新的公屋類型，能夠嵌入那些狹窄而鮮少被使用的城市縫隙。研究先把城市中的閒置地塊依形狀分類為矩形、梯形與三角形，再為每一種形狀繪製方案，包括標準層與地面層平面。設計中的每個居住單元像一頂小帳篷般可以收摺，使用時向下伸展，下方則是共享的起居空間。單元以標準化的組件製作，可以裝進中型卡車運送，再於現場拼接組合。施工時先立起結構，再把單元懸掛其中，節省時間與成本；百葉與遮雨板隨天氣開合，保持空氣流通並阻擋雨水。住宅因此不再需要一整塊完美的基地，而能在城市的邊角裡，為家庭展開一方可負擔的安身之所。

pins.title: Bridge: Renewing the Fengqing Community
pins.description:
A light new layer above old houses joins young newcomers and long-time residents.

Guangzhou, China | Community renewal | Housing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 橋：鳳慶社區的更新
zh-Hant.description:
在老屋之上加建輕量層體，連接年輕新住民與原有居民。

中國廣州｜社區更新｜住宅｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial view of the renewed community.
更新後社區的鳥瞰。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An old community in the historic core of Guangzhou faces an ageing population, ageing houses and many empty homes. Large demolition and rebuilding would erase its history, so the project looks for a gentler way to renew it.
captions: Site status of planning, ownership, height and protection.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州歷史城區中的一個老社區，面臨人口老化、房屋老舊與空置率高的問題。大規模拆除重建會抹去其歷史，因此本案尋找一種更溫和的更新方式。
captions: 規劃、權屬、層數與保護狀態的現況分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each plot was mapped by planning status, land ownership, storey count and protection level. The local tube house type, long and narrow with small courtyards, was studied in section as the base unit.
captions: Sections of the tube house and the new residential building.
Steps for layering and joining the communities.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每塊基地依規劃狀態、土地權屬、樓層數與保護等級逐一標記。並以剖面研究在地狹長、帶小天井的竹筒屋，作為基本單元。
captions: 竹筒屋與新住宅的剖面。
社區分層與整合的步驟。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: New homes and offices for young people are built as a light layer above the old houses, keeping the original structure below. Standard module units for living, work and shared use are joined by simple nodes.
captions: Concept steps for the residential and office buildings.
Floor plans of a residential building.
Module units and their structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 為年輕人設計的新住宅與辦公空間，以輕量層體建於老屋之上，保留下方原有結構。居住、工作與共享用途的標準模組，以簡單節點相互連接。
captions: 住宅與辦公建築的概念步驟。
住宅建築的各層平面。
模組單元與其構造。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A shared upper level links the new and old communities with landscape spaces for rest, shelter and meeting. Over time the new layer grows step by step until the two communities blend into one.
captions: Landscape elements drawn from local street life.
Future growth of the community in stages.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 共享的上層空間以休憩、遮蔽與交流的景觀場所連接新舊社區。隨時間推移，新的層體逐步生長，直到兩個社區融為一體。
captions: 取自在地街道生活的景觀元素。
社區未來的分階段生長。

sections.heading: Fengqing Community Bridge - Adding a Light Layer of New Life Above Old Homes
sections.body: An old community in a historic core faces an ageing population, ageing houses and many empty homes. Large-scale demolition and rebuilding would erase the history it has gathered over generations, so the project searches for a gentler way to renew it. Each plot is surveyed for its planning status, land ownership, number of storeys and level of protection. The local tube house, long and narrow with small courtyards, is studied in section and set as the base unit of the design. New homes and offices for young people are then built as a light layer above the old houses, while the original structures below are kept intact. Standard modules for living, working and shared use are joined to one another by simple nodes. A shared upper level links the new and old communities, offering landscape spaces for rest, shelter and meeting. Over time the new layer grows step by step until the two communities blend into one. Like a bridge, the scheme lets different generations meet beneath the same sheltering roofs.

zh-Hant.heading: 鳳慶社區之橋-在老屋之上輕輕加一層新生活
zh-Hant.body: 一處位於歷史核心區的老社區，面臨人口老化、房屋老舊與大量空屋的困境；大規模的拆除重建，將抹去它累積多年的歷史，作品因此尋找一種更溫和的更新方式。研究逐一調查每塊地的規劃狀態、土地權屬、樓層數與保護等級，並以剖面研究在地的竹筒屋，長而窄、帶著小天井的住屋類型被設定為基本單元。設計把為年輕人而設的住宅與辦公空間，作為一層輕盈的新構造置於老屋之上，原有結構則完整保留於下方；居住、工作與共享的標準模組，以簡單的節點相互接合。一個共享的上層平台串連新舊社區，配置可休憩、遮蔽與相遇的景觀空間。隨著時間推移，新層逐步生長，兩個社區終將交融為一，像一座橋，讓不同世代在同一片屋頂下相遇。

pins.title: Cantonese Opera Street Museum
pins.description:
A path of open stages brings Cantonese opera back into the streets of the old town.

Guangzhou, China | Museum | Cultural heritage | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 粵劇街道博物館
zh-Hant.description:
一條開放舞台的路徑，讓粵劇重回老城的街道。

中國廣州｜博物館｜文化遺產｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial drawing of the opera street by the river.
河畔戲曲街道的鳥瞰圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The existing opera museum stands closed off inside its block and feels apart from the old town around it. The project asks how Cantonese opera could return to the daily life of the streets.
captions: Site analysis of texture, height, green and roads.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 現有的戲曲博物館在街區中自成一體，與周邊老城區顯得疏離。本案探問粵劇如何重新回到街道的日常生活之中。
captions: 肌理、高度、綠化與道路的基地分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Staff, residents, visitors and performers were studied to see how each group meets the opera. Four kinds of stage were compared for sound, light, sight lines and comfort.
captions: Development of four stage forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究工作人員、居民、遊客與演員，了解各群體如何接觸戲曲。並比較四種舞台在聲音、光線、視線與舒適度上的表現。
captions: 四種舞台形式的推演。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A path of open stages winds from the river through the old blocks to the museum. Each of four theme areas ties the opera to a different part of the city, from the river to city life.
captions: The four theme areas at night.
First floor plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一條由開放舞台串成的路徑，從河岸穿過老街區通往博物館。四個主題區各自將戲曲連結到城市的不同部分，從河流到城市生活。
captions: 夜間的四個主題區。
一層平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Light is brought into the halls through roof joints, studied in sections and a physical model. The facade details show how the new building meets the brick fabric of the old town.
captions: Light analysis sections.
Physical model of the lighting construction.
Partial facade and wall section.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 光線透過屋頂接縫引入展廳，並以剖面與實體模型加以研究。立面細部說明新建築如何與老城的磚造肌理相接。
captions: 光線分析剖面。
採光構造的實體模型。
局部立面與牆身剖面。

sections.heading: Cantonese Opera Street Museum - Letting Opera Flow Through the Lanes
sections.body: The existing opera museum stands closed off inside its block, as though it belonged to a different world from the old town around it. The project asks how Cantonese opera might return to the daily life of the streets. Staff, residents, visitors and performers are each observed to understand how every group meets the opera. Four kinds of stage are compared in turn for sound, light, sight lines and comfort. The design draws a path of open stages that sets out from the river, winds through the old blocks and finally reaches the museum. Each of four theme areas ties the opera to a different side of urban life, stretching from the riverbank to the bustle of everyday streets. Light enters the halls through joints in the roof, a move studied carefully in sections and a physical model. Facade details show how the new building meets the brick fabric of the old town. The museum is no longer a box that stores opera away; it becomes a passage through which song and drums can flow along the lanes once more.

zh-Hant.heading: 粵劇街道博物館-讓戲曲沿著街巷流淌
zh-Hant.body: 既有的粵劇博物館封閉在街廓之內，與周圍的老城彷彿兩個世界。作品探問，粵劇能否重新回到街道的日常生活之中？研究分別觀察員工、居民、遊客與表演者，理解每一群人如何與戲曲相遇；四種舞台類型也被逐一比較，檢視其聲音、光線、視線與舒適度。設計以一條開放舞台串成的路徑，從河岸出發，蜿蜒穿過老街區，最終抵達博物館；四個主題區各自把戲曲與城市的不同面向連結起來，從河流一路延伸到市井生活。光線經由屋頂的接縫引入展廳，透過剖面與實體模型細細推敲；立面細部則說明新建築如何與老城的磚砌紋理彼此銜接。博物館不再是收藏戲曲的盒子，而成為讓唱腔與鑼鼓沿著街巷流淌的通道。

pins.title: Spatial Experiment: Gradient Prototype
pins.description:
Model studies turn density into a tower that shifts from closed to open.

Studio study | Model study | Spatial experiment | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間實驗：漸變原型
zh-Hant.description:
以模型研究將密度轉化為由封閉漸變為開放的塔。

設計課研究｜模型研究｜空間實驗｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Fifty test models of tall buildings.
五十個高層建築測試模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: We often notice only what we can see and miss the parts of a space that we cannot. The project explores concentration and density through a series of diagrams and models.
captions: Four ways of joining parts.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 我們常只注意看得見的部分，而忽略空間中看不見的部分。本案透過一系列圖解與模型，探索集中度與密度。
captions: 四種構件的接合方式。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Fifty tall building models were made first to test how a building looks from outside. Simple actions such as inlay, join, hook and collect were then used to build new models.
captions: Models A to D.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 首先製作五十個高層建築模型，測試建築的外在形貌。再以嵌入、接合、勾掛與聚集等簡單動作建構新的模型。
captions: 模型 A 至 D。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each model was rebuilt as a second version that stacks floors of changing density. Openings grow from closed rooms at the base to open space at the top.
captions: Second versions of the four models.
Plans showing the change in opening degree.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 每個模型再發展為第二版本，以密度漸變的樓層堆疊而成。開口由底部封閉的房間，逐漸過渡到頂部的開放空間。
captions: 四個模型的第二版本。
開口程度漸變的平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A final concept model joins the studies into one tower with a soft, blurred edge. Its arches and frames move from public space at the bottom to private space at the top.
captions: Combined concept model.
Close views of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終概念模型將各項研究整合為一座邊界模糊的塔。其拱與框架由底部的公共空間過渡到頂部的私密空間。
captions: 整合概念模型。
模型近景。

sections.heading: Gradient Prototype - Drawing the Unseen Parts of Space Through Density
sections.body: People tend to notice only what they can see, and so they miss the parts of a space that are hard to perceive. The project explores concentration and density through a series of diagrams and models. Fifty tall building models are made first, testing how a building appears when viewed from outside. Simple actions such as inlay, join, hook and collect are then used to construct a fresh set of models. Each of these is rebuilt as a second version that stacks floors of changing density. Openings grow gradually, from closed rooms at the base to open space at the top. A final concept model gathers all of the studies into one tower with a soft, blurred edge. Its arches and frames shift slowly from public space at the bottom to private space near the summit. Gradient becomes a way of seeing as much as a way of building. It invites attention to the spatial layers that hover between clarity and disappearance, the parts of a building that are felt long before they are noticed.

zh-Hant.heading: 漸變原型-以密度描繪看不見的空間
zh-Hant.body: 我們往往只注意到看得見的部分，卻錯過了空間中那些難以察覺的面向。作品以一系列圖解與模型，探索集中與密度如何塑造空間經驗。研究首先製作五十個高層建築模型，測試建築從外部被觀看時的樣貌；接著，以嵌入、接合、勾掛與收集等簡單動作，建構出一批新的模型。每個模型隨後被重新製作為第二個版本，以密度漸變的樓層相互堆疊，開口也從底部封閉的房間，逐步生長為頂部開敞的空間。最後，一個整合性的概念模型把這些研究匯聚成一座塔樓，邊界柔和而模糊，拱與框架由下方的公共空間，緩緩過渡到上方的私密空間。漸變在此成為一種觀看方式，提醒人們留意那些介於清晰與隱沒之間的空間層次。

pins.title: Period of Solidification
pins.description:
A printed vase cut into slices becomes columns that give time a form.

Studio study | Concept design | 3D printing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 凝固期
zh-Hant.description:
將列印的花瓶切片重組成柱體，為時間賦予形體。

設計課研究｜概念設計｜3D 列印｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Render of a hall of reassembled columns.
重組柱體構成的大廳渲染。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Time is everywhere in daily life, yet it is hard to explain what it is. The project tries to give this abstract idea a form through 3D printed models and space.
captions: Circle slices of different sizes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 時間存在於日常生活的每個角落，卻很難說清它是什麼。本案嘗試透過 3D 列印模型與空間，為這個抽象概念賦予形體。
captions: 不同大小的圓形切片。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Ideas of time from several thinkers were read as the starting point. One view, that a life is made of many moments, led to the idea of a column made of slices.
captions: A 3D printed vase model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以多位思想家對時間的看法作為出發點。其中一種觀點認為人生由許多片刻構成，由此發展出由切片組成柱體的想法。
captions: 3D 列印的花瓶模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A printed vase was cut into slices and the pieces were stacked again by hand in new orders. Each new column keeps the same material but takes a different shape.
captions: Stacking the slices again by hand.
Column variants from the same slices.
One reassembled column.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 將列印的花瓶切成薄片，再以手工依新的順序重新堆疊。每根新柱體材料不變，形狀卻各不相同。
captions: 以手工重新堆疊切片。
由相同切片組成的各式柱體。
一根重組後的柱體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The columns are set out as a field that people can walk through at full scale. The space suggests that time is only a period of solidification between city and nature.
captions: Render of the column field.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些柱體以實際尺度排列成可供穿行的柱林。空間暗示時間只是城市與自然之間的一段凝固期。
captions: 柱林的渲染。

sections.heading: Period of Solidification - Slicing Time Into a Forest of Columns
sections.body: Time runs through every part of daily life, yet it remains remarkably hard to say what time actually is. The project tries to give this abstract idea a body through 3D printed models and space. Ideas of time from several thinkers serve as the starting point. One view in particular, that a life is made of countless separate moments, leads to the idea of a column built out of slices. A printed vase is cut into thin layers, and the pieces are stacked again by hand in new orders. Each new column keeps exactly the same material but takes on a completely different shape, much as a single experience may be rearranged within memory. The columns are finally set out at full scale as a field that people can walk through, pause within and look across. In this way the space offers a quiet interpretation, suggesting that time may be no more than a period of solidification between city and nature, briefly taking form before slipping back into flow once again.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝固期-把時間切成可以穿行的柱林
zh-Hant.body: 時間無所不在地穿過日常生活，卻很難被說清它究竟是什麼。作品嘗試以 3D 列印的模型與空間，為這個抽象的概念賦予形體。研究以多位思想家對時間的論述為起點，其中一種觀點認為，生命由無數個瞬間組成；這個想法引出了以切片構成柱體的構想。一只列印的花瓶被切成薄片，再以手工依照新的次序重新堆疊；每一根新柱體保留相同的材料，卻呈現截然不同的形狀，彷彿同一段經歷在記憶中被重新排列。這些柱體最後以足尺配置成一片可以穿行的柱林，讓人們在其間行走、停留與環顧。空間由此提出一個安靜的詮釋：時間或許只是城市與自然之間的一段凝固期，短暫成形，又終將回到流動之中。

pins.title: Reinventing Shape and Spontaneous Growth
pins.description:
Small spaces drawn from three case studies stack into a parasitic architecture for an urban village.

Guangzhou | Parasitic architecture | Urban village | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重塑形態與自發生長
zh-Hant.description:
由三個案例提取的小空間，堆疊成城中村的寄生建築。

廣州｜寄生建築｜城中村｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Timber model of the parasitic cluster.
寄生建築群的木構模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Urban villages near the university town grow on their own, with small rooms and shops added wherever space allows. The project asks how a parasitic architecture could grow from small spaces into a construction mode.
captions: Detail of the parasitic model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 大學城周邊的城中村自發生長，小房間與店鋪在任何可用空間中不斷加建。本案探討寄生建築如何從小空間出發，發展成一種建造模式。
captions: 寄生模型細部。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Three case study buildings were read through writing, critical observation, collage and physical models. The space script of one house was turned into a sequence of section models.
captions: Section models from the case study house.
Site sections of the village.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以寫作、批判性觀察、拼貼與實體模型解讀三個案例建築。其中一棟住宅的空間腳本被轉化為一系列剖面模型。
captions: 案例住宅的剖面模型。
村落的基地剖面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The three cases were broken down into structural types that could be stacked in the village. Their sections were then varied by size, opening and slope into many small space forms.
captions: Structure types drawn from the three cases.
Matrix of small space forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 將三個案例拆解為可在村中堆疊的結構類型。再依尺寸、開口與坡度變化其剖面，衍生出大量小空間形態。
captions: 由三個案例提取的結構類型。
小空間形態矩陣。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Selected forms became small rooms ranked from private to public, each drawn in plan and section. Stacked together in the timber model, they show how the cluster could keep growing over time.
captions: Small rooms drawn in plan, section and axonometric.
More small rooms ranked by privacy.
The full timber model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 選出的形態成為由私密到公共分級的小房間，各自繪製平面與剖面。在木構模型中層層堆疊，呈現建築群如何隨時間持續生長。
captions: 以平面、剖面與軸測繪製的小房間。
依私密程度分級的更多小房間。
完整的木構模型。

sections.heading: Reinventing Shape and Spontaneous Growth - A Way of Building Sprouting From Parasitic Rooms
sections.body: Urban villages beside the university town grow by their own rhythm, adding a small room or a little shop wherever a scrap of space allows. The project asks whether this parasitic architecture could develop from scattered small spaces into a mode of construction that can be sustained. Three case study buildings are read again and again through writing, critical observation, collage and physical models. The space script of one house is translated into a continuous sequence of section models. The three cases are then broken down into structural types that could be stacked within the village, and their sections are varied by size, opening and slope to produce a great many small spatial forms. Selected forms become individual rooms, ranked from private to public, each drawn carefully in plan and section. Stacked together in a timber model, they show how the cluster could keep growing over time. Spontaneous growth is not suppressed by planning here. Instead it is gathered into a grammar, one that lets the village continue to build itself with a little more care and coherence.

zh-Hant.heading: 重塑形態與自發生長-從寄生小屋長出一種營造方式
zh-Hant.body: 大學城旁的城中村依循自己的節奏生長，只要有一點空隙，就會多出一間小房或一爿小店。作品探問，這種寄生的建築能否從零星的小空間，發展為一套可以延續的營造模式？研究以三棟案例建築為對象，透過書寫、批判性的觀察、拼貼與實體模型反覆閱讀；其中一棟住宅的空間腳本，被轉譯為一系列連續的剖面模型。三個案例隨後被拆解為可在村中堆疊的結構類型，其剖面再依尺寸、開口與坡度變化，衍生出大量細小的空間形態。被選出的形態成為一間間小房，依私密到公共的程度排序，並逐一繪製平面與剖面。在木構模型中，它們彼此堆疊，呈現聚落如何隨時間持續生長。自發的力量沒有被規劃壓制，而被整理成一種能延續的語法。

pins.title: Line Offset Pop-up Shop
pins.description:
Offset boxes of different sizes turn a busy square into a pop-up shop to wander through.

Guangzhou | Pop-up shop | Experience space | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 線性偏移快閃店
zh-Hant.description:
不同尺寸的偏移量體，將繁忙廣場轉化為可漫遊的快閃店。

廣州｜快閃店｜體驗空間｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometric of the pop-up shop in the business district.
快閃店位於商業區中的軸測圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The site sits in a busy square of the city's business district, where many people pass through every day. The project asks how a pop-up shop could turn this flow into a space to walk, pause and gather.
captions: Paper study models.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於城市商業區一處繁忙廣場，每天有大量人流經過。本案探討快閃店如何將這股人流轉化為可行走、停留與聚集的空間。
captions: 紙模型研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Paper models and parti diagrams tested how rectangular boxes of different sizes could slide and offset. Line studies then traced how a route could wind between open and narrow, dark and bright.
captions: Brand analysis of the pop-up shop: nature of activity, stationarity and offline experience.
Parti diagrams of the offset boxes.
Line studies from the conception phase.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以紙模型與構想圖測試不同尺寸的矩形量體如何滑移與偏移。再以線條研究描繪路徑如何在開闊與狹窄、明與暗之間迂迴。
captions: 快閃店品牌分析：活動性質、停留性與線下體驗。
偏移量體的構想圖。
構思階段的線條研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Habits such as taking shortcuts, following others and avoiding crowds shaped the plan. A central space holds meetings, parties and talks, while smaller rooms offer screening, rest, reading and snacks.
captions: Behaviour patterns of visitors.
Uses of the central main space.
Smaller experience rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 抄捷徑、跟隨他人與避開人群等行為習慣形塑了平面。中央空間容納聚會、派對與講座，較小的房間則提供放映、休息、閱讀與點心。
captions: 訪客的行為模式。
中央主空間的使用方式。
較小的體驗房間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each box was set out with its own route, enclosure, interface and material, from mirror to perforated metal and glass. Stacked together, the boxes form a light and layered shop that changes as people move through it.
captions: Exploded view of the boxes.
Matrix of routes, interfaces and materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個量體各自設定路徑、圍合、介面與材料，從鏡面到穿孔金屬與玻璃。量體堆疊後構成輕盈而多層次的店舖，隨人們穿行而變化。
captions: 量體爆炸圖。
路徑、介面與材料矩陣。

sections.heading: Line Offset Pop-up Shop - Letting Passing Crowds Wander and Pause Between Boxes
sections.body: The site lies in a busy square in the business district, where great numbers of people hurry past every day. The project asks whether a pop-up shop could turn that flow into a space for walking, pausing and gathering. Paper models and parti diagrams test how rectangular boxes of different sizes might slide and offset against one another. Line studies then trace how a route could wind between open and narrow, dark and bright. Everyday habits such as taking shortcuts, following a crowd and avoiding congestion shape the plan. A central space holds meetings, parties and talks, while smaller rooms offer screening, rest, reading and snacks. Each box is given its own route, enclosure, interface and material, from mirror to perforated metal and glass, so that every room carries a distinct texture. Stacked together, the boxes form a light and layered shop whose appearance keeps changing as people move through it. The rush of commerce is gently slowed down here, leaving just enough room for chance encounters to take place along the way.

zh-Hant.heading: 線性偏移快閃店-讓人流在盒子間迂迴停駐
zh-Hant.body: 基地位於商業區一處繁忙的廣場，每天有大量人流匆匆經過。作品探問，一間快閃店能否把這股人流轉化為可以行走、停留與聚集的空間？研究以紙模型與構想圖，測試不同尺寸的矩形量體如何滑移與偏移；線條研究則描繪一條路徑如何在開闊與狹窄、幽暗與明亮之間迂迴前行。行人的習慣成為平面的依據，例如抄捷徑、跟隨人群或避開擁擠。中央空間容納聚會、派對與講座，較小的房間則提供放映、休息、閱讀與點心。每個量體各自設定路徑、圍合、介面與材料，從鏡面到穿孔金屬與玻璃，質感彼此不同。量體堆疊之後，構成一座輕盈而多層次的店舖，隨著人們的穿行不斷變換樣貌。商業的匆忙在此被輕輕放慢，偶然的相遇也因此有了發生的餘地。

pins.title: Recore: Textile District Renewal
pins.description:
An old textile district keeps its factory roofs and grows new markets, parks and halls beneath them.

Xi'an | Urban renewal | Industrial heritage | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Recore：紡織區更新
zh-Hant.description:
老紡織區保留廠房屋頂，在其下生長出新的市集、公園與展館。

西安｜城市更新｜工業遺產｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometrics of the phased development.
分期開發的軸測圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The textile district grew around large old factories that were later left empty and cut off from the city. The project asks how the district could keep its industrial memory while bringing back jobs and daily life.
captions: Urban texture across four periods.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這片紡織區圍繞大型老工廠發展，後來工廠閒置，與城市脫節。本案探討如何在保留工業記憶的同時，為片區重新帶回工作機會與日常生活。
captions: 四個時期的城市肌理。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Maps of the urban texture showed how the factory blocks broke the street grid over time. A masterplan then linked the old buildings with new uses along a green spine.
captions: Masterplan with the proposed typology.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 城市肌理分析顯示工廠街廓如何隨時間切斷街道網絡。總體規劃再以一條綠色軸線，將舊建築與新功能串連起來。
captions: 配置新類型的總體規劃。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The roof of the main factory is kept as the memory of the city, while the space under it is split into smaller streets. Each old building was tested with moves such as cutting, adding and opening to the street.
captions: Form concept for the factory roof.
Strategies for the existing buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 主廠房的屋頂作為城市記憶被保留，其下空間則被切分為較小的街道。每棟舊建築都以切割、加建與向街道開放等手法進行測試。
captions: 廠房屋頂的形態概念。
既有建築的改造策略。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The renewal grows in three phases, from markets and a park to a mall, theatre and research centre. Layered by function, the new programs sit on top of the old factory as one walkable whole.
captions: Exploded view of the functions.
Program analysis of the main building.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 更新分三期展開，從市集與公園到商場、劇場與研究中心。新功能依類別分層疊加在舊廠房之上，形成可步行的整體。
captions: 功能分層爆炸圖。
主建築的機能分析。

sections.heading: Recore Textile District Renewal - New Streets Growing Beneath an Old Roof
sections.body: This textile district once grew around large factories that were later left empty and slowly drifted away from the city. The project asks how the district could keep its industrial memory while bringing back jobs and everyday life. Analysis of the urban texture shows how the factory blocks broke the street grid over time. A masterplan then uses a green spine to link the old buildings with new uses. The design keeps the roof of the main factory as a memory held by the whole city, while the vast space beneath it is divided into smaller streets that return the scale to people on foot. Each old building is tested in turn with moves such as cutting, adding and opening toward the street, searching for the most fitting way to transform it. Renewal unfolds in three phases, moving from markets and a park to a mall, a theatre and a research centre. Layered by function, the new programmes sit over the old factories as one walkable whole. The skeleton of the past is carefully kept, and fresh life gradually multiplies beneath it.

zh-Hant.heading: Recore紡織區更新-在舊屋頂下長出新街道
zh-Hant.body: 這片紡織區曾圍繞著大型工廠發展，後來廠房閒置，逐漸與城市脫節。作品提問：如何在保留工業記憶的同時，為片區重新帶回工作機會與日常生活？城市肌理的分析顯示，工廠街廓如何隨時間切斷了原有的街道網絡；總體規劃於是以一條綠色軸線，將舊建築與新功能重新串連。設計保留主廠房的屋頂，作為這座城市的記憶，其下的大空間則被切分為較小的街道，讓尺度回到行人身上。每棟舊建築都以切割、加建與向街道開放等手法逐一測試，尋找最合適的轉化方式。更新分為三期展開，從市集與公園，到商場、劇場與研究中心；新功能依類別分層疊加在舊廠房之上，構成一個可步行的整體。過去的骨架被細心留存，新的生活便在其下慢慢繁衍。

pins.title: Entropy: A Folding Market
pins.description:
Folding stalls let a periodic market grow on market days and fold away the rest of the week.

Xi'an | Market design | Temporary structure | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 熵：可折疊的市集
zh-Hant.description:
可折疊的攤位讓定期市集在趕集日展開，其餘時間收合。

西安｜市集設計｜臨時構築｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Bird's-eye view of the market on a weekend.
週末市集的鳥瞰圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A periodic country market gathers crowds of traders on market days but leaves a large empty ground the rest of the week. The project asks how one site could hold both the busy market and quieter weekday uses.
captions: Site history of the Ganji market in Baqiao, with scenes of trading through the ages.
Analysis of activity density, traffic and vendors on the site.
Section of the market and its sheds.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 定期的鄉間市集在趕集日聚集大量商販，其餘時間卻留下一大片空地。本案探討同一基地如何同時容納熱鬧的市集與平日較安靜的使用。
captions: 灞橋趕集市集的基地歷史，以及歷代交易場景。
基地活動密度、交通與攤販分析。
市集與棚架的剖面示意。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings of how traders bargain and agree on a price showed the habits that make the market lively. Stall types, trading areas and use over time were then counted to size the new layout.
captions: Types of stalls with their utilisation and functional area analysis.
Drawn panels of trading gestures.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以手繪記錄商販討價還價與成交的方式，呈現讓市集充滿活力的習慣。再統計攤位類型、交易面積與時段使用量，作為新配置的尺度依據。
captions: 攤位類型與其使用率及機能面積分析。
交易手勢的手繪分格。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A family of folding stalls was designed that open into shops on market days and fold back into walls or benches. A shared tree stall and loose modules can also turn into tables and seats.
captions: Cloud management of the market and its four stages of growth.
Stall modules opening step by step.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 設計一系列可折疊的攤位，趕集日展開成店舖，平日收合成牆或長椅。樹下的共享攤位與可自由組合的模組，也能轉變為桌椅。
captions: 市集的雲端管理與四個發展階段。
逐步展開的攤位模組。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: On weekdays the same ground stays open for other activities, with ramps and a footbridge tying it to the street. The market can grow and shrink each week, so the site is never fully empty.
captions: User experience of the market in a smart city system.
Bird's-eye view of the site on a weekday.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 平日同一片場地開放給其他活動使用，坡道與天橋將其連接到街道。市集可每週擴張與收縮，讓基地不再完全閒置。
captions: 智慧城市系統中的市集使用體驗。
平日基地的鳥瞰圖。

sections.heading: Entropy - A Folding Market That Breathes With the Week
sections.body: A periodic country market fills with traders and crowds on market days, but for the rest of the week it leaves behind a wide, empty ground. The project asks whether one site could hold both the busy market and the quieter uses of ordinary days. Hand drawings record how traders bargain and settle on a price, capturing the small habits that make a market feel alive. Stall types, trading areas and use at different hours are then counted to set the scale of the new layout. The design develops a family of folding stalls that open into shops on market days and fold back into walls or benches when the crowds are gone. A shared stall beneath a tree and loose modules can also become tables and seats. On weekdays the ground stays open for many kinds of activity, and ramps and a footbridge tie it to the street. The market grows and shrinks with the weekly rhythm, almost like breathing, so the site never falls completely idle and keeps moving between order and dispersal.

zh-Hant.heading: 熵-一座會呼吸的折疊市集
zh-Hant.body: 定期的鄉間市集，在趕集日湧入大量商販與人群，其餘的日子卻只留下一大片空地。作品探問，同一片基地能否同時容納熱鬧的集市，與平日較為安靜的使用？研究以手繪記錄商販討價還價與成交的過程，捕捉那些讓市集充滿生氣的細微習慣；接著統計攤位類型、交易面積與各時段的使用量，作為新配置的尺度依據。設計發展出一系列可折疊的攤位，趕集日展開成店舖，平日則收合成牆面或長椅；樹下的共享攤位與可自由組合的模組，也能轉化為桌椅。平日，這片場地開放給各種活動，坡道與天橋把它與街道相連。市集隨著每週的節奏擴張與收縮，像一次次的呼吸，基地也因此不再陷入完全的閒置，而在秩序與散逸之間保持流動。

pins.title: Spotlight: Courtyard House Opera Theatre
pins.description:
A regional courtyard house is opened up to become a small theatre for local opera.

Chaoshan | Theatre | Vernacular dwelling | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 聚光：合院戲曲劇場
zh-Hant.description:
將地方合院民居打開，轉化為地方戲曲的小劇場。

潮汕｜劇場｜傳統民居｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Natural light entering the reworked house.
自然光進入改造後的民居。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Local opera troupes in the region are shrinking, and the old courtyard houses where people once gathered stand empty. The project asks whether one such house could be turned into a small theatre for the opera.
captions: The Sidianjin courtyard house and Teochew Opera, and why small troupes are losing their venues.
The courtyard house type of the region.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 地方戲班日漸萎縮，人們過去聚集的老合院也逐漸空置。本案探討能否將這樣一座合院改造成小型戲曲劇場。
captions: 四點金合院與潮劇，以及小型劇團為何失去演出場地。
當地的合院民居類型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The house type has four wings around a central court, with deep timber roofs and narrow side lanes. Exploded drawings took the original house apart into roof, frame, walls and plan.
captions: Exploded axonometrics of the original house.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 這種民居以四翼圍合中央天井，配有深遠的木構屋頂與狹窄的側巷。爆炸圖將原有民居拆解為屋頂、構架、牆體與平面。
captions: 原有民居的爆炸軸測圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The roofs were lifted and opened so that light and air can reach a larger hall below. New details join the old timber columns and rafters to rebar and a concrete base.
captions: Section of the transformed house.
Structure details of the new joints.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 將屋頂抬升並開啟，讓光線與空氣進入下方更大的廳堂。新的節點把原有木柱與椽條以鋼筋接合到混凝土基座上。
captions: 改造後民居的剖面。
新節點的構造細部。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The court becomes an opera stage with a band stage beside it and seats in the wings around it. The section model shows how the old house can hold a full performance and its audience.
captions: The section model with opera performers on the stage.
Auditorium side of the section model.
Theatre plan drawn over the model base.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 天井成為戲台，旁邊設有樂隊台，四周翼房布置觀眾席。剖面模型呈現老民居如何容納一場完整演出與觀眾。
captions: 剖面模型，舞台上有潮劇演員。
剖面模型的觀眾席一側。
繪於模型基座上的劇場平面。

sections.heading: Spotlight - Letting an Old Courtyard House Hear the Drums Again
sections.body: Local opera troupes are shrinking, and the old courtyard houses where people once gathered are falling empty one after another. The project asks whether such a house could be turned into a small opera theatre, so that two fading traditions might reawaken each other.
