The study first seeks to understand the dwelling itself: four wings around a central court, deep timber roofs and narrow side lanes. Exploded drawings take the original house apart into roof, frame, walls and plan, so that its logic can be read layer by layer. The design then lifts and opens the roofs, letting light and air reach a larger hall below. New details join the old timber columns and rafters to rebar and a concrete base, allowing old material to carry a new use safely. The court becomes an opera stage, a band stage sits beside it, and seats fill the wings around it. A section model shows how the old house can hold a full performance and its audience. Where the beam of light falls, memory and stage are illuminated together.

zh-Hant.heading: 聚光-讓老合院再次響起鑼鼓
zh-Hant.body: 地方戲班日漸萎縮，人們過去聚集的老合院也一座座空置下來。作品提問，能否把這樣一座合院，改造成一處小型戲曲劇場，讓兩種逐漸沉寂的傳統彼此喚醒？研究先理解民居本身：四翼圍合中央天井，配有深遠的木構屋頂與狹窄的側巷；爆炸圖則把原有的房子拆解為屋頂、構架、牆體與平面，逐層看清它的構成邏輯。設計隨後將屋頂抬升並開啟，讓光線與空氣流入下方更大的廳堂；新的節點以鋼筋把原有木柱與椽條接合到混凝土基座上，讓舊材料得以安全地承接新的用途。天井化為戲台，旁邊設有樂隊台，四周翼房布置觀眾席。剖面模型呈現老民居如何容納一場完整的演出與觀眾，光束落下之處，記憶與舞台同時被點亮。

pins.title: Micro Reservoir Construction: A Water-Collecting Tower
pins.description:
A high-rise for young residents that collects rainwater, makes power from it and cleans it for reuse.

Shenzhen | Housing | Water and energy | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 微型水庫建造：集水塔樓
zh-Hant.description:
一座為年輕住戶設計的高層建築，收集雨水、以之發電並淨化再利用。

深圳｜住宅｜水與能源｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Elevation of the reservoir tower.
蓄水塔樓立面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Young people in Shenzhen face rising rents and crowded housing, while the city's rivers and reservoirs are polluted. The project asks whether a high-rise for young residents could also collect, clean and reuse water.
captions: Historical development and network maps of the city.
Housing supply and the case for a vertical answer.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳的年輕人面對不斷上漲的租金與擁擠的居住環境，城市的河流與水庫也受到污染。本案探討一座為年輕住戶設計的高層建築，能否同時收集、淨化並再利用水資源。
captions: 城市的歷史發展與路網圖。
住房供給問題與垂直方案的提出。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A timeline traced how people have stored and moved water, from pile dwellings and canals to water mills and dams. These older devices became the starting point for small water systems inside a tower.
captions: From past to present: ways of storing and moving water.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 時間軸梳理了人們儲水與輸水的方式，從干欄式住屋、運河到水車與水壩。這些傳統裝置成為塔樓內部小型水系統的出發點。
captions: 從過去到現在：儲水與輸水的方式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rainwater is collected at the top and falls through the units, turning small turbines before it is stored and reused. Grey water and sewage pass through a series of planted ponds that clean it step by step.
captions: Water, power and nutrient cycle through the tower.
Micro power generation from falling water.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 雨水在頂部收集，流經各住宅單元並推動小型渦輪，再被儲存與再利用。灰水與污水則流經一系列植栽池，逐步得到淨化。
captions: 水、電與養分在塔樓中的循環。
以落水發電的微型發電系統。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each unit carries a sloped roof reservoir, shading fins tuned to the sun path and a light frame that holds the water. A timber model tests how the roof, frame and living space fit together.
captions: The reservoir tower rising among the city's dense housing.
Unit shape, shading and solar track.
Roof reservoir and hydropower axonometric.
Timber model of one unit.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每個單元配有傾斜的屋頂蓄水池、依日照路徑調整的遮陽板，以及承托水體的輕型構架。木構模型則測試屋頂、構架與居住空間如何組合。
captions: 蓄水塔聳立於城市密集住宅之間。
單元形態、遮陽與日照軌跡。
屋頂蓄水池與水力發電軸測圖。
單一單元的木構模型。

sections.heading: Micro Reservoir Construction - A Tower That Gathers Water for the Young
sections.body: Young people face rising rents and crowded housing, while the rivers and reservoirs of the city are polluted at the same time. The project thinks about these two problems together and asks whether a high-rise for young residents could also collect, clean and reuse water. A timeline traces how people have stored and moved water through history, from pile dwellings and canals to water mills and dams. These older devices become the inspiration for small water systems woven through the tower. Rainwater is collected at the top and falls through the units, turning small turbines on its way before being stored and reused. Grey water and sewage pass through a sequence of planted ponds that clean it step by step. Each unit carries a sloped roof reservoir, shading fins tuned to the path of the sun and a light frame that holds the water. A timber model tests how roof, frame and living space fit together. Dwelling and the water cycle depend on each other here, and the tower becomes a small reservoir standing upright in the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 微型水庫建造-一座為青年蓄水的塔樓
zh-Hant.body: 年輕人面對不斷上漲的租金與擁擠的居住環境，城市的河流與水庫也同時受到污染。作品把這兩個難題放在一起思考：一座為年輕住戶而設的高層建築，能否同時收集、淨化並再利用水資源？研究以一條時間軸，回顧人類儲水與輸水的方式，從干欄式住屋、運河到水車與水壩，這些古老的裝置成為塔樓內小型水系統的靈感來源。雨水在頂部被收集，流經各住宅單元並推動小型渦輪，再被儲存與再利用；灰水與污水則穿過一系列植栽池，一步步得到淨化。每個單元配有傾斜的屋頂蓄水池、依日照路徑調整的遮陽板，以及承托水體的輕型構架，木構模型檢驗屋頂、構架與居住空間如何組合。居住與水循環在此彼此依存，塔樓成為一座垂直的小型水庫。

pins.title: Village in the City: A Street Texture Tower
pins.description:
Small street elements of an urban village are catalogued and rebuilt as the sections of a new tower.

Architecture | Urban village | Street texture | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城中村：街道肌理塔樓
zh-Hant.description:
將城中村的小型街道元素整理成圖錄，再重組為一座新塔樓的剖面。

建築｜城中村｜街道肌理｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A drawn streetscape of the urban village.
城中村的街景繪圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The village in the city grew without a master plan, so its order comes from ownership, use and daily needs rather than from design. The project asks how this unplanned order could be read and carried into a new building.
captions: Detail of the streetscape drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 城中村在沒有總體規劃的情況下生長，其秩序來自產權、使用與日常需求，而非設計。本案探討如何解讀這種非規劃的秩序，並將其帶入一座新建築。
captions: 街景繪圖局部。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Stairs, fences, walls, steps and platforms in the village were drawn one by one as small street elements. They were then sorted by depth and openness to show how each one shapes shared space.
captions: Catalogue of street texture elements.
Depth and openness series.
The elements placed back along the village.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 將村中的樓梯、圍欄、牆體、台階與平台逐一繪製為小型街道元素。再依深度與開放度加以分類，說明每一種元素如何塑造共享空間。
captions: 街道肌理元素圖錄。
深度與開放度序列。
將元素放回村落的軸測長卷。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A hand-drawn profile was rotated, folded and spliced to form four sections of a new building. Point and volume studies then grew a porous shell that links levels from ground industry up to a sky greenhouse.
captions: Point, volume and deepen logic.
Axonometric of the tower and its levels.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 將手繪剖面旋轉、摺疊並拼接，形成新建築的四段剖面。點與體量的研究再生成多孔外殼，串連從地面產業層到空中溫室的各個樓層。
captions: 點、體量與深化的邏輯。
塔樓及其各樓層的軸測圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Study models and scenes test the stacked platforms and stairs inside the tower. A node detail lets rainwater run along the curved shell into a filter, while the same joint carries the weight of each block.
captions: Photos of the tower model.
Study models and interior scenes.
Exploded node and its physical model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 研究模型與場景測試塔樓內層疊的平台與樓梯。節點細部讓雨水沿曲面外殼流入過濾器，同一節點也承托每個量體的重量。
captions: 塔樓模型照片。
研究模型與室內場景。
節點爆炸圖與實體模型。

sections.heading: Village in the City - Stacking Street Texture Into a Tower
sections.body: The village in the city grew without any master plan, so its order comes from ownership, use and daily need rather than from the hand of a designer. The project asks whether this unplanned order could be read with care and carried into a new building. Stairs, fences, walls, steps and platforms in the village are drawn one by one as small street elements. They are then sorted by depth and openness, showing how each quietly shapes the spaces that neighbours share. The design rotates, folds and splices a hand-drawn profile to generate four sections of a new building. Point and volume studies grow a porous shell that links the levels, from ground-floor industry up to a greenhouse in the sky. Study models and scenes test the stacked platforms and stairs inside the tower. One node detail lets rainwater run along the curved shell into a filter, while the same joint carries the weight of each block above. The spontaneous life of the lanes is extended vertically, and the result is a tower that still keeps the warmth of a street.

zh-Hant.heading: 城中村-把街道肌理疊成一座塔
zh-Hant.body: 城中村在沒有總體規劃的情況下生長，它的秩序來自產權、使用與日常需求，而非任何設計師之手。作品探問，這種非規劃的秩序能否被細心閱讀，並轉化為一座新的建築？研究把村中的樓梯、圍欄、牆體、台階與平台逐一繪製為小型的街道元素，再依深度與開放度加以分類，說明每一種元素如何悄悄塑造著共享空間。設計隨後把一段手繪剖面旋轉、摺疊並拼接，生成新建築的四段剖面；點與體量的研究再長出一層多孔外殼，串連從地面產業層到空中溫室的各個樓層。研究模型與場景測試塔樓內層疊的平台與樓梯，一處節點細部讓雨水沿曲面外殼流入過濾器，同時承托每個量體的重量。街巷的自發生命力因此被垂直地延續下來，成為一座仍保有人情溫度的塔。

pins.title: Shiweitang: Industrial Waterfront Regeneration
pins.description:
An old riverside industrial district is reopened to the city with new uses, repaired streets and waterways.

Guangzhou | Urban regeneration | Industrial waterfront | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 石圍塘：工業水岸再生
zh-Hant.description:
以新功能、修補後的街道與水道，讓舊河岸工業區重新向城市開放。

廣州｜城市再生｜工業水岸｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Masterplan of the site strategy.
基地策略總平面圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The old industrial district of Shiweitang in Guangzhou has fallen out of use, leaving empty works and old rail lines. The project asks how the area could become a living part of the city again without losing its industrial past.
captions: The site context: location, existing conditions and the history of the factory area.
Analysis of history, land use, climate and transport.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州石圍塘的舊工業區已逐漸荒廢，留下空置的廠房與舊鐵道。本案探討如何讓這片地區重新融入城市生活，同時保留其工業記憶。
captions: 基地脈絡：區位、現況與工廠區的歷史。
歷史、土地使用、氣候與交通分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Maps of land use, transport, green space and building condition showed where the site was cut off and where it could be joined up. A management study then set out how the government, developers and artists could share the cost and the gains.
captions: Design key nodes with autonomous boats along the waterway.
Management and fund flow among the entities.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 土地使用、交通、綠地與建物現況的分析圖，顯示出基地被切斷之處與可以重新連結之處。管理研究則說明政府、開發商與藝術家如何分擔成本並共享收益。
captions: 沿水道配置自動駕駛船的設計關鍵節點。
各方之間的管理與資金流動。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Five planning concepts were set out, from weaving the site back together to keeping local identity and a sound economy. A hand-drawn concept line followed the river and linked the new uses along it.
captions: Five planning concepts and the programme links.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 本案提出五項規劃概念，從重新編織基地到保留在地特色與健全經濟。手繪概念線沿著河道展開，串連沿岸的新功能。
captions: 五項規劃概念與功能關聯。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The masterplan opens the riverbank, repairs the street network and places a museum, a station, parks, homes and technology spaces across the site. Small self-driving boats on the waterways serve as taxis, markets, stages and carriers between the key nodes.
captions: Long section across the site.
Strategy diagrams for water, green space and mobility.
Key nodes along the waterways.
Axonometric and section of a reused factory.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 總平面打開河岸、修補街道網絡，並在基地中配置博物館、車站、公園、住宅與科技空間。水道上的小型自動駕駛船隻在各關鍵節點之間擔任水上計程車、市集、舞台與運輸工具。
captions: 橫跨基地的長剖面。
水、綠地與交通的策略圖。
沿水道的關鍵節點。
再利用廠房的軸測圖與剖面。

sections.heading: Shiweitang - Reweaving Industrial Memory Along the River
sections.body: An old industrial district has slowly fallen out of use, leaving empty works and abandoned rail lines behind. The project asks how the area could become a living part of the city again without losing its industrial past. Maps of land use, transport, green space and building condition identify where the site has been cut off and where it might be stitched back together. A management study then explains how government, developers and artists could share both the cost and the gains, so that renewal can be sustained over time. Five planning concepts follow, ranging from weaving the site back together to keeping local identity and a sound economy. A hand-drawn concept line unfolds along the river and links the new uses that gather on its banks. The masterplan opens the riverbank, repairs the street network and places a museum, a station, parks, homes and technology spaces across the ground. Small self-driving boats glide between key nodes, serving now as taxis and now as markets, stages or carriers, so that the river becomes once more the moving bloodstream of the district.

zh-Hant.heading: 石圍塘-在河岸重新編織工業記憶
zh-Hant.body: 一片舊工業區逐漸荒廢，留下空置的廠房與停用的鐵道。作品提問：如何讓這裡重新融入城市生活，同時不遺失它的工業過去？研究以土地使用、交通、綠地與建物現況的分析圖，辨認基地被切斷之處與可以重新縫合的位置；一項管理研究進一步說明，政府、開發商與藝術家如何分擔成本、共享收益，使更新得以持續。五項規劃概念由此提出，從重新編織基地，到保留在地特色與維持健全的經濟；一條手繪的概念線沿著河道展開，串起沿岸的新功能。總平面打開河岸、修補街道網絡，在基地中配置博物館、車站、公園、住宅與科技空間。水道上的小型自動駕駛船隻穿梭於各節點，時而是計程車，時而化為市集、舞台或運輸工具，讓河流再次成為這片土地流動的血脈。

pins.title: Vertical Art Settlement: Designing with Sound
pins.description:
Noise recorded on the site is mapped and turned into the form of an art settlement.

Guangzhou | Art settlement | Sound study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 垂直藝術聚落：以聲音設計
zh-Hant.description:
將基地錄下的噪音繪製成圖，轉化為藝術聚落的形態。

廣州｜藝術聚落｜聲音研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Site models of the settlement.
聚落的基地模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A survey of the site recorded air pressure, terrain, sound and the movement of people, and found that noise was the most serious issue. Sound therefore became the starting point for the design of a vertical art settlement in Guangzhou.
captions: City mapping of Guangzhou and analysis of the venue users' behaviour.
Site survey of air pressure, terrain and sound.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 基地調查記錄了氣壓、地形、聲音與人流，發現噪音是最嚴重的問題。因此聲音成為廣州一座垂直藝術聚落的設計出發點。
captions: 廣州城市圖繪與場地使用者行為分析。
氣壓、地形與聲音的基地調查。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sounds recorded on the site were turned into data with software and shown as spectrograms. These readings were then joined with hand-drawn lines of how sound spreads across the ground.
captions: Sketch and photo strip from the sound recordings on site.
A circular collage of the vertical art settlement at work and in life.
Spectrograms of the recorded sound.
Plan composition drawn from the sound.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 將基地錄下的聲音以軟體轉換為數據，並以頻譜圖呈現。再把這些讀數與手繪的聲音傳播線結合起來。
captions: 基地錄音所繪的草圖與照片條。
垂直藝術聚落工作與生活的環形拼貼。
錄音的頻譜圖。
由聲音推演出的平面構成。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The sound map was split into positive and negative forms, raised into a 3D field and cut into blocks. Virtual lines then moved from the flat plan into three-dimensional routes and volumes.
captions: Layers from sound data to form.
Axonometric steps of the settlement.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 將聲音地圖拆分為正形與負形，抬升為三維場域並切分為量塊。虛擬線條再從平面轉化為立體的路徑與量體。
captions: 從聲音數據到形態的圖層。
聚落的軸測推演步驟。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A set of white site models shows the settlement growing over the terrain as a field of studios and shared spaces. Closer model views test how the work and living parts sit together.
captions: Close views of the models.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一組白色基地模型呈現聚落如何在地形上生長為工作室與共享空間的場域。近距離的模型視角則測試工作與生活部分如何並置。
captions: 模型近照。

sections.heading: Vertical Art Settlement - Composing Space Out of Noise
sections.body: A survey of the site recorded air pressure, terrain, sound and the movement of people, and it showed that noise was the most serious problem of all. Rather than shutting the noise out, the project takes sound itself as the starting point for a vertical art settlement. Recordings made on the site are turned into data with software and displayed as spectrograms that reveal their peaks and valleys. These readings are then joined with hand-drawn lines describing how sound spreads across the ground, so that invisible waves leave visible traces on paper. Next the sound map is split into positive and negative forms, lifted into a three-dimensional field and cut into blocks. Virtual lines move from the flat plan into spatial routes and volumes. A set of white site models shows the settlement growing over the terrain as a field of studios and shared spaces, while closer model views study how working and living parts sit together. What began as a nuisance is translated into a piece of music that can be inhabited, and artistic making begins with careful listening.

zh-Hant.heading: 垂直藝術聚落-把噪音譜成空間
zh-Hant.body: 基地調查記錄了氣壓、地形、聲音與人流，結果顯示，噪音是此地最嚴重的問題。作品沒有選擇隔絕它，而是把聲音本身當作一座垂直藝術聚落的設計起點。在基地錄下的聲響，先經軟體轉換為數據，以頻譜圖呈現其起伏；這些讀數再與手繪的聲音傳播線結合，讓看不見的聲波在紙上留下痕跡。隨後，聲音地圖被拆分為正形與負形，抬升為三維的場域並切分為量塊，虛擬的線條也從平面轉化為立體的路徑與體量。一組白色基地模型呈現聚落如何沿著地形生長，成為工作室與共享空間交織的場域；近距離的模型視角則細察工作與生活的部分如何並置。原本令人困擾的噪音，經過轉譯成為一段可以居住的樂章，也讓藝術的創作從聆聽環境開始。

pins.title: Chaotic Era: A Curving Terraced Settlement
pins.description:
Free curves and layered lines loosen rigid building forms into a terraced settlement.

Architecture | Terraced settlement | Curve study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 混沌時代：曲線層疊聚落
zh-Hant.description:
以自由曲線與層疊線條鬆動僵硬的建築形態，形成層疊的聚落。

建築｜層疊聚落｜曲線研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Layered line collage.
層疊的線條拼貼。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project starts from the idea that people are both emotional and rational beings. A dense collage of lines and marks explores how order and disorder can sit together.
captions: Film stills of the actor beside sketches and models of each personality.
A film poster used as a reference.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品從「人同時是感性與理性的存在」這個想法出發。一幅密集的線條與記號拼貼，探討秩序與混亂如何並存。
captions: 演員劇照，並列每種人格的草圖與模型。
作為參考的電影海報。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Free curves traced from living forms are used to loosen the rigid lines of conventional buildings. A hand sketch tests how these curves can wrap and grow over a built mass.
captions: Figure diagrams and photo studies of split personalities.
A drawing of the human figure along a vertical axis between nature and divinity.
Sketch of curves growing over a building.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以從生命形態中描摹出的自由曲線，鬆動傳統建築的僵硬線條。一張手繪草圖測試這些曲線如何包覆並生長於建築量體之上。
captions: 人格分裂的人形圖解與照片研究。
沿著自然與神性之間垂直軸線的人體圖。
曲線生長於建築上的草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A long section sets organic, curving forms against a stepped base and an industrial skyline. It shows complexity and contradiction as a richer choice than a single clear order.
captions: Long section of the curving forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一張長剖面將有機的曲線形態置於階梯式基座與工業天際線之前。它呈現出複雜與矛盾，比單一清晰的秩序更為豐富。
captions: 曲線形態的長剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The renders show a settlement of stacked blocks with terraces, bridges and roof gardens. Paths and green roofs link the levels into one lively, layered place.
captions: View across the terraces.
Aerial view of the settlement.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 渲染圖呈現一座由堆疊量體構成的聚落，配有露台、天橋與屋頂花園。步道與綠屋頂把各層連結成一個生動而多層次的場所。
captions: 橫越露台的視角。
聚落鳥瞰。

sections.heading: Chaotic Era - A Settlement Growing Between Order and Disorder
sections.body: The project begins from a simple yet searching idea: that people are emotional and rational beings at the same time. A dense collage of lines and marks first asks how order and disorder might live side by side without one having to defeat the other. Free curves traced from living forms are then used to loosen the rigid straight lines of conventional buildings. A hand sketch tests how these curves can wrap around a built mass and keep growing over it. A long section sets the organic, curving forms against a stepped base and an industrial skyline, so that softness and hardness stand in open dialogue. It also argues a position, that complexity and contradiction are richer, and closer to real life, than a single clear order. The final renders show a settlement of stacked blocks scattered with terraces, bridges and roof gardens. Paths and green roofs link the levels into one lively and layered place. Chaos is no longer treated as a problem to be removed. It becomes the fertile ground in which many different ways of living can take root together.

zh-Hant.heading: 混沌時代-在秩序與混亂之間生長的聚落
zh-Hant.body: 作品從一個簡單而深刻的想法出發：人同時是感性與理性的存在。一幅密集的線條與記號拼貼，率先探問秩序與混亂如何能並肩共存，而不必由其中一方取勝。接著，從生命形態中描摹而來的自由曲線，被用來鬆動傳統建築僵硬的直線；一張手繪草圖測試這些曲線如何包覆量體，並在其上持續生長。一張長剖面將有機的曲線形態置於階梯式基座與工業天際線之前，讓柔軟與堅硬彼此對照，也提出一種觀點：複雜與矛盾，比單一清晰的秩序更為豐富，也更貼近真實的生活。最終的渲染圖呈現一座由堆疊量體構成的聚落，露台、天橋與屋頂花園錯落其間，步道與綠屋頂把各層連結成生動而多層次的場所。混沌在此不再是需要被消除的問題，而成為容納多樣生活的土壤。

pins.title: Urbanism of Nature: A Furniture Landscape Tower
pins.description:
Furniture forms are sliced into layers and stacked into a tower of flowing interior landscape.

Architecture | Interior landscape | Furniture study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然的都市主義：家具地景塔樓
zh-Hant.description:
將家具形態切分為圖層，堆疊成一座室內地景流動的塔樓。

建築｜室內地景｜家具研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Model of the tower.
塔樓模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Space and human behaviour shape each other, and furniture decides much of how people eat, rest and meet. The project asks how furniture could be turned into interior space itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 空間與人的行為彼此塑造，而家具在很大程度上決定了人們如何用餐、休息與相聚。這個作品探問家具如何能轉化為室內空間本身。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Everyday objects such as a lounge, table, chair, bathtub, sofa, bench and toilet were studied as shared forms. Their profiles were sliced into contour layers so they could become part of a terrain.
captions: Furniture forms sliced into contour layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 躺椅、桌子、椅子、浴缸、沙發、長凳與馬桶等日常物件被當作共通形態加以研究。它們的輪廓被切分為等高層，使其能成為地形的一部分。
captions: 切分為等高層的家具形態。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A basic slope was folded inward to invite conversation, with openings that give vertical circulation. Several layers were combined so the openings also bring in light and air.
captions: Slope, inward flow and access diagrams.
Plans of the layered openings.
Exploded layers of the interior.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一個基本坡面向內折疊以促進交談，並以開口提供垂直動線。多個圖層疊合，使這些開口同時引入光線與空氣。
captions: 坡面、內向動線與可達性圖解。
層疊開口的平面。
室內的分解圖層。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The layers stack into a tower whose floors flow like landscape, shown in section and in interior model views. Laser-cut acrylic and printed models test how the gradient ceilings shape the living space.
captions: Section through the tower.
Interior model views with scale figures.
Acrylic model studies.
Laser-cut acrylic model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些圖層堆疊成一座樓層如地景般流動的塔樓，以剖面與室內模型視角呈現。雷射切割壓克力與列印模型則測試漸變天花如何塑造居住空間。
captions: 塔樓剖面。
附比例人偶的室內模型視角。
壓克力模型研究。
雷射切割壓克力模型。

sections.heading: Urbanism of Nature - When Furniture Grows Into a Landscape
sections.body: Space and human behaviour shape each other, and furniture largely decides how people eat, rest and meet. The project poses a bold question: could furniture stop being an object placed inside a room and instead become the interior space itself? The study starts from everyday things such as a lounge, a table, a chair, a bathtub, a sofa, a bench and a toilet, reading them as shared forms. Their profiles are sliced into contour layers so that they can melt into a terrain. A basic slope is folded inward to invite conversation, while openings cut into it provide vertical circulation. When several layers are combined, the same openings also bring in light and air. In the end the layers stack into a tower whose floors rise and fall like landscape, shown through sections and interior model views. Laser-cut acrylic and printed models test how gradient ceilings shape the space of living. Sitting, lying, leaning and meeting all become part of the ground here, so that dwelling feels less like furnishing a box and more like inhabiting a hillside.

zh-Hant.heading: 自然的都市主義-當家具長成一片地景
zh-Hant.body: 空間與人的行為彼此塑造，而家具在很大程度上決定了人們如何用餐、休息與相聚。作品由此提出一個大膽的問題：家具能否不再只是放置於室內的物件，而直接轉化為室內空間本身？研究從躺椅、桌子、椅子、浴缸、沙發、長凳與馬桶等日常物件出發，將它們視為共通的形態，並把輪廓切分為一層層等高線，使其得以融入地形。一個基本坡面向內折疊，邀請彼此交談，坡面上的開口則提供垂直動線；多個圖層疊合之後，這些開口同時引入光線與空氣。最終，圖層堆疊成一座樓層如地景般起伏流動的塔樓，剖面與室內模型呈現其中的生活場景，雷射切割壓克力與列印模型則測試漸變天花如何塑造居住空間。坐、臥、倚靠與相遇，在此都化為地形的一部分。

pins.title: Beacon of Hope: A Mobile Modular School
pins.description:
A school of folding timber classrooms that can be taken apart and rebuilt wherever children need it.

Architecture | Mobile school | Modular timber | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 希望燈塔：可移動的模組化學校
zh-Hant.description:
以摺疊木構教室組成的學校，可拆解並在孩子需要之處重建。

建築｜可移動學校｜模組化木構｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Plan of the modular campus on its slope.
坡地上模組化校園的平面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Children in unstable regions can lose their schools overnight, and rebuilding takes time that education cannot spare. This competition entry asks how a school could be taken apart quickly and put back together wherever it is needed.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 身處不穩定地區的孩子可能一夕之間失去學校，而重建所需的時間是教育無法等待的。這個競圖作品探問，學校能否被快速拆解，並在需要之處重新組立。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site study mapped where pupils walk, gather, shelter and find quiet on the hillside. A circulation spine inspired by a traditional woven pattern was then simplified step by step to free up open ground.
captions: Layout development from spine to open campus.
Solar, heat gain and airflow analysis of one classroom.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地研究描繪了學生在山坡上行走、聚集、避護與獨處的位置。一條取材自傳統編織圖紋的動線主軸隨後被逐步簡化，以釋放更多開放地面。
captions: 從主軸到開放校園的配置推演。
單一教室的日照、得熱與氣流分析。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Paper folding tests turned the woven grid into a window panel that can be closed, half open or fully open. The panels sit in a light timber frame with fabric and board infill above a gabion base of local stone.
captions: Paper folding tests.
Sketches of the foldable window wall.
Structure details of the folding frame.
Material section with timber, fabric, board and stone.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 摺紙測試將編織網格轉化為可全關、半開或全開的窗板。窗板嵌入輕量木構架，以布料與板材填充，下方則是以在地石材構成的石籠基座。
captions: 摺紙測試。
可摺疊窗牆的草圖。
摺疊框架的構造細部。
木材、布料、板材與石材的材料剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each classroom stacks a gabion base, folding window walls, a timber frame and a lifted canopy, all removable for rapid assembly. Sections and a scale model show how the canopy shades shared roof terraces linked by stairs.
captions: Exploded axonometric of one classroom.
Elevation and section across the slope.
Physical model section.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每間教室由石籠基座、摺疊窗牆、木構架與抬升的頂棚堆疊而成，皆可拆卸以便快速組裝。剖面與比例模型呈現頂棚如何為以樓梯相連的共享屋頂平台遮陽。
captions: 單一教室的分解軸測。
橫跨坡地的立面與剖面。
實體模型剖面。

sections.heading: Beacon of Hope - A School That Can Travel With Its Children
sections.body: Children in unstable regions can lose their schools overnight, and the long time that rebuilding takes is exactly what education cannot afford to wait for. This competition entry asks whether a school could be taken apart quickly and raised again wherever it is needed. The site study maps where pupils walk, gather, shelter and find quiet on the hillside. A circulation spine inspired by a traditional woven pattern is then simplified step by step, freeing more open ground for play and learning. Paper folding tests turn the woven grid into a window panel that can be closed, half open or fully open. The panels sit within a light timber frame filled with fabric and board, resting above a gabion base built from local stone. Each classroom stacks gabion base, folding window walls, timber frame and lifted canopy, and every layer can be removed for rapid assembly. Sections and a scale model show how the canopy shades shared roof terraces linked by stairs. Like a portable lamp, the school can settle anywhere and light a steady place for learning.

zh-Hant.heading: 希望燈塔-一座可以隨孩子遷徙的學校
zh-Hant.body: 身處不穩定地區的孩子，可能在一夕之間失去學校，而重建所需的漫長時間，正是教育最無法等待的。這件競圖作品提問：學校能否被快速拆解，並在需要之處重新立起？基地研究描繪了學生在山坡上行走、聚集、避護與獨處的位置；一條取材自傳統編織圖紋的動線主軸，隨後被逐步簡化，為孩子釋放更多開放的地面。摺紙測試把編織網格轉化為可全關、半開或全開的窗板，嵌入輕量木構架，以布料與板材填充，下方則是以在地石材堆成的石籠基座。每間教室由石籠、摺疊窗牆、木構架與抬升的頂棚依序疊合，皆可拆卸、快速組裝；剖面與比例模型呈現頂棚如何為以樓梯相連的屋頂平台遮陽。學校因此像一盞可攜的燈，無論落腳何處，都能為學習點亮一方安穩。

pins.title: Havenopause: A Cave-like Retreat for Menopause
pins.description:
A soft, cave-like retreat that uses enclosure, gentle light and quiet to support women through menopause.

Architecture | Restorative space | Women's health | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Havenopause：為更年期而設的洞穴休憩所
zh-Hant.description:
以包覆、柔光與寧靜陪伴女性度過更年期的柔軟洞穴休憩所。

建築｜療癒空間｜女性健康｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Elevation of the cave-like retreat.
洞穴般休憩所的立面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Menopause brings physical and emotional changes that are often overlooked or misunderstood. The project asks how architecture could offer a quiet place of calm for women going through this life stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 更年期帶來的身心變化常被忽視或誤解。這個作品探問，建築能否為正經歷這個人生階段的女性提供一處平靜之所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Diagrams map how symptoms rise and fall across three stages, and how reliance on medication has grown. Studies of low-stimulation therapy suggested that enclosure, soft light and muffled sound can ease anxiety and poor sleep.
captions: Symptoms across the three stages.
Medication use and its side effects.
How cave-like qualities answer each need.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 圖解描繪症狀在三個階段中的起伏，以及對藥物依賴的增加。低刺激療法的研究指出，包覆感、柔和光線與減弱的聲響有助於緩解焦慮與失眠。
captions: 三個階段中的症狀分布。
藥物使用及其副作用。
洞穴般特質如何回應各種需求。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Hand-shaped clay models explored enclosure, porosity and flow through touch. Six digital forms, from a listening pod to a grounding garden, were then refined into layered floor plans.
captions: Hand-made clay models.
Six digital concept models.
Floor plans of three levels.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以手捏塑的黏土模型透過觸感探索包覆、孔隙與流動。從聆聽艙到接地花園的六個數位形體，隨後被深化為層疊的樓層平面。
captions: 手作黏土模型。
六個數位概念模型。
三個樓層的平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The retreat becomes a soft shell on slender tree-like legs, with a spiral stair rising through pockets of shade and light. A perspective section and a white physical model show how enclosed and semi-open rooms offer different degrees of privacy.
captions: Perspective section through two retreats.
White physical model.
Details of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 休憩所成為立於纖細樹狀支柱上的柔軟殼體，螺旋梯穿越明暗交錯的空間向上延伸。透視剖面與白色實體模型呈現封閉與半開放的房間如何提供不同程度的私密性。
captions: 穿越兩座休憩所的透視剖面。
白色實體模型。
模型細部。

sections.heading: Havenopause - A Soft Cave for a Quiet Passage of Life
sections.body: Menopause brings physical and emotional changes that are often overlooked or misunderstood. The project asks whether architecture could offer a genuinely calm place for women passing through this stage of life. Diagrams trace how symptoms rise and fall across three stages, and how reliance on medication steadily grows. Studies of low-stimulation therapy suggest that enclosure, soft light and muffled sound can ease anxiety and restless nights. The design therefore begins with touch. Hand-shaped clay models explore enclosure, porosity and flow through the fingers, and six digital forms then follow, ranging from a listening pod to a grounding garden, before being refined into layered floor plans. In the final proposal the retreat becomes a soft shell raised on slender tree-like legs, with a spiral stair climbing gently through pockets of shade and light. A perspective section and a white physical model show how enclosed and semi-open rooms offer different degrees of privacy. Within this cave-like shelter the body is given room to slow down and to rediscover its own rhythm.

zh-Hant.heading: Havenopause-為更年期而築的柔軟洞穴
zh-Hant.body: 更年期帶來的身心變化，常被忽視或誤解。作品提問，建築能否為正走過這段人生階段的女性，提供一處真正平靜的所在？研究以圖解描繪症狀在三個階段中的起伏，以及對藥物日益加深的依賴；低刺激療法的文獻則指出，包覆感、柔和的光線與減弱的聲響，有助於緩解焦慮與失眠。設計於是從觸覺開始，以手捏塑的黏土模型探索包覆、孔隙與流動，再發展出從聆聽艙到接地花園的六個數位形體，並深化為層疊的樓層平面。最終，休憩所成為立於纖細樹狀支柱上的柔軟殼體，螺旋梯穿越明暗交錯的空間緩緩上升。透視剖面與白色實體模型呈現封閉與半開放的房間如何給予不同程度的私密，讓身體在洞穴般的庇護裡，重新找回自己的節奏。

pins.title: Modular LiveBlock: A Reconfigurable Stage System
pins.description:
A kit of printed joints and timber rods that assembles quickly into stadium, festival and arena stages.

Architecture | Stage system | Discrete assembly | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Modular LiveBlock：可重組的舞台系統
zh-Hant.description:
以列印接頭與木桿組成的構件系統，可快速組裝成體育場、音樂節與室內場館舞台。

建築｜舞台系統｜離散組裝｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: From factory printing to assembly in a stadium.
從工廠列印到體育場內的組裝。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Touring concerts spend much of their time and budget building and striking stages, and each venue asks for a different set. The project asks whether one kit of reusable parts could serve many kinds of stage.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 巡迴演唱會的大量時間與預算花在搭建與拆除舞台上，而每個場地又需要不同的配置。這個作品探問，能否以一套可重複使用的構件服務多種舞台。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A study of stage history and current touring shows how construction and load-out dominate the production schedule. A role-based study sets out what designers, engineers, technicians and performers each value in a stage.
captions: Time spent on each production phase and growth trends.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 對舞台演變與當代巡演的研究顯示，搭建與撤場佔據了製作時程的大部分。一項以角色為基礎的研究，釐清了設計師、工程師、技術人員與表演者各自重視的舞台面向。
captions: 各製作階段的時間分配與成長趨勢。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: H-shaped joints were 3D printed, tested and redesigned with a carved connection and bolted plates for stability. Small S-scale joints combine into M-scale floors, walls, stairs and columns, which then form L-scale stage spaces.
captions: 3D-printed joint tests.
Redesigned component after structural testing.
Timber model exploration.
S-scale joints with single, double and triple passes.
M-scale floor, wall, stair and column assemblies.
L-scale configurations at human scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: H 形接頭經 3D 列印與測試後，改以刻槽接合與螺栓固定板重新設計以提升穩定性。小尺度的 S 級接頭組合成 M 級的樓板、牆、樓梯與柱，再構成 L 級的舞台空間。
captions: 3D 列印接頭測試。
結構測試後重新設計的構件。
木材模型探索。
單、雙、三向穿接的 S 級接頭。
M 級的樓板、牆、樓梯與柱組合。
人體尺度下的 L 級配置。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Parts are printed in a factory, trucked to the venue and assembled by robotic arms into the stage. The same kit forms a stadium stage, an open festival stage and an arena stage viewed from all sides.
captions: Assembled and exploded views of the system.
Stadium, festival and indoor arena configurations.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 構件在工廠列印、以卡車運至場地，再由機械手臂組裝成舞台。同一套構件可組成體育場舞台、開放的音樂節舞台，以及四面觀看的室內場館舞台。
captions: 系統的組合與分解視圖。
體育場、音樂節與室內場館的配置。

sections.heading: Modular LiveBlock - One Kit of Parts for Countless Stages
sections.body: Touring concerts spend a great share of their time and budget building and striking stages again and again, and every venue asks for a different set. The project asks whether a single kit of reusable parts could serve many kinds of stage. A study of stage history and of current touring shows that construction and load-out dominate the production schedule. A role-based study then sets out what designers, engineers, technicians and performers each value most in a stage. The design starts from the smallest node. H-shaped joints are 3D printed, tested and redesigned with a carved connection and bolted plates for greater stability. Small S-scale joints combine into M-scale floors, walls, stairs and columns, which in turn form complete L-scale stage spaces, a system that grows from detail to whole. Parts are printed in a factory, trucked to the venue and assembled by robotic arms. The same kit can become a stadium stage, an open festival stage or an arena stage viewed from every side, so that each performance grows from one shared vocabulary rather than from waste.

zh-Hant.heading: LiveBlock模組舞台-一套構件演繹萬種場景
zh-Hant.body: 巡迴演唱會的大量時間與預算，耗費在一次又一次的搭建與拆除上，而每個場地又要求不同的舞台。作品追問，能否以一套可重複使用的構件服務多種舞台？研究回顧舞台的演變與當代巡演，發現搭建與撤場佔據了製作時程的大半；一項以角色為基礎的研究，則釐清設計師、工程師、技術人員與表演者各自重視的面向。設計從最小的節點開始，H 形接頭經 3D 列印與測試後，改以刻槽接合與螺栓固定板提升穩定性。小尺度接頭組合成樓板、牆、樓梯與柱，再進一步構成完整的舞台空間，形成由小到大的三級系統。構件在工廠列印，以卡車運抵場地，由機械手臂組裝；同一套構件可化身體育場舞台、開放的音樂節舞台，或四面觀看的室內場館舞台，讓每一次演出都從同一組語彙中生長。

pins.title: Re:Opera: A Pop-up Cantonese Opera Stage
pins.description:
A modular pop-up stage that brings Cantonese opera back into the streets as a walkable garden of scenes.

Guangzhou | Pop-up architecture | Cantonese opera | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: Re:Opera：快閃粵劇舞台
zh-Hant.description:
將粵劇帶回街頭的模組化快閃舞台，化為一座可漫遊的場景庭園。

廣州｜快閃建築｜粵劇｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Bird's-eye view of the pop-up opera garden.
快閃粵劇庭園的鳥瞰。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Cantonese opera has moved from open public settings into enclosed theatres, and fewer young people now come across it by chance. The project proposes a temporary, modular stage that brings the opera back into everyday streets in Guangzhou.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 粵劇已從開放的公共場域移入封閉的劇院，年輕人偶然接觸它的機會也越來越少。這個作品提出一座臨時的模組化舞台，讓粵劇重新回到廣州的日常街道。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Audience data shows a falling and ageing audience, held back by rigid formats, language barriers and little presence in public space. A renewal district by the waterfront was chosen because walking routes from residents and visitors meet there.
captions: Audience trend, age and attendance constraints.
Strategy from fixed stage to pop-up movement.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 觀眾數據顯示觀眾數量下降且日趨高齡，受限於僵化的演出形式、語言門檻與在公共空間中的缺席。基地選在一處水岸更新街區，因為居民與遊客的步行路線在此交會。
captions: 觀眾趨勢、年齡與觀演限制。
從固定舞台到快閃動線的策略。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The scenes of one classic opera were read as a journey from movement to enclosure and finally revelation. Stage stills were translated into spatial sketches, required scenes and four spatial frameworks that guide the massing.
captions: Plot analysis with stage stills as reference.
From storyboard to diagram, sketch and required scene.
Conceptual massing evolution.
Four spatial frameworks with study models.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一齣經典粵劇的場景被解讀為從移動、封閉到最終揭示的旅程。舞台劇照被轉譯為空間草圖、所需場景，以及引導量體配置的四種空間框架。
captions: 以舞台劇照為參考的情節分析。
從分鏡到圖解、草圖與所需場景。
概念量體演變。
四種空間框架與研究模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Six loosely arranged pop-up spaces form a walkable garden where the audience follows the story from scene to scene. Light timber frames allow the stage to be assembled and taken down easily.
captions: Living room and corridor scenes.
Study room scene.
Palace and mansion scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 六個鬆散配置的快閃空間構成一座可漫遊的庭園，觀眾隨著故事在場景之間移動。輕量木構架讓舞台能輕鬆組裝與拆卸。
captions: 客廳與迴廊場景。
書房場景。
宮殿與府邸場景。

sections.heading: Pop-up Cantonese Opera Stage - Letting Opera Wander Back Into the Streets
sections.body: Since Cantonese opera withdrew from open public settings into enclosed theatres, young people have had fewer and fewer chances to come across it by accident. Audience data shows a shrinking and ageing public, held back by rigid formats, language barriers and an almost total absence from public space. The project therefore chooses a renewal district by the waterfront, a place where the walking routes of residents and visitors already meet. The scenes of one classic opera are read as a journey that moves from motion to enclosure and finally to revelation. Stage stills are then translated into spatial sketches, a list of required scenes and four spatial frameworks that guide the massing. Six loosely arranged pop-up spaces form a walkable garden, and the audience follows the story from scene to scene as if stepping into the libretto itself. Light timber frames let the stage be assembled and taken down with ease. Opera no longer waits for people to enter a theatre; it walks back into the streets and is seen again within ordinary life.

zh-Hant.heading: 快閃粵劇舞台-讓戲曲重新走回街巷
zh-Hant.body: 粵劇從開放的公共場域退入封閉的劇院後，年輕人偶然與它相遇的機會便越來越少。觀眾數據顯示，觀眾正在減少並日趨高齡，原因包括僵化的演出形式、語言門檻，以及在公共空間中的缺席。作品因此選擇一處水岸更新街區，那裡正是居民與遊客步行路線交會之處。一齣經典劇目的場景被解讀為一段旅程：從移動、封閉，到最終的揭示；舞台劇照隨後被轉譯為空間草圖、所需的場景，以及引導量體配置的四種空間框架。六個鬆散配置的快閃空間共同構成一座可漫遊的庭園，觀眾隨著故事在場景之間移動，彷彿親身走進戲文。輕量木構架讓舞台得以輕鬆組裝與拆卸，戲曲因此不再只等人走進劇院，而能主動走回街巷，在日常裡重新被看見。

pins.title: Fragmented Self: A Tower of Many Personalities
pins.description:
Six personalities from a film are translated into six spatial fragments and assembled into one tower.

Architecture | Character-based spatial study | Fragmentation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 破碎的自我：多重人格之塔
zh-Hant.description:
將一部電影中的六種人格轉譯為六個空間碎片，並組裝成一座塔樓。

建築｜角色空間研究｜碎片化｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometric of the tower inside its mesh skin.
包覆於網狀表皮中的塔樓軸測圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A single person can hold several conflicting identities at once, yet buildings usually assume one coherent user. The project asks how a fragmented mind could be translated into one inhabitable tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個人可能同時擁有數種相互衝突的身分，建築卻往往假設只有一位一致的使用者。這個作品探問，一個破碎的心智能如何被轉譯為一座可居住的塔樓。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A film about a character with several personalities served as the reference, and its storyline was mapped chapter by chapter. Each personality was then read as a set of traits such as fear, control, innocence or defence.
captions: A fearful self as a maze of soft fragments.
An artistic self as a stretched canopy.
An ordered self as a stacked, guarded volume.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 作品以一部描寫多重人格角色的電影為參考，逐章梳理其敘事結構。每一種人格再被解讀為一組特質，例如恐懼、控制、天真或防衛。
captions: 恐懼的自我化為柔軟碎片構成的迷宮。
藝術性的自我化為延展的頂棚。
秩序的自我化為層疊而戒備的量體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Six personalities were abstracted into six drawings and six study models, each with its own spatial logic and material feel. Contrasting conditions such as control, vulnerability and protection were kept side by side instead of resolved.
captions: A childlike self as playful arches and holes.
A controlling self as rigid walls and frames.
A defensive self as a swollen, cave-like ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 六種人格被抽象為六張圖面與六個研究模型，各自擁有獨特的空間邏輯與材質感。控制、脆弱與保護等對立狀態被並置保留，而非被調和。
captions: 孩子般的自我化為輕快的拱與孔洞。
控制的自我化為剛硬的牆與框架。
防衛的自我化為膨脹如洞穴的地景。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The fragments are assembled into a vertical tower around a central core, wrapped in a soft mesh skin. Plans and a section show how the different spaces interlock floor by floor.
captions: Two floor plans.
Section through the tower.
Model views of the coloured fragments.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些碎片沿著中央核心組裝成一座垂直塔樓，外覆柔軟的網狀表皮。平面與剖面呈現不同空間如何逐層交錯咬合。
captions: 兩層平面圖。
塔樓剖面。
彩色碎片的模型視角。

sections.heading: Fragmented Self - A Tower Built for Many Selves at Once
sections.body: A single person may hold several conflicting identities at once, yet buildings usually assume one coherent user who stays the same from room to room. The project therefore asks whether a fragmented mind could be translated into a tower that can actually be inhabited. A film about a character with many personalities serves as the reference, and its story is mapped chapter by chapter. Each personality is then read as a cluster of traits such as fear, control, innocence or defence. Six personalities are abstracted into six drawings and six study models, each with its own spatial logic and material feel. Opposing conditions, control against vulnerability and exposure against protection, are kept side by side rather than resolved into harmony. Finally the fragments are assembled around a central core into a vertical tower wrapped in a soft mesh skin, and plans and a section show how the different spaces interlock floor by floor. The tower does not smooth away inner contradiction. Instead it lets the cracks become structure, admitting that a whole self has always been made of many voices.

zh-Hant.heading: 破碎的自我-為多重人格築起一座塔
zh-Hant.body: 一個人可能同時懷抱數種彼此衝突的身分，建築卻往往預設只有一位前後一致的使用者。作品由此提問：一個破碎的心智，能否被轉譯為一座可以居住的塔樓？研究以一部描寫多重人格角色的電影為參照，逐章梳理敘事，再把每一種人格解讀為一組特質，例如恐懼、控制、天真或防衛。六種人格被抽象為六張圖面與六個研究模型，各自擁有獨特的空間邏輯與材質感；控制與脆弱、暴露與保護等對立狀態被並置保留，而不急於調和。最後，這些碎片沿著中央核心組裝成垂直的塔樓，外覆柔軟的網狀表皮，平面與剖面揭示不同空間如何逐層交錯咬合。塔樓沒有抹平內在的矛盾，反而讓裂縫成為結構，承認完整的自我，本就由許多聲音共同構成。

pins.title: Edge of Production: Industrial Waterfront Regeneration
pins.description:
A former port waterfront in Shenzhen is reconnected to the city through industrial reuse and a continuous public realm.

Shenzhen | Urban regeneration | Adaptive reuse | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 生產的邊緣：工業水岸再生
zh-Hant.description:
透過工業再利用與連續的公共領域，讓深圳一處昔日港口水岸重新與城市相連。

深圳｜都市再生｜適應性再利用｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial view of the regenerated waterfront district.
更新後水岸街區的鳥瞰。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A former port and heavy-industrial waterfront in Shenzhen is fragmented by large brownfields and port infrastructure. These barriers cut the city off from its shoreline and leave open spaces scattered and disconnected.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳一處昔日港口與重工業水岸被大片棕地與港口設施切割得支離破碎。這些屏障使城市與海岸線隔絕，開放空間也零散而互不相連。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Six map layers trace roads, metro, bus routes, green areas, industrial land and new development zones across the district. Reading them together shows where pedestrian links break and where old industrial structures still hold a strong presence.
captions: Site layers from roads to new development.
District plan with green and industrial areas.
Waterfront site plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 六張圖層分別梳理道路、地鐵、公車路線、綠地、工業用地與新開發區。疊合閱讀後，可以看出步行連結在哪裡中斷，以及哪些舊工業構造仍具強烈的存在感。
captions: 從道路到新開發區的基地圖層。
標示綠地與工業區的街區平面。
水岸基地平面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The strategy is grouped into three families of moves for the waterfront, the industrial heritage and the city centre. Abandoned tanks and sheds are reused as parks, exhibition spaces and performance areas.
captions: Waterfront moves.
Industrial heritage reuse.
City centre blocks with green terraces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 策略被歸納為三組操作，分別對應水岸、工業遺產與城市中心。廢棄的儲槽與廠房被再利用為公園、展覽空間與表演場地。
captions: 水岸操作。
工業遺產再利用。
帶有綠化露台的城市中心街廓。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A continuous pedestrian network now ties commercial, residential and public spaces back to the sea. The former industrial edge becomes an inclusive public landscape for everyday life.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一條連續的步行網絡將商業、居住與公共空間重新連回海邊。昔日的工業邊緣轉化為一片支持日常生活的包容性公共地景。

sections.heading: Edge of Production - Turning an Industrial Waterfront Back Toward the Sea
sections.body: A former port and heavy-industrial waterfront has been broken apart by vast brownfields and port infrastructure. These barriers cut the city off from its shoreline and leave its open spaces scattered and unrelated to one another. The project reads the district through six map layers, tracing roads, metro, bus routes, green areas, industrial land and zones of new development. Laid over one another, the layers reveal where pedestrian links break and where old industrial structures still hold a powerful presence. The strategy is then gathered into three families of moves, addressing the waterfront, the industrial heritage and the city centre in turn. Abandoned tanks and sheds are not erased but reused as parks, exhibition spaces and performance areas, so that their scale and character survive. In the final scheme a continuous pedestrian network ties commercial, residential and public spaces back to the sea. An edge that once belonged only to machines and containers turns around to become an inclusive public landscape, where everyday life can finally reach the water again.

zh-Hant.heading: 生產的邊緣-讓工業水岸重新面向海洋
zh-Hant.body: 昔日的港口與重工業水岸，被大片棕地與港口設施切割得支離破碎，城市因此與海岸線隔絕，開放空間也零散而互不相連。作品以六張圖層展開閱讀，分別梳理道路、地鐵、公車路線、綠地、工業用地與新開發區；當它們疊合在一起，步行連結在哪裡斷裂、哪些舊工業構造仍擁有強烈的存在感，便一一浮現。策略隨之被歸納為三組操作，分別回應水岸、工業遺產與城市中心。廢棄的儲槽與廠房沒有被抹去，而是被轉化為公園、展覽空間與表演場地，延續其原有的尺度與氣質。最終，一條連續的步行網絡把商業、居住與公共空間重新連回海邊。曾經只屬於機器與貨櫃的邊緣，轉身成為一片包容的公共地景，讓日常生活得以重新抵達水面。

pins.title: Silvertown Vertical Farm: Urban Food Infrastructure
pins.description:
A modular vertical farm that brings food production back into post-industrial London as public infrastructure.

London | Vertical farming | Urban food infrastructure | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 銀城垂直農場：城市糧食基礎設施
zh-Hant.description:
將糧食生產以公共基礎設施的形式帶回後工業倫敦的模組化垂直農場。

倫敦｜垂直農業｜城市糧食基礎設施｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Axonometric of the vertical farm along the waterfront.
沿著水岸展開的垂直農場軸測圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: London's food system is detached from the city it serves, with long supply chains and uneven access to fresh food. Silvertown, a former landscape of production and logistics, now sits between regeneration pressure and food insecurity.
captions: Site context: a timeline of the Silvertown docklands from industry to regeneration.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 倫敦的糧食系統與它所服務的城市彼此疏離，供應鏈漫長，新鮮食物的取得也不平均。銀城一帶曾是生產與物流的地景，如今夾在都市更新壓力與糧食不安全之間。
captions: 基地脈絡：銀城碼頭區從工業到再生的時間軸。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A concept model of stacked rhombus cells tested how light, air and views can pass through a dense vertical structure. Holographic paper on the cells made the paths of sunlight and reflection visible.
captions: Concept model seen from below.
Cells aggregated into one porous system.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以層疊菱形單元構成的概念模型，測試光線、空氣與視線如何穿透密集的垂直結構。單元上的全像紙讓日照與反射的路徑變得可見。
captions: 從下方仰望概念模型。
單元聚合成一個多孔的系統。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: By day the porous structure supports learning, research and public circulation, while by night it switches to grow-lighting and automated irrigation. Each module stacks a roof canopy, a control deck, growing platforms and a community deck on a hexagonal frame.
captions: Daytime light and public use.
Nighttime system operation.
Exploded production module.
Layers from canopy to structural frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白天，多孔的結構容納學習、研究與公共動線；夜間則切換為植物補光與自動灌溉。每個模組在六角形框架上依序疊合屋頂膜、控制層、栽培平台與社區作業層。
captions: 白天的採光與公共使用。
夜間的系統運作。
生產模組爆炸圖。
從屋頂膜到結構框架的分層。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The modules link to a low-temperature district energy loop that exchanges heat with neighbouring buildings. Food production returns to the city as everyday infrastructure that also offers local work.
captions: Final view of the market under the vertical farm.
Connection to the district energy loop.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模組連接一套低溫區域能源迴路，與鄰近建築交換熱能。糧食生產因此以日常基礎設施的姿態回到城市，同時提供在地就業。
captions: 垂直農場下方市集的最終視圖。
與區域能源迴路的連結。

sections.heading: Silvertown Vertical Farm - Food Returning to the City as Infrastructure
sections.body: In a large city the food system has drifted away from the people it feeds, with long supply chains and uneven access to fresh produce. This former landscape of production and logistics now sits caught between regeneration pressure and food insecurity. The project begins with a concept model of stacked rhombus cells that tests how light, air and views can pass through a dense vertical structure. Holographic paper fixed to the cells makes the paths of sunlight and reflection visible, so that the invisible becomes a material to design with. By day the porous structure supports learning, research and public circulation, and by night it switches to grow-lighting and automated irrigation. Each module stacks a roof canopy, a control deck, growing platforms and a community deck on a hexagonal frame. The modules also join a low-temperature district energy loop that trades heat with neighbouring buildings. Food production is no longer hidden somewhere far away. It returns to the city as everyday infrastructure, offering local work and a shared rhythm of care that the neighbourhood can see, touch and rely upon.

zh-Hant.heading: 銀城垂直農場-讓糧食以基礎設施之姿回到城市
zh-Hant.body: 大城市的糧食系統與它所餵養的人們彼此疏離，供應鏈漫長，新鮮食物的取得也並不平均；這片昔日屬於生產與物流的地景，如今夾在都市更新的壓力與糧食不安全之間。作品從一個層疊菱形單元的概念模型出發，測試光線、空氣與視線如何穿透密集的垂直結構，單元上貼附的全像紙，讓日照與反射的路徑變得清晰可見。白天，多孔的結構容納學習、研究與公共動線；夜晚，它切換為植物補光與自動灌溉的生產模式。每個模組在六角形框架上依序疊合屋頂膜、控制層、栽培平台與社區作業層，並接入低溫區域能源迴路，與鄰近建築交換熱能。糧食生產於是不再藏身遠方，而以日常基礎設施的姿態回到城市，同時帶來在地的工作與彼此照應的生活。

pins.title: Longyearbyen Coastal Ecological Framework
pins.description:
A sediment-driven nearshore infrastructure that helps the Arctic coast grow new habitat over time.

Svalbard | Coastal ecology | Nearshore infrastructure | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 朗伊爾城海岸生態框架
zh-Hant.description:
以沉積作用驅動的近岸基礎設施，讓北極海岸隨時間長出新的棲地。

斯瓦巴｜海岸生態｜近岸基礎設施｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The Arctic region with the site marked.
標示基地位置的北極區域圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Climate change is reshaping ocean currents, sediment flows and coastlines across the Arctic. In Longyearbyen, sediment slowly builds new land, yet coastal habitats remain fragmented and vulnerable.
captions: Site selection from geological analysis, with a temporal comparison of the shoreline.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷正在改變北極的洋流、沉積物流動與海岸線。在朗伊爾城，沉積物緩慢地堆積出新的土地，海岸棲地卻依然破碎而脆弱。
captions: 依地質分析選址，並比較海岸線的時間變化。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Maps of vulnerable species, tidal currents, fresh water and vegetation show where the coast is most sensitive and where links are missing. Shallow, stable water near the shore was found suitable for light-touch structures that guide sedimentation.
captions: The existing edge at year 0: land, sediment flow and the buildings along the shore.
Sensitive and common species along the coast.
Tidal currents and critical water resources.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 針對脆弱物種、潮流、淡水與植被的分析圖，揭示海岸最敏感的區段與缺失的生態連結。近岸淺而穩定的水域被判定適合設置輕觸式構造，以引導沉積。
captions: 第 0 年的現況海岸：陸地、沉積物流向與沿岸建築。
沿岸的敏感物種與常見物種。
潮流與關鍵水資源。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Rock-filled gabions act as groynes that slow the water and trap sediment over time. Over two decades they are expected to fill, grow over with mosses and grasses, and turn into new coastal habitat.
captions: From gabion structure to land formation.
Branching concept model of sediment growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 填滿石塊的石籠作為突堤，減緩水流並逐步攔截沉積物。在二十年間，它們預期會被填滿、長出苔蘚與草本，轉化為新的海岸棲地。
captions: 從石籠構造到土地成形。
呈現沉積生長的分枝狀概念模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A raised corridor follows the sediment flow and stitches inland vegetation to the shore. After twenty years an emergent green corridor and a stabilised platform offer habitat and quiet public access.
captions: Final view at year 0: a light bridge over the bare coast.
Final view at year 20: new land and plants beneath the corridor.
Accretion-led growth after twenty years.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一條架高的廊道順著沉積物流向延伸，將內陸植被縫合到海岸。二十年後，新生的綠色廊道與穩定的平台同時提供棲地與低干擾的公共通道。
captions: 第 0 年的最終視圖：輕盈的步橋跨越裸露的海岸。
第 20 年的最終視圖：步道下方長出新土地與植物。
二十年後由淤積帶動的生長。

sections.heading: Longyearbyen Coastal Ecological Framework - Waiting for New Land Within the Sediment
sections.body: Climate change is rewriting ocean currents, sediment flows and coastlines across the far north. On the shore of one small northern town, sediment slowly builds new land, yet the coastal habitats there remain fragmented and fragile. The project begins with maps of vulnerable species, tidal currents, fresh water and vegetation, which locate the most sensitive stretches of coast and the ecological links that are missing. Shallow, stable water close to the shore emerges as the right place for light-touch structures that can guide sedimentation. Rock-filled gabions are designed as groynes that slow the water and trap silt over time. Across two decades they are expected to fill, grow over with mosses and grasses, and turn into new coastal habitat. A raised corridor follows the direction of the sediment and stitches inland vegetation to the shoreline. In the end an emergent green corridor and a stabilised platform hold both wildlife and quiet public access. Design here is not a finished object but a patient collaboration with time, allowing the coast to grow its own answer gradually.

zh-Hant.heading: 朗伊爾城海岸生態框架-在沉積中等待新生的土地
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷正改寫極地的洋流、沉積物與海岸線；在這座北方小鎮的岸邊，沉積物緩慢堆出新的土地，海岸棲地卻依舊破碎脆弱。作品先以脆弱物種、潮流、淡水與植被的分析圖，辨認出最敏感的岸段與缺失的生態連結，並發現近岸淺而穩定的水域，適合放置輕觸式的構造來引導沉積。填滿石塊的石籠被設計為突堤，減緩水流、攔截泥沙；二十年間，它們將逐漸被填滿，長出苔蘚與草本，成為新的海岸棲地。一條架高的廊道順著沉積的方向延伸，把內陸植被縫合到岸邊，最終形成新生的綠色廊道與穩定的平台，同時容納棲息的生物與低干擾的人群。設計在此不是一次完成的作品，而是一份與時間合作的耐心，讓海岸自己慢慢長出答案。

pins.title: Holding the Crossing
pins.description:
A layered pedestrian bridge that turns a busy crossing into a place to pause, gather and move with ease.

Shenzhen | Pedestrian bridge | Urban connector | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 守住通道
zh-Hant.description:
一座層疊式人行橋，讓繁忙的通道成為可以停留、聚集並從容通行的地方。

深圳｜人行橋｜城市連接體｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A woven canopy over the crossing at dusk.
黃昏時覆蓋在通道上方的編織頂棚。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A large plaza next to a busy railway crossing in Shenzhen is used almost only for passing through. It lacks shade, shelter and places to pause, so it feels empty despite the crowds.
captions: The Lo Wu district: the site between the railway station, coach station and checkpoint.
Four challenges of the plaza: no climate comfort, emptiness, transit-dominated, no identity.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳一處緊鄰繁忙鐵路通道的大型廣場，幾乎只被用來穿越。這裡缺乏遮蔭、庇護與停留的地方，即使人潮眾多，仍顯得空曠。
captions: 羅湖區：位於火車站、客運站與口岸之間的基地。
廣場的四項挑戰：缺乏氣候舒適、空曠、交通主導、缺乏認同。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Site diagrams trace roads, green space, water and pedestrian access around the plaza. They show that daily movement is strong while comfort and a sense of place are missing.
captions: Roads, access and surrounding uses.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地分析圖梳理廣場周邊的道路、綠地、水系與步行動線。分析顯示這裡日常人流強勁，卻缺乏舒適感與場所感。
captions: 道路、動線與周邊使用。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A pedestrian bridge is stacked in layers, from a ground concourse to play platforms, green terraces and a glass climate veil. Section studies test how people can either keep moving or slow down and stay.
captions: A speculative scenario of people staying under the glass veil.
Operational layers of the shared section.
Section analysis of the bridge.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一座人行橋以層疊方式組成，從地面通廊到遊憩平台、綠色露台與玻璃氣候罩。剖面研究測試人們如何能持續通行，或放慢腳步停留。
captions: 人們在玻璃罩下停留的推想場景。
共享剖面的運作層次。
人行橋的剖面分析。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A second, water-based connector extends the route with a curved envelope over a framework of ribs. Its plan holds seating, gardens and small leisure spaces, turning the crossing into an extension of everyday city life.
captions: The water-based connector in its urban context.
Envelope, structure and pedestrian layers.
Masterplan of the water-based connector.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第二段臨水連接體以曲面外殼覆蓋肋狀結構，延續步行路徑。平面中配置座位、花園與小型休閒空間，讓通道成為日常城市生活的延伸。
captions: 水上連接廊道與城市脈絡。
外殼、結構與步行層。
臨水連接體的總平面圖。

sections.heading: Holding the Crossing - Teaching a Passage to Let People Stay
sections.body: A large plaza beside a busy railway crossing receives crowds every day, yet it is used almost only for passing through. With little shade, shelter or anywhere to pause, it feels strangely empty in the middle of all that movement. Site diagrams trace the roads, green space, water and pedestrian access around it, and they reveal a contradiction: daily flow is strong, while comfort and a sense of place are missing. The answer is a pedestrian bridge stacked in layers, rising from a ground concourse to play platforms, green terraces and finally a glass climate veil. Section studies test again and again how people might keep moving, or instead slow down on one level and stay a while. A second connector by the water extends the route, its curved envelope drawn over a framework of ribs, and its plan holds seating, gardens and small leisure spaces. The crossing is no longer just a shortcut between two points. It becomes an extension of everyday city life, a place where hurried travellers are offered, between rush and rest, a moment to breathe.

zh-Hant.heading: 守住通道-讓穿越的人流願意停留
zh-Hant.body: 緊鄰繁忙鐵路通道的大型廣場，每天湧過無數人潮，卻幾乎只被用來穿越；缺乏遮蔭、庇護與停留之處，熱鬧之中反而顯得空曠。基地分析圖梳理周邊的道路、綠地、水系與步行動線，揭示了一個矛盾：日常人流強勁，舒適感與場所感卻付之闕如。作品的回應，是一座層層疊起的人行橋，從地面通廊、遊憩平台、綠色露台一路升至玻璃氣候罩，剖面研究反覆推敲人們如何能繼續趕路，或在某一層放慢腳步留下來。第二段臨水的連接體延伸了路徑，以曲面外殼覆蓋肋狀結構，平面中安置座位、花園與小型休閒空間。通道不再只是兩點之間的捷徑，而成為城市日常生活的延伸，在匆忙與停駐之間，為過路的人留下一處可以喘息的位置。

pins.title: Weaving Back the Sugar Factory
pins.description:
Pedestrian links and a woven walkway that reconnect a former sugar factory to its neighbourhood and river.

Industrial heritage | Pedestrian linkage | Riverfront regeneration | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重新編織糖廠
zh-Hant.description:
以步行連結與編織般的步道，讓舊糖廠重新接回社區與河流。

工業遺產｜步行連結｜河岸再生｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The regenerated sugar factory from above.
俯瞰再生後的糖廠。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A former riverside sugar factory sits cut off from the new town around it, its sheds and silos left behind. Residents face a long detour to reach the riverfront, and the site offers little to the people who live nearby.
captions: The history of the sugar factory and silk industry, and the site on the river.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座臨河的舊糖廠被周邊新城隔離，廠房與筒倉閒置多年。居民須繞遠路才能抵達河岸，基地也幾乎無法回應附近居民的需求。
captions: 糖廠與絲綢產業的歷史，以及河畔的基地。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Site analysis weighs the heritage value of the factory against its spatial fragmentation and an unused stretch of riverfront. The findings point to linkage, not new buildings, as the key to reviving the area.
captions: Population analysis of former workers, new residents and visitors.
Heritage value, fragmentation and waterfront potential.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地分析權衡工廠的遺產價值、空間破碎化與閒置的河岸地帶。分析結果指出，振興此地的關鍵在於連結，而非新建築。
captions: 前糖廠工人、新住民與訪客的人口分析。
遺產價值、空間破碎與河岸潛力。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The local craft of silk making, from cocoon to thread to fabric, is translated into pods, an elevated passage and a link bridge. Five strategies then layer community commons, slow mobility, heritage, creative work and a riverfront corridor onto the site.
captions: Conceptual framework: from cocoon to thread to fabric.
Forms drawn from cocoon, thread and fabric.
Five layered strategies.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在地的絲綢工藝，從蠶繭、絲線到布料，被轉譯為聚集艙體、架高步道與連接橋。五項策略再將社區共享、慢行系統、遺產軸線、創意工坊與河岸廊道疊加到基地上。
captions: 概念框架：從蠶繭到絲線再到布料。
取自蠶繭、絲線與布料的形態。
五項疊加策略。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The masterplan weaves a continuous walkway through a play area, museums, workshops and a waterfront green park. Old industrial fabric becomes an everyday public landscape that reconnects the neighbourhood to the river.
captions: The ribbon walkway entering the silk museum.
The waterfront green park with the red ribbon path.
Masterplan with key spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 總平面以一條連續步道串起遊戲區、博物館、工坊與濱水綠地公園。舊工業紋理成為日常的公共地景，讓社區重新與河流相連。
captions: 緞帶步道延伸進入絲綢博物館。
設有紅色緞帶步道的濱水綠地公園。
標示主要空間的總平面圖。

sections.heading: Weaving Back the Sugar Factory - A Silken Thread Sewn Back to the River
sections.body: A riverside sugar factory has long sat cut off from the new town around it, its sheds and silos silent, and residents must take a long detour simply to reach the water. Rather than filling the empty ground with new buildings, the project first learns to read the site: the heritage value of the works, the fragmentation of its spaces and a stretch of riverfront that nobody uses. The conclusion is clear and restrained, since linkage, not construction, is what can revive the place. The local craft of silk making then becomes the language of the whole design. Cocoon, thread and fabric are translated in turn into gathering pods, an elevated passage and a link bridge. Five strategies are layered across the ground, namely community commons, slow mobility, a heritage axis, creative workshops and a riverfront corridor. The masterplan weaves one continuous walkway through a play area, museums, workshops and a waterfront park. Old industrial fabric becomes an everyday public landscape, and like a fine thread drawn through cloth, the walkway quietly stitches a severed neighbourhood back to its river.

zh-Hant.heading: 重新編織糖廠-以一縷絲線縫回河岸
zh-Hant.body: 一座臨河的舊糖廠被新城隔在一旁，廠房與筒倉沉默多年，居民只能繞遠路才抵達水邊。作品並不急於在空地上增添新的建築，而是先讀懂這片基地：遺產的價值、破碎的空間，以及一段長久無人使用的河岸。分析的結論清楚而節制，振興此地的關鍵在於連結。於是，在地的絲綢工藝成為整套設計的語言，從蠶繭、絲線到布料，依序轉譯為聚集的艙體、架高的步道與跨越的連接橋。社區共享、慢行系統、遺產軸線、創意工坊與河岸廊道五項策略層層疊加，總平面再以一條連續步道串起遊戲區、博物館、工坊與濱水綠地。舊工業的紋理因此成為日常可行走的公共地景，彷彿一縷細絲穿過布面，把被割斷的鄰里重新縫回河流身旁。

pins.title: Spatial Development Plan for Enfield
pins.description:
A spatial plan that links housing, jobs and transport to reduce inequality across a London borough.

London | Spatial planning | Just city | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 恩菲爾德空間發展規劃
zh-Hant.description:
一份串連住宅、就業與交通的空間規劃，縮小倫敦一個行政區內的不平等。

倫敦｜空間規劃｜公正城市｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Key spatial diagram of the plan.
規劃的關鍵空間圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The eastern side of Enfield in north London has weaker public transport, fewer local services and a concentration of deprivation. A divide between east and west shapes access to jobs, homes and everyday amenities.
captions: The borough with the eastern priority areas highlighted.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 倫敦北部恩菲爾德的東側大眾運輸較弱、在地服務較少，貧困也較為集中。東西之間的落差，影響了居民取得工作、住宅與日常設施的機會。
captions: 行政區地圖，標示東部優先發展區。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A SWOT map marks town centres with good and poor provision, growth areas and places where transport access is very low. It turns scattered data into a clear picture of where the plan should act first.
captions: Site selection: brownfields and masterplans with planning permission.
Affordable housing allocation analysis by deprivation level.
Case study: the car-free Vauban district.
SWOT analysis across the borough.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: SWOT 分析圖標示服務良好與不足的城鎮中心、成長地區，以及大眾運輸可及性極低的地點。它把零散的數據整理成清楚的圖像，指出規劃應優先介入之處。
captions: 選址分析：棕地與已獲規劃許可的總體規劃。
依剝奪程度分析可負擔住宅分配。
案例研究：無車的沃邦社區。
全區的 SWOT 分析。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Housing growth is steered to well-connected brownfield sites near stations, protecting green belt and heritage areas. Each site is tested for density, height and the share of affordable homes it can carry.
captions: The affordable housing allocation plan and housing targets.
A 15-minute city example, before and after.
Sites for new housing.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 住宅成長被引導至車站周邊交通便利的棕地，同時保護綠帶與歷史保存區。每處基地都經過密度、高度與可負擔住宅比例的檢驗。
captions: 可負擔住宅空間分配計畫與住宅目標。
十五分鐘城市示例的前後對比。
新住宅的開發基地。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Employment land is placed beside new bus and cycling routes so that jobs sit close to the homes that need them. Together the layers form a spatial plan for a fairer, fifteen-minute borough.
captions: Sites for employment land.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 就業用地沿著新的公車與自行車路線配置，讓工作機會靠近需要它的住宅。這些圖層共同構成一份更公平的十五分鐘城市空間規劃。
captions: 就業用地的開發基地。

sections.heading: Spatial Development Plan for Enfield - Mending an East-West Divide
sections.body: The eastern side of a borough has weaker public transport, fewer local services and a concentration of deprivation, and the divide between east and west shapes residents' access to jobs, homes and everyday amenities. A SWOT map marked town centres with good and poor provision, growth areas and places where transport access is very low, turning scattered data into a clear picture of where the plan should act first. Housing growth was then steered toward well-connected brownfield sites near stations, protecting green belt and heritage areas. Every site was tested for density, height and the share of affordable homes it could carry. Finally, employment land is placed beside new bus and cycling routes so that jobs sit close to the homes that need them, and together these layers form a spatial plan for a fairer, fifteen-minute borough. Data here becomes a concrete promise of fairness, drawn patiently onto the map.

zh-Hant.heading: 恩菲爾德空間發展規劃-縫合東西落差的十五分鐘城區
zh-Hant.body: 城區東側大眾運輸較弱、在地服務較少，貧困也較為集中，東西之間的落差，影響了居民取得工作、住宅與日常設施的機會。一張SWOT分析圖標示服務良好與不足的城鎮中心、成長地區，以及大眾運輸可及性極低的地點，把零散的數據整理成清楚的圖像，指出規劃應優先介入之處。住宅成長隨後被引導至車站周邊交通便利的棕地，同時保護綠帶與歷史保存區，每處基地都經過密度、高度與可負擔住宅比例的檢驗。最終，就業用地沿新的公車與自行車路線配置，讓工作機會靠近需要它的住宅，各圖層共同構成一份更公平的十五分鐘城區空間規劃。數據在此化為對公平的具體承諾。

pins.title: The Floating Community
pins.description:
A floating, 3D-printed settlement that turns plastic waste into homes and supports marine life below.

New York | Floating settlement | Circular construction | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮社區
zh-Hant.description:
一座以 3D 列印打造的漂浮聚落，將塑膠廢料轉化為住宅，並支持水下的海洋生態。

紐約｜漂浮聚落｜循環營建｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The floating settlement seen from above.
俯瞰漂浮聚落。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Jamaica Bay in New York is an ecologically dynamic edge where water, wetland and city meet. The project asks how a community could live on the water while giving back to the habitat beneath it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 紐約牙買加灣是水域、濕地與城市交會、生態變動劇烈的邊緣地帶。這個專案提問：一個社區如何生活在水上，同時回饋水面下的棲地。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Collage and site mapping study the bay, its marine life and the neighbourhoods along its shore. Plastic waste collected from nearby homes is identified as a local resource for building.
captions: Concept collage of life above and below the water.
Site context around the bay.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 拼貼與基地圖研究海灣、海洋生物與沿岸社區。從附近住宅收集的塑膠廢料，被視為可用於建造的在地資源。
captions: 水上與水下生活的概念拼貼。
海灣周邊的基地脈絡。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Plastic waste is mixed with concrete and 3D-printed on site into housing units tailored to each household. Walls and furniture slide along integrated tracks, so homes can be reconfigured over time.
captions: Unit plans for four households, with movable walls and furniture for their changing needs.
Printed unit modules, plan and section.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 塑膠廢料與混凝土混合，在基地現場以 3D 列印製成依各戶需求量身打造的住宅單元。牆體與家具可沿整合軌道移動，讓住家能隨時間重新配置。
captions: 四個家庭的單元平面，以可移動牆面與家具因應需求變化。
列印單元模組、平面與剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Hexagon-based islands of lightweight concrete form a modular archipelago with solar panels above and turbines and artificial reefs below. Aquaponic farms complete a closed loop of food, energy and housing on the water.
captions: Masterplan of the hexagon islands.
Turbines and reefs below the waterline.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 以輕質混凝土構成的六角形島嶼組成模組化群島，上方設置太陽能板，下方則有水力渦輪與人工魚礁。魚菜共生農場讓水上的食物、能源與住宅形成封閉循環。
captions: 六角形島嶼的總平面圖。
水面下的渦輪與魚礁。

sections.heading: The Floating Community - An Archipelago Printed from Plastic Waste
sections.body: An ecologically dynamic bay edge, where water, wetland and city meet, is the site of this project, which asks how a community might live on the water while giving back to the habitat beneath it. Collage and site mapping studied the bay, its marine life and the neighbourhoods along its shore, and plastic waste collected from nearby homes was identified as a local building resource. Mixed with concrete, the plastic is 3D-printed on site into housing units tailored to each household. Walls and furniture slide along integrated tracks, so homes can be reconfigured over time. Hexagon-based islands of lightweight concrete then form a modular archipelago, with solar panels above and turbines and artificial reefs below, while aquaponic farms close the loop of food, energy and housing on the water. Discarded material becomes a home afloat, and people and sea begin to nourish one another rather than merely coexisting.

zh-Hant.heading: 漂浮社區-以塑膠廢料列印的水上群島
zh-Hant.body: 一處水域、濕地與城市交會、生態變動劇烈的海灣邊緣，是這件作品的基地；它追問一個社區如何生活在水上，同時回饋水面下的棲地。拼貼與基地圖研究海灣、海洋生物與沿岸社區，從附近住宅收集的塑膠廢料，被視為可用於建造的在地資源。塑膠廢料與混凝土混合，在現場以3D列印製成依各戶需求量身打造的住宅單元，牆體與家具可沿整合軌道移動，讓住家能隨時間重新配置。最終，以輕質混凝土構成的六角形島嶼組成模組化群島，上方設置太陽能板，下方則有水力渦輪與人工魚礁，魚菜共生農場讓食物、能源與住宅形成封閉循環。廢棄之物在水上成為家園，人與海洋彼此滋養。

pins.title: Wetland Gallery
pins.description:
An educational bird-watching gallery on a floodplain, held up by hollow tree-like columns that double as nests.

New Jersey | Bird-watching gallery | Wetland education | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 濕地藝廊
zh-Hant.description:
一座位於氾濫平原上的教育型賞鳥藝廊，以兼作鳥巢的中空樹狀柱撐起。

新澤西｜賞鳥藝廊｜濕地教育｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The gallery with its sloped rooftop deck above the river.
沿河而立、設有斜屋頂平台的展館。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Along the Hackensack River in New Jersey, wetland birds and a low-lying neighbourhood share a floodplain that floods again and again. The brief asks for an educational bird-watching site where people can learn about the wetland without disturbing it.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在新澤西州哈肯薩克河沿岸，濕地鳥類與低窪社區共享一片反覆淹水的氾濫平原。題目要求一座教育型賞鳥基地，讓人們在不打擾濕地的前提下認識它。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Seasonal studies map the birds, plants and flood records of the site and its surroundings. Winter backyard feeders, where people and birds meet at close range, become the starting idea.
captions: Location analysis: seasonal wildlife, flora and fauna, and records of local floods.
Chunk model of the structure and nests.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 季節性研究整理了基地及周邊的鳥類、植物與淹水紀錄。冬季後院餵鳥器讓人與鳥近距離相遇，成為設計的出發點。
captions: 區位分析：季節性野生動物、動植物與當地洪水紀錄。
結構與鳥巢的局部模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Hollow steel columns, narrow at the base and wide at the top, carry the floors and hold nesting cavities of different sizes. Feeder tubes link the nests to the rooms inside, so visitors can watch birds return without being seen.
captions: The design process, from bird feeder concept to roof and facade.
Tree-like column types.
Plan with nests and supports.
How people and birds meet at the nest.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 下窄上寬的中空鋼柱承托樓板，柱內設有大小不一的築巢空間。餵食管將鳥巢與室內相連，讓訪客能在不被察覺的情況下觀察鳥類歸巢。
captions: 設計過程：從餵鳥器概念到屋頂與立面。
樹狀柱的類型。
鳥巢與支撐的平面配置。
人與鳥在巢邊相遇的方式。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Classrooms, an exhibition space and a glasshouse garden sit above the floodplain, while the ground stays open for a wildlife garden and boat mooring. A polycarbonate skin filters light and a bamboo roof deck turns visitors toward the water and the sunset.
captions: Exploded axonometric of the layers.
Plans from ground floor to roof.
Long section through the gallery.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 教室、展覽空間與溫室花園抬升於氾濫平原之上，地面層則保留給野生動物花園與船隻停泊。聚碳酸酯外皮過濾光線，竹製屋頂平台則將訪客的視線引向水面與夕陽。
captions: 各層構造的爆炸軸測圖。
從地面層到屋頂的各層平面。
穿越展館的長向剖面。

sections.heading: Wetland Gallery - Nests and Watching Eyes Hidden in Steel Columns
sections.body: Along a river, wetland birds and a low-lying neighbourhood share a floodplain that floods again and again, and the brief asks for an educational bird-watching site where people can learn about the wetland without disturbing it. Seasonal studies mapped the birds, plants and flood records of the site and its surroundings, and winter backyard feeders, where people and birds meet at close range, became the starting idea. Hollow steel columns, narrow at the base and wide at the top, carry the floors and hold nesting cavities of different sizes. Feeder tubes link these nests to the rooms inside, so visitors can watch birds return without being seen. Classrooms, an exhibition space and a glasshouse garden are finally lifted above the floodplain, leaving the ground open for a wildlife garden and boat mooring, while a polycarbonate skin filters light and a bamboo roof deck turns visitors toward the water and the sunset. Watching becomes a humble form of coexistence.

zh-Hant.heading: 濕地藝廊-藏身鋼柱中的鳥巢與目光
zh-Hant.body: 一條河流沿岸，濕地鳥類與低窪社區共享一片反覆淹水的氾濫平原；題目要求一座教育型賞鳥基地，讓人們在不打擾濕地的前提下認識它。季節性研究整理了基地及周邊的鳥類、植物與淹水紀錄，冬季後院的餵鳥器讓人與鳥近距離相遇，成為設計的出發點。下窄上寬的中空鋼柱承托樓板，柱內設有大小不一的築巢空間，餵食管將鳥巢與室內相連，讓訪客能在不被察覺的情況下觀察鳥類歸巢。最終，教室、展覽空間與溫室花園抬升於氾濫平原之上，地面層保留給野生動物花園與船隻停泊；聚碳酸酯外皮過濾光線，竹製屋頂平台將視線引向水面與夕陽。觀看由此成為一種謙和的共處。

pins.title: Reimagining Tegel
pins.description:
Courtyard urbanism for a disused airport terminal, where housing, gardens and workshops support refuge and exchange.

Berlin | Airport transformation | Courtyard urbanism | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重新想像泰格爾
zh-Hant.description:
為閒置機場航廈提出的中庭都市主義，以住宅、花園與工作坊支持安置與交流。

柏林｜機場轉型｜中庭都市主義｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The hexagonal courtyard reimagined as a shared garden and neighbourhood.
六角形中庭被重新想像為共享花園與社區。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The decommissioned Tegel Airport in Berlin leaves a large hexagonal terminal and its courtyard without a use. The project asks how the site could give displaced families a home while opening it to the people of the city.
captions: A history of the airport, from the airlift to its closing.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 柏林已停用的泰格爾機場，留下一座大型六角形航廈與中庭無人使用。這個專案提問：基地如何為流離失所的家庭提供居所，同時向城市居民開放。
captions: 機場的歷史：從空運到關閉。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Mapping and user studies compare the needs of new residents with those of local visitors. Timber stick models test a branching, lightweight structure that could grow across the courtyard.
captions: The needs of German visitors and Syrian residents.
The airport site within the city.
Early timber stick models.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地圖與使用者研究比較了新住民與在地訪客的不同需求。木構桿件模型則測試一種可在中庭中延展、輕巧的分枝結構。
captions: 德國訪客與敘利亞居民的需求。
機場基地在城市中的位置。
早期的木桿件模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Homes, schools and cafeterias line the terminal ring, while the courtyard fills with planting beds, workshops and trellises for growing herbs and spices. Unit plans use sliding doors and storage walls so each family can reshape its rooms over time.
captions: Adaptable family units and their uses.
Model of the planting trellis.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 住宅、學校與餐廳沿著航廈環狀配置，中庭則布滿種植床、工作坊與用來栽種香草與香料的棚架。單元平面以拉門與收納牆組成，讓每個家庭能隨時間調整房間。
captions: 可調整的家庭單元與使用方式。
種植棚架模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A bike lane and a communication park run beneath an open roof whose angled tiles control light and collect rain. Raised walkways, a viewing tower and workshops turn the courtyard into a garden for exchange between residents and visitors.
captions: Roof tiles that control light.
Long section across the courtyard.
Viewing tower and rain-fed workshops.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 自行車道與交流公園位於開放式屋頂之下，屋頂以不同角度的板片調節光線並收集雨水。高架步道、瞭望塔與工作坊，讓中庭成為住民與訪客交流的花園。
captions: 調節光線的屋頂板片。
橫跨中庭的長向剖面。
瞭望塔與雨水回收工作坊。

sections.heading: Reimagining Tegel - A Garden of Exchange Inside a Hexagonal Terminal
sections.body: A decommissioned airport leaves a large hexagonal terminal and its courtyard without a use, and the project asks how the site could give displaced families a home while opening it to the people of the city. Mapping and user studies compared the needs of new residents with those of local visitors, while timber stick models tested a light, branching structure able to spread across the courtyard. Homes, schools and cafeterias line the terminal ring. Within, the courtyard fills with planting beds, workshops and trellises for herbs and spices, and unit plans use sliding doors and storage walls so each family can reshape its rooms over time. In the final design, a bike lane and a communication park run beneath an open roof whose angled tiles control light and collect rain, and raised walkways, a viewing tower and workshops turn the courtyard into a garden of exchange. A former place of departure becomes a place of arrival and encounter.

zh-Hant.heading: 重新想像泰格爾-六角航廈中的交流花園
zh-Hant.body: 一座已停用的機場，留下大型六角形航廈與中庭無人使用；作品追問，這處基地如何為流離失所的家庭提供居所，同時向城市居民開放。基地圖與使用者研究比較新住民與在地訪客的不同需求，木構桿件模型則測試一種可在中庭延展、輕巧的分枝結構。住宅、學校與餐廳沿航廈環狀配置，中庭布滿種植床、工作坊與栽種香草香料的棚架，單元平面以拉門與收納牆組成，讓每個家庭能隨時間調整房間。最終，自行車道與交流公園位於開放式屋頂之下，屋頂以不同角度的板片調節光線並收集雨水，高架步道、瞭望塔與工作坊讓中庭成為住民與訪客交流的花園。曾經的出發之地，成為落腳與相遇的所在。

pins.title: Floating Eco-Islands
pins.description:
Artificial habitats made from abandoned bamboo rafts that move feeding grounds away from the busy shore.

Shenzhen Bay | Floating habitat | Bird conservation | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 漂浮生態島
zh-Hant.description:
以廢棄竹筏打造的人工棲地，將鳥類覓食區移離熱鬧的岸邊。

深圳灣｜漂浮棲地｜鳥類保育｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Planted bamboo rafts give waterbirds a safe place to feed.
種上植物的竹筏，為水鳥提供安全的覓食處。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Shenzhen Bay is a tidal estuary where resident and migratory waterbirds feed close to busy promenades and seawalls. Human disturbance near the shore pushes the birds away from the places they rely on.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳灣是一處潮汐河口，留鳥與候鳥在熱鬧的步道與海堤旁覓食。岸邊的人為干擾，正把鳥類推離牠們依賴的棲地。

sections.heading: Research
