zh-Hant.title: 東山公車站
zh-Hant.description:
廣州老街區中一座帶有折板頂篷的小型公車站。

中國廣州｜建築｜公車站｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aerial render of the station and its folded canopy.
車站與折板頂篷的鳥瞰渲染圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Dongshankou in Guangzhou is an old residential quarter that mixes Eastern and Western building styles and has recently become a social media hotspot. The project asks how a small bus station can respond to this crowded image of the place.
captions: Volume studies from floor to main structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州東山口是融合中西建築風格的老住宅區，近年成為社群媒體上的熱門地點。專案思考一座小型公車站，如何回應這個被大量影像包圍的場所。
captions: 從樓層到主結構的量體研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student reads the district as a mix of the real street and its online image. Floors are stacked as varied blocks and then tied together by a simple frame.
captions: Isometric drawing of the station.
Selection of floor plates and materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把街區解讀為真實街道與網路影像的混合。各樓層以不同的量塊堆疊，再由簡潔的框架串連起來。
captions: 車站的等角透視圖。
樓板與材質的選擇。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A beam and column grid holds the stacked rooms and a folded canopy above them. Bus bays sit on the ground floor while the upper floors open to the street.
captions: Beam and column construction.
Plans of the four floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 梁柱網格承托堆疊的房間與上方的折板頂篷。公車停靠位設在地面層，上層樓面則向街道開放。
captions: 梁柱構造。
四個樓層的平面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Street views show the canopy as a strange flash above the old lanes at night. By day the station reads as a light marker that invites people in from the street.
captions: Night view from the west street.
View from the fourth floor.
Street view of the station.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 街景圖中，頂篷在夜晚的老街上方如同一道奇異的閃光。白天車站則像一個輕盈的地標，邀請行人從街上進入。
captions: 西側街道的夜景。
四樓視角。
車站街景。

sections.heading: A Bus Station in the Old Quarter - Between the Real Street and Its Online Image
sections.body: An old residential quarter that mixes Eastern and Western building styles has lately become a social media hotspot, and the project considers how a small bus station might respond to a place so crowded with images. Reading the district as a blend of the real street and its online image, the student stacked the floors as varied blocks and tied them together with a simple frame. A beam and column grid holds the stacked rooms and a folded canopy above. Bus bays sit on the ground floor, while the upper floors open toward the street. In the final street views, the canopy appears at night as a strange flash above the old lanes, and by day the station reads as a light marker inviting people in from the pavement. An everyday piece of transport infrastructure thus becomes a gentle commentary on the image of a city, opening a fissure between the real and the virtual.

zh-Hant.heading: 老街公車站-真實街道與網路影像之間
zh-Hant.body: 一處融合中西建築風格的老住宅區，近年成為社群媒體上的熱門地點；作品思考一座小型公車站，如何回應這個被大量影像包圍的場所。學生將街區解讀為真實街道與網路影像的混合，各樓層以不同的量塊堆疊，再由簡潔的框架串連起來。梁柱網格承托堆疊的房間與上方的折板頂篷，公車停靠位設在地面層，上層樓面則向街道開放。最終的街景圖中，頂篷在夜晚的老街上方如同一道奇異的閃光，白天車站則像一個輕盈的地標，邀請行人從街上進入。日常交通設施由此成為對城市形象的溫和評論，在真實與虛擬之間開出一道縫隙。

pins.title: Campus District Reformation
pins.description:
Looping public routes that open a closed campus to its city.

Guangzhou, China | Landscape urbanism | Campus district | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 校園街區再造
zh-Hant.description:
以環狀公共路徑把封閉校園向城市打開。

中國廣州｜地景都市主義｜校園街區｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Overhead perspective of the new campus district.
新校園街區的俯瞰透視圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A university district in Guangzhou presents itself as a symbol of progress, yet its campus is closed and cut off from the city around it. The project asks how planning can open this gap between the official image and everyday space.
captions: Industrial and public service heat maps.
Landscape analysis of the district.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州的一處大學街區以進步的象徵自居，校園卻封閉且與周邊城市隔絕。專案探問規劃如何打開官方形象與日常空間之間的落差。
captions: 產業與公共服務熱度圖。
街區的地景分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student maps industry, public services and green space to find where the campus and the city could meet. Three kinds of lines from philosophy, rigid, supple and flight, become a way to turn these readings into space.
captions: Site plan with the new routes.
Studies of rigid, supple and flight lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生分析產業、公共服務與綠地，找出校園與城市可以相遇的地方。哲學中的剛性線、柔性線與逃逸線，成為把分析轉化為空間的方法。
captions: 加入新路徑的配置圖。
剛性線、柔性線與逃逸線的研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Looping corridors lift public routes over roads and link campus buildings, parks and the waterfront. A layered section stacks academic, public and natural levels across the district.
captions: Corridor structure.
Field structure logic of order and conflict.
Stereoscopic structure of the layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 環狀廊道把公共路徑抬升越過道路，串連校園建築、公園與水岸。分層剖面把學術、公共與自然三個層次疊合在街區之中。
captions: 廊道結構。
秩序與衝突的場域結構邏輯。
各層次的立體結構。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The plan turns the closed campus into a network of shared paths, gardens and gathering places. Views of a waterfront chapel and a central park show the calm everyday spaces it creates.
captions: Waterfront chapel.
Central park after the rain.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 方案把封閉的校園轉化為共享路徑、花園與聚集場所的網絡。水岸禮拜堂與中央公園的視角，呈現它所創造的寧靜日常空間。
captions: 水岸禮拜堂。
雨後的中央公園。

sections.heading: Campus District Reformation - Three Kinds of Lines Opening a Closed Campus
sections.body: A university district presents itself as a symbol of progress, yet its campus is closed and cut off from the city around it, and the project asks how planning might open the gap between official image and everyday space. Mapping industry, public services and green space, the student located places where campus and city could meet, and three kinds of lines from philosophy, rigid, supple and flight, became a way of turning these readings into space. Looping corridors lift public routes over roads, linking campus buildings, parks and the waterfront. A layered section stacks academic, public and natural levels across the district. The final plan transforms the closed campus into a network of shared paths, gardens and gathering places, and views of a waterfront chapel and a central park reveal the calm everyday spaces it creates. Philosophical lines come down to earth here, becoming a city one can walk.

zh-Hant.heading: 校園街區再造-以三種線打開封閉校園
zh-Hant.body: 一處大學街區以進步的象徵自居，校園卻封閉且與周邊城市隔絕；作品追問，規劃如何打開官方形象與日常空間之間的落差。學生分析產業、公共服務與綠地，找出校園與城市可以相遇的地方，哲學中的剛性線、柔性線與逃逸線，成為將分析轉化為空間的方法。環狀廊道把公共路徑抬升越過道路，串連校園建築、公園與水岸，分層剖面則把學術、公共與自然三個層次疊合在街區之中。最終，方案把封閉的校園轉化為共享路徑、花園與聚集場所的網絡，水岸禮拜堂與中央公園的視角，呈現它所創造的寧靜日常。哲學的線條在此落地，化為可以行走的城市。

pins.title: Rooftop Farm in an Urban Village
pins.description:
A light rooftop farm frame that brings light and nature to an urban village.

Shenzhen, China | Urban design | Urban village rooftop | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城中村屋頂農場
zh-Hant.description:
以輕盈的屋頂農場框架，為城中村帶來光線與自然。

中國深圳｜都市設計｜城中村屋頂｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A rooftop farm frame rising above the lanes of an urban village.
在城中村巷弄上方升起的屋頂農場框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Urban villages in Shenzhen are dense, dark and left out of formal planning. Many residents live in rooms with little sunlight, few shared spaces and almost no contact with nature.
captions: A collage on the history of capitalist planning.
Regulatory planning map of the city.
Sections of village life by day and night.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深圳的城中村密集、昏暗，長期被排除在正式規劃之外。許多居民住在缺乏日照與共享空間、幾乎接觸不到自然的房間裡。
captions: 關於資本主義規劃史的拼貼。
城市的控制性規劃圖。
城中村日夜生活的剖面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student compares problems inside the village with possible fixes such as shared rooms, greenery and rooftop light. Sunlight studies show that the rooftop is the brightest and most natural place left in the village.
captions: Density maps of the village and diagrams of the discourse of consumerism.
A circular map collage of the village and its digital life.
Problem and solution diagrams.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生把城中村內部的問題與可能的對策對照，例如共享空間、綠化與屋頂採光。日照分析顯示，屋頂是城中村裡最明亮、也最接近自然的地方。
captions: 城中村密度地圖與消費主義論述圖解。
城中村與其數位生活的圓形地圖拼貼。
問題與對策分析圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A light steel frame is added on top of existing buildings, with a roof that collects rainwater and modules for planting. Simple joints let the parts be assembled and grown step by step.
captions: Structure, water and planting systems.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在既有建築頂部加建輕鋼框架，屋頂收集雨水，並配置種植模組。簡單的接頭讓構件可以逐步組裝與擴展。
captions: 結構、水與種植系統。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Folded canopies spread across the rooftops and form a shared farm above the lanes. Residents gain bright rooms for growing food, resting and meeting neighbours.
captions: Rooftop canopies across the village.
Shared rooftop room.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 折板頂篷在屋頂之間延展，在巷弄上方形成共享農場。居民因此獲得明亮的空間，可以種植、休息並與鄰居相遇。
captions: 橫跨城中村的屋頂頂篷。
共享的屋頂空間。

sections.heading: Rooftop Farm in an Urban Village - Farming the Brightest Rooftops
sections.body: Urban villages are dense, dark and long left out of formal planning, and many residents live in rooms with little sunlight, few shared spaces and almost no contact with nature. Setting problems inside the village against possible remedies such as shared rooms, greenery and rooftop light, the student found through sunlight studies that the rooftop is the brightest and most natural place left. A light steel frame was therefore added atop existing buildings, with a roof that collects rainwater and modules for planting. Simple joints let the parts be assembled and extended step by step. In the final proposal, folded canopies spread across the rooftops and form a shared farm above the lanes, giving residents bright places to grow food, rest and meet neighbours. Above a dim density, a luminous field quietly takes root, and the overlooked top of the city becomes its most generous ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 城中村屋頂農場-在最明亮的屋頂上耕種
zh-Hant.body: 城中村密集、昏暗，長期被排除在正式規劃之外，許多居民住在缺乏日照與共享空間、幾乎接觸不到自然的房間裡。學生將村內的問題與可能的對策逐一對照，例如共享空間、綠化與屋頂採光；日照分析顯示，屋頂是城中村裡最明亮、也最接近自然的地方。於是，輕鋼框架被加建於既有建築頂部，屋頂收集雨水並配置種植模組，簡單的接頭讓構件可以逐步組裝與擴展。最終，折板頂篷在屋頂之間延展，於巷弄上方形成共享農場，居民因此獲得明亮的空間，可以種植、休息並與鄰居相遇。陰暗的密度之上，一片光亮的田園悄然生長。

pins.title: Turning Waste Into Treasure
pins.description:
A waste transfer station reborn as a public recycling exhibition hall.

Guangzhou, China | Architecture | Waste transfer station | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 變廢為寶
zh-Hant.description:
將垃圾轉運站改造為公共回收展覽館。

中國廣州｜建築設計｜垃圾轉運站｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The renewed waste transfer station on a busy city street.
位於繁忙街道上、經過改造的垃圾轉運站。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: An old waste transfer station sits in the middle of a historic shopping and tourist district in Guangzhou. Its single treatment method and strong smell cut it off from the schools and attractions around it.
captions: Site axonometric with nearby schools, community and attractions.
Design vision and recycling process.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座老舊的垃圾轉運站位於廣州歷史商業與觀光街區的中心。單一的處理方式與強烈異味，使它與周邊的學校和景點隔絕。
captions: 標示周邊學校、社區與景點的基地軸測圖。
設計願景與回收流程。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student maps how each kind of waste is collected, sorted and processed. These flows become the strategy that separates dirty work from clean public space.
captions: Graded waste disposal process.
Design strategy and concept models.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生梳理每一種垃圾的收集、分類與處理流程。這些流線成為將作業區與潔淨公共空間分開的設計策略。
captions: 分級垃圾處理流程。
設計策略與概念模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The volume is stacked floor by floor, with trucks and pipes feeding waste into a central core. Visitors walk around this core and watch the sorting process through glass.
captions: Form generation steps.
Garbage transport by truck in the first phase.
Waste classification floors around the core.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 量體逐層堆疊，卡車與管道把垃圾送入中央核心。參觀者環繞核心行走，隔著玻璃觀看分類過程。
captions: 量體生成步驟。
第一階段以卡車運送垃圾。
環繞核心的垃圾分類樓層。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The station becomes a public science hall where recycling is shown as an exhibition. Handmade modules let visitors turn sorted material into new objects.
captions: Handmade module models.
Long section through the station.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 轉運站成為一座公共科普展館，把回收過程當作展覽呈現。手作模組讓參觀者把分類後的材料轉化為新物件。
captions: 手作模組模型。
轉運站長向剖面。

sections.heading: Turning Waste into Treasure - A Transfer Station Becomes a Science Hall
sections.body: An old waste transfer station sits at the heart of a historic shopping and tourist district, its single treatment method and strong smell cutting it off from the schools and attractions around it. Mapping how each kind of waste is collected, sorted and processed, the student turned these flows into a strategy that separates dirty work from clean public space. The volume is stacked floor by floor, with trucks and pipes feeding waste into a central core. Visitors circle this core and watch the sorting process through glass. Ultimately, the station becomes a public science hall where recycling itself is presented as an exhibition, and handmade modules let visitors turn sorted material into new objects. A facility the city once shunned thus becomes a place of learning and participation, and what was discarded is given value again, its journey made visible rather than hidden away behind walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 變廢為寶-垃圾轉運站化為科普展館
zh-Hant.body: 一座老舊的垃圾轉運站，位於歷史商業與觀光街區的中心，單一的處理方式與強烈異味，使它與周邊的學校和景點隔絕。學生梳理每一種垃圾的收集、分類與處理流程，這些流線成為將作業區與潔淨公共空間分開的設計策略。量體逐層堆疊，卡車與管道把垃圾送入中央核心，參觀者環繞核心行走，隔著玻璃觀看分類的過程。最終，轉運站成為一座公共科普展館，把回收過程當作展覽呈現，手作模組更讓參觀者把分類後的材料轉化為新物件。被城市嫌棄的設施，就此成為教育與參與的場所，廢棄物也重新獲得價值。

pins.title: Haizhu Lake Wetland Museum Hub
pins.description:
An ecological renewal that turns a lake front plaza into a wetland museum hub.

Guangzhou, China | Urban design | Wetland museum | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 海珠湖濕地博物館樞紐
zh-Hant.description:
把湖畔前廣場轉化為濕地博物館樞紐的生態更新。

中國廣州｜都市設計｜濕地博物館｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The wetland museum hub on the lake front plaza.
位於湖畔前廣場的濕地博物館樞紐。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The front plaza of a city lake in Guangzhou is underused and lacks shops and public amenities. Its wetland ecology is also weakly connected to the busy new district around it.
captions: Site analysis of the lake, wildlife and access.
Space types mixing wetland, lawn and buildings.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 廣州一座城市湖泊的前廣場使用率低，缺乏商業與公共設施。它的濕地生態也與周邊繁忙的新城區連結薄弱。
captions: 湖泊、生物與交通的基地分析。
混合濕地、草坪與建築的空間類型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studies the current plants, water edges and how people move across the plaza. A layered landscape of canopy, wetland and water becomes the base of the design.
captions: Current plant status and layered landscape.
Form derivation in six steps.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究現有植栽、水岸以及人們穿越廣場的方式。由樹冠、濕地與水域組成的分層地景，成為設計的基礎。
captions: 現有植栽狀況與分層地景。
六個步驟的形體推演。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The building sinks into the ground and opens toward the lake in curved terraces. Shops, a gym and a wetland exhibition hall are linked by ramps and vertical paths.
captions: Exploded axonometric of programs and circulation.
Floor plans from basement to upper level.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 建築下沉入地面，以弧形平台向湖面展開。商店、健身空間與濕地展覽館由坡道和垂直動線相互連接。
captions: 功能與動線的爆炸軸測圖。
從地下層到上層的各層平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Green terraces and trails let visitors move from the city edge down to the water. A wetland museum hangs over the lake so people can watch birds and plants up close.
captions: Bird's-eye view from the city side.
Section through the wetland museum.
Physical model of the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 綠色平台與步道讓參觀者從城市邊緣一路走到水邊。濕地博物館懸挑於湖面上，讓人近距離觀察鳥類與植物。
captions: 從城市一側看的鳥瞰圖。
濕地博物館剖面。
專案實體模型。

sections.heading: Wetland Museum Hub - Descending from the City Edge to the Lake
sections.body: The front plaza of a city lake is underused and short of shops and public amenities, and its wetland ecology is only weakly connected to the busy new district around it. Studying the existing plants, water edges and the ways people cross the plaza, the student made a layered landscape of canopy, wetland and water the foundation of the design. The building sinks into the ground and opens toward the lake in curved terraces. Shops, a gym and a wetland exhibition hall are linked by ramps and vertical paths. In the final scheme, green terraces and trails let visitors move from the city edge down to the water, while a wetland museum cantilevered over the lake allows birds and plants to be watched up close. The rift between city and wetland is thus stitched together by a gentle slope, and the descent itself becomes a slow lesson in how urban life might lean toward the water.

zh-Hant.heading: 濕地博物館樞紐-從城市邊緣走向湖水
zh-Hant.body: 一座城市湖泊的前廣場使用率低，缺乏商業與公共設施，濕地生態也與周邊繁忙的新城區連結薄弱。學生研究現有植栽、水岸以及人們穿越廣場的方式，由樹冠、濕地與水域組成的分層地景，成為設計的基礎。建築下沉入地面，以弧形平台向湖面展開；商店、健身空間與濕地展覽館，由坡道與垂直動線彼此相連。最終，綠色平台與步道讓參觀者從城市邊緣一路走到水邊，懸挑於湖面的濕地博物館，則讓人近距離觀察鳥類與植物。城市與濕地之間的斷裂，就此被一道溫和的坡度縫合。

pins.title: Occupying the Void
pins.description:
A vertical logistics and greenhouse frame that revives a historic fruit market.

Hong Kong | Architecture | Market adaptive reuse | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 佔據虛空
zh-Hant.description:
以垂直物流與溫室框架，活化一座歷史果欄。

香港｜建築設計｜市場活化再利用｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A new structure rises above the historic fruit market roofs.
新結構在歷史果欄的屋頂上方升起。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A historic fruit market in Hong Kong works mostly at night, and its trucks crowd the narrow streets. During the day much of its space stands empty while the area around it is very dense.
captions: Site analysis of the market blocks and streets.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 香港一座歷史果欄主要在夜間運作，貨車塞滿狹窄的街道。白天大部分空間閒置，而周邊地區卻極度密集。
captions: 果欄街區與街道的基地分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student records how goods, trucks and traders move through a full week. A time and cost study shows how the night delivery cycle could be sorted by floor.
captions: Nighttime distribution cycle in section.
Truck routes to the loading floors.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生記錄一整週貨物、貨車與商販的移動方式。時間與成本研究顯示，夜間配送流程可以按樓層加以分流。
captions: 夜間配送流程剖面。
通往各裝卸樓層的貨車路線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A vertical frame stacks loading, parking and cold storage above the old market without touching its structure. A greenhouse farm and retail floor sit on top under a light glass shell.
captions: Plans from loading area to greenhouse farm.
Layers of the greenhouse shell.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一個垂直框架在舊市場上方堆疊裝卸、停車與冷藏空間，而不觸碰原有結構。頂層在輕盈的玻璃外殼下設置溫室農場與零售空間。
captions: 從裝卸區到溫室農場的各層平面。
溫室外殼的構造層次。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The market keeps its historic halls while gaining new space for logistics and public life. Clear targets show expected gains in traffic, land use, food waste and noise.
captions: Long section through the market and new frame.
Cross section toward the street.
Key metrics and improvement targets.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 果欄保留了歷史建築，同時獲得物流與公共生活的新空間。明確的指標呈現交通、土地利用、廚餘與噪音方面的預期改善。
captions: 穿越市場與新框架的長向剖面。
朝向街道的橫向剖面。
關鍵指標與改善目標。

sections.heading: Occupying the Void - Stacking a New Day Above a Historic Fruit Market
sections.body: A historic fruit market works mostly at night, its trucks crowding narrow streets, while by day much of its space stands empty in the middle of a very dense area. Over a full week, the student recorded how goods, trucks and traders move, and a time and cost study showed how the night delivery cycle could be sorted by floor. A vertical frame then stacks loading, parking and cold storage above the old market without touching its structure. On top, a greenhouse farm and retail floor sit beneath a light glass shell. As a result, the market keeps its historic halls while gaining new space for logistics and public life, and clear targets set out expected gains in traffic, land use, food waste and noise. The rhythms of day and night are rewritten here, and an idle void becomes a source of renewal for a crowded city that has little room left to spare.

zh-Hant.heading: 佔據虛空-在歷史果欄上方疊起新的一天
zh-Hant.body: 一座歷史果欄主要在夜間運作，貨車塞滿狹窄的街道；白天，大部分空間閒置，周邊地區卻極度密集。學生記錄了一整週貨物、貨車與商販的移動方式，時間與成本研究則顯示，夜間配送流程可以按樓層加以分流。一個垂直框架隨之在舊市場上方堆疊裝卸、停車與冷藏空間，而不觸碰原有結構；頂層在輕盈的玻璃外殼下，設置溫室農場與零售空間。最終，果欄保留了歷史建築，同時獲得物流與公共生活的新空間，明確的指標呈現交通、土地利用、廚餘與噪音方面的預期改善。日與夜的節奏在此被重新編排，閒置的虛空成為城市的新生。

pins.title: Healing Anchor
pins.description:
An old agricultural machinery factory adapted into a care campus for older residents.

Jiangmen, China | Architecture | Adaptive reuse for elderly care | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 療癒錨點
zh-Hant.description:
將舊農業機械廠改造為長者照護園區。

中國江門｜建築設計｜長照活化再利用｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The old factory reborn among blossoming trees.
在繁花樹木間重生的舊工廠。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A disused agricultural machinery factory in Jiangmen sits in an area with a fast-ageing population. Older residents lack nearby places for care, social life and medical support.
captions: Site analysis with nearby health facilities.
Urban regeneration options for the factory blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 江門一座廢棄的農業機械廠，位於人口快速老化的地區。年長居民附近缺乏照護、社交與醫療支援的場所。
captions: 標示周邊醫療設施的基地分析。
工廠街廓的都市再生方案。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studies the factory layout, local demographics and how older people use the area each day. These findings shape a plan that keeps the industrial halls and adds care uses.
captions: Planning flow across the factory area.
Regenerative synergy between heritage and wellness.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究工廠配置、在地人口結構，以及長者每天如何使用這個地區。這些發現形成一個保留工業廠房並加入照護功能的計畫。
captions: 整個廠區的規劃流程。
工業遺產與健康照護的再生協同。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The ground floor becomes a senior activity space with gardens and a winding water path. Upper floors hold a high-care hub and assisted living rooms linked by a second-floor walkway.
captions: Ground floor senior activity space.
Second floor high-care hub.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一樓成為長者活動空間，配有花園與蜿蜒的水景步道。上層設置高度照護中心與協助生活住房，並以二樓連廊相連。
captions: 一樓長者活動空間。
二樓高度照護中心。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The factory turns into a care campus where daily life, nursing and community meet. Unit plans show rooms sized for different levels of care.
captions: Third floor assisted living.
High-care and intermediate care unit plans.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 工廠轉化為一座照護園區，讓日常生活、護理與社區交會。單元平面呈現對應不同照護等級的房間尺度。
captions: 三樓協助生活樓層。
高度照護與中度照護單元平面。

sections.heading: Healing Anchor - A Disused Factory Reborn as an Elder Care Campus
sections.body: A disused agricultural machinery factory stands in an area with a fast-ageing population, where older residents lack nearby places for care, social life and medical support. Studying the factory layout, local demographics and the ways older people use the area each day, the student shaped a plan that keeps the industrial halls while adding care uses. The ground floor becomes a senior activity space with gardens and a winding water path. Above, a high-care hub and assisted living rooms are linked by a second-floor walkway. In the end, the factory turns into a care campus where daily life, nursing and community meet, and unit plans show rooms sized for different levels of care. A former space of labour thus becomes an anchor for later life, where memory and care settle beneath one roof and the bones of industry learn to hold a gentler kind of work.

zh-Hant.heading: 療癒錨點-廢棄廠房化為長者照護園區
zh-Hant.body: 一座廢棄的農業機械廠，位於人口快速老化的地區，年長居民附近卻缺乏照護、社交與醫療支援的場所。學生研究工廠配置、在地人口結構，以及長者每天如何使用這個地區，這些發現形成一個保留工業廠房、並加入照護功能的計畫。一樓成為長者活動空間，配有花園與蜿蜒的水景步道；上層設置高度照護中心與協助生活住房，並以二樓連廊相連。最終，工廠轉化為一座讓日常生活、護理與社區交會的照護園區，單元平面呈現對應不同照護等級的房間尺度。舊日的勞動空間由此成為晚年的錨點，記憶與照護在同一屋簷下安頓。

pins.title: The Wave
pins.description:
A woven bamboo pavilion that people can climb, touch and plant in.

Taiwan | Installation | Bamboo pavilion | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 浪
zh-Hant.description:
一座可攀爬、觸摸與種植的編織竹構亭。

台灣｜裝置設計｜竹構亭｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Elevation of the woven bamboo pavilion.
編織竹構亭的立面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The brief asks for a temporary installation in an outdoor museum plaza. The student wants it to be more than a shade, a place people can climb, touch and live with.
captions: Pavilion views from different angles.
Location analysis of bamboo resources.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 任務要求在戶外美術館廣場設計一座臨時裝置。學生希望它不只是遮蔽物，而是人們可以攀爬、觸摸並與之共處的場所。
captions: 不同角度的亭子視圖。
竹材資源的區位分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studies a traditional pressure-one-pick-one bamboo weaving technique. Simple triangle units are tested and grown into larger structural parts.
captions: Evolution of unit components.
Evolution of larger components.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究傳統的「壓一挑一」竹編技法。簡單的三角單元經過測試，再發展成更大的結構構件。
captions: 單元構件的演變。
大型構件的演變。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Planting units with soil and small plants are woven into the bamboo frame. A series of models refines the canopy shape step by step.
captions: Planting units of plants, soil and bamboo.
Model evolution toward the final form.
Steps for bamboo weaving.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 含土壤與小型植物的種植單元被編入竹構框架中。一系列模型逐步修正頂篷的形態。
captions: 由植物、土壤與竹材組成的種植單元。
邁向最終形態的模型演變。
竹編步驟。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final wave is a self-supporting bamboo shell with stairs and platforms inside. Tested node joints show how the parts are tied together by hand.
captions: Partial view of the woven structure.
Node construction and joint tests.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的波浪是一座自承重竹殼，內部設有樓梯與平台。經過測試的節點顯示構件如何以手工綁接。
captions: 編織結構的局部視圖。
節點構造與接頭測試。

sections.heading: The Wave - A Bamboo Shell to Climb, Touch and Grow
sections.body: The brief asks for a temporary installation in an outdoor museum plaza, and the student wanted it to be more than shade: a place people could climb, touch and live alongside. A traditional pressure-one-pick-one bamboo weaving technique became the starting point, with simple triangular units tested and then grown into larger structural parts. Planting units filled with soil and small plants were woven into the bamboo frame. A series of models refined the shape of the canopy step by step. The final wave is a self-supporting bamboo shell with stairs and platforms inside, and tested node joints show how each part is tied together by hand. Ancient weaving knowledge thus becomes a contemporary public space, where bamboo and plants grow together and the installation turns into a breathing landscape that invites the body in rather than merely sheltering it from the sun.

zh-Hant.heading: 浪-可攀爬、可生長的竹編殼體
zh-Hant.body: 任務要求在戶外美術館廣場設計一座臨時裝置，學生希望它不只是遮蔽物，而是人們可以攀爬、觸摸並與之共處的場所。傳統的「壓一挑一」竹編技法成為研究的起點，簡單的三角單元經過測試，再發展為更大的結構構件。含有土壤與小型植物的種植單元被編入竹構框架之中，一系列模型則逐步修正頂篷的形態。最終，這道波浪成為一座自承重的竹殼，內部設有樓梯與平台，經過測試的節點顯示各構件如何以手工綁接。古老的編織智慧在此化為當代的公共空間，竹與植物一同生長，讓裝置成為一處會呼吸的風景。

pins.title: Turtle Tower
pins.description:
A tower of shell-like rooms inspired by how turtles stack.

Spatial Design | Model | Shell tower | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 龜塔
zh-Hant.description:
一座受烏龜堆疊習性啟發的殼狀空間塔。

空間設計｜模型｜殼體塔｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Final model of the turtle tower.
龜塔的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student has kept turtles for years and noticed that they stack on top of each other. The project asks whether this habit of stacking for safety and sunlight can become a spatial tower.
captions: Concept drawing of stacked shell volumes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生多年飼養烏龜，觀察到牠們會彼此堆疊。這個作品探問，這種為了安全與日照而堆疊的習性，能否轉化為一座空間塔。
captions: 堆疊殼體量體的概念圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student draws the plates of shells and undersides to learn their patterns and joints. These drawings become a kit of interlocking plates.
captions: Sketches of shell and underside plates.
Sketches of shell patterns.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生描繪龜甲與腹甲的甲片，以理解其紋理與接合方式。這些圖面成為一套可互相嵌合的板片系統。
captions: 龜甲與腹甲板片的草圖。
龜甲紋理的草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Paper plates are cut to mimic shell plates, and wooden sticks form the frame that holds them. Painted panels, jelly-wax water and small stones tie the tower to a pond setting.
captions: Shell plate studies in paper and wood.
Cutting, painting and assembling the plates.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 紙板被裁切成仿龜甲的板片，木條則構成支撐它們的框架。上色的板片、果凍蠟水面與小石頭，讓塔與池塘環境相連。
captions: 以紙與木製作的甲片研究。
裁切、上色與組裝板片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model stacks shell-like rooms on a light frame above a pond. Close views show how scale figures move through the layered shells.
captions: Close views of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型將殼狀空間堆疊在池塘上方的輕框架上。近景顯示比例人如何穿行於層層殼體之間。
captions: 模型近景。

sections.heading: Turtle Tower - A Shell Tower Grown from the Habit of Stacking
sections.body: Having kept turtles for years, the student noticed that they stack on top of one another, and the project asks whether this habit of stacking for safety and sunlight could become a spatial tower. Drawings of shell plates and undersides were made to understand their patterns and joints, and these drawings became a kit of interlocking plates. Paper plates were cut to mimic the shell, while wooden sticks formed the frame that holds them. Painted panels, jelly-wax water and small stones then tied the tower to a pond setting. In the final model, shell-like rooms stack upon a light frame above the pond, and close views show scale figures moving through the layered shells. An everyday observation is magnified into architecture here, and the survival wisdom of a small animal becomes the seed of a human space, patient and protective as a carapace.

zh-Hant.heading: 龜塔-從疊龜習性長出的殼狀之塔
zh-Hant.body: 多年飼養烏龜的學生，觀察到牠們會彼此堆疊；作品追問，這種為了安全與日照而堆疊的習性，能否轉化為一座空間之塔。龜甲與腹甲的甲片被仔細描繪，以理解其紋理與接合方式，這些圖面隨後成為一套可互相嵌合的板片系統。紙板被裁切成仿龜甲的板片，木條構成支撐的框架；上色的板片、果凍蠟水面與小石頭，則讓塔與池塘環境相連。最終模型將殼狀空間堆疊在池塘上方的輕框架上，近景中，比例人穿行於層層殼體之間。日常的觀察由此被放大為建築，動物的生存智慧，也成為人類空間的靈感。

pins.title: Turtle Habitat
pins.description:
A landscape model that gives turtles water, caves, grass and islands.

Landscape Design | Model | Animal habitat | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 烏龜棲地
zh-Hant.description:
一座為烏龜提供水域、洞穴、草地與島嶼的地景模型。

地景設計｜模型｜動物棲地｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Final model of the turtle habitat.
烏龜棲地的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: After years of building small habitats at home, the student asks what an ideal home for turtles could be. The design must offer water, caves, grass and islands in one landscape.
captions: A painting of a turtle swimming through litter, the starting point of the habitat.
Photos of my turtles and their habitats.
Outline studies of the terrain.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 多年在家中搭建小型棲地後，學生探問烏龜理想的家是什麼樣子。設計必須在同一地景中提供水域、洞穴、草地與島嶼。
captions: 海龜在垃圾中游動的繪畫，是這座棲地的起點。
我的烏龜與其飼養環境照片。
地形輪廓研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each zone is matched to a need: caves for rest, grass for basking and water for swimming. A plan sketch arranges these zones around a looping stream.
captions: Plan sketch of the habitat zones.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個區域都對應一種需求：洞穴供休息、草地供曬背、水域供游泳。平面草圖將這些區域安排在一條環繞的溪流周圍。
captions: 棲地分區的平面草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The base terrain is shaped in clay, with caves built over a wire frame. Sand, grass powder and small shrubs are added, and wax is poured to form the water.
captions: Clay terrain with caves and islands.
Planting and water surfaces added.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 基地地形以黏土塑造，洞穴則建在鐵絲框架上。接著加入沙、草粉與小型灌木，再倒入蠟形成水面。
captions: 帶有洞穴與島嶼的黏土地形。
加上植栽與水面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model joins shallow and deep water, streams, caves and marsh into one habitat. It shows how zoning and material choices can shape a whole ecosystem.
captions: Views of water and cave spaces.
Close views of islands and caves.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把淺水、深水、溪流、洞穴與濕地整合為一個棲地。它展示分區與材料選擇如何塑造完整的生態系統。
captions: 水域與洞穴空間的視圖。
島嶼與洞穴的近景。

sections.heading: Turtle Habitat - Water, Caves, Grass and Islands for Turtles
sections.body: After years of building small habitats at home, the student asks what an ideal home for turtles might be, and the design must offer water, caves, grass and islands within a single landscape. Each zone answers a specific need: caves for rest, grass for basking and water for swimming, with a plan sketch arranging them around a looping stream. The base terrain was shaped in clay, and caves were built over a wire frame. Sand, grass powder and small shrubs were then added, before wax was poured to form the water. The final model joins shallow and deep water, streams, caves and marsh into one habitat, showing how zoning and material choices can shape an entire ecosystem. Years of quiet care for small lives settle here into a careful design inquiry, one in which empathy for another creature becomes the most precise brief of all.

zh-Hant.heading: 烏龜棲地-為龜打造水、穴、草與島
zh-Hant.body: 多年在家中搭建小型棲地之後，學生追問烏龜理想的家究竟是什麼樣子；設計必須在同一地景中提供水域、洞穴、草地與島嶼。每個區域都對應一種需求：洞穴供休息，草地供曬背，水域供游泳，平面草圖將這些區域安排在一條環繞的溪流周圍。基地地形以黏土塑造，洞穴建於鐵絲框架之上；沙、草粉與小型灌木隨後加入，再倒入蠟形成水面。最終模型把淺水、深水、溪流、洞穴與濕地整合為一個棲地，展示分區與材料選擇如何塑造完整的生態系統。對小生命長年的照料，就此沉澱為一份細膩的設計思考。

pins.title: Metallic Foam Morphologies
pins.description:
Porous printed forms that turn a lab material into a home for fish.

Spatial Design | Material study | Porous habitat | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 金屬泡沫形態
zh-Hant.description:
將實驗室材料轉化為魚類棲所的多孔列印形態。

空間設計｜材料研究｜多孔棲地｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Printed porous model with small fish.
帶有小魚的列印多孔模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The project grows out of a summer research study on nickel foam used to break down an antibiotic in water. The student asks how such porous materials could later return to nature as shelter for fish and other sea life.
captions: Hand-drawn diagram of the material preparation.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個作品源自一項暑期研究，主題是用於分解水中抗生素的鎳泡沫。學生探問，這類多孔材料日後能否回到自然，成為魚類與其他海洋生物的棲身之所。
captions: 材料製備流程的手繪圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The hand-drawn diagram records each step from mixing to firing the porous structure. This lab process sets the logic of pores and channels that the design follows.
captions: Parametric script that grows the porous form.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 手繪圖記錄了從混合到燒製多孔結構的每一個步驟。這個實驗流程確立了設計所依循的孔洞與通道邏輯。
captions: 生成多孔形態的參數化程式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A parametric script turns the foam pattern into hollow units under a hexagon cap. The units can hang alone or join into clusters like a reef.
captions: Renders of single and clustered units.
Hexagon caps seen from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 參數化程式將泡沫紋理轉化為六角形頂蓋下的中空單元。這些單元可以單獨懸掛，也可以像礁石一樣組合成群。
captions: 單一與群組單元的渲染圖。
從上方看六角形頂蓋。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The resin models are hung in water, and small fish swim in and out of the pores. The test shows how a lab material can be reshaped into a living habitat.
captions: Hanging columns in water.
Fish moving through the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 樹脂模型被懸掛在水中，小魚在孔洞間穿梭進出。這次測試展示實驗室材料如何被重塑為有生命的棲地。
captions: 水中的懸掛柱體。
在模型中穿梭的魚。

sections.heading: Metallic Foam Morphologies - A Lab Material Turned Fish Habitat
sections.body: A summer research study on nickel foam used to break down an antibiotic in water lies at the root of this project, in which the student asks whether such porous materials might later return to nature as shelter for fish and sea life. A hand-drawn diagram records each step from mixing to firing the porous structure, and this laboratory process set the logic of pores and channels that the design follows. A parametric script then turned the foam pattern into hollow units beneath a hexagonal cap. These units can hang alone or join into reef-like clusters. Finally, resin models were suspended in water, and small fish swam in and out of the pores. The test shows how a material born in the lab can be reshaped into a living habitat, where scientific rigour and ecological tenderness meet within the same porous body, and research finds a second life beneath the surface.

zh-Hant.heading: 金屬泡沫形態-實驗室材料化為魚的棲所
zh-Hant.body: 一項關於分解水中抗生素之鎳泡沫的暑期研究，是這件作品的源頭；學生追問，這類多孔材料日後能否回到自然，成為魚類與海洋生物的棲身之所。手繪圖記錄了從混合到燒製多孔結構的每一個步驟，這個實驗流程確立了設計所依循的孔洞與通道邏輯。接著，參數化程式將泡沫紋理轉化為六角形頂蓋下的中空單元，可以單獨懸掛，也能像礁石般組合成群。最終，樹脂模型被懸掛在水中，小魚在孔洞間穿梭進出。實驗室裡的材料由此被重塑為有生命的棲地，科學的嚴謹與生態的溫柔，在同一片孔隙裡相遇。

pins.title: Travel Tales
pins.description:
Travel sketches cut, recombined and built into a layered landscape.

Spatial Design | Model | Landscape collage | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 旅行故事
zh-Hant.description:
將旅行速寫裁切、重組，並建構成層疊地景。

空間設計｜模型｜地景拼貼｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Final model of layered landscapes.
層疊地景的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student keeps a sketchbook on every trip and is drawn to natural landscapes. The project asks how scattered travel memories could become one three-dimensional space.
captions: Travel photos of the landscapes behind the sketches.
Travel sketches cut and collaged into new scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生每次旅行都帶著速寫本，並深受自然地景吸引。這個作品探問，零散的旅行記憶能否成為一個立體空間。
captions: 速寫背後的旅途風景照片。
旅行速寫被裁切並拼貼成新的場景。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches of favourite places are cut into distinct fragments and recombined into new images. Each fragment keeps one strong trait of its scene, such as layers of rock or lines of trees.
captions: Cutting and assembling board pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生將喜愛地點的速寫裁切成不同碎片，再重新組合成新的畫面。每個碎片都保留其場景的一項鮮明特徵，例如岩層或樹列。
captions: 裁切與組裝板材構件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The collages are translated into two volumes built from stacked and slotted board. Solid and void are balanced so that each volume reads as one composition.
captions: Volume one from above.
Volume one from the side.
Volume two from above.
Volume two from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 拼貼被轉譯為兩個以堆疊與插接板材構成的量體。實與虛之間取得平衡，使每個量體都成為完整的構圖。
captions: 從上方看第一量體。
從側面看第一量體。
從上方看第二量體。
從側面看第二量體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model hangs a cloud of layers over thin columns and terraced ground. Close views show how lines from the sketches become ramps, ribs and caves.
captions: Close-up views of the model.
Layered details of ground and canopy.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型將層層雲狀量體懸於細柱與階梯狀地面之上。近景顯示速寫中的線條如何化為坡道、肋片與洞穴。
captions: 模型近景。
地面與頂蓋的層疊細部。

sections.heading: Travel Tales - Sketch Fragments Stacked into Clouds and Caves
sections.body: Carrying a sketchbook on every trip and drawn to natural landscapes, the student asks in this project whether scattered travel memories could become a single three-dimensional space. Sketches of favourite places were cut into distinct fragments and recombined into new images, each fragment keeping one strong trait of its scene, such as layers of rock or lines of trees. These collages were then translated into two volumes built from stacked and slotted board. Solid and void are balanced so that each volume reads as one complete composition. In the final model, a cloud of layers hangs above thin columns and terraced ground, and close views reveal how lines from the sketches have turned into ramps, ribs and caves. Fragments of many journeys are stitched into one imagined landscape, so that memory no longer lies scattered across pages but becomes a place one could step into and wander through.

zh-Hant.heading: 旅行故事-把速寫碎片疊成雲與洞穴
zh-Hant.body: 每次旅行都帶著速寫本、深受自然地景吸引的學生，在這件作品中追問：零散的旅行記憶能否成為一個立體空間。喜愛地點的速寫被裁切成不同的碎片，再重新組合成新的畫面，每個碎片都保留其場景的一項鮮明特徵，例如岩層或樹列。拼貼隨後被轉譯為兩個以堆疊與插接板材構成的量體，實與虛之間取得平衡，使每個量體都成為完整的構圖。最終模型將層層雲狀的量體懸於細柱與階梯狀地面之上，近景中，速寫裡的線條化為坡道、肋片與洞穴。旅途的片段由此被縫合成一處想像的風景，記憶不再散落，而是可以步入其中。

pins.title: The Carbon Sink of Scars
pins.description:
An installation of three damaged habitats that absorb our carbon.

Spatial Design | Installation | Carbon sink | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 傷痕碳匯
zh-Hant.description:
以三個受損棲地構成、吸收人類碳排放的裝置。

空間設計｜裝置｜碳匯｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The three habitats joined into one installation.
三個棲地組合成一件裝置。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Oceans, forests and the atmosphere absorb most of the carbon people release. The project asks how a small installation could show both their role as carbon sinks and the damage they carry.
captions: Silent Sea: resin water over a white foam base.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 海洋、森林與大氣吸收了人類排放的大部分碳。這個作品探問，一件小型裝置如何同時呈現它們作為碳匯的角色，以及它們所承受的傷害。
captions: 沉默之海：樹脂水面覆於白色發泡底座上。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each habitat is read through one kind of harm: acidifying water, burned forest and polluted air. Industrial materials such as PVC board, wax, clay, wire and acrylic are chosen to tell that story.
captions: Carving and casting the sea model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個棲地都透過一種傷害來解讀：酸化的海水、焚燒的森林與污染的空氣。學生選用 PVC 板、蠟、黏土、鐵絲與壓克力等工業材料來講述這個故事。
captions: 雕刻與澆鑄海洋模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A white foam base stands for bleached coral, and a clay block with wire trees stands for a forest stripped by fire. A cotton cloud hangs over a small clay city to make the invisible air visible.
captions: Entombed Life: wire trees on a burned clay ground.
Miasma: a cotton cloud over a clay city.
Cloud studies from two angles.
The city beneath the cloud.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 白色發泡底座象徵白化的珊瑚，黏土塊與鐵絲樹則代表被大火剝奪養分的森林。棉花雲懸於小型黏土城市之上，讓看不見的空氣變得可見。
captions: 掩埋之生：焦土黏土上的鐵絲樹。
瘴氣：黏土城市上空的棉花雲。
從兩個角度觀看雲的研究。
雲層下的城市。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The three pieces sit side by side as one carbon sink at a scale of about thirty centimetres. Together they show places that sustain life while bearing the scars of human actions.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 三件作品並列為一個約三十公分尺度的碳匯。它們共同呈現了維繫生命、同時承受人類行為傷痕的場所。

sections.heading: The Carbon Sink of Scars - Three Habitats Bearing Human Harm
sections.body: Oceans, forests and the atmosphere absorb most of the carbon that people release, and the project asks how a small installation could show both their role as carbon sinks and the damage they carry. Each habitat is read through one kind of harm, acidifying water, burned forest and polluted air, while industrial materials such as PVC board, wax, clay, wire and acrylic were chosen to tell that story. A white foam base stands for bleached coral. Beside it, a clay block with wire trees evokes a forest stripped by fire, and a cotton cloud hangs over a small clay city to make the invisible air visible. Placed side by side, the three pieces form one carbon sink at a scale of about thirty centimetres, showing places that sustain life while bearing the scars of human action. Industrial materials narrate the cost of industry itself, and the modest scale only sharpens the weight of the question it poses.

zh-Hant.heading: 傷痕碳匯-承載人類傷害的三處棲地
zh-Hant.body: 海洋、森林與大氣吸收了人類排放的大部分碳；作品追問，一件小型裝置能否同時呈現它們作為碳匯的角色，以及所承受的傷害。每個棲地都透過一種傷害被解讀：酸化的海水、焚燒的森林與污染的空氣，PVC板、蠟、黏土、鐵絲與壓克力等工業材料則被選來講述這個故事。白色發泡底座象徵白化的珊瑚，黏土塊與鐵絲樹代表被大火剝奪的森林，棉花雲懸於小型黏土城市上方，讓看不見的空氣變得可見。最終，三件作品並列為一個約三十公分尺度的碳匯，共同呈現維繫生命、同時承受傷痕的場所。工業材料講述工業的代價，微小的尺度反而放大了沉重的提問。

pins.title: Motion Morphology
pins.description:
A hurdling jump traced, lofted and hung as a spatial form.

Spatial Design | Installation | Motion study | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 運動形態學
zh-Hant.description:
將一次跨欄動作描繪、放樣並懸掛成空間形態。

空間設計｜裝置｜動態研究｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final installation hung in space.
懸掛於空間中的最終裝置。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student trains as a hurdler and wanted to turn this movement into a spatial form. The project asks how running, leaping and landing could be held still as one object.
captions: A motion study plate of a running figure.
Gesture drawings of eight frames from the jump.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生是一名跨欄選手，希望將這項運動轉化為空間形態。這個作品探問，奔跑、躍起與落地如何被凝結成單一物件。
captions: 人物奔跑的連續動作研究圖版。
跨欄動作中八個畫格的動態速寫。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Still frames from practice videos were studied, and six key moments of the jump were picked out. The path of each joint was traced and the frames were layered into one composite drawing.
captions: Frame-by-frame photos of my hurdling motion.
Joint paths layered across the key frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生研究練習影片中的靜止畫格，並挑選出跨欄動作中的六個關鍵瞬間。每個關節的運動路徑都被描繪下來，並疊合成一張多畫格合成圖。
captions: 我跨欄動作的逐格照片。
關鍵畫格中疊合的關節路徑。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The limb paths were lofted into smooth curves that pass through a row of vertical panels. These curves were then thickened into ribbons that read as a trace of the body in space.
captions: Lofted curves through the panels.
The body trace cut by the panels.
Shaping the ribbons.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 四肢的路徑被放樣成平滑曲線，穿過一列垂直板片。這些曲線再被加厚成帶狀體，成為身體在空間中留下的軌跡。
captions: 穿越板片的放樣曲線。
被板片切分的身體軌跡。
塑造帶狀體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final piece hangs panels, a frame and textured ribbons on thin wires. It turns the timing and rhythm of one jump into a ghosted memory of movement.
captions: Side view of the ribbons.
Ribbons between two panels.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終作品以細線懸掛板片、框架與帶有質感的帶狀體。它將一次跨欄的節奏與時序，轉化為一段如殘影般的運動記憶。
captions: 帶狀體側視。
兩片板片之間的帶狀體。

sections.heading: Motion Morphology - Freezing the Afterimage of a Hurdle
sections.body: Training as a hurdler, the student wanted to turn this movement into spatial form, and the project asks how running, leaping and landing might be held still within a single object. Still frames from practice videos were studied closely, and six key moments of the jump were picked out. The path of each joint was traced, and the frames were layered into one composite drawing. Lofted into smooth curves, the limb paths were then threaded through a row of vertical panels and thickened into ribbons that read as a trace of the body in space. In the final piece, panels, a frame and textured ribbons hang on thin wires, turning the timing and rhythm of one jump into a ghosted memory of movement. A fleeting bodily experience is gently held back here, and speed becomes a shape that can be quietly contemplated, its every phase suspended in the air like breath caught mid-stride.

zh-Hant.heading: 運動形態學-凝結一次跨欄的殘影
zh-Hant.body: 身為跨欄選手，學生希望將這項運動轉化為空間形態，作品於是追問，奔跑、躍起與落地能否被凝結為單一物件。練習影片中的靜止畫格被逐一研究，從中挑出跨欄動作的六個關鍵瞬間；每個關節的運動路徑都被描繪下來，疊合成一張多畫格的合成圖。接著，四肢的路徑被放樣成平滑曲線，穿過一列垂直板片，再加厚為帶狀體，成為身體在空間中留下的軌跡。最終作品以細線懸掛板片、框架與帶有質感的帶狀體，把一次跨欄的節奏與時序，轉化為如殘影般的運動記憶。轉瞬的身體經驗在此被溫柔地挽留，速度化為可以靜靜凝視的形狀。

pins.title: Pulling, Intersect, Arrange
pins.description:
Three spatial verbs tested in sticks and card, then joined in one hybrid model.

Spatial Design | Model | Spatial tension | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 拉伸、交錯、排列
zh-Hant.description:
以木條與紙板測試三個空間動詞，再結合成一個混合模型。

空間設計｜模型｜空間張力｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The hybrid model in card, wood sticks and PVC sheet.
以紙板、木條與 PVC 片製作的混合模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The student was drawn to the layered triangular geometry of a well-known pavilion. The project asks how that tension could be turned into simple actions that make space.
captions: Diagrams of pulling, intersecting and arranging.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生深受一座知名展館層疊三角幾何的吸引。這個作品探問，這種張力如何轉化為能生成空間的簡單動作。
captions: 拉伸、交錯與排列的圖解。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Three verbs were drawn out of the geometry: pulling, intersecting and arranging. Each verb was tested with wooden sticks and card in small study models.
captions: Study models of pulling.
Study models of intersecting and arranging.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生從幾何中提煉出三個動詞：拉伸、交錯與排列。每個動詞都以木條與紙板在小型研究模型中測試。
captions: 拉伸的研究模型。
交錯與排列的研究模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Of the three verbs, pulling gave the strongest sense of spatial tension and became the focus. Drawings and a tall study model pushed the stretched triangles into denser layers.
captions: Pattern drawing of stretched triangles.
Vertical study model.
Tension drawings and an elevation study.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三個動詞之中，拉伸最能表現空間張力，因此成為重點。圖面與高聳的研究模型將被拉伸的三角形推向更密集的層次。
captions: 被拉伸三角形的圖樣繪圖。
垂直研究模型。
張力繪圖與立面研究。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The hybrid model, about thirty-two inches long, combines all three verbs along one ground. Pulled peaks rise over intersecting frames and arranged planes to form a continuous landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 約三十二英吋長的混合模型將三個動詞結合於同一基地上。被拉起的尖峰升起於交錯的框架與排列的平面之上，形成連續的地景。

sections.heading: Pulling, Intersect, Arrange - Three Verbs Woven into One Landscape
sections.body: The layered triangular geometry of a well-known pavilion caught the student's attention, and the project asks how that tension could be turned into simple actions that make space. From the geometry, three verbs were drawn out, pulling, intersecting and arranging, each tested with wooden sticks and card in small study models. Pulling, of the three, conveyed the strongest sense of spatial tension and so became the focus. Drawings and a tall study model then pushed the stretched triangles into ever denser layers. Measuring about thirty-two inches long, the final hybrid model combines all three verbs along a single ground, where pulled peaks rise above intersecting frames and arranged planes to form a continuous landscape. Verbs become a grammar of construction here, and tension shifts from something admired in another building to something generated by hand, layer upon layer, until a field of peaks seems to breathe across the board.

zh-Hant.heading: 拉伸交錯排列-三個動詞織成連續地景
zh-Hant.body: 一座知名展館層疊的三角幾何吸引了學生，作品因而追問，這種張力能否轉化為生成空間的簡單動作。從幾何之中，拉伸、交錯與排列三個動詞被提煉出來，各自以木條與紙板在小型研究模型中接受測試。三者之中，拉伸最能表現空間張力，於是成為重點；圖面與一座高聳的研究模型，將被拉伸的三角形推向更密集的層次。最終，一件約三十二英吋長的混合模型將三個動詞結合於同一基地之上，被拉起的尖峰升起於交錯的框架與排列的平面上方，形成連續的地景。動詞在此成為構築的語法，張力也從欣賞的對象轉化為親手生成的空間。

pins.title: Echoes of the Horizon
pins.description:
A pavilion of stretched card planes over a timber frame.

Spatial Design | Pavilion | Model | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 地平線的回聲
zh-Hant.description:
在木構架上撐開紙板平面的展亭。

空間設計｜展亭｜模型｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The pavilion model in card, wood sticks and PVC sheet.
以紙板、木條與 PVC 片製作的展亭模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The pavilion grows from the pulling studies of an earlier exercise. The project asks how stretched planes could become a roof that people walk beneath.
captions: The roof planes seen from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這座展亭延續自先前練習中的拉伸研究。這個作品探問，被拉伸的平面如何成為人們可在其下行走的屋頂。
captions: 從上方看屋頂平面。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Thin sticks act as cables that pull folded card planes into sharp peaks. The frame below sets a raised floor and a stair so the roof can be seen from inside.
captions: Side view of the frame and roof.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 細木條如拉索般將折疊紙板拉成尖峰。下方的構架設定了抬高的樓板與樓梯，使人能從內部觀看屋頂。
captions: 構架與屋頂的側視。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The model was photographed from eye level to test the feeling of the interior. A charcoal drawing then studied light, shadow and the stair inside the space.
captions: Eye-level view inside the model.
Charcoal drawing of the interior space.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 學生從視線高度拍攝模型，測試室內的空間感受。接著以炭筆繪圖研究空間中的光影與樓梯。
captions: 模型內部的視線高度視角。
室內空間的炭筆繪圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model is about twenty-five inches wide and eighteen inches tall. Its peaks and cables echo a horizon line seen from the raised floor.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型約二十五英吋寬、十八英吋高。其尖峰與拉索呼應從抬高樓板望出的地平線。

sections.heading: Echoes of the Horizon - Stretched Planes Becoming a Roof
sections.body: Growing out of the pulling studies of an earlier exercise, the pavilion asks how stretched planes could become a roof under which people walk. Thin sticks act like cables, drawing folded card planes into sharp peaks, while the frame below sets out a raised floor and a stair so the roof can be seen from within. The model was then photographed from eye level to test the feeling of the interior. A charcoal drawing went further, studying light, shadow and the stair inside the space. At about twenty-five inches wide and eighteen inches tall, the final model lets its peaks and cables echo a horizon line seen from the raised floor. An abstract exercise in tension thus grows into a place where one might linger, and stretching becomes not merely a formal operation but a posture of gazing outward, toward the far line where land and sky meet.

zh-Hant.heading: 地平線的回聲-被拉伸成屋頂的平面
zh-Hant.body: 這座展亭延續自先前練習中的拉伸研究，追問被拉伸的平面能否成為人們可以在其下行走的屋頂。細木條如拉索一般，將折疊的紙板拉成尖峰；下方的構架則設定了抬高的樓板與樓梯，讓人得以從內部仰望屋頂。模型隨後從視線高度被拍攝，用以測試室內的空間感受，一張炭筆繪圖又進一步研究空間中的光影與樓梯。最終模型約二十五英吋寬、十八英吋高，尖峰與拉索呼應著從抬高樓板望出的地平線。抽象的拉伸練習由此長成一處可以停留的場所，張力不再只是形式，而成為一種凝望遠方的姿態。

pins.title: Garden
pins.description:
A cliffside sculpture garden shaped through colour collages and small cuboid models.

Landscape Design | Sculpture garden | Model | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 花園
zh-Hant.description:
透過色彩拼貼與小型立方體模型塑造的崖邊雕塑花園。

景觀設計｜雕塑花園｜模型｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Small cuboid models in foam-core and card.
以泡沫板與紙板製作的小型立方體模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The brief is a sculpture garden on a cliffside site, shielded by buildings and facing the sea. The garden must hold two sculptures, one tall and one flat, set in visual contrast.
captions: Colour collage of flowing shapes.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 題目是一座位於崖邊、被建築包圍且面向大海的雕塑花園。花園須容納一高一平的兩件雕塑，並形成視覺對比。
captions: 流動形狀的色彩拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A first model set out the layout and the spatial links across the site. Collages then explored texture, colour and the character of each sculpture.
captions: Collage and plan study of the garden.
A second collage and plan study.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 第一個模型先確立配置與基地中的空間關係。接著以拼貼探索質感、色彩與每件雕塑的性格。
captions: 花園的拼貼與平面研究。
第二組拼貼與平面研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Small models about two inches on each side tested how solid blocks could be carved and opened. Each cuboid tried a different balance of mass, void and surface.
captions: More cuboid studies of carving and opening.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 邊長約兩英吋的小模型測試實心量體如何被切削與打開。每個立方體都嘗試不同的量體、虛空與表面平衡。
captions: 更多切削與開口的立方體研究。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The work brings together visual appeal, user comfort and smooth circulation along the cliff. The collages and cuboids give the garden a clear and distinct character.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這件作品在崖邊兼顧視覺吸引力、使用者舒適度與流暢的動線。拼貼與立方體賦予花園清晰而獨特的性格。

sections.heading: Garden - A Tall and a Flat Sculpture on the Cliff Edge
sections.body: The brief is a sculpture garden on a cliffside site, sheltered by buildings and facing the sea, which must hold two sculptures, one tall and one flat, set in clear visual contrast. A first model established the layout and the spatial links across the site, after which collages explored texture, colour and the distinct character of each sculpture. Small models, about two inches on each side, then tested how solid blocks might be carved and opened. Every cuboid tried out a different balance of mass, void and surface. The finished work brings together visual appeal, user comfort and smooth circulation along the cliff, while the collages and cuboids lend the garden a clear and distinctive character. Between sea wind and sheer rock, these tiny blocks carry a careful meditation on scale and contrast, showing how a handful of carved volumes can tune an entire landscape to the rhythm of looking and walking.

zh-Hant.heading: 花園-崖邊立方體中的一高一平
zh-Hant.body: 題目是一座位於崖邊、被建築環抱且面向大海的雕塑花園，須容納一高一平的兩件雕塑，並讓兩者形成鮮明的視覺對比。第一個模型先確立了配置與基地中的空間關係，拼貼接著探索質感、色彩與每件雕塑各自的性格。隨後，邊長約兩英吋的小模型被用來測試實心量體如何被切削、被打開，每個立方體都嘗試一種不同的量體、虛空與表面之間的平衡。最終，作品在崖邊同時兼顧視覺吸引力、使用者的舒適與流暢的動線，拼貼與立方體共同賦予花園清晰而獨特的性格。在海風與懸崖之間，微小的方塊承載了對尺度與對比的細膩思考。

pins.title: Vertical Garden
pins.description:
A knitted wall garden where other species are invited to settle and grow.

Landscape Design | Vertical garden | Habitat | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 垂直花園
zh-Hant.description:
一面編織的牆面花園，邀請其他物種前來棲居與生長。

景觀設計｜垂直花園｜棲地｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished wall of sticks, soil, stones and plants.
以木條、土壤、石頭與植物完成的牆面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In traditional gardens, people are the only authors of the design. The project shifts the act of drawing a garden to other species and lets them choose where to settle.
captions: Natural materials collected around the community.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在傳統花園中，人類是唯一的設計者。這個作品將「繪製花園」的行為交給其他物種，讓牠們自行選擇棲居之處。
captions: 在社區周邊收集的天然材料。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Natural materials were collected nearby and sorted into small micro-environments. Tests of dry to moist soil, stone and mixes found that a soil and stone mix worked best for plant growth.
captions: Soil, stone and mixed samples at four wetness levels.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生在附近收集天然材料，並將其分成不同的微環境。從乾燥到濕潤的土壤、石頭與混合物測試中，發現土石混合最有利於植物生長。
captions: 四種濕度下的土壤、石頭與混合樣本。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Knitted patterns turn the wall into a habitat with zones for plants, rocky insect shelters and flowers for butterflies. Branches woven through the panels support soil health.
captions: Knitted panels with mapped habitat zones.
Panels after planting.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 編織圖樣將牆面轉化為棲地，劃分出植物、多岩昆蟲棲所與吸引蝴蝶的花卉區。穿插於板片間的枝條則維持土壤健康。
captions: 標示棲地分區的編織板片。
種植後的板片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final wall is about forty-five inches tall and built from wooden sticks, soil, branches, stones and plants. Over time the growth on the wall records where life chose to stay.
captions: Close-up of the growing surface.
The panels during the growing process.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終牆面約四十五英吋高，以木條、土壤、枝條、石頭與植物構成。隨著時間推移，牆上的生長記錄了生命選擇停留之處。
captions: 生長表面的近景。
生長過程中的板片。

sections.heading: Vertical Garden - Handing the Garden's Pen to Other Species
sections.body: In traditional gardens, people are the only authors of the design; this project instead hands the act of drawing a garden to other species and lets them choose where to settle. Natural materials were collected nearby and sorted into small micro-environments, and tests ranging from dry to moist soil, stone and mixtures showed that a blend of soil and stone worked best for plant growth. Knitted patterns then turned the wall into a habitat, with zones for plants, rocky shelters for insects and flowers for butterflies. Branches woven through the panels help sustain the health of the soil. The finished wall stands about forty-five inches tall, built from wooden sticks, soil, branches, stones and plants. Over time, the growth across its surface records where life chose to stay, and as the designer steps back, the garden comes to belong to every creature that makes a home within its woven folds.

zh-Hant.heading: 垂直花園-把繪製花園的筆交給別的物種
zh-Hant.body: 在傳統花園中，人類是唯一的設計者；這件作品則把繪製花園的行為交給別的物種，讓牠們自行選擇棲居之處。學生在附近收集天然材料，並分成不同的微環境進行測試，從乾燥到濕潤的土壤、石頭與混合物之間，發現土石混合最有利於植物生長。編織圖樣接著將牆面轉化為棲地，劃分出植物、多岩的昆蟲棲所與吸引蝴蝶的花卉區，穿插於板片間的枝條則維持土壤健康。最終，一面約四十五英吋高的牆，以木條、土壤、枝條、石頭與植物構成。隨著時間推移，牆上的生長記錄了生命選擇停留之處，設計者退後一步，花園因而真正屬於眾生。

pins.title: Rowing
pins.description:
Hand-drawn studies that map the motion of a rowing stroke and the anatomy of the boat.

Design Drawing | Motion study | Rowing | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 划船
zh-Hant.description:
以手繪研究划船動作的節奏，以及船身與船槳的構造。

設計繪圖｜動作研究｜划船｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Aquatic kinetic sketch in pencil and pen.
以鉛筆與鋼筆繪製的水上動態草圖。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Rowing is felt as rhythm, force and repetition, which is hard to show in a single picture. The project asks how a first-person experience of the sport can become a set of drawings.
captions: Photos from my own rowing training.
A collage of rowing from a first-person perspective.
Motion studies of the stroke, first frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 划船的感受來自節奏、力量與重複，很難以單一畫面呈現。這個作品探問如何將第一人稱的運動經驗轉化為一組繪圖。
captions: 我自己划船訓練的照片。
以第一人稱視角呈現划船的拼貼。
划槳動作研究的前段畫格。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The stroke was broken into a sequence of frames seen from above. Each frame records the angle of the oars and the position of the body in the boat.
captions: Later frames of the stroke sequence.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生將划槳動作拆解為一系列俯視畫格。每一格記錄船槳的角度與身體在船中的位置。
captions: 划槳序列的後段畫格。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The overlapping frames were layered into a kinetic sketch built with ruler and compass. A sectional drawing then studies the boat hull, rigger and oar as one connected machine.
captions: Sectional drawing of the boat and oar.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 重疊的畫格以尺規與圓規疊合成一張動態草圖。接著以剖面圖研究船身、槳架與船槳如何連成一部機械。
captions: 船身與船槳的剖面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The series ends with a long drawing that follows the full sweep of the oar. Together the sheets turn a physical sport into a precise record of motion and structure.
captions: Crew boats on the water at sunset and by day.
Sectional drawing of the oar sweep.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 系列以一張追蹤船槳完整划幅的長幅繪圖作結。這些圖面將一項身體運動轉化為精確的動作與構造紀錄。
captions: 黃昏與白天水面上的划船隊。
船槳划幅的剖面圖。

sections.heading: Rowing - Recording Motion and Structure with Ruler and Compass
sections.body: Rowing is felt as rhythm, force and repetition, qualities that are hard to show in a single picture, and the project asks how a first-person experience of the sport could become a set of drawings. The stroke was broken into a sequence of frames seen from above, each recording the angle of the oars and the position of the body in the boat. Overlapping frames were then layered into a kinetic sketch built with ruler and compass. A sectional drawing went on to study the hull, rigger and oar as one connected machine. Closing the series, a long drawing follows the full sweep of the oar from catch to finish. Together the sheets turn a physical sport into a precise record of motion and structure, letting sweat and cadence settle into line, and giving sensation a clear shape within the disciplined strokes of the drafting hand, where feeling and measurement finally agree.

zh-Hant.heading: 划船-以尺規記錄動作與構造
zh-Hant.body: 划船的感受來自節奏、力量與重複，很難在單一畫面中呈現；作品因此追問，第一人稱的運動經驗能否轉化為一組繪圖。划槳動作被拆解為一系列俯視的畫格，每一格都記錄船槳的角度與身體在船中的位置。重疊的畫格隨後以尺規與圓規疊合成一張動態草圖，剖面圖則把船身、槳架與船槳視為一部相連的機械加以研究。系列最終以一張追蹤船槳完整划幅的長幅繪圖作結。這些圖面將一項身體運動轉化為精確的動作與構造紀錄，讓汗水與節拍沉澱為線條，也讓感覺在理性的筆觸中獲得清晰的形狀。

zh-Hant.body: 這個作品分析划船時手臂的動作。它將節奏、幅度與力量轉化為結構，而非單純的圖像。

zh-Hant.body: 塑膠桿模擬手臂的骨骼結構，並以尼龍束帶固定。多層描圖紙則顯示手臂在動作中體積的變化。

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型將塑膠手臂結構與編織竹籤底座結合。它成為一個承載完整划槳節奏的整體。

sections.heading: Rhythm - Turning a Rowing Arm into Structure
sections.body: The motion of the arm during a rowing stroke is the subject of this analysis, which maps rhythm, amplitude and force as a structure rather than a picture. A line drawing traces the arm through each stage of the stroke, while early study models test how frames of the movement might be joined in space. Plastic rods were then used to simulate the arm's skeletal structure, held together with nylon cable ties. Layers of tracing paper reveal how the volume of the arm changes as it moves. In the final model, the plastic arm structure is joined to a woven bamboo base, reading as one body that holds the rhythm of the whole stroke. A fleeting motion is frozen here, the rise and fall of force becoming a skeleton that can be seen and touched, so that bodily memory gains an almost architectural weight and the pulse of the water is kept within a still, articulated frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 節奏-把划槳的手臂化為結構
zh-Hant.body: 划船時手臂的動作，是這件作品分析的對象；節奏、幅度與力量被轉化為結構，而非停留於單純的圖像。一張線描圖追蹤手臂在划槳各階段的位置，早期研究模型則測試動作的各個畫格如何在空間中相連。接著，塑膠桿模擬手臂的骨骼結構，以尼龍束帶固定，多層描圖紙則透露出手臂在動作中體積的變化。最終，塑膠手臂結構與編織竹籤底座結合為一體，成為承載完整划槳節奏的單一身體。轉瞬即逝的運動在此被凝固，力量的起落化為可觸可見的骨架，身體的記憶也因此有了建築般的重量。

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 這個系列延續先前關於「破碎自我」的研究。它探問韌性與柔軟如何共存於同一個構成之中。

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 簡單的線條圖測試幾何與有機邊緣如何結合。小幅色彩研究接著引導每件浮雕的材料選擇。

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 銳利量塊象徵韌性，瓦楞紙板的曲層則表達柔軟。兩件浮雕以不同方式拿捏兩者的平衡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The reliefs are lifted into a free-standing framework of folded planes and sticks. Seen from different sides, the hard and soft parts keep changing places.
captions: Framework model from above.
Framework model, side view.
Framework model, another side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 浮雕最終被延伸為由摺面與木條構成的獨立框架。從不同角度觀看，硬與軟的部分不斷交換位置。
captions: 框架模型俯視。
框架模型側視。
框架模型另一側。

sections.heading: Identity II - Twin Reliefs of Resilience and Softness
sections.body: Continuing an earlier study of a fragmented self, the series asks whether resilience and softness can live together within a single composition. Simple line drawings first tested how geometric and organic edges might combine, and small colour studies then guided the choice of material for each relief. Sharp blocks stand for resilience, while curved layers of corrugated board express softness. Across the two reliefs, the balance between these qualities is struck in different ways. Lifted finally into a free-standing framework of folded planes and sticks, the reliefs reveal a further shift: seen from different sides, the hard and soft parts keep changing places. Selfhood is no longer understood as a single face but as a doubled presence, negotiated anew with every turn of the body, where strength and tenderness do not cancel each other but complete one another, and where the act of walking around a form becomes a way of knowing it.

zh-Hant.heading: 身分II-韌性與柔軟的雙重浮雕
zh-Hant.body: 延續先前關於破碎自我的研究，這個系列追問韌性與柔軟能否共存於同一個構成之中。簡單的線條圖首先測試幾何與有機的邊緣如何結合，小幅色彩研究接著引導每件浮雕的材料選擇。銳利的量塊象徵韌性，瓦楞紙板的曲層則表達柔軟，兩件浮雕以不同方式拿捏兩者之間的平衡。最終，浮雕被延伸為由摺面與木條構成的獨立框架；從不同角度觀看，堅硬與柔軟的部分不斷交換位置。自我不再被理解為單一的面貌，而是在轉身之間持續協商的雙重存在，堅強與溫柔在此彼此成全。

sections.body: The project starts from a question the student carried since childhood: why some colours and spaces feel calm, safe or overwhelming. It aims to create an emotional space that supports, soothes or gently activates young children.
captions: The student's own childhood drawings.

zh-Hant.body: 作品源自學生從小就有的疑問：為什麼某些色彩與空間讓人感到平靜、安全或不知所措。它希望創造一個能支持、安撫或溫和激發幼兒的情緒空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The student studied their own childhood drawings for the colours, forms and marks used in different moods. These traces were translated into abstract colour compositions.
captions: Abstract compositions from colour relationships.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生分析自己童年畫作中，不同情緒下使用的色彩、形狀與筆觸。這些痕跡被轉譯為抽象的色彩構成。
captions: 從色彩關係發展的抽象構成。
由抽象構成發展的空間研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The abstractions became spatial studies that use colour psychology to shape volumes, thresholds and light. Process models test these ideas at a child's scale.
captions: Process models.
Overview of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 抽象構成被發展為空間研究，以色彩心理學塑造量體、門檻與光線。過程模型則以兒童尺度測試這些想法。
captions: 過程模型。
模型全景。

sections.body: The final model joins red, orange and blue volumes with stairs, platforms and a mirrored threshold. It reflects how children perceive space long before they can describe it.
captions: Front view of the model.
Side view with the mirrored threshold.
Details of the volumes.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以樓梯、平台與鏡面門檻串連紅、橘、藍三色量體。它反映出兒童在能夠言說之前，便已感知空間的方式。

帶鏡面門檻的側面。
量體細部。

sections.heading: Design From Childhood - Colour That Soothes Young Minds
sections.body: Why do some colours and spaces feel calm, safe or overwhelming? A question carried since childhood became the starting point here, with the aim of creating an emotional space that supports, soothes or gently activates young children. Returning to childhood drawings, the student studied the colours, forms and marks used in different moods, then translated these traces into abstract colour compositions. Those abstractions grew into spatial studies that use colour psychology to shape volumes, thresholds and light. Process models tested each idea at a child's scale. The final model joins red, orange and blue volumes through stairs, platforms and a mirrored threshold. It reflects how children perceive space long before they can describe it, and the marks of an early hand quietly grow into a tender architecture, one that listens to feeling first and treats colour as a language that the very young already speak fluently.

zh-Hant.heading: 來自童年的設計-以色彩安撫幼小心靈
zh-Hant.body: 為什麼某些色彩與空間讓人感到平靜、安全，或不知所措？這個學生從小便懷抱的疑問，成為作品的起點，目標是創造一個能支持、安撫或溫和激發幼兒的情緒空間。學生回頭分析自己童年的畫作，找出不同情緒下所使用的色彩、形狀與筆觸，並將這些痕跡轉譯為抽象的色彩構成。抽象構成接著發展為空間研究，以色彩心理學塑造量體、門檻與光線，過程模型則以兒童的尺度驗證這些想法。最終，紅、橘、藍三色量體由樓梯、平台與鏡面門檻串連起來。作品映照出兒童在能夠言說之前便已感知空間的方式，童年的筆觸也在此長成溫柔的建築。

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 框架單元被串接成能彎成弧形與群組的鏈狀結構。接著將摺紙板固定於木條之間，形成表皮。

zh-Hant.body: 最終結構可以徒手摺疊與展開，同時支持互動與退隱。一系列照片呈現空間在運動中的變化。

徒手摺疊結構。
運動中的空間。

sections.heading: Transformable Shelter - Folding Between Openness and Enclosure
sections.body: Growing out of an earlier personal project by the student, this work explores adaptable space that can shift between openness and enclosure. Small stick frames first tested how joints allow a unit to open and close, while origami studies searched for folds that could cover the frames and still move with them. The frame units were then joined into chains that bend into arcs and gather into clusters. Folded paper panels, fixed between the sticks, formed a continuous skin. In its final state the structure folds and unfolds by hand, supporting both interaction and retreat, and a sequence of photographs records the space changing as it moves. Shelter here is no longer a fixed box but a condition that fingers can rewrite, breathing softly between gathering and dispersal, between opening outward and drawing in, so that a single structure can offer company one moment and solitude the next.

zh-Hant.heading: 可變形庇護所-在開放與圍合之間摺疊
zh-Hant.body: 延伸自學生先前的一個個人計畫，這件作品探索能在開放與圍合之間轉換的可變空間。小型木條框架首先被用來測試節點如何讓單元開合，摺紙研究則尋找既能覆蓋框架、又能隨之活動的摺法。框架單元隨後被串接成鏈狀結構，可以彎成弧形，也能聚成群組；摺紙板被固定在木條之間，形成一層表皮。最終，整座結構可以徒手摺疊與展開，同時支持互動與退隱，一系列照片記錄了空間在運動中的變化。庇護不再是一個固定的盒子，而是一種可以被手指改寫的狀態，在聚與散、敞開與收攏之間輕輕呼吸。

sections.heading: Summer Studio I - Building Space from the Verbs of Form
sections.body: Rather than beginning with a building programme, the studio starts from the simple verbs of form, and each operation has to be shown clearly in a small physical model. Six operations were tested in turn: reflection, stack, geometry, intersect, span and filter, with quick diagrams fixing the logic of each before anything was built. Rotating sticks around black blocks turned repetition into a spiral of movement. On stacked boxes, wavy cut screens explored how light is filtered as it passes through a surface. The final piece layers these earlier operations over a large line drawing, where curved screens, stick fans and black frames meet in a single composition. Simple verbs thus accumulate into a complex spatial grammar, letting the thinking of form come before questions of use and laying a clear foundation for future design, one in which every gesture can be named, tested and recombined.

zh-Hant.heading: 暑期設計課I-以形式動詞構築空間
zh-Hant.body: 這門課不從建築機能出發，而是以形式的基本動詞作為起點，每一種操作都必須在小型實體模型中清楚呈現。反射、堆疊、幾何、交錯、跨越與過濾六種操作逐一被測試，動手之前，先以快速圖解確立每一種操作的邏輯。木條繞著黑色量塊旋轉，讓重複化為螺旋的運動；堆疊盒體上的波浪鏤空面，則探討光線如何穿過表面而被過濾。最終作品將先前的操作疊合在一張大幅線稿之上，曲面屏、木條扇形與黑色框架在同一個構成中交會。簡單的動詞由此累積成複雜的空間文法，讓形式的思考先於用途，也為日後的設計奠下清晰的根基。
